title: Agent Constructor — Design Plan
content: *Drafted 2026-06-12 from design discussion. Owner: Ara + brain.*

title: Cloud policy (three tiers)
content:
Context: no income at present; local 3060 Ti is the workhorse. Cloud is
for leverage, not volume, until the brain pays its own way.

- **Tier 0 — local Ollama (default).** Everything routes here unless a
  policy explicitly elevates it. This is current behavior, kept.
- **Tier 1 — Ollama Cloud free models, higher-order steps only.**
  Allowed for: `construct_agent` planning, model selection, evaluator
  scoring. Low call volume, high leverage. The existing 429→local
  fallback is the safety net. Ollama does not document which cloud
  models are free, so the brain measures it: a probe records which
  models respond vs. return payment/quota errors, written into the model
  catalog as observed availability with a timestamp.
- **Tier 2 — Gemini / Anthropic: locked.** Keys stay configured; policy
  refuses them until an explicit income-mode flag is flipped. The
  constructor may still log "would have chosen X" so the cost of the
  lock is measurable later.

The "which model is best" question is answered empirically, not from
benchmarks: evaluator scores accumulate per (model × task type) on the
actual workload via PERFORMED edges, and the constructor prefers
observed winners. The catalog only needs a periodic refresh of what is
installed/reachable; quality ranking builds itself.

title: Constructor flow
content:
```
Task → decompose_goal (exists)
  → per subtask:
      1. query self-model: candidate tools (semantic match on tool
         descriptions), best profile or note the gap, candidate models
         by capability within the active cloud tier
      2. consult PERFORMED history for similar steps
      3. reuse a winning AgentSpec, or assemble a new one; emit
         ChainSteps with per-step model + context_profile + provider_hint
  → adversarial pre-flight, elevated min_robustness (exists)
  → enqueue_chain (exists) → evaluator grades (exists)
  → write PERFORMED edge → constructor gets smarter
```

Capability gaps (no decent tool/profile/model for a step) auto-create
improvement tasks — red-run takeaway #4.

title: Open questions
content:
- Income-mode flag shape: env var, config file, or a graph policy node?
- Free-tier probe cadence and which models to probe first.
- Whether evaluator scoring itself earns Tier 1 by default or stays local.

title: Phase 0a — usage accounting fix (trust gate, in progress)
content:
Audit findings (2026-06-12), all confirmed in code:

1. Token counts never reach the ledger. Providers parse a combined
   `tokens_evaluated` (and Ollama drops prompt tokens entirely), but
   `SharedLlm` discards it and `model_usage.tokens_in/out` stay NULL.
   Calls are counted, tokens are not; quotas are token budgets.
2. `clients/chat.rs` (and `context_builder.rs`) build LLM clients
   directly — zero telemetry. Chat is the main cloud consumer.
3. Rate-limited cloud calls are dropped from the ledger: the 429→local
   fallback in `shared_llm.rs` returns early without recording the
   failed cloud call — the most valuable quota signal is the one
   guaranteed missing.
4. `model_usage.cost` hardcoded NULL despite registry carrying rates.
5. No time-windowed stats (quotas are hourly/daily; ledger is all-time)
   and no usage tool since the April tool reduction (REST only).

Fix scope:

- Extend `GenerateResult` with `tokens_in` / `tokens_out`; populate in
  every provider parser (Ollama `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`,
  Anthropic `usage`, Gemini `usageMetadata`, openai-compat `usage`).
- `SharedLlm`: pass real token counts to `record_model_usage`; record
  the failed cloud call (with an `error_kind`-style marker) before
  falling back to local.
- Instrument chat: record one `model_usage` row per chat LLM call with
  whatever usage the stream exposes (all four providers emit usage in
  their final chunk).
- `record_model_usage`: compute cost from `model_registry` rates when
  tokens are present.
- Windowed aggregation (`?hours=24`) in `get_model_stats` + restore
  brain-callable usage visibility (extend the existing tool, no new
  tool).

title: Phasing
content:
- **0a. Usage accounting** — above. Trust gate for any cloud autonomy.
  ✅ implemented + live-verified 2026-06-12.
- **0b. Self-model sync** — introspection meta-graph. No behavior change.
  ✅ implemented 2026-06-12 (`services/self_model.rs`).
- **1. Per-step model selection** — `ChainStep.required_capabilities`,
  resolved at execution within the active `CLOUD_TIER` (default 1).
  ✅ implemented 2026-06-13 (`services/model_router.rs`, `SELECTED_LLM`
  task-local in queue.rs, precedence selected > local-pin > active in
  SharedLlm; learn chain's reason step is the first consumer). Known
  limitation: semaphore selection still follows `provider_hint`, so a
  capability-routed cloud call runs under the ollama semaphore.
- **2. `construct_agent` tool** — LLM-planned AgentSpec constrained to
  the self-model; Tier 1 model for the planning call itself.
  ✅ implemented 2026-06-13 (`skills/constructor.rs`). Plans are validated
  against the live ToolDef inventory (unknown tools rejected, self-modifying
  tools denylisted, step budget capped at 10); specs persist as
  `(:AgentSpec)` with a `CONSTRUCTED_FOR` edge to the dispatched Task;
  dispatch always prepends adversarial review at min_robustness 3.0 and
  appends the evaluator when success_criteria is set. Phase 2 limitation:
  an adversarial abort retries through the standard keyword pipeline,
  not the constructed spec (reuse-before-construct is Phase 3).
- **3. Learning loop** — PERFORMED edges, reuse-before-construct,
  capability-gap tasks, usage-aware tier escalation proposals.
  ✅ implemented 2026-06-13: the queue's evaluator hook writes
  `(:AgentSpec)-[:PERFORMED {score, passed, at}]->(:Task)` on every graded
  constructed run (pass and fail); `construct_agent` reuses the best
  word-overlap-matching spec with avg score ≥ 3.5 (override with
  `force_new: true`), re-validating its steps against the current tool
  inventory; unknown-tool plan rejections auto-create deduped
  "Capability gap" tasks. Deferred: usage-aware tier escalation
  proposals, model-level preference from PERFORMED history (the router
  still ranks by cost/context only).

title: Self-model schema (Phase 0b — absorbs the "Build schema" todo) ✅ implemented 2026-06-12
content:
Meta-graph generated by introspection at the end of every `build_skills()`
(`services/self_model.rs`) — never hand-maintained (same philosophy as
`managed_by`: files/code are truth, the graph reflects them). Full-refresh
sync: stale nodes are deleted.

- `(:ToolDef {name, description, skill, synced_at})` — from the live tool registry
- `(:ContextProfile {name, description, model_preference, provider_hint,
  allows_all, synced_at})` — from `contexts/*.yaml` via `ContextBuilderService`
- `(:ModelDef {name, provider, model, context_window, cost_per_1k_input,
  cost_per_1k_output, capabilities, synced_at})` — from the DuckDB model
  registry. (Label is `ModelDef`, not the planned `ModelSpec`, to avoid
  confusion with the Rust `ModelSpec` struct.) Observed availability /
  rate-limit annotations come later with the Tier-1 probe.
- `(:ContextProfile)-[:ALLOWS]->(:ToolDef)` — `allows_all: true` instead of
  edges when the profile's allowlist is empty
- Chains/schedules are NOT duplicated as `ChainTemplate` — `(:SchedulerChain)`
  and `(:ScheduledTask)` nodes already are the graph representation.

Phase 3 additions (✅ built 2026-06-13):
- `(:AgentSpec {name, model, profile, steps_json, created_by})`
- `(:AgentSpec)-[:PERFORMED {score, task_type, duration_ms, cost, at}]->(:Task)`
  — written by the evaluator loop after every graded run

title: Settled decisions (2026-06-12)
content:
1. **Explicit `construct_agent` tool** callable from chat and chains;
   wired into the scheduler only after it has earned trust.
2. **Persistent AgentSpecs** — `(:AgentSpec)` nodes with performance
   history, not ephemeral plans. The history is the learning loop.
3. **Adversarial review is mandatory** for every constructed
   (non-template) chain, with a higher `min_robustness` than template
   chains get.
4. **Tiered cloud policy** (below) — enforced in code, gated on fixed
   usage accounting.

title: Vision
content:
An agent that assembles other agents. Given a Task (or subtask), the
constructor deliberately picks the four ingredients that today are chosen
statically and separately:

| Ingredient | Existing primitive | Today's selection |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `ModelSelector` (capability filter → cheapest-first, DuckDB catalog) | Background jobs pinned to `provider_hint: ollama` |
| Tools + prompt | `ContextProfile` (YAML personas: allowlist + system prompt) | Keyword `auto_assign(goal)`, one profile per chain |
| Steps | `SchedulerChain` templates / `decompose_goal` | Static keyword pattern match |
| Quality gate | Evaluator loop + adversarial pre-flight | Per-task via `success_criteria` |

An **AgentSpec** is the tuple *(model, context profile, chain steps,
success criteria)*. The constructor composes AgentSpecs per subtask,
records how they perform, and prefers what has demonstrably worked.

~70% of the pipeline already exists. The new pieces are the self-model
schema, the assembly logic, and honest usage accounting.

title: Not doing
content:
- **YouTube 404s (problem 7):** documented throttling, already retried; leave it.
- **The `nia-actor-motivation-monitoring` schedule from the chat:** it was never saved, and the draft had several defects:
  - `provider_hint` inside `arguments`.
  - `:Actor`/`:Threat` labels that don't exist.
  - Search results dropped before `reason`.
  - `source_record` used for the brain's own speculation.

  If we still want to watch actors' motives, design it on purpose, as a claim-based monitor of named, sourced reports with `unsourced_synthesis` for anything inferred, and only after Step 1. Otherwise the verifier would mark its speculation corroborated.

title: Step 1 — Stop the verifier from citing the graph (problem 1)
content:
**Mechanism.** `verify_one` (`crates/app/src/skills/claims.rs`) calls `search_web`. Since 2026-09-12, `SearchSkill::with_prior_knowledge` (`skills/search.rs`) prefixes every successful result with a "WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW" block of matching notes. That block quotes the claim itself. `assess_evidence` reads it and answers "supports", often naming the claim's own note as `source`. `check_independence` then counts domains across the whole text, unrelated web results included, and passes. Example: the quote "My legs!" was corroborated by a sleep.com article on vivid dreams.

**Changes.**
1. `SearchInput` (`skills/search.rs:1505`): add `#[serde(default = "default_true")] prior_knowledge: bool`. Skip `with_prior_knowledge` when it's false, on all three return paths (lines ~981, ~995, ~1011). Add it to the tool's `input_schema` and describe it as meant for verifiers, which need external evidence only.
2. `verify_one`: pass `"prior_knowledge": false`.
3. Also in `verify_one`: after an `assess_evidence` "supports", reject the verdict unless `verdict.source` is a URL, or a domain, that appears among the search results' `link` fields. Record it as `support_rejected_unsourced`, following the `support_rejected_not_independent` pattern.
4. `evidence_domains` / `check_independence`: count domains from result `link` fields only, not from any text in the body, so a quoted note can't add domains.
5. Tests:
   - `search_web` with `prior_knowledge:false` returns no block.
   - A support whose source is a graph note is rejected.
   - Domains are counted from `link` fields only.

**Check it worked.** After a rebuild, run `verify_claims` with a small `limit`. New `claim_evidence` notes contain no "WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW". Over a day or two the corroboration rate should drop back toward the 40% range, and refutations should reappear.

title: Step 2 — Undo the contaminated corroborations (problem 1, data)
content:
The judge's input was contaminated for **every** verification since 09-12, not only the 169 edges whose source isn't a URL. So reset all corroborations recorded since then and let the fixed verifier re-earn the real ones. This is a separate deliverable from Step 1.

Create `scripts/reset_selfcorroborated_claims.cypher`. Count first, then run the reset with the brain stopped or the verifier paused:

```cypher
// 1. Count (dry run)
MATCH (c:Note {note_type:'claim'})-[r:CORROBORATED_BY]->()
WHERE r.found_at >= datetime('2026-09-12')
RETURN count(DISTINCT c) AS claims, count(r) AS edges;

// 2. Reset
MATCH (c:Note {note_type:'claim'})-[r:CORROBORATED_BY]->()
WHERE r.found_at >= datetime('2026-09-12')
WITH c, collect(r) AS rs
FOREACH (x IN rs | DELETE x)
WITH DISTINCT c
SET c.claim_status = CASE
      WHEN EXISTS { (c)-[:CORROBORATED_BY]->() } AND EXISTS { (c)-[:CONTRADICTED_BY]->() } THEN 'disputed'
      WHEN EXISTS { (c)-[:CORROBORATED_BY]->() } THEN 'corroborated'
      WHEN EXISTS { (c)-[:CONTRADICTED_BY]->() } THEN 'refuted'
      ELSE 'unverified' END,
    c.last_verify_attempt_at = NULL,
    c.reset_reason = 'self-corroboration via search_web prior_knowledge, 2026-09-12..2026-09-24'
RETURN c.claim_status AS status, count(*) AS n;
```

Before running it:
- Check that the `CASE` matches `recompute_status` in `services/claims.rs`, including whether it also sets `corroborating_count` / `contradicting_count`. If it does, set those here too.
- Setting `last_verify_attempt_at` to null puts these claims at the front of the verification queue. With about 300 claims, that's about 300 web searches spread over the daily sweeps.

Leave the old `claim_evidence` notes in place, since they're the audit trail, and optionally tag them `contaminated: true`.

title: Step 3 — Tell the user when a tool call fails to parse (problem 2)
content:
`extract_tool_call` (`clients/chat.rs:4017`) logs at WARN and returns `None`. The caller at `:3688` then treats the text as a finished answer, so the user reads "I am now setting this up" and nothing happened.

**Change.** When the text contains a `<tool_call>` opener but parsing fails, return an error variant instead of `None`. The loop then feeds a correction back to the model, as it does for other tool errors: "your tool call was not valid JSON: <serde error>; re-emit it." Allow one retry. If the retry also fails, append a visible line to the reply saying the tool call was malformed and did not run, and name the tool. Never let prose that promises an action stand when the action didn't run. `tool_trace_receipt` already exists for this kind of check, so reuse it.

**Test.** Feed the 03:42 malformed `manage_scheduled_task` payload (the third step object is never closed) and assert the turn does not end with a silent success.

title: Step 4 — Front-door model choice (problem 3). Decision needed
content:
In the same chat, gemma4:31b-cloud handed every question to `knowledge-worker` (turns 1–5). After the profile was saved at 03:34 UTC pinned to `gemini-2.5-flash`, Gemini answered turn 7 from conversation memory, with no tool calls and invented citation IDs.

Options:
- **A.** Pin the front door back to `gemma4:31b-cloud` (free Ollama Cloud, `no_log`, so the profile could also go back to `data_class: private`).
- **B.** Keep Gemini and add a rule: any answer with `[[id:…]]` citations must come from a turn in which a retrieval tool ran.
- **Structural either way:** after the reply is composed, check each cited `id:` against the graph and flag the ones that don't exist. This catches invented IDs whichever model is in use.

Recommendation: A plus the ID check. Measure against a twin before deciding, the way CLAUDE.md's "Going local" section does.

title: Step 5 — GDELT (problem 4). Decision needed
content:
The schedule calls `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/events/events`, which doesn't exist. Its `mode:"timeline"` and `timespan:"24"` aren't valid GDELT values either. The real keyless API is the DOC 2.0 API. A probe on 2026-09-24 of `…/api/v2/doc/doc?query=(Mossad OR GRU OR CIA) sourcelang:english&mode=artlist&format=json&timespan=24h` worked, but the results were noisy (a wrestling preview, Oscars coverage, sott.net).

Options:
- **Fix it for volume signals:** `mode=timelinevol` with `timespan=7d`, and feed the `reason` step only the spike. Treat GDELT as a "coverage is spiking" tripwire, never as evidence. If articles are needed, add `domainis:` filters from the `news` SourceList.
- **Disable it:** `SET s.enabled=false, s.paused_reason='GDELT endpoint 404 since 09-08; see BRAIN_ASSESSMENT_FIXES_PLAN'`.

Either way:
- Delete or label the 15 "no data" inference notes (`Q: Based on the GDELT event data…`).
- Make the schedule's `http_request` step fail on a non-2xx status, or add a step that checks the result, so a 404 stops counting as completed. Longer term, this is a lint idea: an `http_request` step whose result is never checked.

title: Step 6 — Mount `schemas/` (problem 5)
content: Add `- SCHEMAS_DIR=/home/agent/agent-brain/schemas` to the `agent-brain` environment in `docker-compose.yml`, next to `CHAINS_DIR`. The directory is already under the mounted repo; confirm with `docker exec agent-brain-agent-brain-1 ls /home/agent/agent-brain/schemas`. **Check it worked:** the startup WARN disappears.

content:
Google News through SerpApi works (143 of 149 calls succeeded in 30 days). Switching to the `serpapi` engine wouldn't save anything, because it uses the same 250-a-month account. What drained the quota was a burst of 88 `serpapi` calls on 08-31, on top of about 210 a month from the news brief.

- Optional: find the source of the 08-31 burst (`search_usage` rows for that day) and cap it.

title: 0. The reframe that makes this tractable
content:
The obvious framing — "pick a mesh network for the brains" — is the wrong
question, and answering it first produces an unbuildable design. (See
`CLAUDE.md` § *Self-knowledge*: a chat session on 2026-08-23 confidently
proposed a three-tier Nebula/Meshtastic/Reticulum architecture that could not
work, because Nebula is an IP overlay, Meshtastic carries ~1 kbps of non-IP
packets, and Reticulum has no IP layer at all.)

Two observations reorder the problem:

1. **Brain-to-brain traffic is message-shaped, not RPC-shaped.** What brains send
   each other is claims, notes, source records, task offers, and capability
   announcements. Small, self-contained, latency-tolerant, safe to reorder. It is
   not "call this function and block."
2. **Every transport gives transport authentication, and transport
   authentication is not provenance.** TLS, WireGuard, mTLS, QUIC — all of them
   authenticate *the channel*. The instant a payload leaves the connection and
   lands in Neo4j, that guarantee is gone and the brain is trusting its own
   ingest path. But `asserted_by` is a durable graph property that outlives the
   connection by months.

So the load-bearing artifact is **a signed envelope**, not a network. The
transport is a swappable detail — and once the envelope exists, we can run more
than one transport with different failure modes.

---

title: 1. Design decisions (locked)
content:
| Decision | Choice |
|----------|--------|
| Primary abstraction | **Signed envelope, transport-agnostic.** Defined once as a `.proto`; every transport carries the same bytes. |
| Identity | **One Ed25519 keypair per brain instance**, independent of transport. The public key *is* the brain's address on every transport. |
| Trust model | **Message-level signatures, verified at ingest.** Transport auth is defence-in-depth, never the provenance record. |
| Transport count | **Two, with different failure modes.** Transport A (online, high-throughput) and Transport B (degraded, permissionless, store-and-forward). Never one. |
| Transport A, phase 1 | **HTTP + protobuf over Tailscale.** Already deployed, already trusted, zero new infrastructure. |
| Transport B | **LXMF over Reticulum**, via a Python sidecar. Survives no-IP and offline peers. |
| Reticulum implementation | **RetiNet (AGPL-3.0) or Reticulum_CE — never `markqvist/Reticulum`.** See § 6.1; the upstream license conflicts with `digest_experiences`. |
| Peer list | **`peers/*.yaml`, seeded ON CREATE, graph-owned afterwards.** Follows the `SourceList` / `MediaSource` pattern exactly. |
| Peer claims and independence | **A peer brain never counts toward `MIN_INDEPENDENT_DOMAINS`.** New `peer_brain` tier in `classify_domains`. See § 5.2 — this is the highest-risk item in the plan. |
| Rejected | WebRTC, Meshtastic, IP-over-Reticulum, bare Tailscale-only. See § 7. |

---

title: 2. Why this fits the current architecture
content:
Most of the primitives already exist:

- **The claims layer is the consumer.** `(:Note {note_type:'claim', claim_status,
  asserted_by, asserted_at})` with `ASSERTED_IN` / `CORROBORATED_BY` /
  `CONTRADICTED_BY` edges, status *derived* by `recompute_status` rather than
  asserted. A peer brain's identity hash is a far better `asserted_by` value
  than a domain string, because it is self-certifying.
- **Retrieval labelling already exists.** `label_claims` in
  `services/knowledge.rs` prefixes claims and source records on the way out.
  Peer-sourced material needs one more prefix variant, not a new mechanism.
- **The sidecar pattern is established.** `sandbox`, `whisper`, and `searxng` are
  all compose services the brain talks to over HTTP on an internal network. A
  Reticulum sidecar is the fourth instance of a pattern, not a new one.
- **YAML-seeded, graph-owned config lists.** `sources/*.yaml` and
  `sources-media/*.yaml` are seeded ON CREATE and owned by the graph afterwards.
  `peers/*.yaml` is the same seeder with a different node label.
- **Timestamps are already one representation.** Every temporal property is a
  native `DATETIME` in UTC (`project-docs/schema.md`), so a received envelope's
  timestamps have an unambiguous home. Envelope wire format stays RFC 3339
  strings; conversion happens at ingest via `datetime($param)`.
- **Snapshots already exist for bulk sync.** `services/snapshot.rs` produces
  gzipped JSON. Transport A's bulk path is "ship a snapshot", not a new
  serialization format.

**Net new surface:** one crate-level module for identity/envelope, one skill, one
sidecar, one seed dir, and three graph additions.

---

title: 3. Architecture
content:
```
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Layer 3 — Ingest & epistemics   │
                    │  verify sig → classify → graph   │
                    └────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                     │
                    ┌────────────────▼─────────────────┐
                    │  Layer 2 — Envelope (.proto)      │
                    │  signed, transport-agnostic       │
                    └────┬──────────────────────┬───────┘
                         │                      │
              ┌──────────▼─────────┐  ┌─────────▼──────────┐
              │   Transport A      │  │   Transport B      │
              │  online / bulk     │  │  degraded / async  │
              │  HTTP over         │  │  LXMF over         │
              │  Tailscale         │  │  Reticulum         │
              │  → iroh (phase 5)  │  │  (Python sidecar)  │
              └──────────┬─────────┘  └─────────┬──────────┘
                         │                      │
                    ┌────▼──────────────────────▼───────┐
                    │  Layer 0 — Identity                │
                    │  one Ed25519 keypair per brain     │
                    └────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The two transports are **not** a primary and a fallback in the failover sense.
They carry different traffic:

| | Transport A | Transport B |
|---|---|---|
| Carries | snapshots, embeddings, transcripts, bulk note sync | claims, task offers, capability announces |
| Payload size | MB | < 1 KB |
| Peer must be online | yes | no (propagation nodes hold messages) |
| Needs IP | yes | no |
| Needs a control plane | yes (tailnet) | no |

---

title: 4. New components › 4.1 `crates/models/src/envelope.rs` + `proto/brain_envelope.proto`
4. New components › 4.2 `crates/app/src/services/peer_identity.rs`
content:
Loads or generates the brain's keypair. Storage: a real secret store, **not** a
file next to the binary. (The old `SECRET_PROVIDER` local AES-GCM / Vault / AWS
module was never wired into anything and was removed as dead code on 2026-10-02;
the replacement is the age-based vault design.) —
this key is the brain's identity and leaking it lets anyone forge its assertions.

Exposes `sign(&Envelope) -> Signature` and `verify(&Envelope) -> Result<PeerId>`.

title: 4. New components › 4.3 `crates/app/src/skills/peer.rs` — new skill
content:
| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `peer_send` | Assert a claim / share a note / offer a task to a named peer or broadcast |
| `peer_list` | List known peers, their transports, last-seen, trust state |
| `manage_peer` | Upsert / activate / deactivate a peer (mirrors `manage_media_source`) |

Register to **both** `tool_registry` and the `skills` vec in `build_skills()` —
forgetting either yields an invisible tool or a dispatch failure.

`peer_send` must be **safe to insert mid-chain**, which means it echoes its input
as `answer` (like `store_note`, `notify_user`, and `claim` do). A tool that
silently replaces the chain payload with its own metadata breaks every downstream
step — see `CLAUDE.md` on the `claim` tool echo fix.

title: 4. New components › 4.4 `reticulum-sidecar/` — new compose service
content:
Python, owns the RNS Identity and LXMF. Exposes a minimal HTTP/JSON API on
`brain-internal`:

- `POST /send` — `{peer_hash, envelope_b64}` → queued for LXMF delivery
- `GET  /inbox` — long-poll or drain received envelopes
- `GET  /status` — RNS interface state, propagation node reachability

Compose constraints, modelled on the `sandbox` service:

- On `brain-internal` only, **no `ports:` mapping**.
- Needs *outbound* network for its Reticulum interfaces (unlike `sandbox`, which
  is deliberately on an `internal: true` network). This is the one sidecar that
  legitimately reaches the outside world, so it gets no credentials: no
  `env_file`, therefore no `NEO4J_PASSWORD` / `OLLAMA_API_KEY` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `read_only: true` root with a named
  volume for the RNS identity + config.

title: 4. New components › 4.5 `peers/*.yaml` — new seed dir
content:
```yaml
name: workshop-brain
pubkey: "b3f1…"            # 32-byte Ed25519, hex
description: "Bench instance, LoRa-attached"
active: true
transports:
  - kind: tailscale_http
    endpoint: "http://workshop-brain:3000"
  - kind: reticulum_lxmf
    destination_hash: "a17c…"
trust:
  accept_claims: true
  accept_task_offers: false   # default deny — see § 5.3
```

Seeded ON CREATE only, graph-owned afterwards (the `SourceList` model). Missing
directory is non-fatal. **Add `PEERS_DIR` to compose env** — a new seed dir that
isn't in the compose environment is invisible in Docker, which is where the brain
actually runs.

title: 4. New components › 4.6 Graph additions
content:
```
(:PeerBrain {pubkey, name, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, active, managed_by})
(:Note)-[:RECEIVED_FROM {message_id, received_at, transport}]->(:PeerBrain)
(:PeerBrain)-[:ASSERTED]->(:Note {note_type:'claim'})
```

`pubkey` is the unique key, not `name`. All three timestamps are native
`DATETIME` — the `no_string_timestamps` integration test will catch it if not.

---

title: 5. Epistemics integration — the part that matters most
content:
Getting bytes between brains is the easy half. This is the half that decides
whether federation makes the brain smarter or just louder.

title: 5. Epistemics integration — the part that matters most › 5.1 Received claims are labelled, not laundered
content:
A claim arriving from a peer is **not** knowledge this brain established. It
takes `note_type: 'claim'` with `asserted_by` set to the peer's pubkey, and
`label_claims` gains a variant:

```
[CLAIM · unverified · asserted by peer workshop-brain (b3f1…) · 2 days ago]
```

The peer name appears for readability; the truncated pubkey appears because names
are untrusted. Both, always — a label with only the name is a label that can lie.

title: 5. Epistemics integration — the part that matters most › 5.2 A peer brain is never independent corroboration
content:
**This is the highest-risk item in the plan.** `check_independence` currently
requires `MIN_INDEPENDENT_DOMAINS` (2) distinct non-self-referential domains
before support counts. Naively feeding peer claims into that check breaks it in
the exact way the existing code already tries to prevent:

- Identity keypairs are **free to generate**. N brain identities are not N
  independent sources.
- A fleet of *your own* brains corroborating each other is precisely the circular
  case `check_independence` rejects for `skywatcher.ai`.
- Worse, the brains share ingest paths, source lists, and models — so they will
  frequently agree because they read the same page, not because two independent
  observers converged.

Required changes:

- Add a **`peer_brain` tier** to `classify_domains`, alongside `primary`,
  `established`, and `unclassified`.
- Peer assertions **never increment the independent-domain count.** They are
  recorded, labelled, and visible — but a claim corroborated only by peer brains
  stays `unverified`.
- Label renders the distinction explicitly:
  `[CLAIM · corroborated · peer brains only, not independent · …]`
- A peer claim's *underlying* sources (the URLs it cites) **do** count normally —
  those are real independent domains. Propagate them in `ClaimAssertion` so
  corroboration works on evidence rather than on hearsay.

The general rule, consistent with the rest of the epistemics layer: never gate
*storage* on trust tier, always gate *status* on it. Dropping peer claims would
destroy the record needed to notice a peer drifting; promoting them would launder
an assertion into established knowledge.

title: 5. Epistemics integration — the part that matters most › 5.3 Task offers default to deny
content:
`TaskOffer` lets a peer enqueue work in this brain. That is remote code execution
by a slightly longer path — the scheduler will route the goal to a chain and run
it. So:

- `accept_task_offers: false` is the **default** in `peers/*.yaml`.
- An accepted offer creates a `(:Task)` with `status: 'created'` and the peer's
  pubkey in `context`, so chain-death attribution and the evaluator loop both
  work normally.
- Offers are rate-limited per peer. A peer that can create unbounded tasks can
  exhaust the queue and the LLM quota.

title: 5. Epistemics integration — the part that matters most › 5.4 Contradiction between brains is a first-class outcome
content:
Two brains asserting incompatible claims should produce `disputed`, not a winner.
`recompute_status` already handles support-and-contradiction without collapsing
to a verdict, so this mostly falls out — but the reconciliation path must not
"prefer local" or "prefer newest". Both assertions are preserved with their
provenance.

---

title: 6. Constraints discovered during research › 6.1 The Reticulum license conflicts with `digest_experiences`
content:
Reticulum License 1.0 states:

> The Software shall not be used, directly or indirectly, in the creation of an
> artificial intelligence, machine learning or language model training dataset,
> including but not limited to any use that contributes to the training or
> development of such a model or algorithm.

The brain's `digest_experiences` / `SleepSkill` exports training data to
`DATASET_DIR`. That is literally creating a training dataset. The author's own
license primer argues "use" means technical incorporation rather than content
flowing through, and explicitly permits open-source AI development — but that
reading should not be load-bearing for a system whose stated purpose includes
training-data export.

**Mitigation, and it is clean:** the Reticulum *protocol* is public domain. Use a
wire-compatible implementation under an ordinary license:

| Implementation | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| RetiNet (`codeberg.org/skyguy/retinet`) | AGPL-3.0 | Drop-in RNS replacement, RNS 1.0 compatible. **Verify PyPI packaging** — Codeberg-hosted. |
| Reticulum_CE (`Reticulum-Community/Reticulum_CE`) | community fork | Same compatibility claim |
| Reticulum-rs (`BeechatNetworkSystemsLtd`) | MIT | Rust, but **LXMF not documented as supported** — see § 6.3 |

Running Reticulum in a *sidecar* rather than linking it into the Rust binary also
keeps the question at arm's length regardless of which implementation is chosen.

title: 6. Constraints discovered during research › 6.2 Reticulum's governance is unsettled
content:
Mark Qvist announced he was leaving development in December 2025; the issue
tracker was hidden and community management stopped. The ecosystem has since
fragmented across the Python original, RetiNet, Reticulum_CE, Reticulum-rs,
microReticulum (embedded C++), and a Go+WASM implementation — with known config
incompatibility between them. FOSDEM 2026 filled two sessions working out what to
do.

The protocol is stable and public domain; the *ecosystem* is in flux. This is a
direct argument for the two-transport design: Transport B must never be the only
way two brains can talk.

title: 6. Constraints discovered during research › 6.3 Reticulum's Rust implementation lacks the piece we want
content:
Reticulum-rs (MIT, actively developed) supports TCP, serial, and Kaonic — but
LXMF is not documented as supported, and neither is AutoInterface or RNode/LoRa.
LXMF store-and-forward is the entire reason Transport B exists, so the Rust path
does not currently work. Hence the Python sidecar. Revisit if `rsLXMF` matures.

title: 6. Constraints discovered during research › 6.4 Reticulum's byte budget shapes what can cross it
content:
Packet data field is 0–465 bytes; it needs only a 500-byte physical MTU and works
down to ~5 bits/sec. Large transfers use the `Resource` mechanism
(auto-compress, chunk, sequence, verify, reassemble) over an established Link,
but slowly. This is why snapshots go over Transport A and claims go over
Transport B — and why Phase 0 measures before anything is built.

---

title: 7. Rejected alternatives
content:
| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **WebRTC** | Its value proposition is NAT traversal via ICE/STUN/TURN. Tailscale already solves exactly that. Adopting it means reimplementing the hard part of Tailscale inside the application, building an SDP signaling channel, and operating a TURN server, to obtain a capability already deployed. Revisit only if a browser must be a *peer* rather than a client — and then prefer WebTransport. |
| **gRPC as the transport** | The *contract* half is valuable and is adopted (protobuf envelope, § 4.1). The transport half assumes a reachable `host:port` with no NAT traversal and no store-and-forward, so it cannot be Transport B. Adding `tonic` also means a second RPC paradigm and `protoc` in the build, alongside the HTTP+JSON the brain already speaks everywhere (MCP, sandbox, whisper, searxng). Not worth the tax at low message volume. |
| **Meshtastic** | Wrong layer. No general transport abstraction, flood routing that degrades badly, ~200-byte payloads, built for human chat and GPS. Note RNode and Meshtastic are alternative firmwares for overlapping LoRa boards, so hardware spend isn't wasted either way. |
| **IP-over-Reticulum** | Does not exist. There is no TUN device to point Bolt or HTTP at. `rngit` exists for git specifically and the manual warns it "has not been tested extensively in the wild." |
| **Tailscale/Nebula alone** | Gives transport auth only. Provenance dies at the graph boundary, which defeats the purpose (§ 0). Fine as *a* transport — it is Transport A — but not as the whole design. |
| **Nebula instead of Tailscale** | Not rejected, just orthogonal. Transport A talks HTTP to an endpoint; whether that endpoint is reachable via Tailscale or Nebula is a deployment detail the envelope never sees. Migrating later costs nothing. |

---

title: 8. Phases
content: Each phase is independently shippable and leaves the system working.

title: 8. Phases › Phase 0 — Measure before building
content:
No code. Answer these with numbers:

- How large is a real knowledge snapshot (`services/snapshot.rs` output, gzipped)?
- How many claims per day does the brain currently extract? (That is Transport B's
  actual load.)
- Bring up two RetiNet nodes on the LAN — `AutoInterface` discovers them via IPv6
  link-local multicast with zero config — and time `rncp` of a real snapshot.
  Inspect with `rnstatus` / `rnpath` / `rnprobe`.

**Exit criterion:** a measured split of which traffic belongs on which transport.
The architecture diagram in § 3 asserts this split; Phase 0 verifies it. If a
snapshot crosses Reticulum acceptably, Transport A gets simpler. If claims are
higher-volume than expected, Transport B needs batching.

title: 8. Phases › Phase 1 — Identity and envelope
content:
`proto/brain_envelope.proto`, `crates/models/src/envelope.rs`,
`services/peer_identity.rs`. Key stored via the secret store (see §4.2).

**Tests:** sign/verify round-trip; canonical-encoding stability across
re-serialization; tampered-field rejection; unknown-version rejection; unknown
pubkey rejection.

**Exit criterion:** a brain can sign an envelope and verify its own, with no
network involved.

title: 8. Phases › Phase 2 — Transport A over Tailscale
content:
`peers/*.yaml` + seeder, `(:PeerBrain)` node, `skills/peer.rs` with `peer_send` /
`peer_list` / `manage_peer`. HTTP POST of a protobuf envelope to a peer's
existing HTTP transport, plus a receive endpoint.

**Exit criterion:** two brains on the tailnet exchange a signed `NoteShare`,
verified at ingest, with a `RECEIVED_FROM` edge in the graph.

title: 8. Phases › Phase 3 — Ingest and epistemics
content:
The `peer_brain` tier in `classify_domains`, the `label_claims` variants, the
independence exclusion (§ 5.2), task-offer default-deny and rate limiting
(§ 5.3), idempotent ingest on `message_id`.

**Exit criterion:** a claim asserted by a peer and corroborated *only* by peers
remains `unverified`, and retrieval labels it as peer-sourced. This is the test
that proves federation didn't degrade the epistemics.

title: 8. Phases › Phase 4 — Transport B: Reticulum sidecar
content:
`reticulum-sidecar/` compose service on RetiNet/CE, LXMF send + inbox, transport
selection in `peer_send`. Start with Reticulum's `TCPClientInterface` pointed at
a *tailnet address* — this exercises the whole stack with zero radio hardware,
and swapping in an `RNodeInterface` later touches no brain code.

**Exit criterion:** brain A asserts a claim while brain B is *stopped*; brain B
receives it on next start via a propagation node.

title: 8. Phases › Phase 5 — Evaluate iroh (optional)
content:
[iroh](https://docs.iroh.computer/what-is-iroh) reached 1.0 in June 2026:
Rust-native QUIC peer-to-peer, hole punching with relay fallback (~90% success,
comparable to WebRTC in practice), and — the relevant part — **node identity is
an Ed25519 public key** (`EndpointId`, formerly `NodeId`), authenticated so it
cannot be impersonated. That is the same identity-as-address model as Reticulum
destination hashes, so one identity concept spans both transports and the
envelope design carries over unchanged. QUIC's independent streams also mean a
bulk snapshot transfer won't head-of-line-block a claim stream.

`tonic-iroh-transport` (0.9.2, May 2026) runs tonic services directly over iroh
connections — typed protobuf contracts over p2p QUIC. Pre-1.0 with nine breaking
changes across sixteen releases; treat as promising, not settled.

Caveat from its own docs, which reinforces § 0: iroh's DHT discovery is *"a
bootstrap mechanism, not a trust anchor... the shared DHT buckets are still
globally writable and can be spammed or overwritten."* The envelope signature is
what makes that acceptable.

**Exit criterion:** a decision, recorded here, on whether iroh replaces or
supplements Transport A's Tailscale dependency.

---

title: 9. Open questions
content:
- **Peer authorization.** `peers/*.yaml` is a manual allowlist. Is there ever an
  auto-discovery path, and if so what stops a hostile peer from being added?
  Current answer: no auto-discovery. Revisit only with a concrete need.
- **Conflict resolution beyond `disputed`.** § 5.4 preserves both assertions.
  Does anything ever need to *resolve* them, or is `disputed` the terminal state?
- **Snapshot sync semantics.** `SnapshotService` restore uses MERGE, which is
  safe on a non-empty graph — but does a peer's snapshot merge into the local
  graph, or land in a quarantined subgraph first? Leaning quarantine.
- **Does RetiNet ship on PyPI?** It is Codeberg-hosted; packaging story unverified.
- **Rate limits and quota.** A peer whose task offers or claim volume exhausts the
  local LLM quota is a denial-of-service by accident. Where does the limit live —
  the skill, the queue, or the sidecar?
- **Key rotation.** If a brain's keypair is compromised or rotated, what happens
  to the months of `asserted_by` history pointing at the old pubkey?

---

title: Brain-to-Brain Transport Plan — Federated Knowledge Exchange Between Brain Instances
content:
Handoff plan for letting multiple Agent Brain instances exchange knowledge with
**provenance that survives storage**. Goal: brain A can assert a claim to brain B
such that brain B can still verify *who said it* months later, after the message
has been relayed, stored, consolidated, and retrieved.

This document is the spec. Implement it in phases; each phase is independently
shippable and testable.

---

title: 2026-10-16: three version sets and no pin
content: Found while checking the DuckDB json extension: the container ran DuckDB 1.5.6, host tests 1.4.4. Cause: Cargo.lock was in .gitignore and the Dockerfile did not copy it, so there were three version sets: the host's private lock (165 packages behind crates.io), the container's (resolved by `rust:latest` whenever a Cargo.toml change missed the Docker layer cache, then frozen there until the next miss), and crates.io. The compiler floated too (`rust:latest` in Docker, rustup `stable` on the host; 1.99.1 was out while the host built with 1.98.1, and the Rust sandbox was pinned to 1.98.1 by hand). Owner: copying the lock into the image "made things go bad". Not reproduced; the likely cause is that the lock copied was the stale private one, which a fresh `rust:latest` then had to build. Fixed by updating first (251 lock changes, 1,017 unit tests and clippy clean on 1.99.1), then committing the lock, building `--locked`, pinning the compiler once and guarding the sandbox pin.

title: One set of versions: committed Cargo.lock, --locked image, one compiler pin
content:
- **Cargo.lock is committed** (it was git-ignored until 2026-10-16) and the brain image builds with `cargo build --release --locked`, so the container runs exactly the versions the host built and tested. A build whose Cargo.toml no longer matches the lock fails instead of re-resolving.
- **The compiler is named once, in `rust-toolchain.toml`.** rustup obeys it on the host and in the Docker builder (`FROM rust:1-trixie`, Debian matched to the `trixie-slim` runtime; rustup installs the pinned rustc on the first cargo call). The Rust sandbox builds from its own context and names `FROM rust:<same>-slim-trixie`; `the_rust_sandbox_runs_the_pinned_compiler` (host plugin tests) fails if the two disagree.
- **Update on purpose, never by accident:** `scripts/update_deps.sh` (semver-compatible crates) or `scripts/update_deps.sh --rust X.Y.Z` (also both compiler pins). It builds, runs clippy `-D warnings` and the unit tests, restores the previous lock and pins if any fails, and lists newer versions held back by version requirements without applying them (each major bump is its own code change). Then rebuild the image (and `docker compose build rust-sandbox` if the pin moved) and commit.
- Integration tests (`cargo test --test '*'`) default to `bolt://localhost:7688`, and there is no separate test Neo4j: the live graph is on 7689. Do not point them at it for a dependency check.
- Other images still float by design or by omission: neo4j:5, searxng and faster-whisper `latest`, yt-dlp `latest` (deliberate: YouTube breaks old versions), node/nginx in the HBI.

title: Named step outputs and step defaults
content:
A workflow step may carry an `id`. Any later step reads that step's output as `{{steps.<id>}}` (the same text `{{_prev}}` would give) or `{{steps.<id>.<path>}}` (a JSON path into its result, like `{{_prev.<path>}}`). `{{_prev}}` still means the step immediately before.

How it works: `enqueue_chain_owned` stamps `__step_jobs` ({id: job id} of every earlier named step) into the args of each step that references `{{steps.`; `resolve_named_steps` (queue.rs) loads those jobs when the step runs. A step that did not complete resolves to "[step '<id>' produced no output (<status: error>); say this section is unavailable]", never to an empty string, so a reader can tell a quiet day from a failed fetch. A path into a missing output is empty, as with `{{_prev.x}}`.

Validation (`validate_step_array`, so every save — `manage_workflow` upsert and REST `/workflows` — and lint): a reference must name an EARLIER step's id; ids are unique, non-empty, with no `.` or `}`. `{{inputs.<name>}}` must name a declared input (`validate_input_refs`). The unit test `every_workflow_file_is_valid` checks both over every `workflows/*.yaml`.

`defaults:` at the top of a workflow file is merged into every step by the seeder (`apply_step_defaults`); a field the step sets wins. Files only; `manage_workflow` upserts take full steps.

Why (2026-10-10, CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN Phase 2a): daily-news staged every section through push_context into a `news-raw-{{date}}` WorkingMemory session, read it back with a query, and needed a delete step at both ends because a failed run left blocks that compounded into a 306K-token context (yaml/schedules-daily-news-1). Named outputs removed 14 push_context steps and both cleanups: 32 steps to 18. Verified live: all 18 completed, every section populated, 6 claims ASSERTED_IN the stored brief via `{{steps.stored.id}}`.

title: The front door routes a turn before it runs; stored before the web is a rule, our names go with the task
content:
Rules (built 2026-10-14; `crates/chat/src/chat/route.rs`, the front door's `routing:` block):

- **A front door routes before it runs.** A profile with `routing:` gets each turn's first stop picked by the local model (E4B on the llama.cpp sidecar) from the live spawnable roster plus the profile's own choices (its tools as `self:<tool>`, and `answer`). The pick goes into the prompt as a short block. Routing is advice: a failure or a timeout (12 s) leaves the turn unrouted, never failed.
- **The routing data is the profile's, not Rust:** the rules, the choices, `stored`/`web` agents, the `web_words` pattern, `confident`. The rules are the owner's, graded on `eval/routing_golden.yaml`; change them there first, then measure (`route_bench.py` in the Phase 3 harness).
- **Stored before the web is a rule in code, not a model's choice.** A web pick for a turn that does not match `web_words` goes to the stored agent first. Both E4B and Nimble sent "Have you looked at Nebula" and "tell me about Adam Kinzinger" to the web, where the answer was stored.
- **Our names go with the task.** A turn or a delegated task naming one of our topics (by name, label or alias, whole words) is told to read it with `lookup`. A worker given "Opensource Intelligence Agency" otherwise searches the words and misses topic `nia`.
- **A model's self-rated confidence is not a signal.** E4B and codestral said ~0.95 whether right or wrong. Only Nimble's probability was calibrated (picks at ≥0.85 right 89%), so only it may split a turn (`CHAT_ROUTER_CHECKER`, off by default).
- **Host Ollama's GPU slice holds one of Nimble and bge-m3.** Each evicts the other; Nimble reloads in ~15 s. Don't turn the checker on without moving one of them (Nimble CPU-only costs ~8.5 s a call).
- **Every route is logged** to DuckDB `interactions` as `route: {message, session_id}` → `{plan, picked, checked, why, named}`, so mining can compare the route with the agents the turn used.
- **Behaviors before agents (Phase B).** A routing block's `behaviors:` entry `{name, view, says, slots, when, unless}` is offered as `lookup:<name>`. When it is picked, code runs it: E4B fills only `slots` (held to the view's schema), `lookup` runs, the rows go into the prompt, and that turn's front door gets no `delegate`. Its prompt says to always delegate, and the first live run delegated past the rows. A failed behavior goes to the stored agent.
- **A behavior fits by pattern, not by the model.** `when`/`unless` regexes decide that it applies. As a bare choice, `learned` drew 8 "what have we learned about X" turns and routing fell from 52 to 42; with the patterns, 57 of 66.
- **Every front-door turn logs one `turn:` row** (route, behavior call, every tool call from the stream, answered), and every 👍/👎 a `feedback:` row; the weekly `behavior-candidates` workflow mines them. Keep both row shapes stable, or the workflow's SQL silently counts nothing. The embedded DuckDB has no ICU: compare `epoch(timestamp)`, never a timestamptz minus an interval.
- **A report built from rows is rendered by SQL, not a model.** E4B given six rows to write up filed one under the wrong section, dropped another, and contradicted itself.

title: Chat wire adapters: which provider takes which wire, and why
content:
Three adapters feed the one round loop (`round_loop.rs`, `ProviderTurn`); `turn.rs` picks one by `LlmProviderType`. There is no text-parsing (`<tool_call>`) adapter any more (Phase 6a, 2026-10-11).

- **Anthropic** → `anthropic_loop.rs` (native Messages API, tool_use blocks).
- **Host Ollama** → `ollama_loop.rs` (native `/api/chat`). It stays native because Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint ignores `options`, so `num_ctx` cannot be set there, and without `num_ctx` host Ollama reads only the first ~2K tokens (measured 2026-10-11, Ollama 0.40.2: a ~15K-token prompt read as 2,050 tokens with no `num_ctx`, 15,293 with 16384). Every call sends `num_ctx` (`config.num_ctx`, else `ollama_num_ctx()`). Before 6a chat sent none, and 9 granite4 chat turns in 30 days answered from a truncated prompt.
- **Everything else** (Ollama Cloud, llama.cpp, Gemini, `OpenAiCompat` providers from models.yaml) → `openai_loop.rs`, `run_openai_loop`.

Gemini on the OpenAI wire:
- The endpoint is `{base_url or https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai}/chat/completions` (no `/v1`). `completions_url` reads `base_url`, so a Gemini config must carry `base_url: None` unless it really points at Google. The router gets None from models.yaml, and `main.rs` clears the default's host-Ollama URL when `LLM_PROVIDER=gemini`. Background `generate` takes the same URL since 6b: the native `GeminiProvider` is gone and Gemini runs on `OpenAiCompatProvider`, both built from `llm_providers::openai_compat::api_root` (measured against `generateContent` first: same latency, same prompt/completion counts; thinking happens on both wires, and the OpenAI wire only shows it in `total_tokens`).
- Gemini 3.x returns each tool call with `extra_content.google.thought_signature` and answers 400 "missing a thought_signature" unless the next request echoes it on that call. The adapter keeps each call's `extra_content` and sends it back in `push_assistant`. 2.5 doesn't require it.
- Gemini's streamed tool-call deltas carry no `index`; the accumulator keys them by `id` instead.

A call whose arguments are not valid JSON becomes `RoundReply.malformed` (one correction round, then a visible "did NOT run" line), never prose. A body cut off mid-stream is recorded as a failed call in the ledger by both text adapters.

title: History trimming never splits a round: a tool result stays with the assistant message that called it
content:
The OpenAI-wire loop trims its history to system + user + about the last MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES (10) messages each round (openai_loop.rs, trim_messages). The cut moves back to the round's assistant message when it would start on a tool result, so a wide round is kept whole and the tail may exceed the budget.
History: until 2026-10-11 the cut was at a fixed index. A round with more than 9 parallel calls (a code-analyst round of 11 searches, then 25 file reads) kept tool results whose assistant message was gone; Mistral refused with 400 'Unexpected role tool after role user' (strict OpenAI-wire servers do too). Both code-analyst runs of a chat turn died after reading about 30 files each, the fallback handed 40 results to host granite4, which timed out at 120 s, and the turn answered from 7-month-old notes. Re-run after the fix on the same Mistral rung: a 10-search round, eight more rounds, no 400, an answer from the code.
The anthropic and host-Ollama adapters do not trim.

title: Code Review Fixes — Implementation Plan
content:
Source: full-codebase review on 2026-08-03 (queue, scheduler, LLM client, knowledge
service, repository layer, schema, HTTP auth). Each phase is independently
shippable and ordered by value-for-effort. Phases 1–3 are the priority batch.

**Conventions (do not skip):**
- Update docs (CLAUDE.md / project-docs) in the same commit as the behavior change.
- No LLM attribution in commit messages (see CLAUDE.md Branch Strategy note).
- Work on `dev`. `cargo fmt && cargo clippy && cargo test --lib` must pass per phase.
- Integration tests (`cargo test --test '*'`) require Neo4j running (`docker compose up -d`).

---

title: Phase 1 — Chain template substitution breaks on quotes (bug)
content:
**Files:** `crates/app/src/services/scheduler.rs` (~line 1265 `try_load_chain_from_neo4j`,
~line 499 `dispatch_one_scheduled_task`)

**Problem:** `{{goal}}` / `{{task_id}}` / `{{date}}` / `{{file_slug}}` are substituted
into the chain's **serialized JSON string** before `serde_json::from_str`. A goal
containing `"`, `\`, or a newline corrupts the JSON → parse fails → task silently
falls back to `build_diagnosis_chain`. Real occurrence in the graph: task
`fill knowledge gap: The "Priority Research Topic" section is not present…` (status
blocked). LLM-generated goals contain quotes routinely.

**Fix:**
1. Parse `steps_json` into `Vec<ChainStep>` (or `serde_json::Value`) FIRST.
2. Substitute template vars at the Value level — walk string values only, exactly
   like `substitute_prev()` in `crates/app/src/services/queue.rs:1522`. Extract a
   shared helper, e.g. `substitute_template_vars(val: &Value, vars: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Value`,
   put it in `queue.rs` next to `substitute_prev` (or a small `services/template.rs`),
   and reuse it for both `substitute_prev` and chain substitution.
3. Apply the same fix in `dispatch_one_scheduled_task` (same pattern, `st.steps`).

**Tests:** unit test: a chain step template `{"arguments":{"question":"{{goal}}"}}`
with goal `say "hello" \ world` round-trips to valid steps with the literal quote
preserved. Existing chain-routing tests must still pass.

**Docs:** CLAUDE.md "Chain YAML schema" section — note that template substitution is
value-level and quote-safe.

---

title: Phase 2 — Missing constraints/indexes on hot labels (perf + integrity)
content:
**File:** `crates/repository/src/client.rs` (`init_schema`, lines ~36–72)

**Problem:** No unique constraint on `Note.id` or `Task.id`. Every by-id MATCH
(`get_note`, access-stat updates after each search hit, `SUMMARIZED_BY` linking,
`update_task_status` every scheduler tick) is a full label scan (~3k notes). Also
missing: index on `Task.status` (scanned every tick via `list_tasks(Some("created"))`)
and `AgentJob.parent_job_id` (used by `unpark_children` / `cancel_parked_children`).

**Fix:** add to `init_schema`:
```cypher
CREATE CONSTRAINT note_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Note) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT task_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (t:Task) REQUIRE t.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE INDEX task_status IF NOT EXISTS FOR (t:Task) ON (t.status)
CREATE INDEX agent_job_parent IF NOT EXISTS FOR (j:AgentJob) ON (j.parent_job_id)
```
`init_schema` runs on `init-db`; confirm whether it also runs at server startup —
if not, note in the rollout section of the commit message that `cargo run -- init-db`
(or the dockerized equivalent) must be run once after deploy.

**Pre-check:** a unique constraint fails to create if duplicates exist.
✅ Already verified on the live DB (2026-08-03): zero duplicate `Note.id` and zero
duplicate `Task.id` — the constraints will create cleanly. Make
`init_schema` log-and-continue on individual statement failure if it doesn't already,
so one failed constraint doesn't abort the rest.

**Docs:** `project-docs/schema.md` — add the new constraints/indexes.

---

title: Phase 3 — Evaluator score parse failure = spurious task failure (bug)
content:
**File:** `crates/app/src/services/queue.rs` (`parse_evaluator_score`, ~line 1398;
call site ~line 999)

**Problem:** When evaluator output has no `Score: N/5` line and no verdict keyword,
`parse_evaluator_score` returns 3.0 — **below** the default `min_score` 3.5 — so
format drift from the local model fails the task and burns up to 3 retry chains.
Note the inconsistency: the adversarial gate's fallback (3.0 vs threshold 2.5) passes.

**Fix:** make "unparseable" explicit instead of a fake mid-scale score:
1. Change signature to `parse_evaluator_score(text: &str) -> Option<f32>`; return
   `None` when no score line AND no verdict keyword matches.
2. At the call site: on `None`, log a warning (`"Evaluator output unparseable — treating as pass"`),
   skip the requeue gate (treat as pass), and still record nothing onto the AgentSpec
   PERFORMED edge (don't grade with invented numbers).
3. Keep the existing keyword fallbacks (FULLY/PARTIALLY/NOT MET) as real parses.

**Tests:** unit tests for: explicit score, each verdict keyword, garbage text → `None`.
Verify the requeue path is NOT taken for `None`.

**Docs:** CLAUDE.md "Evaluator Loop" section — document the unparseable-output behavior.

---

title: Phase 4 — Cancel race: finalizers overwrite `cancelled` (bug)
content:
**Files:** `crates/repository/src/agent_job.rs` (`set_job_started` ~174,
`set_job_completed` ~189, `set_job_failed` ~226, `set_job_dead` ~242,
`requeue_for_retry` ~211); `crates/app/src/services/queue.rs` (`execute_job` ~903)

**Problem:** `cancel()` sets status `cancelled` in Neo4j, but a job already executing
finishes and `set_job_completed` unconditionally overwrites the status — the
"cancelled" job completes and its chain children unpark.

**Fix (guard at the Cypher level, races resolve in the DB):**
1. `set_job_started`: add `WHERE j.status = 'queued'` and return whether a row was
   updated (e.g. `RETURN count(j) AS n`). In `execute_job`, if no row updated, log
   and return — the job was cancelled (or already picked up) between pop and start.
2. `set_job_completed` / `set_job_failed` / `set_job_dead` / `requeue_for_retry`:
   add `WHERE j.status = 'running'`. Return updated-count; when 0, skip the
   follow-on effects in `execute_job` (unpark children, evaluator gate, events).
3. Keep the tombstone `cancelled_ids` heap mechanism as-is (it handles the
   not-yet-popped case; the Cypher guards handle the already-running case).

**Tests:** repository integration test: create job → set running → cancel →
`set_job_completed` → status must still be `cancelled`. Unit-level: `execute_job`
skips unpark when finalize reports 0 rows (may need a small refactor for testability;
keep it minimal).

---

title: Phase 5 — Coordinator head-of-line blocking + slow permit wakeup
content:
**File:** `crates/app/src/services/queue.rs` (`run_coordinator` ~771–833,
`execute_job` end)

**Problem (two parts):**
- Drain loop pops a job; if that provider's semaphore is full it pushes the job back
  and `break`s — blocking dispatch for OTHER providers with free permits.
- Nothing notifies the coordinator when a permit frees: after a completed job, the
  next queued job waits up to `poll_interval_secs` (30 s).

**Fix:**
1. End of `execute_job` (all paths — completed, failed, dead): `self.notify.notify_one()`.
   (The permit drops when the spawned task ends; notify right before so the coordinator
   re-drains promptly.)
2. In the drain loop, replace push-back-and-`break` with skip-and-continue: keep a
   local `Vec<PrioritizedJob> blocked`; on `try_acquire` failure push the job there and
   `continue`; after the loop, push all `blocked` back onto the heap. Break only when
   the heap is empty or every provider seen this pass is saturated (i.e. all remaining
   pops land in `blocked` — a simple guard: stop after N consecutive blocked pops
   where N = heap size at loop entry, to avoid spinning).

**Tests:** hard to unit test end-to-end; at minimum add a test for the skip logic if
the drain loop is factored into a testable function. Otherwise verify via
`cargo test --lib` regressions plus a manual smoke: enqueue 3 ollama jobs with
max_concurrent_ollama=1 and observe they run back-to-back without 30 s gaps
(job `updated_at` timestamps in Neo4j).

---

title: Phase 6 — Lucene query sanitization in BM25 search
content:
**File:** `crates/app/src/services/knowledge.rs` (`search_notes_inner` ~827–849,
same pattern in `search_notes_with_ids` ~1420)

**Problem:** raw query text goes to `db.index.fulltext.queryNodes` (Lucene syntax).
Special chars (`:` `/` `[` `]` `(` `)` `~` `^` `"` `AND/OR/NOT`, unbalanced quotes —
note content is full of URLs) throw; the `if let Ok` swallows the error and search
silently degrades to the CONTAINS fallback scan.

**Fix:**
1. Add `fn sanitize_lucene_query(q: &str) -> String` — escape Lucene special
   characters with `\` (list: `+ - && || ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ * ? : \ /`), collapse
   to terms. Simplest robust approach: escape everything, join terms with spaces
   (Lucene ORs terms by default).
2. Apply in both call sites.
3. Replace the silent `if let Ok` on BOTH vector and fulltext calls with
   `match … Err(e) => warn!(…)` so infra failures are visible in logs (behavior
   unchanged: continue with empty hits).

**Tests:** unit test sanitizer (URL input, colons, quotes, `AND`). Integration test
(Neo4j): `search_notes("https://example.com/path: [test]")` returns Ok.

---

title: Phase 7 — Meta-learning fires on quota/transient errors
content:
**File:** `crates/app/src/services/queue.rs` (dead-job branch of `execute_job`
~1146–1219, `should_meta_learn` ~1462)

**Problem:** a dead `search_web` job from `429 "run out of searches"` triggers a full
meta-learning chain — the brain has repeatedly hypothesized about a billing limit
(11 `dead_job:search_web` notes). Wasted LLM cycles and graph noise.

**Fix:**
1. Add `fn is_transient_infra_error(error_text: &str) -> bool` — case-insensitive
   match on: `429`, `too many requests`, `rate limit`, `quota`, `run out of searches`,
   `timeout`, `timed out`, `connection refused`, `503`, `502`. When true, store the
   reflection note (keep forensics) but skip the meta-learning chain.
2. Dedup: before enqueuing, query for an existing note with
   `source_context = 'dead_job:<tool>'` created in the last 24 h
   (`note_type = 'meta_learning_result'`); skip if found. One Cypher lookup, cheap.

**Tests:** unit test `is_transient_infra_error` against the SerpApi 429 string and a
genuine logic-error string.

---

title: Phase 8 — Recursive chain cancellation
content:
**File:** `crates/repository/src/agent_job.rs` (`cancel_parked_children` ~427)

**Problem:** cancellation reaches only direct children; grandchildren wait for the
5-minute orphan audit, one generation per pass (a 5-step chain takes ~15 min to
fully clear).

**Fix:** loop `cancel_parked_children` until it cancels 0 rows (each pass turns the
next generation's parents terminal), cap at e.g. 32 iterations. Do the loop in the
repository fn so all call sites (cancel, drain, dead-job path, evaluator gate)
benefit. Alternative single-query approach is awkward because `parent_job_id` is a
property, not an edge — the loop is fine at these sizes.

**Tests:** integration test: 4-step chain, kill step 1 (cancel), assert steps 2–4 are
all `cancelled` immediately.

---

title: Phase 9 — Small cleanups (batch into one commit)
content:
1. **Constant-time API key compare** — `crates/app/src/mcp/auth.rs:137`. Add `subtle`
   crate (`ConstantTimeEq` on bytes) or fold a manual XOR loop. One line + dependency.
2. **`enqueue` create-then-refetch round trip** — `crates/repository/src/agent_job.rs`
   `create_agent_job` / `create_agent_job_parked`: append `RETURN j` and map with the
   existing `node_to_agent_job`; return `AgentJob` instead of `String` id (or add a
   `_returning` variant). Update `QueueService::enqueue` / `enqueue_chain` / `retry`
   to drop the extra `get_agent_job` calls.
3. **`drain()` completeness** — `crates/app/src/services/queue.rs:489`: after draining
   the heap, also cancel Neo4j `queued` jobs not in the heap
   (`MATCH (j:AgentJob {status:'queued'}) SET j.status='cancelled'` + cancel their
   parked children). Otherwise the next 30 s poll resurrects them.
4. **Delete `goal_to_steps_legacy`** — `crates/app/src/services/scheduler.rs:1324`,
   ~650 lines of `#[allow(dead_code)]` heuristics. Chain seeding is mandatory now
   (missing `schedules/` aborts startup; chains seed on first tick). Also delete any
   helpers only it used (compiler will tell). Keep `build_diagnosis_chain` (live
   fallback).

---

title: A profile save is checked like a form; the startup audit runs the same checks
content:
`profiles::validate` (2026-10-16, validation Phase 2) runs on every save (`ContextBuilderService::save_profile`, POST/PUT /api/contexts, the HBI) and over every stored profile in `audit_profiles`.
- **Refused on save (hard):** a body key that is not a profile field (the field list is asked of serde itself, `profiles::struct_fields`, so it cannot drift), with a did-you-mean; a tool that does not exist (a plugin-off tool is not missing); a name that is not `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}`; a model_preference not in the catalog with no provider_hint (it could never resolve); a fallback model not in the catalog; side_effects other than read_only/writes; a routing target (stored/web) that is not a spawnable profile; a `self:` routing choice naming a tool the profile does not hold; a routing regex (web_words, behavior when/unless) that does not compile.
- **Advice (soft), returned as `warnings` and shown in the editor:** a model outside the catalog with a provider_hint; spawnable with no specialty (the roster uses the description); a local-pinned profile whose prompt exceeds ~3,000 characters.
- **Stored profiles are reported, never dropped:** the startup audit puts hard findings in `problems` and soft in `warnings` on GET /api/contexts and in the HBI notice; a bad checked-in file must not wedge the boot. A save refreshes the audit.
- The schema files `context_profile.json` and `task.json` were deleted (never read; this validator is the contract). Test `every_shipped_profile_passes_the_validator` keeps our own files clean.

title: Analyst merge eval 2026-10-16: code-analyst + self-analyst
content:
Tested before merging (owner's call). Arms: today's profile (code-analyst for code questions; self-analyst, made spawnable for the test, for state questions) vs one merged candidate (union of tools minus consolidate_memories, code-analyst's navigation procedure then self-analyst's method and state map, self-analyst's Cypher pre-load; 5.2K-char prompt vs 1.8K / 3.4K). Same model for both, ministral-14b-latest (ollama-cloud was cooling down on its account limit), read_only, 6 questions x 2 reps, graded against source and live queries. Files: workspace/analyst-merge-eval-2026-10-16/.

Fully right, of 12: today's profiles 4, merged 6. Never worse on any question.
- C1 queue retry/backoff (queue.rs:1624-1658, no backoff, default 3 at :418): base 1/2 (rep 2 invented a `retry` fn at :650 and an exponential backoff), merged 2/2.
- C2 run_agent model admission: all 4 runs read only skills/agent_runner.rs and stopped; none reached chat/agent_runner.rs pinned_config. Partial everywhere.
- C3 orphaned yaml profile at startup (profiles.rs seed() prune): 0/4 in both arms; base rep 1 asserted "no automatic cleanup on startup", which is false. Both found delete_profile and stopped.
- S1 top sub-agents, 14 days: base 0/2 confidently wrong (answered tool names, called them sub-agents); merged 0/2 but said plainly it could not measure (8 failed duckdb queries).
- S2 scheduled workflows: base 1/2 (rep 1 sorted by next_run_at), merged 2/2. S3 failure share: 4/4.
Two weaknesses common to both arms, independent of the merge: (1) on ministral the code worker stops after the first file that looks relevant (C2, C3); (2) duckdb here has no timestamptz minus interval, so every time-window query first fails; CAST(created_at AS TIMESTAMP) works.
Verdict: the merge did not cost accuracy on a weaker model; small sample, not re-run on gpt-oss.

title: Before adding an agent profile, rule out a twin
content:
A new profile is justified only by a different job: a different toolset or a different prompt procedure. Not by:
- a different model: pin it per step with `run_agent`'s `model` argument (deep-dive-hard does). A pin inside a spawnable profile is offered to every model that delegates.
- a different mode of the same job (scout vs integrate): a section of the one profile, chosen by the workflow's `task` text.
- a different set of interests or inputs: those are the workflow's `task`, not the agent.
Check the ledger (`model_usage` where tool_name = 'subagent:<name>') before keeping or adding one; the `AgentJob.context_profile` label is annotation only and proves nothing. The 2026-10-16 consolidation removed seven twins and stubs (18 profiles to 11) (`dev_docs search "profile consolidation"`).

title: Profile consolidation 2026-10-16: 18 agents to 11
content:
The owner found the agent list redundant (api-builder / api-integrator / api-scout; general / GeneralDefault-Orchrestator / orchestrator; scheduler / schedule-author / task-manager). Audited by real use, not the `AgentJob.context_profile` label: that label is `auto_assign` annotation only and never read at execution, so 88 "toolsmith" jobs were ordinary workflow steps. The evidence is the sub-agent ledger (`model_usage.tool_name = 'subagent:<agent>'`, from 2026-09-08) plus which workflows, code and HBI name each profile.

Retired, zero ledger runs: `api-builder` (5-tool stub, superseded by api-integrator), `orchestrator` (the Phase 0 front door the default merged in), `scheduler` and `task-manager` (4-tool non-spawnable stubs; the front door holds their tools), the old 31-tool `general` (nothing selected it: CHAT_DEFAULT_PROFILE and MCP_TOOL_PROFILE both name the front door).
Merged: `api-scout` (65 runs) into `api-integrator` (49): scout's tools were integrator's plus notify_user; its procedure became api-integrator's SCOUTING section and its interest list the personal `api-scout` workflow's task. Cost: the scout was `data_class: public` and now runs private (stricter of caller and profile).
Folded: `deep-diver-hard` was deep-diver with only the model changed; `deep-dive-hard.yaml` now runs `agent: deep-diver, model: claude-sonnet-5`. Paid use is gated by purpose (ROUTING_PAID_FOR), not profile name, so nothing about spend changed; a refused Sonnet pin now fails the run with the reason instead of silently running on the chat default. Its ledger rows now read `subagent:deep-diver` (model_name tells them apart).
Dead extension removed: personal `general-job-application` extended `general`, which no chat ran; `job-applicant` (session_prefixes jobsearch-) already carries the newer flow.
Found and fixed on the way: a chat naming an unknown profile got EVERY tool and no system prompt (`turn.rs` else-branch); it now runs as the default. The code fallback name moved from `general` to `GeneralDefault-Orchrestator` (the owner kept the name on purpose).
Kept: knowledge-worker vs researcher (the router's stored/web split), deep-diver, schedule-author, scribe, toolsmith, job-applicant, code-analyst, self-analyst (merge measured separately).

title: Second extraction round (6g): sandboxes and dev notes are plugins; the rest of the core retrieves, stores or reasons
content:
CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN 6g, 2026-10-11, measured before anything moved (60 days of tool calls, interactions + AgentJob).
- The WebSocket tools were already gone (Phase 0).
- execute_code is the sandbox plugin (plugins/sandbox: crate/, python/, rust/ service images). Its 4,596 calls in 60 days were 4,556 fine-tuning benchmark runs on 09-12/13; organic use is about 40. With it off, a workflow step on execute_code makes that workflow unavailable with the reason; agent profiles just lack the tool. The sub-agent runner's Rust verification calls execute_code by name and reads plugins/sandbox/rust/crates/Cargo.toml.
- Dev notes (:DevNote, dev_docs) are the developer plugin's: knowledge about building the brain, read only by coding agents (all 112 calls). The plugin creates the label's constraint and indexes in start and reaches the graph and embedder through the Graph and Llm capabilities. With developer off they go dark in the graph; devdocs/devnotes.jsonl stays greppable.
- The gpu_lease MCP tool was deleted (0 calls ever; scripts/gpu_lease.sh uses POST /api/gpu-lease), with a tombstone. The lease itself is core: routing, the queue, knowledge and topics pause on it.
- Kept, measured: manage_job (0 calls as a tool, but the HBI's Cancel/Retry buttons call it, so a zero there is not evidence), snapshots (taken before every prune), the self-model (tombstones and the seeding rule), retrieval_eval (the CLI every phase measures with), items/todos, topics, entity resolution, the HBI REST API.
- Result: owner decision to record and stop. Core code ~59.6K, not ~32K: what remains retrieves, stores or reasons, or is the machinery for that.

title: 2026-10-11: daily-news died on the retired :ScheduledTask label
content: The daily-news status step counted ScheduledTask nodes, a label retired when chains and schedules became :Workflow (phase 2b). The query kept passing while old nodes lingered; once none were left, the Cypher schema guard rejected the unknown label, the step dead-lettered, and every later step (reason, store_note, claim, notify_user) was cancelled, so no brief went out. Fix: count :Workflow by enabled. When a label is retired, grep workflow YAML (core plugins and the personal bundle) for Cypher that still names it.

title: Deep research: paid Parallel runs, cap, reuse, delivery
content:
Rules (built 2026-10-16; `plugins/research/`, crate `agent-brain-plugin-research`):

- **`deep_research` is paid, so the cap is checked before every run.** Prices, per-processor waits and `monthly_cap_usd` (5.0 = Parallel's monthly free credit) live in the bundle's `parallel.yaml`, not in Rust. Spend is the sum of `usd` over this calendar month's `(:ResearchRun)` nodes (UTC); a run that would pass the cap is refused with the spend, the cap and `action=list` to drill into it. Every run Parallel accepts counts, failed ones too (Parallel does not say whether a failed run bills). A Mutex spans the check and the create, so two calls cannot both take the last room. An unreadable `parallel.yaml` means no tool, never an uncapped one.
- **Only the question leaves the brain** (owner's decision 2026-10-16: "like search_web"). Parallel keeps request logs (zero retention is Enterprise-only), so the tool is not gated on `data_class`, but it takes one self-contained question (≤ 2,000 chars) and no context, and its description and the researcher section forbid personal details. Don't add a context or file argument without revisiting that decision.
- **Never pay twice for one question.** The same question + processor within 24 h that has not failed is reused: a completed one returns its stored report, a running one is resumed. That is also what makes a workflow step's retry safe. `fresh=true` is the only way to pay again.
- **Who waits.** Inside a workflow run (`ctx.current_task()` is set) the call waits up to the processor's `wait_minutes` (long-polling Parallel's `result?timeout=` in ≤ 300 s slices); running out of time is an *error* there, so the step retries (resuming the run) instead of storing "still running" as its output. Anywhere else (chat, a sub-agent answering one, a direct call) it returns the run id at once.
- **One delivery per run.** `status` leaves `running` through a conditional SET; only the caller whose SET matched delivers. A waiting tool call marks `waiting_until` (+1 min grace); the background collector (every 60 s, deployed brain only) takes only runs nobody waits on, stores the report as a `deep_research` note (provenance `synthesis_inference`: Parallel's model wrote it) and puts it in the Feed (origin `deep_research`/run id), or a "failed" item; it gives up on a run after 6 h. A run finished by the tool is *not* noted by the plugin: the caller (the `deep-research` workflow's `store_note`) decides.
- Output is requested as `output_schema: text` (a markdown report with inline citations); the answer adds confidence and the first 15 cited sources, the node keeps 50 plus `source_count`. Measured 2026-10-16: one `core` run (41 s) answered a llama.cpp KV-cache question with exact perplexity figures, flags and the source issue, "medium" confidence.
- Reach: the core `researcher` allowlists it (shown as "plugin off" when the plugin is), and the plugin's `contexts/researcher-deep-research.yaml` adds the when-to-spend section. Item dispatch can route to `researcher`, so autonomous work can reach it; the cap is the backstop. Not wired into `deep-dive`/`deep-dive-hard` yet: measure a few runs first.

title: Dev notes: how the brain's developer documentation works
content:
Rules (CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN.md §5, built 2026-10-10):

- **`:DevNote` is a separate label, never `:Note`.** Dev history must not surface in the brain's retrieval about the world (a news question about GDELT must not return our GDELT incident). It has its own indexes, `dev_note_embeddings` (vector, bge-m3 1024) and `dev_note_fulltext` (title, content, subsystem); nothing that reads `:Note` sees it.
- **The graph is the authority; git keeps a seed.** `devdocs/devnotes.jsonl` (no embeddings) seeds an EMPTY graph, create-only, at startup. Every `dev_docs write` rewrites the file (atomic rename), so commit it with the change that wrote the note. Never hand-edit the jsonl while the brain runs: the next write overwrites it from the graph.
- **Embeddings are backfilled** at every start for notes without a vector (a GPU lease or a down embedder leaves them BM25-only until then). The embedded text is title + the first 4000 chars (bge-m3 fails on long dense text); the rest is found by BM25.
- **Kinds:** `rule` (must hold when changing code), `history` (incident, measurement, the why), `decision` (a finished plan), `plan` (designed, not built).
- **Search** is vector + BM25 merged by reciprocal rank (k=60), then filtered: `kind`, `subsystem` (substring of subsystem OR source, so a former doc name like `HBI_REDESIGN_PLAN` or `subsystem-rules` works), `path` (a file the note names or mentions). Results are RANKED, not counted: `candidates` is the merged pool after filters (top 60 by meaning + top 60 by keyword; 400 each when a filter is set, since filters apply after the merge), not a number of relevant notes.
