subsystem: ETL datasets: GDELT events, ReliefWeb reports (removed 2026-10-10)
title: ETL datasets: GDELT events, ReliefWeb reports (removed 2026-10-10)
content:
Removed in Phase 0 of CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN.md: GDELT was retired as a source on 2026-10-06 and the owner dropped ReliefWeb on 2026-10-10. The code is at commit `1aed101`. The rules below were in subsystem-rules.md and still apply to any future ETL into DuckDB.

`repository/src/datasets.rs` (`DatasetStore`, own DuckDB file `DATASETS_DB_PATH`) + `services/datasets/{gdelt,reliefweb}.rs` + `skills/datasets.rs` (`gdelt_events`, `reliefweb_reports`, `dataset_status`, `dataset_sync`). Config in `datasets/*.yaml`. Schedules: `gdelt-sync` (15 min), `reliefweb-sync` (hourly), `dataset-review` (weekly, notifies the user). **GDELT is retired as a source (2026-10-06)**: its schedule is disabled and `gdelt_events` is in no agent's allowlist; the code stays dormant and tested. The researcher agent has `reliefweb_reports`.

- **Rows go to DuckDB, never the graph.** ~86k GDELT events/day is a table, not notes. **A separate DuckDB file from telemetry**: a killed container mid-bulk-load must not corrupt telemetry's WAL. The store checkpoints on open and after each load, and is opened **once per process** (`OnceLock`) — `build_skills` re-runs on a model hot-swap and a second open of the same file fails on its lock.
- **Every load is one transaction that records its file/batch** (`etl_files`), so a dead run leaves nothing half-loaded and the next run resumes from the last committed file. Every run is logged to `etl_runs` (calls, files, rows, pruned, error).
- **GDELT: raw 15-minute export files, not the DOC API.** The DOC API refused ~12 of 13 requests from this host (2026-10-06) even 35 s apart; the files at `data.gdeltproject.org` were reliable. Pending files are computed by stamp arithmetic from the last recorded file, not listed; a 404 for a slot older than the newest published is recorded `missing` so the resume point moves on. DuckDB parses the TSV in SQL (`read_csv … ignore_errors`, `TRY_*` casts): malformed lines are skipped, not fatal.
- **GDELT answers say what they are:** counts measure news coverage, not occurrence; default `min_sources: 1`, with the multi-source share reported (**not 2**: an export row counts only the outlets in its own 15-minute window, so ~97% say 1 — a default of 2 turned 88 Ukraine fighting events into 0); places mis-geocode (Gaza → Israel); files carry events dated up to a year back (query by `event_date`, retention prunes by it). Every answer carries a **source mix** — outlets classed by SourceList (`SourceClasses`: role lists `platform`/`state_media` first, then approved list names, else `unlisted`) — and its zero-result path names the loaded country spellings that resemble the request.
- **ReliefWeb: v2 POST, `appname` required, two budgets** — `max_calls_per_run` and `max_calls_per_day` summed from `etl_runs` (ReliefWeb's own limit is 1,000/day). Resumes from the newest `date_created` held (inclusive; upsert by id dedups). Cite the report's publisher (`sources`, `source_types`), not ReliefWeb.
- **`dataset_status` states freshness; it does not leave it to a reader.** Each dataset carries `freshness.state` (`current` / `behind` with hours and files behind / `never loaded` / `paused`, read from the schedule / `failing` with the last error) and a `summary` the weekly review copies verbatim. Why: the first review (local model, given only timestamps) called a week-old backfill "Current … no backlog". Same doctrine as count-then-drill: a judgement a tool can compute must arrive computed.
- **The bundled DuckDB has no ICU:** `TIMESTAMPTZ` cannot even cast to `DATE`, and `now()` is `TIMESTAMPTZ`. Dataset timestamps are UTC `TIMESTAMP`; cutoffs (retention, "today") are computed in Rust and bound as parameters. `query_json` returns numbers/text/bool/NULL only — select dates as text.

subsystem: Epistemics: claims, source records, retrieval labelling
title: Grounding gate: a supports must be grounded in its cited results, read together
content: After the independence gate, every 'supports' verdict in verify_one goes to a second model: granite4.1-guardian on host Ollama (GROUNDING_CHECK_MODEL, 'off' disables), criterion groundedness, with the claim as the assistant turn and ALL cited results' titles+snippets as one numbered document (grounding.rs). Ungrounded => verdict support_rejected_ungrounded, no evidence edge, claim stays unverified (same shape as the unsourced and not-independent gates). Cannot run => the support counts and the edge records grounding: 'unchecked: <why>'; checked edges record 'grounded'; edges from before 2026-10-13 or with the check off have no grounding property. Rules: (1) never per result: a snippet is a fragment, and per result it flagged 37 of 60 good citations; together it caught 5 of 7 wrongly corroborated claims and flagged 6 of 18 good ones, 4 of those real wording faults ('embargo' for temporary restrictions, 'Activist Post claims' for a MintPress article, 'MI6' for 'British handlers'). (2) think: false: guardian thinks ~240 hidden tokens by default (~57 s a check, mostly on CPU beside the sidecar); off it is 3-5 s and no worse on the measured sets; thinking made it stricter, not better. (3) It does not check attribution (0 of 4 who-said-it faults caught) or vagueness ('this maritime junction' passed); those belong to extraction's stand-alone check. (4) context_relevance was useless on this task. Measured 2026-10-12 on 25 random corroborated claims (92 cited results) graded by hand; 7 of 25 (28%) were wrongly corroborated, mostly 'the X segment/show/forum said Y' corroborated by any news about Y, a gap the guardian only partly closes.

subsystem: Epistemics: claims, source records, retrieval labelling
title: Internal claims: about the brain itself, never extracted, never verified
content:
Rule (2026-10-16; `plugins/epistemics/internal-claims.yaml`, `crate/src/internal.rs`): **a claim about the brain itself is never extracted and never verified.** "The brain logged 176 notes", "One dead-letter job was recorded": the brain's own ledger answers those, and no web search can (owner: "we shouldn't be doing websearches on internal activity or processes"). Found when the search ledger showed the verifier searching "The brain logged 37 dispatches of scheduler activity in the last 24 h."; one such claim had been "refuted".

- **At the source:** `claim extract` takes `exclude_sections` (Markdown heading prefixes, case-insensitive; a section runs to the next heading of ANY level, because briefs mix `##` and `###` for siblings). The daily brief excludes EXECUTIVE SUMMARY, WHAT I DID, SYSTEM STATUS, YOUR ITEMS: claims come from its news sections only. The result reports `excluded_sections`.
- **In the prompt:** "NEVER a claim about the brain that wrote or collected the SOURCE". Live test: with no exclusion, the model took only the news claim.
- **The check that holds when a model does not listen:** `InternalRules::is_internal` = a self name (`the brain`, `agent-brain`, `the system`, …) followed within `verb_window` (4) words by a bookkeeping verb (logged, watched, dispatched, …) AND a bookkeeping noun anywhere (notes, videos, jobs, knowledge gaps, …). Both, so neuroscience is not caught ("the brain actively establishes a target level for body fat", "the brain processed visual input"). Dropped at extraction (reason in `dropped`); at verification `verify_one` returns `skipped_internal` without searching and sets `c.verify_skipped = 'internal'`, which `unverified_claims` excludes. Dry run over all 4,748 claims: 30 caught, 0 false positives. Not caught (too far from a subject, or none): "The system detailed in the executive summary logged…", "One dead-letter job was recorded." — the section exclusion is what stops those.
- **Data:** 40 claims (30 detected + 10 by hand, incl. August's claims about the brief itself) and their 7 evidence notes deleted by `scripts/retire_internal_claims.cypher`; backup `workspace/backups/internal-claims-2026-10-16.json`.
- Words are data: add a self name or bookkeeping word to the YAML, rerun the dry run (`internal_dry_run`, ignored test, `CLAIMS_JSON=` export) before shipping it.

title: Constraints to design around
content:
- **Licensing of teacher outputs.** Only distil from models whose terms permit
  training other models on their outputs. gpt-oss (Apache-2.0) and our own
  local models are fine. **Exclude Gemini and Anthropic outputs** from training
  datasets. Their terms restrict using outputs to build competing models. This
  is why `llm_transcripts` records the provider on every row, and why recipes
  filter on it by default. Verify Gemma's current terms for fine-tuning and
  redistribution of adapters. The Reticulum license issue in
  `BRAIN_TO_BRAIN_PLAN.md` hits this same dataset path.
- **The self-grading trap.** A model graded by itself (or by an adapter of
  itself) and trained on those grades compounds its errors. Rewards come from
  compilers, validators, ground-truth tools, humans, or a *different and
  stronger* model, never the model being trained.
- **Contamination between train and eval.** Split by time. Never generate
  training data from the eval suite's prompts.
- **GPU contention.** Training evicts serving (see Hardware). No run starts
  without a human-approved window.
- **Small data overfits.** Start narrow (B1 routing, Track 0), and check the
  canary suite for forgetting on every promotion.

---

title: Experiment 2 starts from scouted data, trained off-box
content: Experiment 1 concluded negative because of data, not compute: ~200 Exercism-derived examples taught gemma4:e4b a style without the skill. Experiment 2 therefore starts by finding what others built. Workflow rust-training-data-scout (plugins/core/workflows/, every 30d, data_class public) runs four search_web sweeps (datasets, Rust fine-tuning prior work, compiler-verified/RL training, hard Rust benchmarks) and writes a delta report under source_context rust_training_data_scout; its reason step must flag any dataset built from Exercism, HumanEval or MBPP as contaminated against our benchmarks. Training compute: Lightning AI (rented L4, $0.79/h on gcp-lightning-public-prod) so the brain need not rest; first step is a v3 parity run (workspace/finetune/scripts/lightning/) that must reproduce local losses (valid 0.1796->0.1603, anchor 0.1647->0.1213) before the platform is trusted. Evaluation stays local through the identical GGUF pipeline. Blocked 2026-10-16 by a Lightning security incident (every Studio start HTTP 500).

title: Fine-Tuning: Teaching the Brain's Models to Behave
content:
**Status: design only, nothing implemented.** Written 2026-09-12.

The long goal is a brain that can build itself: a small local model that writes
Rust well enough to change this codebase, and a small Gemma that *is* the
orchestrator and the voice instead of being prompted into acting like one. The
near goal is experience. Run a fine-tune end to end on something that isn't
brain-specific, and record every result (including the failures) in the graph.

---

> **Before fine-tuning anything, read [`FINE_TUNING_PLAYBOOK.md`](FINE_TUNING_PLAYBOOK.md)**: the
> process and the silent failures learned from Experiment 1.
>
> **Experiment 1 CONCLUDED 2026-09-13, negative:** [`RUST_FINETUNE_EXPERIMENT.md`](RUST_FINETUNE_EXPERIMENT.md).
> No adapter improved gemma4:e4b on Rust. Teacher distillation harmed it through style drift;
> self-only guarded training avoided harm but added nothing. Revisit the tracks below with
> that result in mind: behaviour with a verifier is still the right target, but "a few
> hundred easy examples" is not enough to teach skill to a 4B-effective model.
>
> **First experiment runs outside the brain:** [`RUST_FINETUNE_EXPERIMENT.md`](RUST_FINETUNE_EXPERIMENT.md).
> A QLoRA fine-tune for Rust, trained on compiler-filtered solutions and
> benchmarked on Aider's polyglot Rust exercises before and after, using plain
> Python in `workspace/finetune/`. It builds the `rust-sandbox` the rest of this
> plan needs, and should surface what this plan hasn't considered before any
> of the brain-integrated machinery below gets built.

title: Hardware budget
content:
RTX 3060 Ti, 8 GB. **Serving already uses ~4.8 GB** (llama.cpp E4B + KV, bge-m3,
whisper). Training and serving can't share the card.

- **Local training runs in a maintenance window:** pause the scheduler, stop
  `llamacpp`/`whisper`, unload bge-m3 (`keep_alive: 0`), train, restart. The
  front door is down for the window. Schedule it overnight.
- **QLoRA is the only local option.** Full fine-tuning even a 1B model won't
  fit. Which sizes fit (1.5B / 3B / 4B / 7B at useful sequence lengths) is a
  **Phase 0 measurement**, not an assumption. Rust examples are long, and
  sequence length drives memory as much as parameter count does.
- **Rented GPU is an opt-in escape hatch**, not the default: an hourly
  community GPU for a run that won't fit. Everything in this plan must also
  work on the local card, even if more slowly or at a smaller size.

---

title: Open decisions
content:
1. **Track 0 task:** text-to-SQL on DuckDB (recommended) vs structured extraction.
2. **Trainer stack:** Unsloth (lowest VRAM, model support lags) vs TRL + PEFT (broadest support, more memory). Decide after Phase 0 measures both on the target bases.
3. **Adapter granularity:** one adapter per narrow behaviour (clean rollback, needs per-request selection) vs one merged orchestrator adapter (simpler serving). Depends on what Phase 0 finds about llama-server.
4. **Rented GPU:** allowed at all, and with what monthly cap?

title: Phases
content:
- [ ] **Phase 0: Measure (no code).** VRAM + wall time for QLoRA at 1.5B/3B/4B/7B at realistic sequence lengths with serving evicted; whether Gemma-4-E4B is supported by the chosen trainer; llama.cpp LoRA adapter loading in our b10900 build (launch vs per-request); baseline Rust ability of candidate code models on ~20 held-out repo commits with a manual compile loop; front-door routing-miss rate from the ledger.
- [ ] **Phase 1: Capture + ledger.** `llm_transcripts` + `transcript_labels` tables; HBI 👍/👎 writing `feedback_score`; `(:Dataset)/(:TrainingRun)/(:Adapter)/(:EvalRun)` schema; fix or retire `digest_experiences`'s `is_error` success filter.
- [ ] **Phase 2: Track 0 practice run.** `trainer` sidecar, dataset recipe, eval runner, one recorded run with a baseline, win or lose.
- [ ] **Phase 3: Rust sandbox + repo-commit eval suite.** `rust-sandbox` sidecar with a vendored toolchain; the SWE-bench-shaped suite from our history; baseline scores recorded.
- [ ] **Phase 4: Rust adapter.** Public-data SFT, then rejection sampling on brain tasks; promotion gated on the held-out commit suite.
- [ ] **Phase 5: Orchestrator adapters.** B1 routing → B2 task strings → B3 voice, each promoted separately; front-door prompt shrinks as each lands (measure the char count before and after).
- [ ] **Phase 6: The brain proposes its own runs.** A schedule notices a behaviour with enough labelled data and a measured gap, drafts a recipe and a run request, and `notify_user`s for approval. The human approves the run, the eval gate promotes, and the human merges any code.

title: Shared infrastructure (all tracks use it) › 1. Capture: record what the model actually did
content:
New DuckDB table `llm_transcripts`, one row per LLM call: `id`, `ts`,
`tool_name` (same attribution as `model_usage`: `CURRENT_TOOL` /
`USAGE_TOOL_LABEL` / `chat`), `model`, `provider`, `messages` (JSON, including
tool calls and tool results), `completion`, `session_id`, `task_id`, `job_id`,
`profile`, `turn_id`. Links to `model_usage` by call id.

- **Provider of origin is recorded on every row** and is load-bearing for
  licensing (below).
- Size-bounded: store over-long tool results as a hash + length rather than the
  full bytes; retention window configurable.
- Capture is **off by default** (`TRANSCRIPT_CAPTURE_ENABLED`) until the size
  cost is measured.

title: Shared infrastructure (all tracks use it) › 2. Label: attach outcomes after the fact
content:
New table `transcript_labels(transcript_id | turn_id, grader, verdict, score,
detail, labelled_at)`. Many graders per row. Labels come from:

- the deterministic graders above, run offline over captured rows
- ground-truth reconciliation (e.g. the answer said zero while `recall_recent` returned 43 → `contradicts_ground_truth`)
- **human feedback: 👍/👎 on HBI chat messages.** This finally writes
  `feedback_score` and is the only source of truth for *voice*

title: Shared infrastructure (all tracks use it) › 3. Curate: the sleep cycle's real job
content:
`digest_experiences` evolves into a dataset builder driven by a declarative
recipe (YAML in a `datasets/recipes/` seed dir, not Rust literals): which
source, which label filter, which chat format, a dedupe key, and a **held-out
split fixed by time** (train on older, evaluate on newer, never shuffled
together). Output: versioned JSONL + a manifest with counts and label
distribution.

title: Shared infrastructure (all tracks use it) › 4. Train: a sidecar, never the brain process
content:
A `trainer` compose service (Python; Unsloth or TRL + PEFT), in the same
spirit as `sandbox`: no credentials, no brain volumes except a read-only
dataset mount and a write-only adapter output mount. The brain **requests** a
run; a human approves it; the trainer runs in the maintenance window. The
output is a LoRA adapter converted to GGUF for llama.cpp.

title: Shared infrastructure (all tracks use it) › 5. Evaluate: gate on the answer, not the loss
content:
Generalise `retrieval_eval` into an eval runner: a suite (golden cases, or a
held-out split, plus graders) × a model (base, base + adapter, cloud twin).
**Every training run has a base-model baseline measured under identical
conditions; a run without a baseline is not a result.** Promotion requires
beating the currently promoted adapter on the held-out suite *and* not
regressing a small general-capability canary suite (forgetting check).

title: Shared infrastructure (all tracks use it) › 6. Serve: adapters on one base
content:
llama.cpp `llama-server` supports LoRA adapters at launch (`--lora`) with
runtime scaling via its adapters endpoint. One E4B base could carry several
narrow adapters without extra VRAM per model. **Phase 0 verifies this works in
our CUDA-12.2 source build (b10900)** and whether a per-request adapter choice
is available or whether adapters are per-instance.

title: Shared infrastructure (all tracks use it) › 7. Record: the experiment ledger lives in the graph
content:
```
(:Dataset {id, recipe, version, n_train, n_eval, created_at, manifest_path})
(:TrainingRun {id, base_model, method, hyperparams, started_at, finished_at,
               status, gpu, wall_secs, peak_vram_mb, notes})
(:Adapter {id, path, format, size_mb, promoted, promoted_at, retired_at})
(:EvalRun {id, suite, model_label, metrics, at})

(:TrainingRun)-[:TRAINED_ON]->(:Dataset)
(:TrainingRun)-[:PRODUCED]->(:Adapter)
(:EvalRun)-[:EVALUATED]->(:Adapter)          // or a base model label
(:Adapter)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(:Adapter)
```

Negative results are first-class: a run that failed to beat baseline is
recorded with its metrics and a `semantic` note saying what was tried and why
it probably didn't help. This is the "gives all of us the experience" half: a
queryable history of what worked on this hardware.

---

title: The thesis: weights for behaviour, graph for knowledge, prompt for state
content:
| layer | holds | changes how often | how it changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **weights** (base + LoRA adapter) | *how* to behave: routing policy, tool-call habits, Rust idiom, the brain's voice | per training run (weeks) | train, evaluate, promote |
| **graph** | *what* is known: notes, claims, APIs, media, tasks | continuously | tools write it |
| **prompt** | *what is true right now*: roster, allowlist, date, `LIVE SELF-STATE` | every turn | built by `build_system_prompt` |

The model doesn't need to know everything; the graph does that. Fine-tuning
facts in is the wrong tool: facts go stale, can't be cited, and would get around
the epistemics layer (`label_claims`, claim status). **Do not train knowledge
into weights.**

The failure to design against is a **stale-state adapter**: an orchestrator
trained with the roster baked in keeps routing to agents that were renamed or
removed. Training examples must therefore *include* the dynamic context
(roster, allowlist) as input, so the model learns to read it rather than
memorise it.

title: The thesis: weights for behaviour, graph for knowledge, prompt for state › Why this is worth doing: two measured findings point here
content:
1. **The front door has a prompt-size budget.** Same model, same tools, same
   question: at 2332 chars E4B delegates, at 6801 it refuses (CLAUDE.md
   § Context Profiles). The `general.yaml` rules that push it over are narrative
   policy. Context distillation moves them into weights, so the prompt shrinks
   back to state only.
2. **The local-model gap is result-directed iteration** (CLAUDE.md § Going
   local). E4B stops at the first obstacle or loops without progress; the cloud
   twin closes the loop. That is a *behaviour* over tool results, which is
   exactly what trajectory distillation targets.

---

title: Track 0: a practice run that isn't brain-specific
content:
**Purpose:** exercise capture → curate → train → eval → record end to end on a
task with a public dataset and an automatic metric, before any of it touches
the brain's own behaviour. Pick something small enough to train in under an
hour locally.

| candidate | metric | why | concern |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Text-to-SQL on DuckDB** (recommended) | execution accuracy: run both queries, compare result sets | DuckDB is already in the stack; a checker is a few lines; generally useful; public datasets exist | check each dataset's license before use |
| Structured extraction to a JSON Schema | schema-valid + field exact-match | reuses the `jsonschema` validator; directly relevant to `generate_json` | examples must be generated, so a teacher model is needed |
| Rust compile-error repair | fixed code passes `cargo check` | a warm-up for Track A | needs the Rust sandbox first, so it can't be the first run |

Deliverable: one `(:TrainingRun)` with a baseline, an adapter, an `(:EvalRun)`
on each, and a written note, whether or not it helped.

---

title: Track A: a Rust coder
content:
**Goal:** a small code-pretrained model that writes Rust *in this codebase's
idiom*, verified by the compiler, usable by `code-analyst` and eventually a
code-writing agent.

title: Track A: a Rust coder › Data
content:
1. **Eval set from this repo's own history (the most valuable asset).** 237
   commits, most touching `.rs`, each with a detailed message. Case = parent
   tree + commit message (+ the files it touched) → model produces a patch →
   grader applies it and runs `cargo check` plus the tests that commit added or
   changed. This has the shape of SWE-bench, on our own code. **Hold out the
   most recent commits by date.** It is too small to train on alone and exactly
   the right size to evaluate on.
2. **Training data: permissively-licensed public Rust**, license-filtered and
   recorded in the `(:Dataset)` manifest. Filtered by *compiles*, not just
   *parses*.
3. **Rejection sampling on the brain's own tasks.** Generate N patches per task,
   keep those that compile and pass, and train on the survivors. The compiler is
   the reward, with no model grading involved.

title: Track A: a Rust coder › Start by measuring, not training
content:
CLAUDE.md's standing lesson: **when a local model underperforms, check its
tools before concluding the model is too small.** Before any Rust fine-tune,
Phase 0 measures candidate bases (the `qwen2.5-coder` family already in
`models.yaml`, plus any current small code model that fits) on the repo-commit
eval below, with a real compile loop. The baseline may already be usable with
a compiler in the loop, and the gap may turn out to be tool access, not
weights.

title: Track A: a Rust coder › "The brain builds itself" safety contract
content:
Non-negotiable, and enforced structurally rather than by prompt:

- Model-written code lands **only in a git worktree on a `feature/*` branch**.
  Never `dev`, never a push.
- **A human reviews and signs every commit** (GPG, as today). The brain can
  propose a branch; it can't merge or deploy.
- The brain can't promote an adapter trained on data that includes its own
  promotion or eval code, and can't edit the eval suites or the graders it's
  scored by. Eval suites and grader code are human-owned, like
  `eval/retrieval_golden.yaml`.

---

title: Track A: a Rust coder › The verifier: a Rust sandbox
content:
The existing `sandbox` is Python-only and deliberately has no egress. A second
sidecar, `rust-sandbox`, with the same isolation contract (`internal: true`
network, no credentials, `cap_drop: ALL`):

- Rust toolchain baked into the image, **dependencies vendored at build time**
  (`cargo vendor` of this workspace's lockfile), since there's no network at
  run time
- a warm `target/` cache volume **owned by the sandbox**, not shared with the
  brain, because cold builds of a 62K-line workspace are slow
- `mem_limit` sized by measurement; the Python sandbox's 2 GB won't compile
  this workspace
- returns structured `cargo check` / `clippy` / `test` diagnostics, and a
  failing build is a successful tool call (same rule as `execute_code`)

title: Track B: Gemma as orchestrator and voice (distilled, not prompted)
content:
**Goal:** E4B that routes, delegates and speaks like the brain with a prompt
that carries only live state.

title: Track B: Gemma as orchestrator and voice (distilled, not prompted) › B1: routing first (narrow, verifiable)
content:
- **Task:** given the user message, roster and allowlist, emit the right
  `delegate(agent, task)` call, or answer directly.
- **Labels:** a turn is correctly routed when the delegated agent's run answered
  without contradicting ground truth. Known misses are already documented
  (meta-questions sent to `researcher`; "how many agents" matched on a word).
- **Data trick:** vary the roster in training examples (rename, drop and add
  agents) so the model learns to *read* the roster.
- Small, short examples. This is the best first real adapter.

title: Track B: Gemma as orchestrator and voice (distilled, not prompted) › B2: the task string (preserve intent through delegation)
content:
The front door rewrote *"I want to see all of what we learned"* into a search
query and lost the presentation intent (CLAUDE.md § bulk channel). Pairs:
(user message, roster) → a task string that keeps the imperative. Graded by
whether the worker's result satisfied the original request.

title: Track B: Gemma as orchestrator and voice (distilled, not prompted) › B3: voice via context distillation
content:
- **Teacher:** a strong model given the *full* policy prompt (the `general.yaml`
  ABSENCE / TOOL-RESULT / CITATION / TIME rules and the style guidance) plus
  the gathered tool results.
- **Student:** E4B given only live state and the same tool results, trained to
  produce the teacher's reply.
- **Human 👍/👎 is required here.** Voice has no deterministic checker.
- **Attribution must survive, and is checked mechanically.** The worker/voice
  split was turned off partly because the voice pass stripped "based on what
  the knowledge-worker found". Any reply that drops a citation or attribution
  present in the tool results is excluded from training.

title: Track B: Gemma as orchestrator and voice (distilled, not prompted) › What gets lost, and the mitigation
What exists today, and why it can't produce training data yet
content:
`SleepService::digest_experiences` (`crates/app/src/services/sleep.rs:29`)
writes ChatML JSONL from DuckDB `interactions`. Three defects:

1. **It records tool I/O, not model I/O.** `log_interaction`
   (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:136`) stores `tool name + args → tool result
   text`. The model's actual prompt, tool calls and completion are never saved.
   `model_usage` has token counts but no text.
2. **`feedback_score` is never written.** Nothing in the codebase sets it, so
   `digest_experiences(min_score: Some(n))` always exports zero rows.
3. **"success" means `is_error.is_none()`.** The brain's worst misses all had
   `isError: false`: "no videos were watched" on an 11-video day, the fabricated
   GDELT probe, "10 tools" against a registry of 90. A dataset filtered on this
   flag would train in exactly the failures this codebase has spent months
   removing.

**The label is the hard part, and the brain already owns most of the graders:**

| grader | kind | exists as |
|---|---|---|
| step args match the tool's `input_schema` | deterministic | `services/validation.rs` |
| schedule is lint-clean | deterministic | `lint_chain_steps` |
| Cypher uses real labels/props | deterministic | `services/cypher_guard.rs` |
| claimed tools actually ran | deterministic | `tool_trace_receipt`, `AgentFindings.tool_trace` |
| an answer contradicts a count we hold | ground truth | `recall_recent`, `list_capabilities`, `list_apis` |
| Rust compiles / lints / passes tests | deterministic | **missing**: needs a Rust sandbox (Track A) |
| work met its success criteria | model-graded | evaluator `Score: N/5` |
| plan is robust | model-graded | adversarial critic |
| local vs cloud on the same task | preference pair | the 2026-09-11 twin head-to-head |
| retrieval quality | golden set | `services/retrieval_eval.rs` |

Prefer deterministic and ground-truth labels. Model-graded labels are for
filtering only, never for rewards, because of the self-grading trap below.

---

title: Generic Tools Refactor Plan
content:
> **Goal:** Replace ~31 thin-wrapper tools and 7 HTTP-calling tools with a small set of
> generic primitives (`neo4j_query`, `http_request`) backed by a data-driven procedure +
> context layer. Make the scheduler's `goal_to_steps()` async so routing chains live in
> Neo4j rather than Rust code.
>
> Work through phases in order. Each phase is independently deployable.

---

title: Implementation Notes › Branch strategy
content:
- Each phase on its own `feature/generic-tools-phaseN` branch
- Merge to `dev` after tests pass
- Phase 1 is the only one touching the scheduler — keep it narrow

---

title: Implementation Notes › Cargo dependencies
content:
Phase 3 (`HttpSkill`) needs `reqwest` with the `json` feature — already present.
No new dependencies required for any phase.

title: Implementation Notes › `goal_to_steps` ChainStep substitution
content:
`SchedulerChain.steps` is stored as JSON. When loaded, substitute:
- `{{task_id}}` → the actual task UUID
- `{{goal}}` → the task goal string
- `{{date}}` → `chrono::Utc::now().format("%Y-%m-%d")`

This mirrors what the hardcoded branches do today.

title: Implementation Notes › Security considerations
content:
- `neo4j_query` with `readonly=false` is a powerful tool. Consider requiring an explicit
  confirmation parameter or restricting to specific node types.
- `http_request` with no `context_name` makes arbitrary outbound calls. Consider an
  allowlist of domains or require `context_name` for production deployments.
- `ApiContext.auth_env_var` stores the env var NAME, not the value — credentials never
  touch Neo4j.

title: Motivation
content:
The current 76-tool surface has two populations:

| Population | Count | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| Thin Neo4j wrappers | ~31 | Each is one Cypher query wrapped in Rust boilerplate |
| HTTP-calling tools | 7 | Hardcode specific APIs; can't reach new ones without a recompile |
| Algorithmic skills | ~30 | Real logic (RRF, chunking, embedding, decay scoring) — **keep as code** |
| Control/status tools | ~8 | In-process state management — **keep as code** |

The scheduler's `goal_to_steps()` is a `sync fn` with hardcoded keyword→chain mappings.
This means adding a new scheduler route requires a Rust recompile and redeploy.
Making it `async` allows routing rules to be stored as Neo4j nodes that the agent can
write and modify itself at runtime.

---

title: New Node Types (Neo4j Schema)
content:
```cypher
// API context — credentials + base URL for an HTTP API
(:ApiContext {
    id: String,           // UUID
    name: String,         // unique key, e.g. "github", "serpapi", "brave"
    base_url: String,     // https://api.github.com
    auth_scheme: String,  // "bearer" | "query_param" | "header" | "none"
    auth_param: String,   // header name ("Authorization") or query param name ("api_key")
    auth_env_var: String, // env var holding the secret, e.g. "GITHUB_TOKEN"
    default_headers: String,  // JSON object of headers always sent
    result_path: String,  // JSONPath to extract results from response body
    description: String,
    created_at: DateTime
})

// Scheduler routing chain — replaces a branch in goal_to_steps()
(:SchedulerChain {
    id: String,           // UUID
    pattern: String,      // substring to match in goal (lowercased)
    priority: Integer,    // checked in ascending order (lower = checked first)
    steps: String,        // JSON: Vec<ChainStep> serialized
    description: String,
    created_at: DateTime,
    updated_at: DateTime
})
```

---

title: Open Questions
content:
1. **`procedure_executor` conditional fallback** — **Resolved: Option A for `search_web`.** `on_failure: "continue"` already exists in the executor (it is the default). The real obstacle is result normalization: SerpApi, Brave, and Google CSE return completely different JSON shapes (`organic_results[].link` vs `web.results[].url` vs `items[].link`). A procedure cannot remap these into a unified `[{title, url, snippet}]` array — that is logic, not data. `search_web` therefore stays as Rust code (Option A) and simply delegates its outbound HTTP calls to `HttpSkill` instead of owning a `reqwest::Client` directly.
2. **`init-db` vs boot protocol for seeding** — **Decided: `boot.yaml`.** `SchedulerChain` and `Procedure` seeds run via boot protocol on every startup using idempotent `MERGE` so upgrades automatically apply new chains without manual `init-db` reruns.
3. **DuckDB / model contexts** — **Decided: yes, add `duckdb_query`.** See Phase 2 — `duckdb_query` is added to `QuerySkill` alongside `neo4j_query`. DuckDB is analytics-only (telemetry, model usage stats), so it is naturally read-only and lower risk than Neo4j writes.

title: Design
content:
**Schema source: live-introspected at boot, never a hand-authored file.** The
graph *is* the source of truth (honors the no-hardcoded-data rule and never goes
stale). `services/graph_schema.rs::introspect()` runs `db.schema` metadata
procs; lazily cached on first use in `QuerySkill`. Fails open (guard skips if
introspection fails).

title: Design › Phase 1 — deterministic tools + visibility (fixes every observed miss)
content:
All in `QuerySkill` (`skills/query.rs`) — it already owns `neo4j` and is
registered in both the registry and the handler vec:

- **`describe_graph`** — returns the live compact schema (labels, properties,
  which are temporal, relationship types). Lets the model *see* that
  `Task.updated_at` exists instead of inventing its absence.
- **`recent_tasks(limit, status?)`** — bakes `ORDER BY t.updated_at DESC`. The
  session-A miss, gone.
- **`list_apis()`** — the `(:ApiContext)-[:EXPOSES]->(:ApiEndpoint)` aggregate.
  The session-B miss, gone.

Profiles (`contexts/general.yaml`, `contexts/knowledge-worker.yaml`): add the
three tools (+`neo4j_query` to knowledge-worker, which lacked it — the exact
reason a *delegated* structural question could not be answered), plus two
position-zero rules:

- **STRUCTURAL QUERY RULE** — counts / "last N" / "what X do we have" / a
  specific note_type go to a deterministic tool or `neo4j_query` with the right
  MATCH/ORDER BY, never semantic search.
- **ABSENCE RULE** (fix #2, the behavioural half of the grounding guard) — never
  report "not found / none / not stored" off a semantic search alone; a negative
  claim about the graph requires a deterministic query that actually ran this
  turn (the tool-trace receipt already shows what ran).

title: Design › Phase 2 — the Cypher guard
content:
`services/cypher_guard.rs::check(cypher, &schema, readonly) -> Vec<Violation>`
(reuses `validation::{Severity, Violation}`), called inside
`neo4j_query` before dispatch:

- **readonly reads only:** unknown label / unknown rel type → **Hard** reject
  (a read of something that cannot exist is a bug; naming the valid set lets the
  model self-correct). Skipped for writes — `CREATE`ing a new label is legal.
- **any mode:** datetime-vs-string literal, and a `var.prop` where `var:Label`
  is bound and `prop` isn't in the label's introspected properties → **Soft**
  (advisory; introspection only sees properties present on ≥1 node, so a
  brand-new optional property must not hard-block). Soft violations ride out as
  a `warning` in the result envelope.

Fails open: no schema (introspection failed) ⇒ no guard, query runs.

title: Graph-Schema Guard + Deterministic Query Tools
content: **Status:** Phase 1 + Phase 2 implemented 2026-09-10 (uncommitted on `dev`).

title: Not done / follow-ups
content:
- Relationship endpoint-pair validation (`(:A)-[:R]->(:B)` shape) — only rel
  *types* are checked now; endpoint pairs need a data scan or `db.schema.visualization`.
- A hard code-level block on absence claims (vs the prompt rule) — deferred; the
  receipt + rule is the shippable form tonight.
- Routing knowledge lookups to local `gemma4:e4b` — **wired** 2026-09-10 (a
  `llamacpp` branch in `config_for_catalog_entry`, `LlamaCpp` in the sub-agent
  unmetered clamp, `LlamaCpp`→`run_ollama_cloud_loop` dispatch, a `gemma4-e4b`
  catalog entry, and the spawnable `contexts/knowledge-local.yaml`). **Unverified
  until the probe** (`scripts/probe_e4b_subagent.py`, run after a rebuild) shows
  E4B actually tool-calls across rounds; `knowledge-worker` stays on cloud until
  it passes. See CLAUDE.md § Context Profiles.

title: What "enforce correct Cypher" can and cannot mean
content:
It cannot mean *prove the query answers the question* — you can't statically
know `ORDER BY updated_at` was intended. Exactly like `services/validation.rs`
(structural, not semantic), the guard enforces a **known bad-set**:

- unknown node **label** / **relationship type** referenced in a read
- reference to a **property** no node of that label carries
- the **datetime-vs-string** comparison anti-pattern
- (already in `neo4j_query`) write keywords in readonly mode

A linter over a known bad-set, not a prover.

title: Why
content:
A chat-turn evaluation on 2026-09-10 (worker `gpt-oss:120b-cloud`, voice
`gemma4:31b-cloud`) found a recurring **quality** failure — zero errors in
`model_usage`, but the model *missed things* and narrated the gap as fact.
Verified against the live graph:

| Question | Model said | Ground truth |
|---|---|---|
| "last 5 tasks that ran" | 5 stale consolidation/UI tasks + *"completion timestamps were not stored"* | actual last 5 were job-search + gap-fills + video-watch; `Task.updated_at` **is** a native DATETIME on every node |
| "reflection notes today" | "none found" | 4 reflection notes existed |
| "what APIs do we have?" | "no concrete, fully-ingested API resources" | 3 ingested contexts: agent-brain (48 endpoints), aidevboard (27), home_assistant (20) |
| "do we know HomeAssistant?" | only found it **after the user pushed back** | it was there all along |

The pattern is identical every time: for a **structural / temporal / typed /
aggregate** question the model reaches for semantic `search_notes` (which cannot
count, order, or list), gets a thin result, then reports absence confidently —
including a fabricated schema claim ("timestamps weren't stored"). This is the
same disease `recall_recent` fixed for "what did we learn today", resurfacing
for other structural shapes.

**A smaller/local model will not fix this** — the failure is query construction
and tool selection, where a ~4B local model is weaker, not stronger. The fix is
deterministic tools + a schema the model can see + an enforcement guard, all
**model-agnostic**, so a later move of knowledge lookups to local `gemma4:e4b`
becomes *safe* (the tools carry query correctness the small model no longer has
to invent).

title: Agent-drafted workflows are checked on arrival
content:
**An agent-drafted workflow is checked when it arrives, not at Save** (2026-10-16, todo "Scheduled Tasks Editor needs some love").

- The editor's "Ask an agent to design the steps" used to send `schedule-author` only the request and the tool NAMES. So (1) an "update these steps" request never carried the steps and came back as a fresh draft, (2) the agent guessed argument names (Ministral: `reason.prompt` for `question`, `store_note.note` for `content`, `{{steps.1}}` with no step `id`), and (3) nothing checked the draft until Save, so it looked clean in the form and then the save was refused.
- Now the task (`components/schedules/draft.ts` `buildDraftTask`, shared with "Make it a schedule") carries the workflow being edited (name, every, steps), asking for the whole workflow back, plus one signature line per offered tool, `reason(question*, context, mode: infer|explain|…)`, built from `GET /api/tools?schemas=true` (each tool's `input_schema`).
- The draft goes straight through **`POST /workflows/check`**: the same `workflows::check` = the checking half (`prepare`) of `workflows::save`, nothing written; body = a save body, `id` = check it as an edit, no `id` = as a new workflow (an existing name refused). 200 `{ok, warnings}` or 400 with the save's own error. A refused draft goes back to the agent once with the errors (same model it ran on, `AssistRun.requestedModel`); if it still fails, the steps are put in the form with the errors shown, so Save's refusal is never a surprise.
- `AgentAssist.onResult` may be async, and gets the prompt as its 4th argument.
- A step `priority` written as a numeric string ("2") is read as the number the queue's `u8` needs; anything else stays as written so the check names it rather than the editor dropping it.
- schedule-author's output example shows steps with `id`s and a reason step reading `{{steps.news}}\n\n{{steps.known}}` (small models copy the example, not the rule), plus "pass only the arguments a step needs, never null/false/\"\"/[] placeholders; a listed choice exactly". The editor drops `null` arguments. Signature lines show every type, `ask: string` included (Gemma wrote `notify_user.ask: true` without it). A reference error now says how to fix it (`give the step you mean a top-level "id"`), and an edit task says ids may be added to kept steps. The editor also retries once on a reply with no parseable draft (Gemma ~1 in 4 writes its plan and stops).
- **Measured 2026-10-16 (gemma4-e4b, after all of the above):** edit 4/4 and from-scratch 3/3 pass the check, 4 of the 7 after the one fix-up round (before: edit passed once, from scratch 0/3). Ministral: 3/3 + edit. **Passing the check is not a good draft:** Gemma's from-scratch drafts fill optional arguments (`count: 1`, a pinned `engine`), put `store_note` after `notify_user` so `{{_prev}}` saves the notification, and invent templates (`{{datetime.now()}}`). Ministral's were sound apart from hardcoded dates. Gemma is fine for edits; for new workflows prefer a cloud model, and review either.
- **2026-10-16, later:** `reason.action` has an enum (infer|explain|clarify|audit|structured); before it, an invented mode ("summarize") saved and silently ran as infer. The prompt says never write a date into a query or argument (use `recency`; leave `event_at` out). **The step lint (`lint_chain_steps`) moved from `skills/scheduler.rs` to `work::validation`** and runs in `workflows::prepare`, so REST save, `POST /workflows/check` and `manage_workflow` all return it as `step_warnings`; the editor sends lint warnings back in its one fix-up round and shows any left. Before, only `manage_workflow` linted and the HBI never saw a warning.
- **`{{_prev}}` after `store_note`, `push_context` or `notify_user` is the content, not a receipt:** each returns `answer` = what it stored/sent, and the queue unwraps `answer`. A "receipt" lint was proposed and dropped for that reason (existing lint tests caught it: `{{_prev.id}}` after store_note is the note-id link).
- **schedule-author is pinned to `claude-haiku-4-5`** (provider anthropic, fallback ministral-14b-latest). On its pin: edit + 3 new all pass, one after the fix-up round (an invented `action` the enum caught); no dates in new queries.
- schedule-author's prompt says `{{_prev}}` is only the step right before, and an earlier step is used via a top-level `id` + `{{steps.<id>}}`. Ministral before any of this: 4 save errors on an edit.

title: 3. Architecture › 3A. Backend — Server-Side Chat (`POST /chat`)
content:
The brain runs the full LLM ↔ tool loop server-side. No API key is needed in the frontend.

**Rust implementation:** `src/services/chat.rs` → `ChatService`
- Hooked into `McpServerCore` via `chat_service()` factory
- `HttpTransportConfig::with_chat_service()` attaches it to the `/chat` route

**Request** (`POST /chat`, `Content-Type: application/json`):
```json
{
  "message": "What do you know about robotics?",
  "history": [
    { "role": "user",      "content": "Hello!" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "Hi! How can I help?" }
  ],
  "session_id": "optional",
  "tools": ["search_notes", "reason"]
}
```
`history` and `tools` are optional.

**SSE response events:**

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `thinking`    | `{"type":"thinking","content":"..."}` |
| `tool_call`   | `{"type":"tool_call","tool":"...","args":{}}` |
| `tool_result` | `{"type":"tool_result","tool":"...","success":true,"preview":"..."}` |
| `message`     | `{"type":"message","content":"..."}` |
| `error`       | `{"type":"error","message":"..."}` |
| `done`        | `{"type":"done"}` |

Provider strategy selected at runtime from `LlmConfig`:
- **Anthropic** — native `tool_use` blocks via `POST /v1/messages`
- **Ollama / Gemini** — text loop with `<tool_call>{"tool":"...","args":{}}</tool_call>` parsing
