title: Human Brain Interface (HBI) - Implementation Plan
content:
Status as of 2026-02-28: **Phases 1–3 complete. Frontend running.**

> **Layout superseded (2026-10-08)** by `HBI_REDESIGN_PLAN.md`. The transport, SSE and MCP-client notes below still hold.

---

title: 1. Why
content:
The HBI grew one tab per feature. Today it has **9 sidebar tabs**, plus a Settings modal, an Agents modal hidden in Chat, and a `ProposalsPanel` that nothing routes to. Panels that serve one job sit far apart, and several fetch the same data:

| Symptom | Evidence |
|---|---|
| One job, three places | Tasks, Todos and Scheduled are separate tabs. Todo → Task → Job lineage is not visible anywhere. |
| Knowledge split in two | Knowledge (list + reader) and Graph (force view) don't share a selection. Clicking a graph node can't open the reader. |
| Keyword-only search | `/api/notes?q=` is a `toLower(content) CONTAINS` scan over 23k notes. The hybrid search (`search_notes`) isn't reachable from the UI, and neither is lookup by ID. |
| Graph shows "recent", not "what we know" | `/api/graph` returns the 200 most recently *accessed* notes, plus entities and tasks. There is no domain layer, so no mind map is possible today. |
| Duplicate polling | `/api/queue/status` is fetched by Tasks, Logs **and** Architecture. `/api/scheduler/status` by Logs and Architecture. 5 files each define their own `apiFetch`/auth headers. |
| Logs mixes system and activity | LogsPanel shows recent tasks + queue + scheduler next to the tracing stream. |
| Architecture is hand-written and stale | `ArchitecturePanel.tsx` (1201 lines) hardcodes a `DETAILS` map (still describes OpenWebUI and stdio Claude Code as the primary clients) and its own colour palette. |
| Settings are scattered | Brain URL/key in the modal. Agents/profiles in a Chat modal, scheduler config in the Scheduled panel, scheduler start/stop in Architecture, model choice in the chat bar. |
| Style drift | 149 inline `style={{}}` in ScheduledTasksPanel and 75 in Architecture. Architecture has its own palette `C`. |
| Giant files | ScheduledTasksPanel 1910, ChatPanel 1242, ArchitecturePanel 1201 lines. |

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09)
10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › 10.1 What the review found
content:
| Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Career holds other people's careers.** Of 74 notes, about 17 are the user's: the résumé, job-search chats and AI Dev Board results. The rest are video claims and gap syntheses about anyone's career or hiring: Dolly Parton as a "showbiz entrepreneur", a Marine turned contractor, Rossmann Repair hiring, Melania Trump's Imperia. Almost all of them have Career as their only topic. The description says "the user's own career", and the local model reads past it. | live graph 2026-10-09; `topics/career.yaml` |
| **An entity's topics are derived, never stored.** An entity is "in" a topic when a note in that topic mentions it (`/api/topics/map`). Dolly Parton, Texas and New York City sit in Career because those video notes mention them. Fixing the notes fixes the entities, but there is no way to say "Texas is never Career". | `clients/topics.rs` map query |
| **Entities are not related to each other.** There are 24,145 `MENTIONS` edges and one `RELATED_ENTITY` edge. The entity drawer's "Mentioned with" ranks by raw shared-note count, so hubs (C-SPAN 184 notes, Neo4j 112, Rust 91) top every list and the shared notes can't be opened. | live graph; `clients/search.rs` `co_mentioned` |
| **Topics can only be edited in YAML, and a change needs a restart.** `Topics::global()` is a `OnceLock` loaded from `TOPICS_DIR`. Any change to a name or description changes `topics_version`, and every note is classified again. That costs hours of idle time for the whole graph: 13,718 notes, measured at about 56 a minute end to end (Phase 14). | `services/topics.rs` |
| **The NIA has no home.** Its notes name it ("Niche Intelligence Agency (NIA) Project: Critical Tech Dependency Mapping", 2026-08-08). Its schedules are filed under semiconductors (hardware tripwire, tech-dependency synthesis), national-security (intelligence-agency claims monitor) and us-politics (the Trump monitor). | live graph |

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › 10.2 Topics owned in the graph
content:
- **Ownership:** `topics/*.yaml` stays the seed. A topic edited in the HBI becomes `managed_by: runtime`, and the YAML sync then skips it. This is the rule schedules already follow, so a runtime-owned topic shadows its file, and the drawer says so.
- **Reloading:** `Topics::global()` becomes a reloadable current set, read from the graph. Its version is computed from the graph's definitions, so an edit takes effect without a restart.
- **Reclassifying:** a changed definition reclassifies on idle time, and the coverage line shows how many notes are waiting.
- **REST:** create, update and delete. A delete is refused while a schedule declares the topic, and the refusal names those schedules.
- **Career:**
  - Its description says what does not belong: other people's careers, hiring news, biographies and job-market statistics.
  - The fixed notes are checked by hand afterwards: Career should hold the user's own notes, and Dolly Parton, Texas and New York City should leave it on the map.
- **NIA:**
  - A new `intelligence-agency` topic ("Niche Intelligence Agency"). *Built as `nia`, with a narrower definition: see the Phase 14 outcome.* It holds the agency's own products: assessments of who gains or loses from policy, trade, sanctions and supply-chain events, tripwire scans, dependency maps and NIA reports. Plain news on those subjects stays in geopolitics, us-politics or semiconductors.
  - The user reviews the definition, as they did the Phase 11 starting values.
  - The Trump monitor is runtime-owned, so it moves with a targeted `SET`.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › 10.3 Manual topic edits
content:
- **A note's topics:** the note drawer shows its topics as chips that can be added or removed.
  - Edges the user sets are `method: 'manual'`. The note is marked `topics_locked`, and the classifier skips it, through version changes too.
  - "Let the classifier decide" unlocks it.
- **An entity kept out of a topic:** `(:Entity)-[:NOT_IN_TOPIC {at}]->(:Topic)`.
  - The map and the topic drawer leave the entity out. Each says how many entities the user has hidden, and lists them with undo, so a hide is never silent.
  - The entity drawer gains "In topics" (each topic with its note count, and a remove button). The topic drawer's entity list gets a remove button as well.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › 10.4 Co-mentions: how entities relate today
content:
- **`GET /api/entities/{id}/related?topic=`:**
  - Ranks by association strength: shared notes divided by √(mentions of A × mentions of B). A hub then no longer tops every list, and each row still carries its raw shared count.
  - Each pair drills to its notes through `GET /api/entities/pair?a=&b=`.
- **Entity drawer:** "Mentioned with" uses the new ranking, and a pair opens the notes they share.
- **Map:** clicking an entity opens a neighbourhood mode. It's an ego graph that expands on click, edge width shows strength and colour shows topic.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › 10.5 Typed relationships
content:
- **Vocabulary:** `relations/*.yaml` holds a closed list, such as `works_for`, `member_of`, `leads`, `located_in`, `owns`, `part_of`, `allied_with` and `opposes`. Each has a definition and the entity types it allows. Data stays in a seed directory, not in Rust.
- **Edges:** `(:Entity)-[:RELATES {type, method: 'manual'|'llm', status: 'active'|'rejected', evidence: [note ids], confidence, at}]->(:Entity)`.
  - **Editing:** the user adds, relabels and removes relations in the entity drawer and the pair view. A manual edge wins over an extracted one.
  - **Removing:** a removed extracted edge is kept as `rejected`, so extraction never adds it again.
- **Extraction:**
  - **Runs:** on idle time, using the local model, over claim notes (which stand alone since Phase 9), and only between entities the note mentions.
  - **Measured first:** on a hand-labelled sample, as topics were, before any backfill. The existing `RELATED_ENTITY` edge is folded in.
- **Map:** the neighbourhood view draws and labels typed edges beside the co-mention edges.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › 10.6 Phases
content:
| Phase | Scope | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **14. Topics in the graph** | §10.2: runtime-owned, reloadable topics; REST and the topic-drawer editor; the Career fix; the NIA topic; the Trump monitor moved. | Career's reclassified notes are the user's own, and Dolly Parton, Texas and New York City are gone from it; the NIA topic exists and holds the Trump monitor; an HBI edit reclassifies without a restart. |
| **15. Manual topic edits** | §10.3: note topic chips with a lock, entity hides with undo. | Hiding Texas from Career removes it from the map and the drawer, and the hide is shown and undoable; a manually set note keeps its topic through a reclassify. |
| **16. Co-mention view** | §10.4: related-entity ranking, pair evidence, the map's neighbourhood mode. | Amanda Thursk's view shows Prince Andrew, with the claim that she is his chief of staff as the evidence; C-SPAN no longer tops unrelated entities' lists. |
| **17. Typed relationships** | §10.5: vocabulary, user-owned edges, measured extraction, drawn on the map. | Extraction precision is measured on a held-out sample and recorded here; a rejected relation stays rejected through a re-extract; the user can add one by hand. |

**Order rationale:**
- **14 comes first** because it removes the wrong data at the source, and every later view shows topics.
- **15 comes before 16** because the hides decide what a topic-scoped neighbourhood shows.
- **17 comes last** because the user's manual edges need 16's views to edit in, and extraction must be measured before it writes.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › 10.7 Decisions (taken 2026-10-09: every recommendation accepted)
content:
1. **The NIA definition:** the agency's products (above), or everything on its subjects? *Recommend its products.* "Everything on its subjects" would swallow geopolitics, national-security and semiconductors.
2. **Move the other NIA schedules too?** These are the hardware tripwire and the tech-dependency synthesis (both now semiconductors) and the intelligence-agency claims monitor (now national-security). *Recommend the user decides each one in the schedule form;* nothing moves except the Trump monitor.
3. **Can a topic be deleted while schedules declare it?** *Recommend refusing, and naming the schedules.*
4. **Relation vocabulary:** closed or open? *Recommend closed, from YAML.* An open vocabulary from a small model grows synonyms faster than they can be merged.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › Phase 14 outcome (2026-10-09)
content:
Built and deployed:
- **Topics owned in the graph** (`services/topics.rs`):
  - `Topics::global()` is now the graph's set, reloaded after every edit, so the assigner uses an edit from its next batch, with no restart;
  - an HBI edit makes the topic `managed_by: runtime`, and `init-db` then leaves it alone;
  - deleting a seeded topic leaves a `(:RetiredTopic)`, so the sync doesn't bring it back;
  - Reset restores the file's definition;
  - `init-db` now syncs topics before seeding schedules, since a schedule's `topic` is checked against them.
- **Checked before writing** (`check_def`): a slug name set once (`map` and `new` reserved), a description of at most 500 characters, the whole classifier prompt within 3,600 characters, and no delete while a schedule declares the topic (the refusal names the schedules).
- **REST:** `POST /api/topics`, `PUT|DELETE /api/topics/{name}` and `POST /api/topics/{name}/reset`. The topic detail now carries `managed_by`, the YAML `seed` and the reclassify progress.
- **HBI:**
  - the topic drawer has Edit definition, Reset to YAML and Delete, and shows who owns the definition and how many notes are waiting;
  - the map has "+ Topic";
  - the form warns when a changed definition will re-classify every note.
- **Career → `my-job-search`** ("Career & job search"), with a definition limited to the user's own career. The AI Dev Board schedule follows it. *Superseded in Phase 15: the live run showed the classifier filing strays here, and the topic is now `assign: rules`.*
- **The `nia` topic** ("Niche Intelligence Agency") holds the program itself: its plans, verticals, tripwires and the reports that name it. The Trump Benefit Daily Monitor now declares `topic: nia`; it is runtime-owned, so it was moved with a targeted `SET`.

**Measured before deploying** (dry run on the sidecar, no writes): all 74 Career notes, 35 notes from the NIA schedules and 60 random classified notes.

| Definitions tried | The user's notes kept in Career | Other people's career notes still in Career | NIA |
|---|---|---|---|
| `career` + "not other people's careers" | 18 / 18 | 22 / 56 | `intelligence-agency` took a CIA director's claim, a Kushner dark-money note and an FBI espionage case from national-security and us-politics |
| `career`, "only the user's own (Ara Sheperdigian)" | 18 / 18 | 22 / 56 | `nia`, narrow: only notes that name the NIA |
| **`my-job-search`**, same definition | **18 / 18** | **12 / 56** | `nia`: the NIA notes and hardware tripwire reports as a second topic; no CIA or FBI stories |

- **The name outweighs the definition.** The "not this" clause moved nothing, and renaming halved the leak. The other 12 are for Phase 15's manual edits. *The sample was the flaw: it held only notes already in a topic. Live, `my-job-search` drew notes that fit no topic (see Phase 15).*
- **The Trump assessments are classified by subject in every version,** as us-politics or geopolitics. The schedule belongs to the NIA program; its notes belong to their subjects. The Phase 11 topic mix will show that as a mismatch, and the mismatch is accurate.

**Verified live:**
- **Topic edits:**
  - create, a duplicate, a bad name, a rename attempt and an over-long description were each accepted or refused with the stated reason;
  - a label-only edit doesn't re-classify;
  - deleting `nia` was refused, naming the Trump monitor.
- **Michigan, a seeded topic:**
  - deleting it removed 430 edges and left a tombstone;
  - a fresh `init-db` didn't recreate it;
  - Reset restored it as `yaml` and removed the tombstone.
- **Data:** no schedule declares a missing topic, and all 12 topics carry one version.

**Found while building:**
- **A full re-classify takes about 4 hours, not 1.** The model call is about 0.3 s, but end to end it ran at about 56 notes a minute. The UI and docs now say so.
- **A delete followed by a reset brings back the old version.** A note still stamped with it would have looked classified without its topic, so a delete now marks that topic's notes as waiting.

**Not yet verified:** the live re-classify that the new definitions started (13,700 notes, newest first, idle time only). The résumé notes are among the oldest, so Career's live result comes last.

**Tests:** 870 Rust lib tests (2 new) and 95 vitest.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › Phase 15 outcome (2026-10-09)
content:
Built and deployed:
- **A note's topics, edited by hand** (`PUT /api/notes/{id}/topics`, `DELETE /api/notes/{id}/topics/lock`):
  - the note drawer shows its topics as chips: remove, make main, add (at most two), "Lock", and "Let the classifier decide";
  - a set note is `topics_locked` with `method: 'manual'` edges. The classifier skips it, every new version is stamped on it, and deleting a topic unlocks that topic's notes.
- **An entity kept out of a topic** (`PUT|DELETE /api/entities/{id}/topics/{topic}/hidden`, `(:Entity)-[:NOT_IN_TOPIC]->(:Topic)`):
  - the map and the topic drawer leave the entity out;
  - the entity drawer's new "In topics" section lists each topic with its note count, and Keep out / Let back in;
  - the topic drawer has × on its entity chips and a "Kept out by you" list with undo;
  - the map bar counts the hides;
  - an entity merge carries the hides to the surviving entity.
- **Rule-assigned topics** (`assign: rules` + `members:`, in YAML or in the topic form's rule editor):
  - a rules topic is left out of the classifier's prompt and can't be picked even by name;
  - a note joins when it matches a member rule (`note_type` / `source_context` exactly, `content_contains` case-insensitively), ranked first, with `method: 'rule'`, or when the user adds it by hand;
  - the rules count toward the version;
  - `topics::reload` applies the rules at once (they need no model) and drops any classifier edges a rules topic had, so a rules topic is complete straight away, not after the hours-long re-classify.
- **`my-job-search` and `nia` are now rules topics.**
  - `my-job-search` takes the résumé import, the AI Dev Board API spec, and `jobsearch-` chat sessions.
  - `nia` takes notes that name the Niche Intelligence Agency: 34 of them, all about the program.

**Why rules (found live, after Phase 14):**
- **`my-job-search` took only strays.** The first 13 notes the live classifier put in it were all wrong: a murder trial, an Uber case, a news brief, Melania Trump's Imperia, a "what did we learn today" chat.
- **`nia` was mixed:** real NIA chats, but also the brain's daily "logged N notes" reports and GDELT summaries about Mossad.
- **The Phase 14 sample missed this.** It only held notes that were already in some topic, so it never tested the notes that fit no topic. The model files some of those in whichever small, personal-sounding topic its prompt offers.
- **The model can't tell whose career or which agency a note is about,** so for those two topics the classifier is the wrong tool, not a matter of wording.

**Verified live:**
- **Your notes:** six of your job-search notes that match no rule (two AI Dev Board summaries and four chats about applying and your professional history) were set to `my-job-search` by hand. They were in Career before.
- **The lock** held through two version changes, a Michigan edit and its reset. Unlock made the note wait for the classifier, and it relocked.
- **Note refusals:** an unknown topic is refused with the list of topics, and so are three topics on one note.
- **Texas, hidden from Michigan:** it left the map and the topic drawer's entities, appeared under "Kept out by you", and was marked in its own drawer. Undo restored it, and the live state is unchanged.
- **Merges:** a hide on a throwaway entity moved to the entity it was merged into. The test entities were deleted.

- **The done-condition, on the map:**
  - Career & job search holds the 11 résumé notes, the AI Dev Board spec (2), the `jobsearch-` chat, and the six set by hand. Its entities are the user's skills and employers (Rust, Neo4j, Kubernetes, Golang, Python, ElTec Systems, Waterford, aidevboard, Drata), and Dolly Parton, Texas and New York City are gone.
  - `nia` holds the 34 notes that name the program, and its entities are the program and its supply-chain vertical (hardware tripwire, HBM, ABF substrates, SK hynix, ASML, CoWoS).

**Pending:** the live re-classify started by the new definitions (about 4 h of idle time). It decides what the classifier topics now hold.

**Tests:** 874 Rust lib tests (4 new) and 95 vitest.

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › Phase 16 outcome (2026-10-09)
content:
Built and deployed:
- **Related entities ranked by strength** (`clients/related.rs`, `GET /api/entities/{id}/related?topic=`):
  - strength is shared notes ÷ √((mentions A + 3) × (mentions B + 3)), replacing the raw shared-note count;
  - with a topic, only that topic's notes count, and entities kept out of it are left out.
  - Measured over the 300 entities that share notes with C-SPAN: raw counts put C-SPAN first for 30 of them, strength for 1.
- **The evidence for a pair** (`GET /api/entities/pair?a=&b=`): the notes that mention both, newest first.
- **An ego graph** (`GET /api/entities/{id}/neighbourhood`): the entity, its 12 strongest neighbours, and every pair among them that shares a note. It answers in 0.01–0.12 s, Donald Trump and C-SPAN included.
- **HBI:**
  - the entity drawer's "Mentioned with" is now ranked rows with a strength bar, a topic scope, and the shared notes behind each row;
  - "Neighbourhood on the map" opens `#/knowledge?view=map&focus=<id>&scope=<topic>`, as does double-clicking an entity on the topic map;
  - in the neighbourhood, clicking a node expands its neighbours and opens it, clicking a line shows the notes behind the pair, colour is the entity's main topic, and line width is strength.
- **Claims have entities** (`spawn_claim_entity_backfill`): an idle-time loop extracts entities from claims that have none, with a claim-specific prompt, stamping `entities_at` / `entities_found`.

**Found while building:**
- **No claim had an entity.** 0 of 4,546. `store_claim` writes claims in raw Cypher, past `store_note`'s extraction, so the most entity-dense notes in the graph were invisible to every entity view. "Amanda Thursk is Prince Andrew's chief of staff" linked neither person.
  - Phase 17's plan to extract relations from claims depended on those links, so this mattered beyond Phase 16.
- **The general extraction prompt fails on one-sentence claims.** On the local model it answered `[]` for 22 of 30 claims, mostly ones naming someone ("Senator Mitch McConnell was noted as voting 'aye'"). A claim prompt ("a proper name counts even if it appears once") left 5 of the same 30 empty, each naming nothing.
  - A few of its picks are loose ("Iranian Missile Deal", "Flight 7").
  - The general prompt is unchanged: it hasn't been measured on long notes.
  - The first 682 claims stamped under the general prompt were reset and re-run.

**Verified live:**
- **Amanda Thursk:** her related list ranks Prince Andrew first (2 shared, strength 0.338), and NewsNation, a hub in 185 notes, last (0.033).
- **The pair view** opens their two shared notes: a gap synthesis on Thursk's work for him, and the NewsNation video record.

**Pending:**
- The claim backlog: about 4,400 claims at ~25 a minute on idle time, shared with the topic re-classify.
- The chief-of-staff claim itself (2026-08-12) joins the pair's evidence when the backlog reaches it.

**Tests:** 876 Rust lib tests (2 new) and 97 vitest (2 new).

title: 10. Third round: Phases 14–17 (planned 2026-10-09) › Phase 17 outcome (2026-10-09) — the third round is complete
content:
Built and deployed:
- **The vocabulary** (`relations/types.yaml`, `RELATIONS_DIR`): works_for, leads, member_of, part_of, located_in, owns, made_by, allied_with, opposes, and the user-only related_to. Each has a label, its inverse, a definition and the entity types allowed at each end.
- **Storage** (`services/relations.rs`): `(:Entity)-[:RELATES {type, method, status, evidence}]->(:Entity)`.
  - The user's relationships are active. Extracted ones are proposals until accepted or rejected, and a rejected one is kept, so it is never proposed again.
  - A symmetric type is stored once.
  - The merge list's "related" answers (`RELATED_ENTITY`) fold into `related_to`, at `init-db` and at each new answer.
- **Extraction:**
  - `extract_relations` reads claims that name two or more entities and proposes the relationships they state, validating each against the claim's own entities and the vocabulary and reporting every drop with its reason. `note_id` re-reads one claim.
  - `schedules/relation-extraction.yaml` runs it every 30 minutes over 30 claims, with the step pinned to `gpt-oss:120b-cloud`.
- **REST:** the vocabulary; an entity's relationships read from its side; set, decide, relabel and remove; and the proposals to review.
- **HBI:**
  - **Entity drawer:** a Relationships section ("works for Prince Andrew", "employs Amanda Thursk"), with set-by-you / proposed / accepted, evidence links, accept / reject, change type, remove, and "+ Relationship" (type, direction, the other entity).
  - **Pair view:** the relationships between the two, and "+ How A relates to B" with the shared note as evidence.
  - **Feed:** a "relationships to review" card and its review list, each proposal with the sentence that states it.
  - **Neighbourhood:** blue arrows for relationships, labelled when zoomed in, dashed while proposed.

**Measured before anything was written.** Relations were hand-labelled from claims with two or more entities. Strict counts a relation only when the sentence says it and both ends are the right entities. Lenient also accepts defensible readings ("co-founder" → leads, a network layer "part of" a mesh network).

| Model, prompt | Set | Relations kept | Right (lenient) | Right (strict) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma-4-E4B (local), v1 | tuning, 30 claims | 8 | 2 | 2 |
| Gemma-4-E4B, v2 (stricter) / v3 (examples) | tuning | 0 / 1 | — / 0 | — / 0 |
| gpt-oss:120b-cloud, v3 | tuning | 14 | 13 | 11 |
| gpt-oss:120b-cloud, v3 | held out, 30 claims | 8 | 5 | 3 |
| **gpt-oss:120b-cloud, v4** (examples from the held-out failures) | **fresh held out, 30 claims** | **9** | **8** | **5** |

- **The local model can't do this.** With examples it answered `[]` even for the sentence its own example spelled out ("Mossad Director Roman Gofman").
- **The cloud model is useful but not trustworthy alone.**
  - Its misses: something belonging to an entity taken for the entity ("Ford is in Mexico" from "a Ford plant in Mexico"); a forum's place taken for its host's; and a refused relationship read as stated (Will Geer and the Communist Party).
  - v4's examples target those three. It also reaches for outside knowledge ("CIA is in the US").
  - **So every extracted relationship is a proposal.** It is recall-light: 9 relations from 30 claims.
- **Entity types needed loosening.** 3,076 entities are typed `concept`, many of them real things, so the "thing" ends allow concept, product, programme, law and event. Strict typing dropped "Starship is made by SpaceX".

**Verified live (the done-condition):**
- **Precision** is measured on a fresh held-out set and recorded above.
- **Rejected stays rejected:**
  - the first scheduled run read 30 claims and proposed 13, on gpt-oss:120b-cloud per the usage stamp;
  - "Hallelujah Chorus is part of Pentecost Sunday" was rejected, and its claim re-read five times;
  - the model proposed it again once, and it stayed rejected (`seen_again: 1`).
- **A relationship by hand:**
  - "Amanda Thursk works for Prince Andrew" was set with the chief-of-staff claim as evidence, and read "employs Amanda Thursk" from Prince Andrew's side;
  - it was relabelled to related_to with the evidence carried over, then removed;
  - an unknown type and an entity related to itself were refused.
- **The fold:** it turned the one "related" merge answer (MSS ↔ Ministry of State Security) into `related_to`.

**Tests:** 880 Rust lib tests (4 new) and 97 vitest.

**Left as it is:**
- **The backlog:** about 650 claims with entities are waiting, and more arrive as the claim entity backfill continues, so proposals will accumulate in the Feed's review card.
- **The other extraction prompt:** the general one used by `store_note` is unchanged.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09)
content:
Source: the user, reviewing relationships and aliases after Phase 17. Many entities are unfamiliar and need looking up before a relationship or an alias can be decided. The drawer already lists every note that mentions an entity, but nothing says what the entity *is*. The user wants a Wikipedia link for entities and topics.

Decisions taken in the discussion (2026-10-09):
1. **Background lookups only cover entities named in public sources.** A lookup sends the entity's name to Wikimedia, and names also come from private notes (the résumé, job-search chats, other chats). Claims are the public signal: every claim comes from a video, article or news feed and carries a source URL or outlet. `source_record` notes do not qualify, because the résumé is stored as one. Any other entity is looked up only when the user presses a button in its drawer.
2. **Measure first** on a fixed sample, with acronyms and common names included on purpose, before anything is built. Done; see §11.1.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.1 Measured (dry run, nothing written)
content:
**The sample:** 53 entities named in claims, frozen and stratified by type: 45 by a hash of the id, plus 8 short names (accc, tdc, drm, vms, kapo, png, uae, vr).

**The pipeline under test:**
- **Search:** Wikidata `wbsearchentities` for the name, up to 7 candidates.
- **Candidates:** each one's instance-of (P31) kinds and its English Wikipedia title.
- **The pick:** `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` sees the candidates and up to 3 claims that mention the entity, and picks one or answers 0.

Graded by hand.

| Method | Picked | Right | Close but not it | Wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Top search result, no model (the baseline) | 37 (every entity with results) | 24 | 0 | 13 |
| Model, v1 (strict "same kind" rule) | 29 | 29 (1 generic: "county commissioners" → county board) | 0 | 0 |
| Model, v2 (filed type "may be wrong") + a second, model-suggested search when it answers 0 | 38 | 34 | 2 | 2 |
| **v2 with no second search for `concept` entities** (the design below) | **35** | **33** | **2** | **0** |

- **Taking the top result is wrong a third of the time:**
  - William Shakespeare → the family name;
  - DRM → Digital Radio Mondiale;
  - PNG → the image format;
  - VR → a Finnish railway;
  - Venice Beach → a Tony Hawk game level;
  - Cora (a private person's daughter) → the given name.
- **The model's v1 picks were all right, and it answers 0 honestly.** Its reasons:
  - "none of the listed John Houstons is a senator from Ohio" (the transcript garbled Jon Husted);
  - "a private individual named Cora";
  - "Versori is a new product with no candidate".
- **v1 missed Shergar.** Our graph types the racehorse a `person`, and the strict kind rule refused the stallion. v2 tells the model the filed type may be wrong. That fixed it and changed none of the 29 picks.
- **The second search finds:**
  - garbled names (Pento Barbatale → pentobarbital);
  - names that need a fuller official form (Kapo → Estonian Internal Security Service);
  - plurals (VMs → virtual machine; Chinese walls → information barrier).
- **For vague phrases, the second search invents a match:** "system intelligence" → artificial general intelligence, and a UK speech's "European security frameworks" → the EU's Common Security and Defence Policy. So `concept` entities get no second search. That rule also drops one correct pick (Chinese walls).
- **The two "close" picks are related articles, not the entity:**
  - "Emirati" (an official) → United Arab Emirates;
  - "U.S. administrations" → the federal government.
  
  Both are useful context, but neither is the entity.
- **Search misses a deterministic rule can fix:** "metropolitan police department (mpd)" found nothing until the bracket was dropped. The lookup will search the name without its bracket, and the bracket on its own.
- **Not found, correctly:** new bills, new products, video titles, private people, and fine-tune names like jeff-qwen3.5-0.8b.
- **This is the tuning set.** The phase measures the final prompt again on a fresh held-out sample before the backfill.

**Rate limits are a design constraint.** Three parallel lookups got HTTP 429 from Wikidata, then `Retry-After: 41` for a while. Wikimedia's policy asks automated clients to send a contact (a URL or email) in the user agent, and throttles anonymous ones harder.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.10 Alias verdicts from nimble (built 2026-10-09, ahead of the rest of Phase 18)
content:
Source: the user, after the §11 measurement: "lets use nimble for the alias review. Who knows, we may think of something else to use it for later."

**What nimble is:** a 9B decision model from Bespoke Labs, fine-tuned from Qwen3.5, served by host Ollama at `/v1/systemone`.
- It answers fixed questions (pick from a list, true or false, a score) with a probability for each option and no free text.
- It runs as 9.5 GB Q8: about 2.9 GB on the GPU, the rest on the CPU, next to the llama.cpp sidecar.
- About 2 s a question once loaded.

**Measured first, on the brain's data (scripts in the session scratchpad, `nimble/`):**

| Job | Result | Fit |
|---|---|---|
| Aliases: same / related / different, from up to 2 notes with both names and 2 with each alone (40 live candidates, hand-graded) | v1 31/40; **v2 (titles, first names, plurals and misspellings count as the same) 33/40**, no false "same". The names as written (`Senator Collins`) gave 3 false "same"; an "unclear" option was never chosen. | **Built** |
| Checking the cloud model's relationship proposals (50) | Keeping those above 0.5 raised precision from 74% to 82%, but nonsense passed at 0.99 ("democratic control part of the Obama administration") | A sort key at most |
| Extracting relationships itself (Phase 17's held-out claims) | About half right, 12–25 s a claim, and HTTP 400 past its 8K-token prompt cap | No |
| Picking the Wikidata item (§11.1's round-1 candidates) | Agreed with the cloud model on 32 of 38; one confident wrong pick (a private "Cora" → the given name, 0.98) | Not instead of the cloud model |

**Built:**
- **The judge:** `services/alias_judge.rs` judges every merge candidate on idle time.
  - It runs 10 pairs a pass, re-checking for real work between pairs, with a 60 s `keep_alive` so the model leaves the GPU after a batch.
  - `ALIAS_JUDGE_MODEL` names the model (`off` to stop it).
- **Storage:** `(from)-[:ALIAS_VERDICT {verdict, p_same, p_related, p_different, model, version, at}]->(into)`. A new prompt version or model is judged again.
- **The candidate list** (`/api/entities/candidates`) carries `judge` and sorts in this order:
  1. confident same (≥ 0.7);
  2. leaning same, or not judged yet;
  3. related;
  4. different;
  
  then by shared notes. The person still decides every pair.
- **HBI:** each candidate row shows the verdict: "looks the same (0.99)", "leans the same", "looks related, not the same" or "not shown to be the same". The probabilities, model and time are on hover.

**Verified live:**
- All 68 candidates were judged in about 17 minutes of idle time.
- **The first deploy sent the options and texts in alphabetical order** (`serde_json`'s `json!` map), not the measured order, and nimble's answers moved.
  - The 40 tuning pairs matched the dry run only 33 times, with two confident false "same" answers: Mills → Doug Mills at 0.95, and Collins → Mike Collins at 0.92.
  - Resending the dry run's exact requests proved nimble deterministic. Sorting their keys reproduced the flips.
  - The request is now built from structs in the measured order, pinned by a test, under prompt version `v2-ordered`.
- **Graded again after the fix:**
  - 40 tuning pairs: 32 right, and no false "same".
  - 28 held-out pairs: 25 right. Cautious misses: Rajab, and CPUs → CPU. One wrong "same": Kushner → Josh Kushner at 0.41.
  - Before the fix, held-out "General Franks" ≠ Dennis Franks was also a wrong "same", at 0.59. Both are why a "same" under 0.7 only leans.
  - **No confident "same" (≥ 0.7) was wrong across all 68.**
- Good catches: PMCs (contractors) ≠ PMC (PubMed Central), and "the King" ≠ the Jordanian king.

**Left for later:**
- The relationship proposals could use nimble's score as a sort key.
- §11.6's `wikidata` merge reason pairs naturally with a "same" verdict.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.2 Storage
content:
- **`(:WikiItem {qid, label, description, aliases, kinds, wiki_title, fetched_at, summary, summary_at})`:** one node per Wikidata item, shared by every entity that links to it.
  - `summary` is the article's first paragraph, from Wikipedia's REST `page/summary`. It is fetched when first shown and cached for 30 days.
- **`(:Entity)-[:REFERS_TO {status: proposed|confirmed|rejected, method: llm|manual, why, query, model, at, decided_at}]->(:WikiItem)`:**
  - The user's choices are final, as with relationships.
  - A rejected link is kept, so it is never proposed again.
- **Bookkeeping on the entity:** `wiki_checked_at` and `wiki_result` (`proposed` / `none` / `skipped_private`), so nothing is looked up twice. A `none` is re-checked after 90 days: new things get articles.
- **The candidates** each lookup saw are cached on the entity (`wiki_candidates`, ids only), so "choose another" needs no new search.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.3 The lookup (`services/wiki.rs`)
content:
- **Steps:**
  1. Search the name, the name without its bracket, and the bracket on its own.
  2. Fetch the candidates' kinds and English Wikipedia titles.
  3. The model picks one (the v2 prompt).
  4. If it answers 0 and the entity is not a `concept`, the model suggests up to 2 search terms. The second search runs, and the model picks again from the merged candidates. The search term used is recorded on the link.
- **The model:** pinned to `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` (`no_log`, $0), like relation extraction. The local model was not tried, since Phase 17 showed it can't do this kind of choice. The phase measures it once on the held-out set anyway.
- **Etiquette:**
  - one request at a time, at least 1 s apart, honouring `Retry-After`;
  - a user agent with a contact from `WIKIMEDIA_CONTACT`; background lookups stay off until it is set;
  - a 429 ends the run early and says so.
- **Privacy:** a background lookup only takes entities with a `MENTIONS` edge from a claim. The model's suggested search terms come from claim text, which is public. An on-demand lookup of a private entity sends only its name and the model's search terms to Wikimedia. The context goes only to the `no_log` model.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.4 Where it runs
content:
- **Background:** a tool, `link_entities {limit, entity_id}`. It runs on `schedules/entity-linking.yaml`, hourly, 20 entities a run, with the step pinned to the cloud model.
  - **Order:** entities waiting in a review first (relationship proposals, merge candidates), then by how many claims mention them.
  - **Time:** about 2,000 public entities take a few days of hourly runs. Each run reports how many are waiting.
- **On demand:** "Look up" in the entity drawer runs `entity_id` for one entity, private or not, because the user pressed it.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.5 HBI
11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.6 Aliases
content:
- **A new merge reason, `wikidata`:** two entities linked to the same WikiItem become a merge candidate with this reason. Example: MSS and Ministry of State Security.
  - A candidate from two confirmed links ranks above the name rules. A candidate from proposed links shows as "suggested by reference links".
  - Merges stay proposals (decision 4a).
- **Wikidata's English aliases** are shown in the Reference block, so "also known as" is visible. They are not written as `EntityAlias` nodes.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.7 Not in this phase
content:
- **Wikidata statements:** employer, member of, located in and part of could corroborate or contradict relationship proposals. A later phase, once links are trusted.
- **A "Research this" button** that sends the researcher agent to the web for entities with no article.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.8 Phase
content:
| Phase | Scope | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **18. Reference links** | §11.2–11.6: WikiItem + REFERS_TO, the lookup and its etiquette, `link_entities` and its schedule, the drawer's Reference block, descriptions in the review lists, topic reference URLs, `wikidata` merge candidates. | The final prompt is measured on a fresh held-out sample and recorded here; MSS and Ministry of State Security link to the same item and appear as a `wikidata` merge candidate; an entity mentioned only in private notes is never looked up in the background (the run reports it skipped); a rejected link stays rejected through a re-lookup; a topic shows a reference URL the user set. |

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › 11.9 Decisions (taken 2026-10-09)
content:
1. **`WIKIMEDIA_CONTACT`:** what goes in the user agent, an email or a URL such as the repository? *The user chose their email.* It is set in the gitignored `.env`, not in `docker-compose.yml`, which only passes it through.
2. **Close-but-not-it picks** ("Emirati" → UAE): accept them as context, or prompt against them? *Recommend prompting against them:* the link should be the entity itself, and a demonym or an umbrella body is better as "none".
3. **A Feed card for suggested links?** *Recommend none:* a suggested link is low-stakes and gets decided in the drawer, where it is used. The coverage count (linked / none / waiting) goes on the Knowledge page instead, drillable.
4. **Re-check "none" after:** *Recommend 90 days.*

Decisions 2–4 were taken as recommended.

title: 11. Fourth round: Phase 18, reference links (planned 2026-10-09) › Phase 18 outcome (2026-10-09)
content:
Built and deployed:
- **Storage** (`services/wiki.rs`): `(:Entity)-[:REFERS_TO {status, method, why, query, model}]->(:WikiItem {qid, label, description, kinds, aliases, wiki_title, summary})`.
  - The model's pick is `proposed`. Confirming one rejects any other, and a rejected item is never offered to the model for that entity again.
  - Each lookup stamps `wiki_checked_at` / `wiki_result` / `wiki_candidates` on the entity, and "none" is checked again after 90 days.
- **The lookup:**
  - It searches the name, and for `x (y)` also `x` and `y`. It fetches each candidate's English (or language-neutral `mul`) label, description, kinds, aliases and article.
  - `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` picks one or answers 0 (prompt v4).
  - Only for named things (not `concept`, `event` or `programme`), a model-suggested second search follows.
  - All Wikimedia calls go through one gate: serialised, 1.1 s apart, paused by a 429's `Retry-After`, with `WIKIMEDIA_CONTACT` in the user agent.
- **Where it runs:**
  - `link_entities` (tool count +1), run hourly over 20 claim-named entities by `schedules/entity-linking.yaml`. Review queues come first, then the most-mentioned.
  - "Look up" in the drawer enqueues the same step with `on_demand`, so one place pins the model.
- **REST:** the entity's reference, look up, confirm / reject, set by URL, one-line descriptions, and coverage by bucket (drillable).
- **HBI:**
  - The entity drawer's **Reference** block: label, description, kinds, the article's first paragraph, aliases, Wikipedia and Wikidata links, why the model picked it, Confirm / Not this / Choose another / paste a URL / Look up. With no link it says "no article found (checked …)" or why it was not looked up.
  - One-line descriptions beside names in the relationship review, the pair view and the merge candidates.
  - A **References** view under Knowledge: suggested / confirmed / no article / waiting, each drilling to its entities.
  - A topic **reference URL** in the topic form and drawer, outside the topic version.
- **Aliases:** a `wikidata` merge reason for two entities on one item, judged by nimble like any other.

**Measured through the real path** (REST → queue → `link_entities` on the pinned model), graded by hand:

| Prompt | Set | Proposed | Right | Close but not it | Wrong | Correctly none | Missed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v3 | 30 fresh entities | 23 | 19 | 2 (Italian → Italy, Cuban → Cuba) | 2 (a makemore video → WaveNet; "Cuomo Full Show" → CNN's Cuomo Prime Time) | 6 | 1 (Congresswoman Harshbarger) |
| **v4** (nationality rule spelled out; no second search for events and programmes) | **30 more fresh entities** | **20** | **18** | **1** (the Marines → "marine force") | **1** (M5Stack Cardputer kit → M5Core) | **6** | **4** (Senate Agriculture Committee, Invictus, Lambda, "Juggalo gathering") |

- **v3's wrong picks both came from the second search**, on a video and a show title, which it linked to their subject. v4 takes that search away from events and programmes. v4's one wrong pick also came from a second search.
- **The misses are cautious:** the right item wasn't among the candidates (Invictus Games, Lambda the GPU company), or the name was too generic to search ("Juggalo gathering", set by URL in the test below).
- **The first scheduled run** (the 20 most-mentioned waiting entities) gave 17 right, 1 fair reading ("White House" → Executive Office of the President), and 2 close-but-not-it: "United Kingdom" → the UK government, and "Chinese" → the People's Liberation Army, through a second search despite the nationality rule.
- **Wikidata's labels:** Albert Einstein's item has no English label, only a language-neutral `mul` one, so it showed as "Q937". Every request now asks for `en|mul`, and the 5 stored items affected were repaired (2 more have no label at all).

**Verified live (the done-condition):**
- **Measured on a fresh held-out sample:** recorded above.
- **MSS and Ministry of State Security:** both linked to Q1068951 (Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China). They do **not** appear as a `wikidata` merge candidate, because the user answered that pair "related" in the merge review before (Phase 17 folded it into `related_to`), and an answered pair is never proposed again. The new reason does work: "Cuban" ↔ "Cuba" appeared, and nimble judged it "related".
- **Private entities are skipped in the background:** `link_entities` on the résumé-only entity "arabenjamin" returned `skipped_private`, with no candidates and nothing stored.
- **Rejected stays rejected:** WaveNet was rejected for the makemore video, a re-lookup offered the model everything else, and it answered none.
- **Confirm and set by URL:** Ministry of State Security's link was confirmed, with its article summary and aliases (MSS, Guoanbu) shown. "Juggalo gathering" was set from its Wikipedia URL. A bogus item and a non-Wikipedia URL were refused with the reason.
- **A topic's reference URL:** the save path is covered by tests. No topic was edited live, because a save makes the topic runtime-owned. The first one is the user's.

**Tests:** 889 Rust lib tests (5 new) and 97 vitest.

**Left as it is:**
- **The backlog:** about 3,000 claim-named entities are waiting, about a week at 20 an hour.
- **Wikidata statements** (employer, member of, located in) as checks on relationship proposals, and a "Research this" button (§11.7).

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10)
content: Source: the user, after merging aliases. "Waterford" is filed as an organisation; it is a municipality in Michigan, a township the user worked in, named in the résumé. "China" is filed as a location; a country is more accurate. And when researching a knowledge gap, should the brain start with Wikipedia, "the first step that leads you to the next logical step"? Should it have a dictionary?

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10) › 12.1 What the graph shows (measured 2026-10-10, nothing written)
content:
**Why the two examples are wrong:**
- **China is a location because we said so.** `entities/aliases.yaml` folds `country: location`. Phase 18 already linked it (proposed) to Q148, "country in East Asia", kinds `sovereign state`. The right answer is in the graph; nothing reads it back into the type. Votes: location 59, organisation 8.
- **Waterford** is mentioned by two résumé notes ("RCS Technology of Michigan LLC (Waterford, …"). Both mentions predate `MENTIONS.type`, so there is no vote to outvote the first extraction, which read a place inside a company's address as an organisation. It is private, so the background lookup skips it, correctly. An on-demand "Look up" already gives the picker the note text (`services/wiki.rs`, "on demand, whatever mentions it").
- **There is no way to set a type by hand.** The drawer can merge, hide, relate and link an entity, not retype it.

**The vocabulary is flat and its two largest buckets are not things:**

| Type | Entities | Note |
|---|---|---|
| concept | 3,333 | 2,138 have one mention. A sample of 50 is mostly phrases ("missed opportunity in policy messaging", "national security implications", "signs of affection in cats"), with demonyms ("ukrainian", 28 mentions) and some real things (GDPR, right to repair, KV cache) |
| url | 2,248 | 1,351 have one mention |
| organisation | 1,218 | |
| person | 994 | |
| technology | 732 | |
| date | 576 | "july 29, 2026", "news-2026-09-11", a timestamp |
| location | 427 | |
| others | ~460 | including 22 `Concept` and 9 `API` from before types were lowercased |

**Kinds from Wikidata (the 228 linked entities, proposed or confirmed).** Each WikiItem's instance-of (P31) classes were walked up subclass-of (P279) to a 25-kind root table (`scratchpad/kinds_dryrun2.py`, `nearest.py`).
- **Labels can't be mapped one by one:** 214 distinct P31 labels for 228 entities.
- **List-order matching over P279\* is wrong in systematic ways.** With a broad `occurrence` root, YouTube, TikTok, GPS, Meshtastic and Reticulum came out as **events**; with "state" under country, all 9 U.S. states came out as **countries**. Wikidata's upper ontology is tangled.
- **Nearest root wins** (fewest P279 hops; ties by table order) fixed the 9 states, Moscow, New Orleans, NATO, the Air Force, GRU, the GOP convention (→ event) and flydubai (→ organisation), and made 2 worse (WSJ and NYT → website, a same-hop tie). It needs ~1,550 class fetches for these 228 items (7 hops), about 35 serialised requests; cached, later items cost little.
- **Result (nearest root):** the derived coarse type agrees with the filed one for **174**, disagrees for **26**, and gives nothing for **28**.

**The disagreements, graded by hand** (the 23 of the list-order run; the nearest-root run's 26 are the same causes plus the walk's own moves):

| Cause | Examples | Count |
|---|---|---|
| The reference is right, the filed type wrong | palestinian state → country; cold war → event; obama/biden administration → government; USS Abraham Lincoln, Mayflower → vessel; Eyes Wide Shut → film | ~7 |
| Arguable either way | TikTok, YouTube (organisation vs website); Denuvo, GPS, GLP-1, Nasdaq Composite | ~6 |
| **The link is wrong**, so the kind is | "united kingdom" → the UK government; "chinese" → the PLA; "trump administration" → a *set index article*; "cuomo full show"; "lg tvs" → LG Electronics; sx1262 → an unlabelled item | 6 |
| Demonym linked to its country | british → UK, italian → Italy | 2 |
| Ontology noise | "chinese government" → country | 1–2 |

So a disagreement is a **question**, never an automatic retype: a quarter of them come from wrong links.

**The 28 with no kind** are mostly *classes*, not named things: voting machine, mRNA, UFOs, agentic AI, ransomware, large language model, reinforcement learning, logic. Eight have no P31 at all (the item *is* a kind of thing). That answers half the dictionary question: Wikidata already says whether a name is a common noun.

**Demonyms.** Wikidata's English demonyms (P1549) of countries and U.S. states: 369. Matched against entity names, **~48 entities are demonyms** (51 matches minus 3 where the demonym is the country's own name: Taiwan, New Zealand, Philippines), 228 mentions. The same word gets every type: chinese (27, location), american (20, concept), iranian (18, location), british (7, organisation), syrians (5, person). "ukrainian" (28) wasn't matched, so Wikidata's list is incomplete and needs a curated file. Phase 18's known bad picks are demonyms ("Chinese" → PLA, "Italian" → Italy).

**Wikipedia for knowledge gaps.** 942 gap tasks so far, ~20 a day. The question text as a Wikipedia search query fails: of 20 recent gaps, **7 returned nothing** and roughly **5 had a relevant top hit** (Synthetic biology; Regulation of AI / China–US relations; Terminal ballistics; 2020s energy crisis). The rest hit noise ("Hormuz … hunger" → Election denial movement; "Edmond de Rothschild and the DOJ" → Balfour Declaration). Graded loosely, about 12 of the 20 have a background article that would help (Strait of Hormuz, Edmond de Rothschild, John Curtis, Supreme Court independence, Hawaii's military role…); about 2 have the specific answer. So Wikipedia is the background step, the search terms must be the question's *subjects*, not the question, and the web search stays.

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10) › 12.2 Phase 19: types you can trust
content:
- **Two levels.** `entity_type` stays the coarse class the extractor gives (person, organisation, location, …), which the local model does reliably. A new `kind` holds the fine one: country, state or province, county, municipality, region, government agency, military, company, news outlet, political party, vessel, film or book, war or battle, … The `country: location` fold stays (it keeps the coarse vocabulary closed); `kind` carries "country".
- **`entities/kinds.yaml`:** each kind, its coarse type and its Wikidata root classes. A new kind is a YAML edit, not code.
- **Where the kind comes from**, in this order, the first that answers wins:
  1. **set by the user** (`type_source: manual`), final, like topic locks;
  2. a **confirmed** reference link;
  3. a **proposed** reference link, but only when its coarse type agrees with the filed one, so it refines and never changes the type;
  4. otherwise no kind; the type is the extraction vote.
- **Disagreement is a question in the Feed** ("Filed as organisation; its reference says municipality"), answered by Keep / Use the reference / Choose. The answer is stored as `type_source: manual`, and a "keep" is never asked again for that link.
- **The walk** (`services/wiki.rs`): WikiItem gains `class_qids` (the P31 ids, fetched already and thrown away today). `(:WikiClass {qid, label, parents, fetched_at})` caches each class's P279 parents, up to 7 hops, through the same Wikimedia gate; nearest root wins.
- **Items that are not things are refused as links:** a Wikimedia disambiguation page, set index or list article never becomes a proposal ("trump administration" → a set index article). An item with no P31 shows "a kind of thing" in the Reference block.
- **Manual edit in the drawer:** type and kind, with "let the brain decide" to unlock. `PUT /api/entities/{id}/type`.
- **Backfill:** the 228 linked entities at once, then each new link as `link_entities` writes it.

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10) › 12.3 Phase 20: demonyms
content:
- **`entities/demonyms.yaml`:** demonym → canonical place (`chinese: china`, `americans: united states`), generated once from Wikidata P1549, minus the entries equal to the place's name, then reviewed by hand and completed (ukrainian). Curated data in YAML, per the no-hardcoded-data rule.
- **Extraction resolves a demonym to its place,** keeping the surface form on `MENTIONS.surface` ("Chinese hackers" mentions China). This is resolution, so it goes through `entity_resolution.rs` like an alias.
- **The ~48 existing demonym entities become merge candidates** with reason `demonym` through the existing reversible merge (proposals; the user decides), and `link_entities` never looks up a demonym.
- **Not every use is a nationality:** "Chinese" is also a language and "American" an airline in some notes. The candidates list shows the notes, and a "different" answer is remembered (`NOT_SAME`), as for any pair.

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10) › 12.4 Phase 21: Wikipedia first for knowledge gaps
content:
- **A new first web step in `chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml`:** `wiki_background {question}`.
  1. The model names 1–3 **subjects** of the question (Strait of Hormuz, not the question).
  2. Each is searched on Wikipedia and the article picked from the candidates, the Phase 18 way (picked, never the top result; 0 allowed).
  3. The tool returns each article's lead, the section that best matches the question, and the domains of its cited sources.
  4. It banks as `## BACKGROUND (Wikipedia)` in `gap-{{task_id}}`.
- **The next step follows from it:** the web search's query adds the article's terms, and the article's cited domains are offered as preferred sources (`include_domains` on engines that read it). That is the "first step that leads to the next".
- **Nothing found is fine:** the step reports "no article for X" and the chain goes on to the web, as now.
- **Privacy:** gap tasks come from videos and news. The tool refuses a task whose `data_class` is private.
- **Etiquette:** the Phase 18 gate. ~20 gaps a day × ~4 calls is nothing.
- **Measured before it is switched on:** replay 15 past gap tasks with and without the step (the same model), and grade the `## ANSWER`s by hand on correctness, citations and specificity. Ship only if it is not worse anywhere and better somewhere; record the numbers here.

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10) › 12.5 Not in this round
content:
- **The concept and url/date piles.** 2,138 one-mention concepts are mostly phrases, and urls and dates as entities are a decision of their own (they are in the extraction vocabulary on purpose). A later phase: measure what retrieval loses if they go, with `eval-retrieval`, before touching them.
- **A general dictionary** (WordNet, Wiktionary). Wikidata already separates named things from kinds of things (12.1), and demonyms are the measured gap. Revisit if the concept clean-up needs it.
- **Gemma or nimble as typers.** The kind is derived, not judged, and the link itself is already picked by the cloud model (18 of 20 right). Neither local model was measured as a typer, and Phase 17 showed E4B can't make this kind of choice.

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10) › 12.6 Phases
content:
| Phase | Scope | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **19. Types you can trust** | §12.2: `kind`, `entities/kinds.yaml`, `class_qids` + `WikiClass`, nearest-root walk, precedence, Feed type questions, manual edit, refuse disambiguation/set-index items, backfill. | Waterford can be set to location / municipality by hand and stays; China shows kind country; the 9 U.S. states show state or province; "trump administration"'s set-index link is refused on re-lookup; the 26 disagreements appear as questions and no type changes without an answer; measured kinds on a fresh held-out set of linked entities are recorded here. |
| **20. Demonyms** | §12.3: `entities/demonyms.yaml`, resolution at extraction, `demonym` merge candidates, no lookups for demonyms. | A new note saying "Chinese hackers" mentions China with surface "chinese"; the existing demonym entities are candidates, merges reversible; `eval-retrieval` before and after recorded here. |
| **21. Wikipedia first** | §12.4: `wiki_background`, the gap chain's new step, cited domains as preferred sources. | The 15-gap replay is graded and recorded here, and the step is on only if it passed. |

title: 12. Fifth round: Phases 19–21, what an entity is (planned 2026-10-10) › 12.7 Decisions (taken 2026-10-10: every recommendation accepted)
content:
1. **Kind from a proposed link that agrees:** apply it (recommended; 174 of 228 agree, and it never changes the coarse type), or wait for confirmation (5 of 228 are confirmed today)?
2. **Demonyms:** resolve to the place (recommended), or keep them as their own entities with kind `nationality`?
