pseudo-tool added to the orchestrator when `SUBAGENT_ENABLED` is set, intercepted
in `run_ollama_cloud_loop` (the current gpt-oss chat path) and run as a nested,
read-only worker via `ChatService::run_subagent`; a curated hardcoded roster
(`SPAWNABLE_PROFILES`); depth cap 1 (sub-agents get no `delegate`); progress
forwarded to the user, final prose captured and folded back as the tool result.
Guard tests: `general` is never spawnable; the tool contract is `agent`+`task`.

**Measured 2026-09-06 (two turns, "What have we learned today?"):**
- gpt-oss orchestrator (design B): **0 delegations** — it looped its own
  `search_notes` to the 10-round budget. Design B rejected.
- gemma orchestrator (design A, `contexts/orchestrator.yaml`): **delegated on
  its first call** (gemma×3 + gpt-oss×11 = 14 calls). Delegation works; the
  worker (gpt-oss) then looped `search_notes` to *its* budget and summarised
  unrelated notes — the sub-agent cap, not the plumbing, was the problem.

**Phase 1 progress:**
- ✅ **Sub-agent iteration cap** — `MAX_SUBAGENT_ITERATIONS` (3) is threaded
  through all four provider loops via a `max_iterations` param; `run_one_attempt`
  passes `MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS`, `run_subagent` passes `MAX_SUBAGENT_ITERATIONS`.
  Validated 2026-09-07: the delegated worker hit `rounds:3` (vs 11 before), turn
  calls 14→7, latency 20s→11s. Guard: `subagent_budget_is_tighter_than_the_orchestrator`.
- ✅ **`search_notes` empty-query hardening** — an empty/whitespace `entity_name`
  is now treated as absent (mirrors the existing empty-`query` guard), so a
  worker looping `search_notes` with `entity_name: ""` gets a clear "supply a
  real query" error instead of noise it reads as success and loops on. Guards:
  `search_notes_empty_entity_name_is_not_searched`,
  `empty_entity_name_with_a_real_query_falls_through_to_query` (`skills/knowledge.rs`).

- ✅ **Structured findings** — `run_subagent` no longer returns bare prose. It
  collects the worker's successful tool-result previews, and `format_subagent_findings`
  wraps the answer with a relay instruction (cite sources, pass along stated
  limitations, add no facts) plus a `SOURCES:` list of URLs lifted straight from
  the worker's tool outputs via `extract_sources` (the worker's prose can drop
  links; its tool results can't). Guards: `extract_sources_*`, `findings_*`.
  Note: this delivers `answer` + `sources`; a first-class `gaps` array is still
  carried as prose in the answer, not a separate field.

- ✅ **Grounding-flag propagation** — `run_subagent` now also reports whether the
  worker ran ≥1 successful tool (`retrieved`); the dispatcher calls
  `TurnWriteGuard::mark_retrieval()` on a retrieving delegate, so a `semantic`
  note the orchestrator writes afterward is no longer wrongly downgraded to
  `unsourced_synthesis`. Guard: `a_delegate_retrieval_grounds_a_semantic_note`.
- ✅ **All-loop interception** — the delegate interception + grounding was
  extracted into one `ChatService::dispatch_tool_call` that **all four** provider
  loops route through (replacing their direct `execute_guarded` calls). Each
  loop gained an `allow_delegate` param; `run_one_attempt` passes `true`,
  `run_subagent` passes `false` (depth cap 1). Delegation now works whichever
  provider the orchestrator runs on, and the interception is defined once rather
  than copied per loop — closing the "handled in one path, not the other" risk.
- ✅ **Sub-agent cap 3→6 + `note_type` hardening** — a 2026-09-07 orchestrator
  turn ("the latest on Our Niche Intelligence Agency") wrongly answered "no
  information" where `general` succeeded. Root cause was a THIRD empty-arg-as-
  filter bug: the worker passed `note_type: ""`, which `search_notes` treated as
  *filter for type ""* → zero results → false negative. Fixed systematically:
  `serde_flex::empty_string_as_none` normalizes empty/whitespace optional filter
  args to `None` at the **deserialization boundary**, applied to every
  `search_notes` filter (`query`/`entity_name`/`entity_type`/`note_type`) and the
  `search_web` filters (`engine`/`source_list`) — so a new filter field is
  covered by adding the attribute, not by remembering a per-handler guard (this
  was the third reactive patch of the same bug class). Ancillary: the sub-agent
  cap was raised 3→6 (the old junk-loop reason
  was already hardened away, and 3 starved query refinement) and the
  `researcher`/`knowledge-worker` prompts nudged to strip possessives, prefer
  `query` over `entity_name`, and not conclude "not found" from one miss. Guard:
  `empty_note_type_is_not_treated_as_a_filter`.

title: Sub-Agent Orchestration in Chat — Design Proposal (part 2/2)
content:
**Phases 1 and 2 are complete.** The gemma-orchestrator design is validated, the
primitive is hardened (bounded, grounded, structured, provider-agnostic), and the
worker roster is data-driven (`spawnable`/`specialty` profile fields — no
hardcoded list). What remains is forward work: Phase 3 (streaming/episodic-note
polish) and Phase 4 (re-express the worker/voice split on `delegate`).

It also folds in the broader question the work raised — "how agents are put
together and get used" — by formalising **agent = context profile** and giving
the orchestrator a way to see and call the roster of agents that exist.

Read `project-docs/architecture_context.md` and the chat sections of `CLAUDE.md`
(worker/voice split, write guard, fallback ladder, Context Profiles) before
implementing; this design is constrained by hard-won behaviour in those.

---

title: Architecture: subsystem rules
content: > Each subsystem below is stated as its **operative rules only**. The full narrative — root causes, measurements, and the failures that motivated each rule — lives verbatim in **`project-docs/engineering-history.md`** (§ *Architecture & subsystem deep-dives*). Read the matching section there before changing one of these; nearly every rule marks a failure mode the codebase re-learns whenever the reasoning is dropped.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › ACLED conflict data (`acled_events`)
content:
The `osint-data` plugin (`plugins/osint-data/crate/src/client.rs` + `skill.rs`, moved out of `app` in Phase 3c; `dev_docs get plugins/api`); its bundle requires `ACLED_EMAIL`/`ACLED_PASSWORD`, so without them the plugin is skipped and `acled_events` is not registered. **Parked 2026-10-06**: the user's account is Open tier (no API), and Research access needs an organisation; the tool is in no agent's allowlist until that changes. Returns counts by country / event type / sub-type / admin1 / actor / week, a newest-first sample (≤50, notes clipped to 300 chars), `complete:false` + a TRUNCATED note when the row limit (default 500, max 2000) is hit, a "data lags ~a week" note when the window reaches the last 10 days, and on zero rows the six valid event types and the spelling rule.

- **★ Query live; never store ACLED rows in the graph.** ACLED's EULA §7.1 forbids using its content to train, test, develop or improve an AI system in a way that substitutes for ACLED, lets third parties retrieve its content, or exceeds the licence; §3.1 allows published derivatives only when transformative ("not sufficient … to simply be supplemented, appended, excerpted, reorganized"). So: no mirror, no ingest of rows as notes, analysis stored with the attribution line, and **ACLED-derived material never enters a fine-tuning set**. The brain's MCP port is unauthenticated on all interfaces; keep it off the internet, or ACLED content becomes third-party-retrievable.
- Auth is a password grant, not a key — `http_request`/`:ApiContext` cannot do it, hence the native client. Tokens are cached; a 401 re-logs in once.
- **★ API access depends on the account's tier, which ACLED assigns by email domain.** A generic address (gmail.com) gets **Open**: login succeeds, but every read returns `403 {"message":"Access denied"}`, identical to an unauthenticated read. **Research** and above include the API, and Research event data lags **12 months**, so the default 30-day window would come back empty there. Upgrading is by contacting ACLED. The tool's 403 message names this. (Verified 2026-10-06 against the user's Open account.)
- A `$` in an `.env` value is expanded by Compose: single-quote the password (`ACLED_PASSWORD='…'`). ACLED's Cloudflare blocks some default User-Agents (error 1010), so the client sends `agent-brain/<version>`.



`(:SourceList {name, domains, description})` restrict `search_web` to approved domains (`site:` + post-filter). Defined in `sources/*.yaml`, seeded **ON CREATE only** (graph-owned after; delete a node to re-seed; runtime edits persist). An unresolved name degrades to unrestricted search. Built-ins: `news`, `michigan-news`, `ml-research`. Full detail: history § SourceLists.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Adversarial Critic (pre-flight plan review)
content: **Opt-in per workflow (2026-10-10):** a workflow with `checks: [critic]` gets an `adversarial_plan_review` step **prepended** at dispatch (`dispatch_run` → `maybe_prepend_adversarial`), judged against the workflow's `evaluation_rubric`, else the run Task's `success_criteria`. In the 60 days before Phase 2b it never ran, and no migrated workflow opts in. `overall_robustness < min_robustness` (default 2.5) → cancel downstream + `handle_adversarial_requeue()` (mark failed, start a new run of the same workflow with the same inputs, critique in `context`). **Abort cap 3** (`"ADVERSARIAL ABORT"`). Skipped when: the workflow doesn't opt in, there is no rubric or `success_criteria`, or the context already has `"ADVERSARIAL ABORT"`. `ChainStep`: `is_adversarial`/`n_hypotheses`/`min_robustness`/`adversarial_task_id`. `parse_adversarial_robustness()` defaults 3.0. Also callable directly (KnowledgeSkill); each run stores a `semantic` note `source_context: "adversarial_review"`. Full story: history § Adversarial Critic.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Chat context dock (`hbi-frontend/src/lib/chatDock.ts`, 2026-10-08)
content:
- **The dock is derived from the turn's events, never asked of the model.** What ran is the `tool_call` / `tool_result` stream, paired in order. What the turn wrote is the ids in the results of tools that write (`WRITE_VERB` in `chatDock.ts`, or `manage_*` with a writing `action`). What it read is the ids in the rest. A link in the answer is checked against the text every tool returned or was sent this turn. A new writing tool with a different verb belongs in `WRITE_VERB`, or its ids show under Read.
- **Ids resolve in one call:** `POST /api/lookup` (`clients/search.rs`) takes up to 60 full ids or 8+ character hex prefixes. A prefix resolves only when exactly one node has it, and everything unresolved comes back in `missing`, so a cited id that names nothing is shown, not dropped.
- **A chat that names no profile gets the front door.** The HBI sends `context_profile` only when the user picks an agent; `/api/contexts` reports `default_profile` (`CHAT_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, or `null` when the server picks per message). Never default the picker to a profile name: that silently bypasses the deployment's router.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Context Profiles (part 1/2)
content: YAML in `contexts/` define tool allowlists + system prompts per persona; `boot.yaml` runs every startup, `init.yaml` on empty graph; `auto_assign(goal)` keyword-matches. **A profile applies four layers to a chat turn**: `tools` allowlist filters the registry, `system_prompt` appended after the base, `pre_load_query` output appended under `LIVE SELF-STATE` (all three via `build_system_prompt`), and **`model_preference` (+ optional `provider_hint`) overrides the chat model for that turn** (`ChatService::resolve_profile_model` in `clients/chat/turn.rs`). The model is resolved against the DuckDB catalog (exact key/model match → substring for legacy aliases like `sonnet`/`haiku` → `provider_hint` for a non-catalog model), and credentials/endpoint come from the env via `config_for_catalog_entry`, so the checked-in YAML never carries a key; the chat fallback ladder still applies on top (an unreachable pin — e.g. an Anthropic model with no key — falls down it). An unresolvable/blank preference keeps the chat default. **This is honored ONLY on the human `/chat` path, not background jobs** (those use capability routing / `provider_hint`). **Every model a profile turn may use is judged by the routing policy** (`services/routing.rs`), by the profile's **`data_class`** (absent ⇒ `private`, which admits only `no_log` providers — or a provider whose `private_ok_for` in `models.yaml` names the purpose: the owner's per-provider override, kept apart from `data_policy`. `gemini` carries `private_ok_for: [chat]` since 2026-09-26, so a private chat profile may pin it; background and sub-agent private work still cannot). On `/chat` a refused pin is announced in the stream (`⚙ profile model … refused`) and the turn keeps the chat default; every ladder rung and the synthesis model are judged too, and with no admitted rung the turn fails loudly. **A sub-agent (`AgentRunner::run`, i.e. `run_agent`/`delegate`) runs as `purpose: subagent` with the stricter of its caller's and its profile's class**, which refuses paid providers unless `ROUTING_PAID_FOR` names `subagent`, and refuses providers whose declared limits cannot carry a multi-round loop (rpm < 20 or rpd < 500: the Gemini 5-RPM trap, OpenRouter's 50/day). This replaced the provider-type clamp (2026-09-15). **The front door `GeneralDefault-Orchrestator` is on `gemma4:31b-cloud` → `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` → `gemini-2.5-flash` (`fallback_models`), `data_class: private` (2026-10-05, ending a Claude Sonnet pin: paid Sonnet is kept for tasks marked hard, and routing does not need it; from 10-02 it was gpt-oss first).** A Gemini 3.x trial (09-26..10-01) failed 7 of 14 chat calls, all 503s, while `gpt-oss` failed 0 of 79 calls across chat, sub-agents and reasoning. Before that it was on `gemma4:31b-cloud` (09-26). It ran on `gemini-2.5-flash` as `public` from 09-15; on 09-24 Gemini answered three turns from memory with zero tool calls and cited note ids that do not exist, where gemma4 had delegated every question. `researcher` is private. (`api-scout` was the one public worker; it was folded into `api-integrator` on 2026-10-16, so the weekly scout now runs private.) A save lays its body over the stored profile (`profiles::overlay`), so a UI edit cannot silently flip a profile private or drop a field the form does not know (`dev_docs get profiles/graph`). **Routing a sub-agent to the local llama.cpp e4b sidecar** (2026-09-10) needed three changes, not just the clamp: `config_for_catalog_entry` gained a `llamacpp` branch (→ `LlmProviderType::LlamaCpp` @ `LLAMACPP_URL`, embeddings pinned to host Ollama — before this every non-cloud provider collapsed to host Ollama at `OLLAMA_LOCAL_URL`, so a pin could never reach the sidecar); the loop dispatch (`run_one_attempt`) routes `LlamaCpp` to `run_openai_loop` (the OpenAI-wire, tool-call-accumulating adapter; since Phase 6a the only text-wire adapter, the `<tool_call>` text loop is gone); and a `gemma4-e4b` catalog entry (`models.yaml`, provider `llamacpp`) exists so a profile can resolve the pin. **VERIFIED 2026-09-11 — Gemma-4-E4B drives multi-round tool loops in production.** `knowledge-worker` is pinned to it (`model_preference: gemma4-e4b`, `provider_hint: llamacpp`) and runs 7-9 round loops with zero errors (`tokens_in` climbing 3.8k→8.0k, `tokens_out` dipping to 23-24, which is a compact tool-call emission). `contexts/knowledge-local.yaml` was never created; `scripts/probe_e4b_subagent.py` targets it and so has never run — the production ledger is the evidence instead. Peak observed `tokens_in` is 7959, **49% of the sidecar's 16384/request budget** (`-c 32768 -np 2`), which is the real ceiling on moving context-hungry workers (`researcher`, `code-analyst`) local. A **bare `provider_hint` with no `model_preference` is inert** (the resolver is only reached via `model_preference`), so a sub-agent profile that wants local must set `model_preference`, not just the hint. The `:ContextProfile` `model_preference`/`provider_hint` are also mirrored to the meta-graph and echoed by `/api/models` + the frontend "🤖 Agents" modal, which writes them via `/api/contexts`. **`pre_load_query` accepts Cypher or a keyword** — read-only Cypher runs verbatim (`is_read_cypher()` rejects any write token); a failing query warns and continues. `contexts/self-analyst.yaml` is the self-inspection persona (injects `:ModelDef`/`:Workflow`/`:ToolDef` live state; enforces MEASURE→LOCATE→COMPARE→PROPOSE). The old 31-tool `general.yaml` was retired on 2026-10-16 (`dev_docs search "profile consolidation"`).

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Context Profiles (part 2/2)
content:
**★ The front door (`CHAT_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, 2026-09-11).** The chat default is env-selected via `default_profile_name()` (`services/context_builder.rs`), not a code constant; `contexts/general-default-orchestrator.yaml` (`GeneralDefault-Orchrestator`, pinned to local `gemma4-e4b`) is what compose points it at. Four load-bearing rules:
- **When `CHAT_DEFAULT_PROFILE` is set, the chat path SKIPS `auto_assign`.** Keyword routing and roster delegation are two routers, and `auto_assign` runs first, so the dumber one always wins: on 2026-09-11 "What did we learn today?" scored `knowledge-worker`, ran it as the *persona*, answered off its own `recall_recent`, and never reached the orchestrator. The front door IS the router — it reads the live roster and picks with `delegate`. An explicit request `context_profile` and the `jobsearch-` session pin both still win; set the var empty to restore `auto_assign`.
- **The front door is a router, so it has routing misses of its own — and they cost a whole turn while recording `success: true` on every row.** Measured 2026-09-11/12: "what did we learn recently" and "how many agents do we have" both went to `researcher` (a WEB profile holding no `recall_recent`, no `neo4j_query`, no `describe_graph`), which burned all 8 rounds and reported absence — the 2026-09-08 delegated-recall false negative recurring one layer up, now caused by the orchestrator's choice rather than `auto_assign`. Anything about the brain's own tools, agents, schedules, tasks, or stored notes goes to `knowledge-worker`; `ABOUT THE BRAIN ITSELF` in the front-door prompt says so in four lines. Also note `run_agent(agent:"auto")` is a **token-overlap** matcher: "how many **agents**" matches `researcher` on the word alone, so a meta-question must never be left to auto-select.
- **The default profile is excluded from `auto_assign` candidates** (it is the fallback; matching it explicitly would shadow a real specialist), and `delete_profile` protects it. With `CHAT_DEFAULT_PROFILE` unset the code falls back to `GeneralDefault-Orchrestator` (it was `general` until that profile was retired, 2026-10-16). **A chat that names a profile that does not exist runs as the default** (`turn.rs`, with a `⚙ agent … does not exist` thinking line); before 2026-10-16 it got every tool and no system prompt.
- **`delegate` is chat-loop only and is NEVER in the MCP tool registry.** A profile used for `MCP_TOOL_PROFILE` must therefore include **`run_agent`** (the registered equivalent) or an MCP client gets the allowlist with no dispatch path at all — strictly worse than the full registry. Both vars point at the front door, so a connecting client sees 7 tools instead of ~42.
- **★ A front-door prompt is a SIZE BUDGET on a small local model.** Same model, same tools, same question: at 2332 chars E4B delegates; at 6801 it emits prose and refuses. The added bytes were `general.yaml`'s ABSENCE / TOOL-RESULT / CITATION rules — all of which say *don't overclaim* — and a 4B model over-applies them into the exact "I cannot determine this" they exist to prevent. Those rules are persuasive narratives written for a large model. Keep a local profile's prompt near 2-3k chars (the front door is at 4.0k after the `ABOUT THE BRAIN ITSELF` rule and still delegates — re-measure if it grows again), write rules as terse imperatives, and include an explicit floor ("When in doubt, DELEGATE; never answer 'I cannot determine this' without having called delegate at least once this turn"). Narrative rationale belongs in history, never in a local model's prompt.

Full detail: history § Context Profiles.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Curiosity engine (`workflows/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml`) (part 1/2)
content:
Gaps are runs of `workflows/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml` with input `topic`. They come from `spawn_gap_tasks` (a video's `## FOLLOW UP`), gap detection in `services/knowledge/reasoning.rs`, and the workflows that call `create_task` with `workflow: fill-knowledge-gap` (news-analysis, tech-dependency-synthesis, brain-exercise). **A gap task must make sense without its source (2026-10-01).** A gap run searches the graph and the web with no access to the video it came from, so `spawn_gap_tasks` drops follow-ups that point back into it (`is_standalone_gap`: `(Context:`, `(Inferred)`, "the final scene", "this practice", "the speaker", …; under four words), the video-learning prompt asks for at most two general topics a year-from-now reader would want ("NONE" allowed, no sports), and `GAP_TASKS_DAILY_MAX` (20) caps the day. Before this ~30 gaps/day were mostly trivia ("the subtle wave from the daughter in the final scene"), and their answers fed consolidation. The workflow searches **both** graph (`search_notes`) and web (`search_web`) — a gap is by definition what the graph lacks — banks into `gap-{{task_id}}`, reassembles, answers under `## ANSWER` (cited) / `## WHAT THIS ADDS` / `## STILL UNKNOWN`. Search steps use `{{inputs.topic}}` (before 2026-10-10 a regex on the goal routed gap tasks, and `learn.yaml` kept stealing them; naming the workflow ended that). Full story: history § Curiosity engine.
- **A gap is a question a few searches can settle, not an essay prompt (2026-10-03).** Asking for "general topics worth knowing a year from now" swapped trivia for "What are the long-term implications of…", which no search answers. The video FOLLOW UP and news Open Questions prompts now ask for what/how/who/when/how-much questions naming the concrete thing, and `is_standalone_gap` drops essay markers (`implications`, `how might`, `intersect`, …). Answers are capped: ≤5 cited fact bullets.
- **A distilled handoff must fit the distiller's window, or its middle vanishes unmarked** (2026-10-10). `maybe_distill_prev` reads at most 24,000 characters, the first 16,000 and the last 8,000. The gap chain's ALREADY KNOWN section ran to 20,500 characters at the median (67,000 max), so 73 of 143 runs silently lost a median 9,000 characters of stored notes. The reassembly step now caps that section at 15,000 characters with a "stored notes cut here: N more characters" marker. The web section never exceeded 7,412, so the whole handoff stays inside the window (verified on the three largest: 21–23k). It is the only distilling step that overflowed. A new one that reassembles working memory needs the same cap.
- **"Found nothing" is not knowledge.** Research steps write a leading `NO FINDINGS — …` line when the evidence does not answer; `store_note` (`is_null_result`, `skills/knowledge.rs`) stores such a `semantic`/untyped note as **`episodic`**, also catching a short note whose first paragraph opens "The provided context does not contain…". Consolidation reads semantic notes only, so before this it merged empty results as findings: 4 of the 8 sources of a 2026-10-03 consolidation *about the phrase "knowledge gap"* were such notes. 104 existing ones re-typed by `scripts/retype_null_result_notes.cypher` (reversible via `retyped_from`).
- **Self-directed work drills down: `workflows/deep-dive-pick.yaml` → `workflows/deep-dive.yaml` → `contexts/deep-diver.yaml`.** Every 2 days a `reason` step (on gpt-oss: local E4B restated a todo as "How should a Vault be built?" instead of narrowing it) reads open todos, technologies recurring in recent notes, recent research topics and each prior deep dive's `## NEXT` question, and narrows ONE theme to ONE specific question (a technical theme becomes "how does it work / how to build it in Rust for agent-brain"). It starts a `deep-dive` run with that `question` as input, which runs the `deep-diver` agent (gpt-oss, `max_rounds: 16`): graph → web → **read the primary source** (spec, RFC, the reference implementation's raw file) → a minimal Rust example run in `rust-sandbox` **with tests asserting against the source's test vector or an independently computed output** → `file:line` placement in code and `project-docs/`, answered as ANSWER / RUST / IN AGENT-BRAIN / NEXT, every fact tied to a page read that run. **Compiling proves the code runs, not that it is right:** the first test run (Reticulum destination hash, 2026-10-03) shipped a correct hand-written SHA-256 inside the wrong formula — `SHA256(pubkey ‖ app_name)` instead of RNS's `SHA256(name_hash[10] ‖ identity_hash[16])[:16]` — cited to a blog it did not list; that note was re-typed `unsourced_synthesis`. **The re-run then copied that note** — `search_notes` returned it, the agent cited `note:7d75fff5` for every bullet and never read a page — so two prompt rules had been ignored, and both are now enforced in code:
  - **`retrieval_exclude:` on a profile** (`RetrievalExclude`, `services/knowledge/mod.rs`) is scoped as the `RETRIEVAL_EXCLUDE` task-local around the agent's loop in `AgentRunner::run`, and `search_notes_inner` drops matching notes (step 4.77, fails open). `deep-diver` excludes `unsourced_synthesis`/`inference`/`reflection` and `source_context: deep_dive` — the brain's own uncited answers are never shown to it as evidence.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Curiosity engine (`workflows/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml`) (part 2/2)
content:
- **`run_agent`'s `verify`** (`require_tools`, `code_requires_tests`) is checked against the real tool trace after the run (`verification_failures`). `ToolInvocation.tests_passed` is read from the `execute_code` result itself (`passing_tests`: built, ≥1 passed, 0 failed), never from prose. An unmet requirement prefixes the answer `UNVERIFIED — …`, and `store_note` stores a marked `semantic`/untyped note as `unsourced_synthesis`. `cited_paths_exist` fails any `path:line` that is not a file in `CODEBASE_DIR` with that many lines (a path without a line may name a new file; URLs are skipped) — a third run invented `crates/app/src/reticulum.rs:12` and a `ReticulumSkill`. `rerun_answer_code` makes the verifier compile, test and clippy the code SHOWN in the answer itself (`answer_rust_code` → `answer_crate`, dependencies copied from `rust-sandbox/crates/Cargo.toml` for every crate the code names → `execute_code` through `AgentRunner::call_tool`), replacing the trace's test/clippy checks: a 2026-10-05 run passed some other test, then showed one with an invented expected hash that its own function could never return. `code_requires_clippy_clean` requires the LAST clippy run in the trace to report zero `lint_findings` (`ToolInvocation.clippy_clean`). The deep-dive chain requires `mcp_call` + passing tests + clean clippy for Rust + real paths; capability mining's grounding step requires `read_codebase_file` + real paths.
  - **A failed answer is corrected, not just prefixed (2026-10-07).** On a verification failure `mark_unverified_answer` writes the `UNVERIFIED — <reason>` line **and** replaces every line outside code blocks that reports a passing run (`test result: ok`, `N passed`) with `Test result: NOT CONFIRMED — …`; a re-run compile failure names the first `error[…]` line (`first_compile_error`). `label_proposed_placement` renames `## IN AGENT-BRAIN` to `## IN AGENT-BRAIN (proposed — nothing was changed)` on every answer, since no agent run edits the repo. `store_note` records `verification: 'failed'` + `verification_reason` on the note and its chunks (`mark_verification_failed`; `update_note` copies it to regenerated chunks), whatever type the caller asked for.
  - **A question that asks for Rust cannot opt out of code** (`verify.question` + `require_code_if_question_mentions: [rust]`, whole-word so "trust" does not count): an answer with no ```rust block fails. A 2026-10-05 Reticulum run wrote "RUST: not applicable", passed every other check, and carried a wrong identity hash a test against a known example would have exposed.
  - **No chain-made first read.** Two attempts (search + model-picked URL; then a GitHub tree lookup) fetched nothing on 2026-10-05 — a search engine with `site:github.com` returns unrelated repos, and the repo picker answered with an essay — while the agent found RNS's own source unaided. Removed rather than tuned.
  - **Sonnet only when a human asks for it: a `deep-dive-hard` run (input `question`, started by name) → `workflows/deep-dive-hard.yaml` → `contexts/deep-diver-hard.yaml` (Claude Sonnet 5).** On the Reticulum question 8 gpt-oss runs all failed (wrong formula, invented test vectors, invented paths) while one Sonnet run read RNS's own source and passed a test against an independently computed hash — for $2.03 before caching. So the paid agent exists, but no workflow or scan starts it. **`explicit_only: true`** on a profile keeps it out of `spawnable_profiles()` (the `delegate` roster and `run_agent(agent:"auto")`), and chat `delegate` refuses it (`AgentBudget.allow_explicit_only`, true only for `run_agent`): an orchestrating model can never choose to spend. Guard: `the_paid_deep_diver_is_explicit_only`.
  - **The spend cap is checked before EVERY paid call** (`paid_cap_refusal` in `clients/chat/round_loop.rs`, via `ProviderTurn::provider_name`). The routing policy admits a model once per turn or agent run; that one admission let the Sonnet run take 16 calls and spend $2.03 against a $1.00 daily cap. Now a run overshoots by at most the call that crosses the cap, then ends with an error the chat ladder hands to the free models.
  - **The Anthropic tool loop caches its prompt** (`clients/chat/anthropic_loop.rs`): `cache_control: ephemeral` on the system prompt (which also covers the tools, rendered before it) and on the last block of the latest message, added to a copy of the history so breakpoints never accumulate. The ledger records **billed-equivalent** input tokens (`billed_input_tokens`: uncached + 1.25× cache writes + 0.1× cache reads; Anthropic's `input_tokens` is the uncached remainder only), so cost and the cap stay right. Each call logs `input`/`cache_write`/`cache_read` at INFO — the only proof caching works; a cache read of 0 on round 2+ means something in the prefix changed.
  - **The rust-sandbox carries crypto crates** (`sha2`, `hmac`, `hkdf`, `ed25519-dalek`, `x25519-dalek`, `hex`, `base64`; 2026-10-05). Without them a protocol question cannot end in a passing test: gpt-oss and gemma4:31b both reached for `sha2` and failed to compile. In a same-task head-to-head gpt-oss got Reticulum's hash structure right and gemma4:31b did not (it was more candid about the compile failure), so `deep-diver` stays on gpt-oss. It replaces `brain-exercise.yaml` (paused): ranking entities by mentions-minus-notes picked the brain's own vocabulary ("knowledge gap", "brain") and source names, and 0 of 9 runs succeeded. **Capability mining** now hands its first candidate to the same agent, which grounds it in real files and a Rust sketch (`source_context: capability_mining_grounded`) — before, every run ended in general advice with no file or code. `run_agent` takes `max_rounds` (default 8, cap 16) for work that must compile, read the error and retry.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Delivering `notify_user` to the UI (`hbi-frontend`)
content: `App.tsx` **owns the notification list** (`src/api/notifications.ts`); badge and banner read the same array. A notification-only POST to `/mcp` must return **`202 Accepted`** (empty body, session-id header) or the SDK never opens its GET SSE stream — every server push went to zero listeners before this. `resetMcpClient()` must not clear `_notifHandlers`. History labels sessions by kind (`sessionLabel()` in `ChatPanel.tsx`, `SESSION_KINDS` synced to `grep -rhoE 'session_id: *"[^"]+"' workflows/`, longest prefix first — **never add a speculative prefix**); renders every role. Full story: history § notify_user UI.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Entity resolution (`services/entity_resolution.rs`, 2026-10-08) (part 1/2)
content:
One real thing is one `:Entity`. Schema: `schema.md` § Entity / EntityAlias. Plan: `HBI_REDESIGN_PLAN.md` §3.1.
- **Extraction resolves before it creates.** `extract_entities` asks for names *as written* (capitals kept) through `generate_json` (`{"entities":[…]}`), then resolves each one: alias by name → entity by name → alias by key → entity by key → create. Never go back to a bare `MERGE (:Entity {name})`; that is what made `us`/`u.s.`/`usa`/`united states` five nodes.
- **The key folds spelling, not meaning.** It lowercases, keeps only letters and digits, drops a leading article, and drops a leading title **only before a full name** (`president donald trump` = `donald trump`). It does **not** fold `senator johnson` into `johnson` or `speaker johnson`, which are different people; that pair becomes a `title` proposal. All-digit keys never fold (`911` ≠ `9/11`). Names in the seed's `keep_distinct` never fold (`the hacker news` ≠ `hacker news`).
- **A case-sensitive alias needs capitals in the text.** `us` resolves to United States only when the note has `US`/`U.S.` as a whole word. Lowercase mentions stay on their own `us` node. Case sensitivity applies to every alias sharing that key (`u.s.` keys to `us` as well). The same regex runs in Rust and in Cypher (`upper_pattern`; no lookaround, because Rust's `regex` has none).
- **Automatic merges are curated or spelling-only.** `init-db` runs `sync` on every start. It seeds the `entities/*.yaml` canonicals and aliases, rewrites keys, and folds same-key entities and alias-named entities, after a `pre_entity_merge` snapshot (a failed snapshot means no merges). Everything else (surnames, acronyms, title + surname, plurals, demonyms) is a **proposal** in the Work inbox and the entity drawer. `agent-brain resolve-entities --dry-run` prints the plan.
- **Demonyms resolve to their place** (`entities/demonyms.yaml`, HBI plan Phase 20). At extraction "Chinese hackers" mentions China: the probe is rewritten to the place before lookup, `MENTIONS.surface` keeps "Chinese", `via` records "chinese", and the vote counts it as a location.
  - **A pair the user answered stops it.** If the demonym entity and its place have `NOT_SAME` or `RELATED_ENTITY`, the word is left as itself; if that can't be read, every demonym is left as itself for that note. Remove the word from the YAML too.
  - **Existing demonym entities are proposals** (reason `demonym`, only when the place entity exists), not seed aliases, so `sync` never folds them on its own: "Chinese" is also a language, "Spanish" and "French" too.
  - **The table is generated, then reviewed.** Wikidata's English demonyms of sovereign states and U.S. states, a word two places share dropped (georgian, dominican, congolese), words that usually mean something else dropped by hand (finn, dane, vatican, persian…), and curated entries where Wikidata has none (ukrainian, saudi). The header lists every drop. The generator is described in the plan's Phase 20 outcome.
  - **Background lookups skip demonyms** (`wiki.rs` `WAITING`, coverage): they gave Phase 18's worst picks. "Look up" in the drawer still runs.
- **Every merge is reversible.** It repoints mentions, stamping `via` (or appending `"<id>:<count>"` to `absorbed` when the note already mentioned the target), keeps the old id, type and created_at on the `EntityAlias`, and deletes the old node. `unmerge` (HBI Undo, `POST /api/entities/aliases/{name}/unmerge`, `resolve-entities --unmerge NAME`) recreates it as `distinct: true`. Mentions other aliases absorbed into the same edge stay put. A distinct entity is never folded again, and the seeder skips a curated alias with its name, but the YAML still lists it, so remove it there too.
- **Candidates carry a local classifier's verdict, which only orders them** (`plugins/alias-judge/crate/src/judge.rs`, HBI plan §11.10). On idle time, `nimble` on host Ollama (`/v1/systemone`, `ALIAS_JUDGE_MODEL`, `off` to stop) reads up to 2 notes mentioning both names and 2 mentioning each alone, and answers same / related / different with a probability for each. That answer is stored as `ALIAS_VERDICT`. Likely-same pairs sort first, then not judged yet, then related, then different.
  - **It never merges.** Hand-graded live, with the measured field order: 32 of 40 tuning pairs and 25 of 28 held-out pairs right. No confident "same" was wrong.
    - Most misses are cautious (Prince William → related, Oppenheimer → different). Its "different" includes "can't tell", and the HBI labels it "not shown to be the same". A fourth "unclear" option was measured and never chosen.
    - Its wrong "same" answers were all under 0.6: "Kushner" ≠ Josh Kushner (0.41) live, and "General Franks" ≠ Dennis Franks (0.59) before the order fix. So a "same" below `CONFIDENT_SAME` (0.7) shows as "leans the same" and sorts with the unjudged.
  - **Field order is part of the prompt.** The answer depends on the order of the options and of the texts. The first deploy built the request with `json!`, whose map is alphabetical, and Mills / Doug Mills went from different (0.81) to same (0.95). The request is built from structs, which serialize in declaration order, and a test pins the order. Keep any other `/v1/systemone` caller the same way.
  - **Use the stored name, not the surface form.** Feeding the names as written (`Senator Collins`, `Tim Scott`) produced three false "same" verdicts.
  - **A new prompt bumps `PROMPT_VERSION`**, so every pair is judged again. Re-measure on the hand-graded pairs (scratchpad scripts are listed in the plan) before shipping the change.
- **A person's "different" or "related" answer is remembered.** These are `NOT_SAME` / `RELATED_ENTITY` edges, and a pair with either is never proposed again. A merged-away id still opens in the drawer as "merged into X" via `EntityAlias.merged_from_id`.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Entity resolution (`services/entity_resolution.rs`, 2026-10-08) (part 2/2)
content:
- **Prune keeps canonicals.** `prune_stale_entities` skips `type_source: seed` and anything with an `ALIAS_OF` pointing at it, and drops aliases left pointing at nothing.
- **The type is a majority vote.** `MENTIONS.type` records each extraction, and the entity takes the most common one (the first note used to fix it forever). A seed canonical's type is fixed.
- **Measure retrieval around a bulk merge.** Entity expansion (`MENTIONS → Entity ← MENTIONS`) feeds retrieval, so a large merge changes what bridges notes. Run `eval-retrieval` before and after, and record the numbers in `engineering-history.md`.

subsystem: Epistemics: claims, source records, retrieval labelling
title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Epistemics: claims, source records, retrieval labelling (part 1/2)
content:
Three note types the brain used to conflate: `semantic` (knowledge the brain established), `source_record` (what an external source *said* — video summaries, `news`), `claim` (one checkable proposition + evidentiary status).
- **`(:Note {note_type:'claim', claim_status, asserted_by, asserted_at})`** with `ASSERTED_IN`/`CORROBORATED_BY`/`CONTRADICTED_BY` edges. Status is **derived** from edges (`recompute_status`), never asserted; verification attaches evidence and recomputes, never edits the claim. Support+contradiction → `disputed`; absence → `unverified` (never refuted).
- **`label_claims` (`services/knowledge/labels.rs`) runs in BOTH retrieval paths** — miss one and the unlabelled copy still reaches context. Prefixes claims `[CLAIM · status · asserted by X · date]` and source records `[SOURCE RECORD — …]`, with a humanised age. `claim`/`source_record` are **excluded from consolidation source selection** (consolidation would launder the status away).
- **Claim kind** (`event`/`attribution`/`mechanism`/`opinion`/`prediction`/`hypothetical`) separates "was asserted" from "is true"; a corroborated `attribution`, `opinion`, `prediction` or `hypothetical` renders "corroborates that it was asserted, not that it is true". **A source's opinion, forecast or hypothetical is kept, labelled and written as its holder's** ("Julian Dorey argues that…"), never stated as fact (owner, 2026-10-14: traceable to who said it is what matters). The verification sweep skips those three kinds (`UNVERIFIABLE_KINDS`): their ASSERTED_IN source already shows who said it, and no search settles an opinion or a forecast. **Extraction never takes a claim about the source itself** (its title, date, "this video explores…"), and **`asserted_by` is the speaker, not the subject**: the intelligence report's "date — CIA — NPR reports that…" lines made the local model write "the CIA reports" (7 flips in 55 intelligence claims; 2 after the rule). Measured 2026-10-14 on 56 sources, old prompt vs the current one, local E4B: claims about the source 8→5, untraceable asserted_by 12→0, opinions labelled 0→29 (about 4 on things that are not opinions: "urged", "demanded"). Not caught: "has 8 GB VRAM" for "needs" (a garbled relation), and the odd remaining speaker/subject flip. Harness: scratchpad claimq/ (run_extract.py rebuilds the prompt from claims.rs). **`classify_domains`** tiers corroborating domains (primary/established/unclassified; role-less SourceLists only) mechanically and rides it in the label; verification is **never gated** on tier, and `state_media` SourceList domains are **labelled only** (`incl. state media (…)` in the tier). **`check_independence`** requires `MIN_INDEPENDENT_DOMAINS` (2) distinct domains **among the results the judge cited** (`sources: [...]` → `resolve_cited_links`), excluding self-referential and `platform` SourceList domains (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube…: citable, never counted — the one gate, on whether a domain is a source at all, not on reputation). **Platforms match on each cited link's host** (`DomainRoles::is_platform_link`), so an entry can name a subdomain: `markets.ft.com` is a company press-release feed, `ft.com` is FT journalism, and both share the registrable domain `ft.com`. Never count uncited results: a LinkedIn post plus four unrelated hits passed the old any-two-results rule. **Syndication counts once** (`check_independence_titled`): cited results whose headlines reduce to the same `story_key` (outlet suffix peeled — a tail of ≤ 4 words after `|`/`-`/`—`/`–`; keys under 4 words never merge) are one story, so independence counts headline-merged groups of domains, not domains. Search APIs do not reliably flag reposts: Webz returned one Al Jazeera article on aljazeera.com and Yahoo News, neither marked syndicated. Edge carries `r.sources` (cited links) + `r.domains` (counted). Does not solve true independence.
- **Echo results are dropped before judging** (`drop_echo_results`): a search-results-page link (also dropped earlier, in `search_web` itself, for every caller), or a title/snippet containing the whole claim (≥ 40 chars), is the query echoed back, not evidence. The evidence note stores the filtered set. Full story: history § Epistemics (2026-10-06).
- **★ Verifier input is EXTERNAL ONLY.** `verify_one` calls `search_web` with `prior_knowledge: false`; a `supports` verdict must cite a result link (`source_is_in_results`, else `support_rejected_unsourced`); `evidence_domains` counts result `link`/`url` fields only, never URLs in body text. Why: from 2026-09-12 the graph-first block fed the judge our own note restating the claim, and corroboration went 41% → 84% (e.g. "My legs!" corroborated by a sleep.com article). Data reset: `scripts/reset_selfcorroborated_claims.cypher`.
- **Newest unverified claims first, and intake below capacity (2026-10-01).** Never-attempted claims go newest-first (then retries by oldest attempt); the sweep verifies 20 per 6h (~80/day) and video learning extracts 3 claims per video, not 5. Before: ~83/day in, ~32/day verified oldest-first, so none of a week's 584 claims had been attempted.
- **Verification needs a cursor** — "no evidence" is a stable state, so `last_verify_attempt_at` is stamped **before** each attempt and selection orders on `COALESCE(last_verify_attempt_at, epoch) ASC`. Every `verify_one` return path names the `claim`, not just its id.
- **`unsourced_synthesis`** (retrieval-labelled, excluded from consolidation) is the type for the brain's own uncited reasoning; migrating a writer does not fix prior writes (`scripts/migrate_unsourced_gap_notes.cypher`). **A data fix and a code fix are separate deliverables.**
- **`verification: 'failed'` outranks the type in retrieval labels.** `label_claims` prefixes such a note `[FAILED VERIFICATION — <reason>. Its test results and code claims are false or unchecked; nothing in it was built, run successfully, or changed in the codebase]` (`failed_verification_label`). An `unsourced_synthesis` note that lists links says "the links it lists were not checked against its claims" instead of "cites no source" — a label the content visibly contradicts gets discounted. Backfill: `scripts/backfill_failed_verification.cypher`.
- **A claim's provenance is `synthesis_inference`** (an LLM extracted it). Until 2026-10-08 `store_claim` wrote `user_input`, the label for something a person stored, and recall shows it to the model. Existing claims: `scripts/fix_claim_provenance.cypher`. Nothing filters on provenance.
- **Every note's provenance is decided by who writes it** (`knowledge::effective_provenance`, 2026-10-08):
  - **`synthesis_inference`:** anything under a `ROUTE_CONTEXT` (a queue job, a chat turn, a sub-agent). It can't claim `user_input` even if a model passes it, because a model chose the words.
  - **`user_input`:** only an outside MCP client's `tools/call` with no route context of its own (`CLIENT_CALL`, set in `mcp/server.rs`), which may pass any value. `POST /api/notes` also writes it, explicitly.
  - **Unscoped brain code** defaults to `synthesis_inference`.

subsystem: Epistemics: claims, source records, retrieval labelling
title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Epistemics: claims, source records, retrieval labelling (part 2/2)
content:
- **`system_record`:** records the code builds, never words anyone chose (`store_episodic_note`: scheduler dispatches, claim evidence, code-version notes).
  - **Recall shows the label** to the model, and reads a missing one as `unrecorded`, never `user_input`.
  - **Why:** `store_note` used to assume `user_input`, and 11,513 machine-written notes said a person wrote them. Data fix: `scripts/fix_note_provenance.cypher`, which keeps the old value in `provenance_was`.
- **A claim must stand alone** (`claims::standalone_problems`, mechanical, so it holds for the local model that does all extraction). Extraction returns `about: [{name, what}]` for each claim, and three checks apply:
  - every `about` name must appear in the claim as whole words, and must be a name, not a vague noun ("video", "the system");
  - every bare "the/this/these/those + vague noun" ("the software") needs an `about` entry with that `what` that the claim names;
  - the claim may not open with a pronoun.
  
  A claim that fails gets one repair call told exactly what is wrong (`repair_claim`); one that still fails is **dropped and listed** in the tool result's `dropped` with its reasons. Stored claims carry `about`, `source_url` / `source_title` / `source_outlet` (`source_reference`), and the topic classifier reads the source title with the claim.
  
  The prompt rule that matters: when the source gives no name, say whose it is ("Paragon Solutions' spyware"), never "the spyware". On 8 real sources the local model stored 21 claims and dropped 2. The check doesn't catch a missing location ("AI agents were deployed" with no target named).
- **The `rewrite-claims` backfill is gone** (removed 2026-10-11, Phase 4 pack 6: 0 of 4,651 claims pending, and every new claim is stored with `standalone_checked_at`). It restated pre-Phase-9 claims so they stand alone; rewritten ones keep their old text in `content_v1`. Git history has it if another backfill is ever needed. Its checks live on in extraction's repair (epistemics plugin, `claims.rs`):
  - **An answer replaces a claim only if** it passes `standalone_problems` **and loses no number or name**: `rewrite_losses` compares digit runs and each capitalised word part, after `canon` folds Unicode hyphens, quotes and spaces. That fold matters because gpt-oss writes "AP‑NORC" and "2026‑09‑28" with non-breaking hyphens.
  - **Not caught by any check:** verbs that soften meaning ("admitted" → "said").
  - **After a mass rewrite, run `eval-retrieval`.** Rewritten claims name their subjects, so they rise for queries about those subjects and can push an unchanged neighbour out of the top k (the 2026-10-09 run: recall@10 0.920 → 0.880 from one case at rank 10, MRR 0.757 → 0.780).
- **Where a claim was asserted is shown, not only stored.** `GET /api/notes/{id}` returns `asserted_in`: each `ASSERTED_IN` source note with `title` / `url` / `outlet`, read by `claims::source_reference` from the source's summary JSON (`title`, `url`, `site` or `channel`). Without one, the title is the first line (any heading level, ≤ 120 chars), and the URL is taken only from that line: a report's body links could be any of its sources. The note drawer renders it as **Asserted in** above provenance; a claim with no edge says so (25 of 4,510 on 2026-10-08).
- Chain-extracted claims get their `ASSERTED_IN` edge via `{{_prev.id}}` + `prev_result_raw`. The `claim` tool **echoes its input as `answer`** (safe to insert mid-chain). Standing schedules write `source_record` (not `semantic`) + a claim-extraction step + a `source_list` + a recency gate.

Full story (the UAP/ToRA-7B/psionics laundering incidents, the full tier reasoning): history § Epistemics.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Evaluator Loop (Generator-Evaluator)
content: **Opt-in per workflow (2026-10-10):** a workflow with `checks: [evaluator]` gets a `reflect_on_work` evaluator step at dispatch (`dispatch_run` → `maybe_append_evaluator`, inserted before a trailing `update_task`), graded against the workflow's `evaluation_rubric`, else the run Task's `success_criteria`; with neither there is nothing to grade and no step is added. No migrated workflow opts in: in the 60 days before, the evaluator ran once. It parses a `Score: N/5` line; `< min_score` (default 3.5) → mark the task `failed` + start a new run of the **same workflow with the same inputs** (`workflows::start_run`) with the critique in `context`. **Retry cap 3** (`handle_evaluator_requeue` counts `"RETRY —"`). **Unparseable output = pass** (`parse_evaluator_score` → `None`; do *not* fabricate a 3.0 and do not grade the AgentSpec). `ChainStep`: `is_evaluator`/`min_score`/`evaluator_task_id`; args `__evaluator_min_score`/`__evaluator_task_id`. The critic (`checks: [critic]`, `maybe_prepend_adversarial`) is opted into the same way. Full story: history § Evaluator Loop.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Externalized Agent Chains (part 1/2)
content:
Chains are workflows now (2026-10-10, CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN Phase 2b): `workflows/*.yaml` → `(:Workflow)`, run by name with inputs or on `every:`. There is no goal-text routing any more (`goal_to_steps`, `pattern`/`priority`, `no_evaluator`/`no_adversarial`, `{{goal_topic}}` and `{{file_slug}}` are gone). The model: `dev_docs get workflows/model`. The rules below are about the steps themselves.

- **Template vars** in step `arguments`: `{{inputs.<name>}}` (declared under `inputs:`; a run missing a required one is refused, and a reference to an undeclared one is rejected at save), `{{goal}}`, `{{task_id}}`, `{{date}}` (local date), `{{now}}` (local instant), `{{weekday}}` (local), `{{steps.<id>}}` (`dev_docs get chains/named-step-outputs`). **Feed data from `{{inputs.x}}`, never from `{{goal}}`**: the goal is a sentence describing the run (`fill-knowledge-gap: <topic>`, `watch video: <url>`), so a value read out of it carries the prose with it. Substitution is **value-level** (`substitute_template_vars` walks parsed JSON, replaces inside string values only — quote/backslash/newline-safe).
- **`{{_prev}}` vs `{{_prev.<path>}}`:** `{{_prev}}` = the previous step's output *after* `extract_result_text` unwraps `answer`/single-column `rows` (lossy by design). `{{_prev.<path>}}` (e.g. `{{_prev.id}}`, alias `{{result.id}}`) resolves a dotted path against the **pre-unwrap** envelope (`prev_result_raw`), never distilled. Unresolvable path → **empty string**, never the literal placeholder (consumers read empty as absent). Both forms may co-occur; paths substituted first; strings inserted raw.
- **Per-step model routing:** a step may declare `required_capabilities: [...]`; `services/model_router.rs` picks the best catalog model **the routing policy admits for the step's purpose and `data_class`** (`services/routing.rs` `route()`; the log names every better-ranked model it skipped, with the reason), routed via the `SELECTED_LLM` task-local (precedence: capability-selected > `USE_LOCAL_LLM` background pin > active config). Metadata: `__required_capabilities`, `__data_class`. **A step is private unless it or its workflow file says `data_class: public`** (the seeder stamps a file-level value onto steps, and so does a save that passes `data_class`), and private work only reaches `no_log` providers. `ROUTE_CONTEXT` is scoped around the job, so `SharedLlm` judges every fallback rung by the same policy. Guards: `private_reasoning_stays_on_a_no_log_model`, `public_reasoning_routes_to_gpt_oss_like_private`, `private_work_never_reaches_a_training_provider_for_any_capability`. **"Best" = `cost ASC, selection_rank ASC, context_window DESC`** — and since every local/cloud model costs 0.0, **`selection_rank` is the decision** (per model in `models.yaml`, lower wins). Bands: `0–9` reserved (empty since 2026-10-02, when `gemini-2.5-flash` moved from 5 to 98 after failing 2 of 8 reasoning calls at ~31s while `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` failed 0 of 79), `10–99` ollama-cloud (`gemini-2.5-flash` at 98, the band's last rung), `110–199` local, `100–109` free tiers that may train on prompts (Mistral, OpenRouter `:free`), opened to private work for every purpose by their `private_ok_for` (owner's decision 2026-10-10, when the Ollama Cloud free quota ran out), so they are the cloud overflow ahead of local, `210+` paid. **Background fallback** (`SharedLlm::generate`) walks selected → active → `background_fallback_ladder` (models.yaml: Mistral, OpenRouter) → local, each rung admitted by the policy. **An account-wide quota 429** (`ACCOUNT_QUOTA_MARKERS` in `services/budget.rs`, Ollama's "Free usage limit") benches the **whole provider** for an hour, re-probed after; any other 429 benches only the model. Rank is **global, not per-capability**; a single-holder capability is only safe while it stays single. Guards: `selection_order_tests` + `model_config.rs` assert the checked-in `models.yaml` (incl. `reasoning_at_tier2_routes_to_gpt_oss` and `vision_at_tier2_stays_on_the_ollama_cloud_vision_model`). `minimax-m3:cloud` removed 2026-08-31 (left free tier); the seven ollama-cloud entries are the whole free tier. **Gemini free-tier caveat:** `gemini-2.5-flash`/`gemini-3-flash` are catalogued at cost 0.0, which is accurate only on the free tier (429 at the ceiling, no billing) — move them off 0.0 if the deployment ever exceeds it.
- **A step may pin a model: `model: "<catalog model id or name>"`** (`ChainStep.model` → `__model`; HBI plan Phase 10):
  - **Matched exactly** (`model_router::find_model`, case-insensitive), never by substring. A profile's `model_preference` still matches fuzzily (`resolve_profile_model`); a pin does not.
  - **Takes precedence over `required_capabilities`** and goes through the same `SELECTED_LLM`.
  - **A pin, not a preference.** `pinned_config` judges it by the routing policy for the step's data class when the job runs. An unknown or refused model kills the job at once with `Step model cannot run: <reason>` (`STEP_MODEL_ERROR`, no retries, no meta-learning), and the owning task fails with that reason.
  - **The policy's refusal is final; availability isn't.** A cloud pin that later hits quota or a 5xx walks the usual fallback chain, and every rung is in the ledger.
  - **`provider_hint` is derived from the model at enqueue** (`provider_hint_for`: a provider billed `local` gives `ollama`, otherwise the provider's name; only `anthropic` and `gemini` have their own semaphores).
  - **At upsert** (`validation::validate_step_models`, also run by `audit`):
    - an unknown model, or a written hint that contradicts the model's provider, is a hard reject;
    - a pin the policy would refuse right now is a soft `step_warning`;
    - a pinned step isn't asked for a hint.
  - **Why the derivation and the check exist:** the Zero Trust schedule wrote `provider_hint: ollama-cloud` beside the host-local `gemma4:latest`. `model` was ignored then, so nobody could tell what ran.
- **`run_agent` takes `model`** (else a step's `__model`) and `read_only`:

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Externalized Agent Chains (part 2/2)
content:
- the model gets the same exact match and policy check; an unknown or refused one rejects the run with the reason;
  - `read_only` strips write tools, as a chat sub-agent's are stripped: an HBI assist drafts into a form and must never store a note;
  - the result names the `model` the loop started on.
- **A chat turn takes `model`** (`ChatRequest.model`, the HBI header picker). It overrides the profile's pin; an unknown or refused one sends `Error` and `Done` and calls nothing. The front door's `model` names a profile, not a catalog model, and stays separate.
- **`/api/models` rows carry `admission`:** `{background|subagent|chat: {private|public: null | refusal}}`, computed with `RoutingPolicy::admit`, so spend caps and cooldowns show. The HBI `<ModelPicker>` reads it. It is cheap, but a spend-capped paid provider logs its cap warning once per row per request.
- **Paid synthesis (`deep_reasoning`, 2026-10-02).** `cost ASC` sorts every paid model behind every $0 one, so a paid model can only win a capability no free model holds. `deep_reasoning` is held by `claude-sonnet-5` **alone** (guard: `deep_reasoning_is_held_by_sonnet_5_alone`) and is requested by the synthesis `reason` step of the five standing-investigation workflows (intelligence-agency-claims, hardware tripwire, off-grid, SLM watch, tech-dependency synthesis), ~$0.15–0.20 per run, ~$7/month against the `anthropic` cap of $1/day, $10/month. When the policy refuses it (cap reached, `ROUTING_PAID_FOR` unset) no candidate survives and the step runs on its own `provider_hint: ollama-cloud` (gpt-oss), so a spent budget degrades the step instead of failing it. **The Anthropic provider omits `temperature` for models that reject it** (Sonnet 5, Opus 5/4.7/4.8, Fable, Mythos: a 400 otherwise), joins every `text` block (a leading `thinking` block made `content[0].text` empty), defaults `max_tokens` to 16000 (thinking counts against it) and floors its timeout at 300s.
- **`CURRENT_TOOL`** task-local attributes every in-job LLM call to `job.tool_name` in the usage ledger. The **chat path does not use it** — `clients/chat/` records directly (defaulting to `"chat"`). A **sub-agent** run (`delegate`/`run_agent`) is instead labelled by the `USAGE_TOOL_LABEL` task-local, scoped to `subagent:<agent>` in `AgentRunner::run` around the bounded loop (propagates through `join!`, never a `spawn`); before this its LLM cost billed under `chat`, so `run_agent`/`delegate` had **zero** rows in `model_usage` and sub-agent spend was invisible. Query it with `tool_name LIKE 'subagent:%'`. (2026-09-08)
- **`optional: true` on a step** lets a workflow run survive that step dying: the job is still dead-lettered and reflected on, but the next step gets an `[OPTIONAL STEP FAILED — …]` note as `{{_prev}}` and the owning Task is not failed (`__optional` in the job args; `CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS` lists it). For enrichment the chain can do without — the daily brief's weather and ApiTube fetches, after a ~15-minute outage cancelled the whole 2026-09-30 brief. **An optional step may name a tool that is not registered** (its plugin is off): the workflow stays available, and the queue skips the step at once instead of retrying (`ToolHandler::has_tool`). **A skip is not a death:** the job is `cancelled` with the reason, the next step gets `[OPTIONAL STEP SKIPPED — …]`, and there is no dead job, reflection or meta-learning. Found live: routed through the dead-job path, the first test run left a reflection telling the brain to investigate a tool that was off by choice. So a step on another plugin's tool whose result nothing reads is marked optional: the `claim` extract at the end of video-learning, article-learning and two core monitors (Phase 4 pack 6).
- **Distilled handoffs (`distill_prev: true`, `distill_max_chars`, `distill_focus`):** `maybe_distill_prev` compresses upstream output on the **local** model before substitution. Soft budget (overshoots ~50%); only hard guarantee is "never longer than raw". Own `LlmClient` at `num_ctx=16384`. **Never** on a step that persists `{{_prev}}` verbatim, nor on evaluator/adversarial steps. Every failure path falls back to raw. Wired in `workflows/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml` and `workflows/video-learning.yaml`.

Full story (routing-capture incident, selection_rank reasoning, distill measurements): history § Externalized Agent Chains.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Going local: what moved off `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` (2026-09-11)
content:
Measured over 7 days, then migrated. Every spawnable sub-agent except one is pinned `model_preference: gemma4-e4b` / `provider_hint: llamacpp`, as is the front door.

- **The budget is the constraint, and it is roomier than assumed.** Sidecar is `-c 32768 -np 2` ⇒ **16384/request**. Observed 7-day maxima: `api-scout` 7036, `api-integrator` 5935, `knowledge-worker` 5458, `researcher` 5320, `code-analyst` 4249, `job-applicant` 2450, `schedule-author` 2188. All ≤ 43%. An earlier claim that `researcher`/`code-analyst` would overflow was wrong — check the ledger before asserting a ceiling.
- **`reason` is the one that does NOT fit**: avg 20395, max 43493, and 6 of 17 calls errored *on gpt-oss*. Leave it on cloud, or raise `-c` (VRAM allows ~+1.3 GB; `-np 1` would fix context but serialises the front door against its own workers).
- **★ The limit on going local is RESULT-DIRECTED ITERATION, not context and not hop count.** Head-to-head 2026-09-11: each locally-pinned agent against a byte-identical cloud twin (same tools, same prompt, only the model differs), invoked through `run_agent` directly so the front door could not contaminate the comparison. Every failure was `isError: false` — the error counter cannot see any of this.

  | agent | local calls | cloud calls | local outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `schedule-author` | 0 | 0 | **PASS** — lint-clean draft (`provider_hint` top-level, `context: "{{_prev}}"`, `source_context` present) |
  | `code-analyst` | 8 | 8 | FAIL — never used the `path:line` its own grep returned |
  | `researcher` | 4 | 8 | FAIL — no `http_request`, no manufacturers, declined to cite a figure it held |
  | `api-scout` | 3 | 8 | FAIL — verified nothing, returned no base URL or endpoint |
  | `api-integrator` | 1 | 8 | FAIL — quit when the first probe failed |
  | `toolsmith` | **0** | 1 | FAIL — guessed the tool inventory from memory instead of calling `analyze_own_structure`, and leaked chain-of-thought as `step_by_step_thought` |

  E4B fails in two opposite-looking ways — stopping after one call, and looping eight without progress — and both are the same defect: **the result of step N does not shape step N+1.** It halts at the first obstacle or repeats undirected. The cloud model closes the loop (failed probe → search for docs → retry; search hits → probe the candidate → confirm).

  **So the predictor is the shape of the task, not its size.** Local is safe where there is no loop to close: one-shot synthesis (`schedule-author` drafts in a single pass) or a deterministic tool that *returns the answer* (`knowledge-worker`'s `recall_recent`). Everything investigative — where each step is a judgement about what the last result implies — needs cloud. A profile's token budget says nothing about this; `code-analyst` was migrated on a 26%-of-budget measurement and failed anyway. **Measure the ANSWER against a twin before pinning an agent local.**
- **`job-applicant` stays on cloud deliberately** — it fits easily, but it drafts real résumé content for real submissions; quality risk with consequences off this machine.
- **Do not swap the sidecar to Qwen3.** That comparison already ran: Qwen3-8B 6.0 GB / 70 tok/s vs E4B 3.3 GB and ~14% faster, and with bge-m3 + whisper resident there is ~3.0 GB free — Qwen3-8B will not fit alongside a 32k KV pool. Put more work *on* E4B instead.
- **`-np 2` means two local slots.** Front door + one sub-agent saturates it; background jobs already use llamacpp. Contention shows up as latency, absorbed by `OLLAMA_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS`.

**★ A local model's failure is usually a TOOL contract, not model capacity.** A delegated `code-analyst` on E4B reported the queue's retry logic "not present in the knowledge base" — on a codebase where `max_attempts` has 50 hits. The model was right to say so: `search_codebase` is a **literal regex grep**, it was handed a prose question, and it returned an empty result naming nothing to try next. gpt-oss would have hit the identical wall. Two model-agnostic fixes, both the `recall_recent` count-then-drill doctrine applied again: (1) `search_codebase`'s zero-result path now re-probes each significant term (stopword-filtered, counts marked `N+` at the probe cap since an exact count would be a lie at the ceiling) and states plainly that it is literal, not semantic — "absence of the phrase is NOT absence of the code"; (2) `contexts/code-analyst.yaml` gained a LOCATE→READ→reason workflow, because the agent had `read_codebase_file` and never called it, and `reason` retrieves NOTES — which is how a doc's "lacks exponential backoff" claim got reported as a finding about the source. It also passes `file_pattern: ".rs"` now, after an unfiltered grep sent it to summarise CLAUDE.md instead of `queue.rs`. **When a local model underperforms, check what its tools actually returned before concluding the model is too small.** **Same class, also fixed:** `read_codebase_file` had `max_lines` (default 500, cap 2000) and a truncation marker but **no offset**, so everything past line 2000 of a 2790-line file was unreachable at any setting and an agent asked about logic at line ~1572 correctly reported it "not visible in the files examined". It now takes **`start_line`** (1-indexed, matching the `path:line` citations `search_codebase` emits), states the window it returned (`lines 2780-2784 of 2790`), and its continuation marker names the exact next call rather than the dead-end "use max_lines to read more". Past-the-end reads report the valid range instead of an empty result.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › HBI frontend foundations (`hbi-frontend`, 2026-10-08) (part 1/4)
content:
Phase 0 of `HBI_REDESIGN_PLAN.md`. Rules for any new or touched frontend code:

- **One HTTP client** (`src/api/client.ts`). `apiRequest` returns the raw `Response` (callers check `res.ok`); `apiJson` throws `ApiError` (status + the brain's `{error}` text). No component builds an `Authorization` header or prefixes `getBrainUrl()` itself. The MCP SDK transport (`api/mcp.ts`) takes `authHeaders()` from the same module.
- **An endpoint shown in more than one view is a shared query** (`src/api/queries.ts`, TanStack Query). Observers of one key realign their poll timers on every data update, so N views cost one request per tick; `__tests__/queries.test.ts` pins that behaviour with a different-keys control. Job pushes (`notifications/agent_job`) invalidate the status keys through one app-level subscription (`invalidateOnJobPush`), not one per card.
- **The URL owns navigation** (`src/router.ts`): `#/<workspace>?<kind>=<id>`. Hash routing, because nginx serves a static bundle with no SPA fallback and a hash change never reloads (ChatPanel's stream survives). An unknown workspace is replaced by `home`.
- **Chat is the Ask modal, not a workspace** (CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN Phase 5, `components/chat/AskModal.tsx`, `src/lib/ask.ts`). Its state is the `ask` param on whatever route is showing: `ask=1` opens it, `ask=<session id>` opens that conversation, so a thread opened from the Feed opens over the Feed and Back closes it. Ctrl-J toggles it (Ctrl-K stays navigation; the palette and the entity drawer stack above it), and the sidebar's Ask button opens it for mouse and phone. **It stays mounted while closed**, so an answer still streaming finishes and is there when it reopens. `goTo` drops `ask`, so following a link out of the chat closes it. Old `#/chat?session=<id>` links redirect to `#/home?ask=<id>`; nothing that linked to chat dead-ends.
- **Inspection is the entity drawer** (`components/drawer/`), opened with `openEntity(kind, id)` and closed with Esc. Phase 0 knows `note`; other kinds register in `DRAWER_KINDS` as their workspaces land. It sits beside the workspace (overlay below 1100 px), so the thing being worked on stays visible.
- **Colours are tokens** in `styles/main.css` `:root`; kit styles in `styles/ui.css`. Four names were used but never defined (`--blue`, `--surface`, `--bg-base`, `--text-secondary` — queued/created badges and code blocks rendered with no colour); they are aliases now. ArchitecturePanel's private palette `C` stays until Phase 6 replaces the panel.
- **Empty and error states say what was checked** (`EmptyState checked=…`). A capped result says it is capped (the drawer's Related tab: `/api/notes/{id}/related` returns at most 10 outgoing `RELATES_TO`).
- `npm test` (vitest) covers the client, router, time/id helpers and shared polling. The Docker build image is `node:22-alpine` (vitest 5 needs Node ≥ 22.12; Node 20 is EOL).

**Phase 1 (2026-10-08): workspaces, Home, Settings, Ctrl-K.**

- **Navigation is `src/workspaces.ts`**: Home · Chat · Work (jobs/todos/scheduled/proposals) · Knowledge (notes/graph) · System (logs/architecture/tools), plus Settings. A workspace's views are still the old panels. **Old tab URLs redirect** (`LEGACY_PATHS`: `#/graph?note=x` → `#/knowledge?view=graph&note=x`), so links in notifications and notes keep landing; an unknown path goes Home. `goTo()` (`src/nav.ts`) drops the previous workspace's filters but keeps an open drawer.
- **Every Home number is a link to its rows.** Drill-downs are URL params the panel receives as props and is keyed by: Work `?view=jobs&job_status=a,b&since=…` or `&tab=tasks&task_status=…&since=…`; Knowledge `?view=notes&since=…&type=…&verified_since=…&q=…`. A drilled view shows a `DrillBanner` (what is filtered, row count, and "first N rows (the endpoint's limit)" when capped) with Show all.
- **`GET /api/activity?hours=24`** (1..720) counts notes by type and tasks by status created in the window, jobs by status *updated* in it, claims by status whose `verified_at` is in it, media ingested and schedule runs. Each count has a matching list: `/api/notes?since=&note_type=` (and `verified_since=` for claims), `/api/tasks?since=&status=`, `/api/jobs?since=&status=` (jobs: `updated_at`). A section whose query fails is `null` and named in `errors`, never shown as 0.
- **REST list params are bound, never formatted into Cypher.** `/api/tasks` and `/api/jobs` used to splice `?status=` into the query string (`{status: '{}'}`). Now `status` is a comma list bound as `$statuses` with `IN`, and `since`/`verified_since` must parse as RFC 3339 (else 400) and are compared through `datetime($since)`. Helpers: `parse_instant`, `parse_statuses`, `where_clause` in `clients/rest.rs`.
- **A job that will not run again is `failed`, `dead` or `dead_letter`.** The Tasks panel's "Failed / Dead" filter sent `failed` only and showed 0 of 39; the old `/api/health` `alerts.dead_jobs_last_24h` counted `dead` only. Both then included all three; `/api/health` went in CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN 6d (its only caller, Settings, reads `/api/system/health`, whose `queue.by_status` counts `dead` and `dead_letter`). "Active" is `running,queued,parked` on the server; it used to filter a latest-50 page in the browser, which hid older parked jobs.
- **Scheduler on/off is `config.enabled`** (`scheduler_control start|stop` set it; the error budget clears it). `state.is_running` only means a tick is executing. `lib/scheduler.ts` `summariseScheduler` is the one reading (Home, Settings, Architecture); the Architecture card used `is_running` and showed a sleeping scheduler as "paused" with a Start button.
- **Settings → Scheduler saves only the fields you changed**, through `scheduler_control configure` (interval, sleep interval, idle ticks, tasks per tick, error budget). It does not offer `local_model`: the old editor sent it on every save (even a pure Enabled toggle), and that value is written into the live background LLM config, while the scheduler's copy is the `OLLAMA_LOCAL_MODEL` default (`granite4:latest`), not the model llama.cpp serves (`gemma4-e4b` in the ledger).
- **Settings → Agents is the Chat agents editor rendered `inline`** (`ContextProfileModal inline`): no overlay, click edits, Esc returns to the list. Chat and Settings share `useProfiles()`, so an edit shows up in Chat's picker.
- **`/api/health` returns `version`** (the `:BrainVersion {id:'current'}` node: sha, branch, dirty, subject, deployed_at), shown in Settings → About with the bundle's build time (`__BUILD_TIME__`).
- **Ctrl-K** (`components/palette/`): every workspace view and settings section; a pasted note id opens it first; a phrase becomes "search notes for …", placed *after* real matches so Enter on "sched" goes to Scheduled.

**Phase 2 (2026-10-08): Work = lanes + lineage.**

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › HBI frontend foundations (`hbi-frontend`, 2026-10-08) (part 2/4)
content:
- **Work's lanes** (`components/work/`): Inbox (proposals, overdue todos, tasks failed and jobs died in 7 days) · Active (live jobs grouped under their owning task; created tasks waiting to be planned; in-progress tasks with no live job) · Scheduled (list · timeline · routing chains) · Todos · History (tasks or the whole job log, server-filtered by status; Home's drill-downs land here). Phase-1 links `view=jobs` / `view=proposals` redirect by their filters. Every row opens the drawer.
- **Lineage is reconstructed, not stored** (`clients/work.rs`, `/api/work/*`). A workflow run is the Task whose `workflow` property names it (with `inputs_json`; `runs_by_workflow`); its `context` is a readable label only (`run_context`: "Run of workflow '<name>' (<trigger>)"), never parsed; a task's jobs are those whose `args_json` holds `"__owner_task_id":"<id>"`; steps are ordered by `parent_job_id` (`chain_order`); a step's notes/tasks are the ids its result reports **that exist** as a `:Note` / `:Task` (the owner's own id, echoed by `update_task`, is excluded). Job records are pruned, so an old task can have none; `jobs_note` says why. Endpoints: `GET /api/work/{tasks,jobs,workflows,todos}/{id}`, `GET /api/work/workflows` (with last-run outcome), `POST /api/work/workflows/{id}/run` (body `{inputs}`), `POST /api/work/todos/{id}/task`.
- **Run now** is `SchedulerService::run_scheduled_task_now`: the same dispatch a timed run uses (run-record task, owner-stamped chain, `next_run_at` advanced), allowed on a disabled schedule as a one-off. It returns the run task id, which the UI opens.
- **A todo handed to the brain** becomes a Task (goal = title, context = description + `From todo '…' (todo: id)`) linked `(:Todo)-[:SPAWNED]->(:Task)`; the scheduler plans it on its next tick. The todo itself is unchanged.
- **`:Todo` is the one item record** (HBI plan Phase 12, §9.2). Every writer goes through `services/items.rs`:
  - **Checked on write:** status (`TODO_STATUSES`), origin (`TODO_ORIGINS`), `snoozed_until` (RFC 3339), and the assignee, against the live spawnable roster. A typo fails while someone is looking.
  - **Only the user assigns an agent** (§9.9 decision 5): a write under a `ROUTE_CONTEXT` (a job, a chat turn, a sub-agent; `items::written_by_brain`) may assign `user` or nobody. REST and an outside MCP client are the user.
  - **An item is made once per origin** (`create_item` finds it again by `origin_kind` + `origin_ref`), so a retried notification or a re-run backfill never makes two.
  - **An unassigned item is the user's**, as every todo before 2026-10-09 is.
- **`manage_todo`** (`skills/todo.rs`; front door and `general`): `list` (count-then-drill, at most 50 listed, an empty answer names what exists, an unknown status is an error) · `get` · `upsert` · `complete`. What the brain creates is assigned to `user` with origin `agent`.
- **Agent work on items** (HBI plan Phase 13; `services/item_dispatch.rs`). An agent-assigned item is a Task with a delay:
  - **The run:** when it is due, the item gets a Task (`SPAWNED`, so Work's lineage shows it), marked in progress *before* its chain is queued so the planner never takes it. Its chain is `run_agent` (the item's prompt; its `model`) → `manage_todo deliver` (the result as a note `source_context: item:<id>`, posted into the item's thread, status `awaiting_review`) → `update_task completed`.
  - **Asks first** (`items::side_effects`): a profile's `side_effects: read_only | writes`, else derived from its tools. Any of `EXTERNAL_EFFECT_TOOLS` (`http_request`, `mcp_call`, `write_workspace_file`, `write_proposal`, `manage_plugin`) means it waits in `awaiting_approval`, with the reason posted in its thread. An unknown value, an unknown agent and `agent:auto` ask too. `/api/contexts` reports each agent's `asks_first`. **No profile is overridden to `read_only`:** the delayed-prompt plan proposed it for `researcher` when it held only `http_request`, but it now also holds `mcp_call`, which reaches aidevboard's `apply_to_job`.
  - **Guardrails:**
    - an approval is single-use (`approved_dispatch` names the run it allows);
    - at most 3 runs an item (`MAX_RUNS`; sending back counts) and 3 started per poll;
    - a run starts only through a conditional status change that also checks `dispatch_count`, so two callers can't start the same run.
  - **Failure:** a run whose Task failed goes back to `pending` while runs remain, or to `awaiting_review` with the reason once none do (`reconcile`). Either way the reason is posted in the thread.
  - **The user's side is REST only** (`clients/items.rs`: `POST /api/items/{id}/assign | approve | send-back`):
    - `assign` waits for the due date; with none, it is due today;
    - `approve` starts a waiting run now, or accepts a result (done);
    - `send-back` needs a comment, reruns the agent with its previous answer and the comment, and counts as approval for that run.
  - **`dispatch_due_todos`** (TodoSkill), driven by the hourly `workflows/item-dispatch.yaml`, catches due dates and failed runs; a hand-over in the HBI is offered a run at once.
- **"Make it a schedule"** (`components/items/MakeSchedule.tsx`):
  - `schedule-author`, read-only, drafts `{name, interval_seconds, steps}` from the item;
