  - it is created **disabled** with `from_item`, which links `(:Todo)-[:BECAME]->(:Workflow)`, and opens in the workflow drawer;
  - a draft the save rejects goes back to `schedule-author` once with the errors;
  - turning it on (`PUT enabled: true`) closes every open item it came from (`closed_reason: became a schedule`);
  - the button has a model picker: the local `gemma4-e4b` failed both its draft and its repair on the Sodium item, and `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` drafted a clean one first time.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › HBI frontend foundations (`hbi-frontend`, 2026-10-08) (part 3/4)
content:
- **REST `/workflows` runs the full hard step check** (tool exists, arguments fit its `input_schema`, misplaced arguments, step models, step and input references): it and `manage_workflow` share `workflows::save`. Before this, the HBI saved a draft whose `reason` step lacked `question` and would have failed every run. Deleting a workflow is `DETACH DELETE` (a `BECAME` edge made plain `DELETE` fail).
- **The Daily Brief carries a "Your items" block** (overdue, due within 3 days, results to review, runs to approve), replacing the daily Todo Review chat, which is retired (`enabled: false`, `paused_reason`; §9.9 decision 3).
- **`notify_user` with `needs: "action"`** also creates an item for the user, with the notification's session as its thread, and marks the notification `needs_action` + `item_id`. Any other `needs` value is refused before anything is sent. A plain `notify_user` stays a read.
- **A code proposal is an item:**
  - `write_proposal` creates one (origin `proposal`, ref the task id; priority from severity) whose description IS the proposal: diagnosis, fix, snippet. There is no proposal file (Phase 0, 2026-10-10: none had ever been written);
  - the user closes it in the Feed like any item.
- **The Feed** (`GET /api/feed`, `clients/feed.rs`) is the one list of what wants the user. Its rows:
  - items for the user, open and theirs or awaiting their approval or review, unsnoozed, ordered overdue → awaiting → newest;
  - unread notifications that ask nothing;
  - one digest card per signal (entity merges to decide, tasks failed and jobs died this week, schedules with a step whose tool isn't registered).
  
  **`total` is its row count, and is the one number the nav badge (on Work), Home's Needs-you tile and the Feed header show.** The chat banner is gone; `openSession` opens a conversation in the Ask modal over the current page (`ask=<id>`: the Feed, an item's thread, Home). Overdue compares the due *date* with today's local date, as the HBI always did; comparing instants made a todo due today overdue all day west of UTC.
- **Schedule edits respect ownership.** Turning a schedule on/off is a targeted `PUT {enabled}` and survives restarts; the YAML seeder force-syncs a yaml-owned schedule's steps, description and interval on every restart, so the drawer warns that edits to those last only until then.
- **The runner reads `tool_name` / `arguments` only.** A step stored as `tool` / `args` (old editor format) deserializes to an empty tool name and dies "Unknown tool". `step_tools` reports names as the runner sees them and counts such steps in `legacy_steps`; the list and drawer flag them, and Edit → Save converts them. Only the disabled SELF-TEST schedule has them (2026-10-08). The step editor no longer offers a per-step **Model** (`ChainStep` has no such field; it was silently dropped) and offers `ollama-cloud` as a provider, keeping an unknown current value visible.
- **An action button uses `callToolStrict`** (`api/mcp.ts`), which throws when the tool returns `isError: true`; `callTool` returns the error text as if it succeeded, so "not retryable" used to read as done. **Retrying a `dead_letter` job goes through the `dead_letter` tool** — `manage_job retry` takes only failed / dead / cancelled.
- **Overdue is date-based** (`components/todos/model.ts` `isTodoOverdue`): a due date is a calendar date stored at 00:00 UTC, overdue once it is before today's *local* date. Comparing instants (Home) or UTC dates (old TodoPanel) disagreed in the evening west of UTC.
- **The step editor keeps every field it doesn't edit** (`StepDraft.extra`, `components/schedules/model.ts`): `data_class`, `max_attempts`, `description`, `is_evaluator`, `min_score`, `context_profile`, `model`, … ride through a save untouched and are listed under the step as "Also kept". Until 2026-10-08 the converter kept only `tool_name` / `arguments` / `provider_hint` / `priority`, so saving a schedule or routing chain (now both workflows) in the HBI silently dropped the rest (`data_class: public` work became private). It also turned a step with **no** `provider_hint` (cloud) into `ollama` (local). A missing hint now stays missing. Old `tool`/`args` steps are rewritten as `tool_name`/`arguments` on save.
- **The step's "Runs on" says what `provider_hint` does:** only `"ollama"` is local. Every other value, or none, runs on the brain's **active** model (`/api/models` `active_model`; background work uses it, not `chat_model`). The value only chooses the queue semaphore. The editor offers local or cloud and labels any other value it finds ("anthropic: also cloud, on …"). Choosing a model per step is HBI plan Phase 10.
- **The nav rail collapses** to 52 px icons (labels in tooltips, the badge kept), remembered under localStorage `hbi.nav.collapsed`.
- The 1,900-line schedule editor is split into `components/schedules/` (`model.ts`, `useToolGroups.ts`, `StepCard`, `ScheduleForm`; `ChainsView` went with the chains in Phase 2b); `TodoForm` lives in `components/todos/`. Both forms take `embedded` and render inside the wide drawer. `TaskPanel`, `TodoPanel`, `ScheduledTasksPanel` and `ProposalsPanel` are gone.

**Phase 3 (2026-10-08): Knowledge = one search, three views.**

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › HBI frontend foundations (`hbi-frontend`, 2026-10-08) (part 4/4)
content:
- **`GET /api/search?q=&mode=auto|semantic|keyword|id&type=&limit=&hops=`** (`clients/search.rs`). `auto`: a bare UUID is an id lookup, a `"quoted"` query a keyword phrase, anything else semantic. **Semantic is the brain's own hybrid retrieval through the non-perturbing path** (`search_notes_explained` → `search_notes_inner(track_access=false)`), so browsing never moves access/freshness signals; `hops` 0 by default (the brain's `search_notes` uses 2, which adds non-matches). **Keyword** is BM25 alone; bare words are all required (`+a +b`), a quoted query is one phrase; chunks resolve to the parent. **Id** looks across Note, Entity, Task, AgentJob, Workflow and Todo (`/api/lookup/{id}` alone too). Entities are offered when their name contains the query or appears in it as whole words (≥ 4 chars). A capped result says `truncated`; an un-embeddable query says `vector_available: false`.
- **Every hit says why it matched** (`MatchTrace` in `services/knowledge/retrieval.rs`): vector rank + cosine, BM25 rank + Lucene score, `via_chunk`, `added_by` (graph / entity / substring fallback). It is recorded *alongside* the pipeline through an optional `trace` argument the brain's own callers pass as `None`. **Verified to change nothing**: `eval-retrieval` before and after gave recall@10 0.920 / MRR 0.757 with every one of 25 cases identical. The trace already shows a real ranking effect: for "what is happening with sodium-ion batteries" the best semantic match (vector #1, BM25 #1) lands third behind Todo Snapshot notes that RRF + freshness lift from vector ranks 41 and 69.
- **Notes written or edited in the HBI go through the real pipeline.** `POST /api/notes` is now `KnowledgeService::store_note` (embedded, chunked, linked, entity-scanned; `source_context: "hbi"`); `PUT /api/notes/{id}` is `rewrite_note_in_place` (keeps id, created_at and inbound edges; rebuilds embedding, RELATES_TO, chunks and mentions). Both used to be raw Cypher: a UI note was invisible to semantic search, and an edit left the old embedding and chunks describing the old text. `RestState.knowledge` is built from `neo4j` + `llm_config`.
- **`GET /api/notes/{id}`** adds provenance (`source_context`, `provenance`), claim fields (status, kind, corroboration tier and counts, `asserted_by`, `verified_at`, `verification`), `embedded`, `parent_id` (it is a chunk) / `chunks`, and up to 30 mentioned entities (not url/date). **`GET /api/entities/{id}`**: mention count, newest 40 notes, top 15 co-mentioned entities. **`/api/graph?seeds=id,…`** (≤ 60): the seeds (flagged), 4 nearest RELATES_TO neighbours each, and their 40 most-mentioned entities.
- **The frontend** (`components/knowledge/KnowledgeWorkspace.tsx`): Results (match chips, entity strip; with no query the newest notes or a Home drill-down), Neighbourhood (`GraphPanel seedIds=` — clicking a node opens the drawer, the drawer's entity is ringed), Timeline (per day or week; a bar lists its notes). `q`/`mode`/`type`/`hops` are a workspace's `shared` params, kept across its view tabs. Drawer gains `entity`; the note view gains provenance, claim status, chunk parent, mentions, edit/delete, and `note=new`. Ctrl-K resolves a pasted id's kind before opening it. `KnowledgePanel` is gone; `view=notes` redirects to `list`.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Living architecture (`services/architecture.rs`, 2026-10-08)
content:
- **The view is the `developer` plugin's; what it reads is the core's** (CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN Phase 4, split by the owner's choice). The plugin (`arch.rs`, `routes.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, its `layout.yaml`) serves `GET /api/plugins/developer/architecture` and `snapshot_architecture`, creates the `ArchSnapshot` schema and takes the baseline in its `start`. The core keeps `architecture/components.yaml` (system health probes) and `removed-tools.yaml` (tombstones) in `services/architecture.rs`, and hands the plugin its compiled router source, the providers, the components and the declared tools through `introspection`. With `developer` off the HBI's Architecture view says the plugin is not loaded.
- **The architecture is computed, never written down.** The view builds it from what the brain already knows: `(:ToolDef)` (skills and tools, re-synced at every start), `(:ContextProfile)`, `(:Workflow)`, `(:McpServer)`, the declared tools of the loaded bundles, the provider registry, `components.yaml`, and the routes **parsed from the router source** (`mcp/http_transport.rs`, `include_str!`'d by the core as `architecture::ROUTER_SOURCE`). Plugin routes (`/api/plugins/<name>/…`) are not in it. Don't add a route anywhere else: a router outside that file would be invisible to the view. The brain writes no TSX and no layout: a model hand-editing a diagram is the `doc-update` failure in a harder medium (HBI_REDESIGN_PLAN.md §4).
- **The developer bundle's `layout.yaml` holds only what can't be derived:** groups (selectors `kind:name`, a trailing `*` matches a prefix, an exact selector beats a wildcard), the edges between groups, and the container topology. **A new skill is unplaced until you add it to a group.** The view shows it under "Unplaced", and a selector that matches nothing as stale, instead of dropping either silently. A new tool, schedule, agent or route area under `/api` needs no edit.
- **The topology is checked against compose.** `the_layout_topology_matches_docker_compose` fails when `docker-compose.yml` gains a service, a network or a published port that `layout.yaml` doesn't have, and `the_shipped_layout_places_every_route_and_its_edges_name_groups` fails on an unplaced route area. Update the layout in the same change.
- **Snapshots are set arithmetic.** `snapshot_architecture` (first step of the weekly `brain-api-sync`; `dry_run` to look without storing) stores an `(:ArchSnapshot)` with its diff against the previous one and a one-line summary written by code. A baseline is taken at the first start. "What changed" in the HBI compares the **live** inventory with the newest snapshot, so it never lags a deploy.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Media Learning (watch & summarize videos) (part 1/2)
content:
**★ A LIVE broadcast is rejected up front, and `MEDIA_MAX_DURATION_SECS` cannot do it for you.** `fetch_via_ytdlp` bails on `meta.is_live` **before** the caption path. Two independent reasons the old cost guard never fired: it lives on the *no-captions* branch only (a live stream with auto-captions skips it entirely), and yt-dlp reports `duration: null` for a live stream, which parses to `0` — so `0 > 10800` is false. A live broadcast also has no end, so `ingest_media`'s map-reduce has no finite transcript and the job simply hangs. `was_live` (a finished stream, now a normal VOD with a real duration) is deliberately NOT treated as live. Observed 2026-09-11: a `watch video:` task on a broadcasting stream held one of the two local job slots for **3 hours across 29 attempts**, burning zero LLM calls and recording no error.

**`poll_media_sources` filters `is_live` at DISCOVERY too, so a live stream never becomes a Task** — no chain, no retry cycle, no failed owning Task. The probe is deliberately no longer gated on `MEDIA_MAX_DURATION_SECS > 0`, because a live broadcast is unbounded whatever cap is configured. **It records NO dedup `:Media` node**, unlike the over-length path: a video's duration never changes, so `skipped_too_long` is correctly permanent, but "live" is TEMPORARY — the broadcast ends and YouTube republishes it as an ordinary video. A `skipped_live` node would make `media_exists()` suppress the finished recording forever. It stays in the channel RSS feed, so the next poll re-probes and picks it up once `is_live` is false. Motivating source: `c-span`, the highest-volume watchlist entry (25 tasks in 7 days) and the one that broadcasts live.

**A scheduled premiere is skipped like a live stream.** yt-dlp refuses an upcoming event outright ("This live event will begin in N hours"), so the poll's duration probe fails; `media::is_not_yet_available` recognises that and the poll skips it with no dedup node (it is picked up after it airs), and `parse_meta` treats `live_status: is_upcoming` as live. Two premieres dead-lettered in the week to 2026-10-01.

**Every video links to its watchlist source by channel id.** The poll's `watch video:` task carries only the URL, so the source name never reached `ingest_media` and **no video had a `FROM_SOURCE` edge** (0 of 1,089) until 2026-10-01. `ingest_media` now falls back to `link_media_by_channel` (a YouTube `MediaSource.ref` is the channel id); `scripts/backfill_media_from_source.cypher` linked the existing 1,089.

**`workflows/video-learning.yaml` passes `{{inputs.url}}`, never `{{goal}}`.** The run's goal is `watch video: <url>`, so `{{goal}}` hands `ingest_media` a URL with the prefix glued on. Anything consumed as data comes from an input (`dev_docs get workflows/model`).



The `media` plugin (`plugins/media/`, since CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN Phase 4): `MediaSkill` (`crate/src/skill.rs`) + `MediaService` (`crate/src/service.rs`), the `:Media`/`:MediaSource` graph layer (`crate/src/store.rs`, over the host graph), the four workflows and `sources-media/`; spec in `project-docs/VIDEO_LEARNING_PLAN.md`. Captions-first (`yt-dlp` downloads the caption file, parse `json3`); Whisper fallback (`WHISPER_PROVIDER` set → POST audio to OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `crate/src/transcribe.rs`); `WHISPER_PROVIDER=none` errors caption-less videos cleanly. **Map-reduce summarization happens inside `ingest_media`** (transcripts aren't fixed-length, chains are). On-demand: `ingest_media(url)`; a `video-learning` run with input `url` (`manage_workflow run`, `create_task workflow=video-learning`). Autonomous: `poll_media_sources` (RSS → one `video-learning` run per new item, `{url}` as input, `MEDIA_WATCH_ENABLED`-gated, duration pre-filter via `fetch_meta`), `discover_media_sources` (weekly, stages **inactive** sources for review). Watchlist `(:MediaSource {…, active, managed_by})` seeded from `sources-media/*.yaml` ON CREATE. Nodes: `:MediaSource`, `:Media`; edges `FROM_SOURCE`, `SUMMARIZES`, reused `MENTIONS`. Phase 5 (podcast RSS + local files) implemented. **`list_feed_videos` retries transient feed failures with backoff** (3 attempts, 500ms→2s): YouTube throttles the endpoint with 404/429/5xx when a poll fans every source at once, and the *same* channel_id returns 200 minutes later — a bare `error_for_status()?` dropped each source for a whole 12h cycle. The channel IDs are correct; the failures are IP throttling, so don't "fix" the IDs. Full detail: history § Media Learning.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Media Learning (watch & summarize videos) (part 2/2)
content: **Articles ride the same watch loop (2026-10-06).** `kind: article_rss` (`ref` = the feed URL; RSS 2.0 or Atom, `parse_article_feed`) fans each new item into an `article-learning` run with input `url` → `workflows/article-learning.yaml` (`ingest_article` → new-vs-known `reason` → ≤1 gap task → `source_record` note, `source_context: article_learning` → `claim` extract, limit 2). The yt-dlp probe (duration/live/premiere) is skipped for articles. `ingest_article` fetches ≤4 MB (`ARTICLE_MAX_BYTES`; a 36 MB single-page app exists), extracts text with `extract_article_text` and summarizes with `Medium::Article` prompts. Dedup id `art-{fnv1a(url)}` (`article_id`), shared by poll and ingest. **A page with < 800 chars of extracted text is permanent** (`ARTICLE_UNEXTRACTABLE`: paywall, script-rendered, index stub): it is recorded as a `:Media {transcript_source:'unextractable'}` node so the next poll does not re-create the run; a network error records nothing. **Extraction keeps lines of ≥ 6 words that are not wholly one link's text**: related-story cards wrap title + excerpt in a single `<a>`, and their headlines would otherwise be extracted as claims of the article. Feeds: `sources-media/osint.yaml` (8; each newest article checked live — see its header for the five left out and why). **Rendering fallback (2026-10-06):** when the direct fetch is refused (401/403/429/451/503) or yields < 800 chars, `fetch_article` asks Anakin.io's headless browser (`ANAKINIO_API_KEY`, ~1 of 300 credits/month) and runs its markdown through the same paragraph filter (`markdown_article_text`). Only if that also fails is the page recorded unextractable, and the error names both attempts. A 404/410/500 is not retried that way — gone is not blocked. Verified on ISW, which answers our fetcher 403.

subsystem: OpenAI-compatible front door (`/v1`, for Conduit and other OpenAI-wire clients)
title: Architecture: subsystem rules › OpenAI-compatible front door (`/v1`, for Conduit and other OpenAI-wire clients)
content:
`mcp/http_transport/openai_compat.rs` serves `GET /v1/models` + `POST /v1/chat/completions` (streaming and not) over the SAME `ChatService::run` as `/chat`. It is an adapter, not a model proxy: the model id picks a **context profile** (`brain` = the `CHAT_DEFAULT_PROFILE` front door, `brain:<profile>` = that profile), and the routing policy still decides which LLM runs. Client setup (Conduit → direct OpenAI-compatible connection): base URL `http://<host>:3001/v1`, API key = `MCP_API_KEY` (any value while auth is off).

- **Progress goes to `reasoning_content`, never `content`.** Tool calls/results/thinking stream there; the client sends assistant `content` back as history next turn, so narration in `content` would be re-read as something the brain said. Incoming assistant history is also stripped of `<think>` blocks.
- **Client `system` messages are dropped** — the profile owns the system prompt.
- **A `Token` stream is followed by a full `Message`**; `Translator` forwards only what the tokens did not already send, or the answer prints twice.
- **Session id** = `conduit-<FNV-1a(model, first user message)>` (the OpenAI wire has no conversation id; FNV because `DefaultHasher` is not stable across Rust releases). `X-Session-Id` overrides. Two conversations opening with the identical first message share a session — persistence only, since history comes from the client.
- Auth is the shared `auth_middleware` (Bearer `MCP_API_KEY`). Guards: `openai_compat::tests`.

subsystem: Outbound MCP client (call other MCP servers)
title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Outbound MCP client (call other MCP servers)
content: The brain is an MCP **server**; `McpClientSkill` (`skills/mcp_client.rs`) + `services/mcp_client.rs` make it an MCP **client** of external servers too. Two passthrough tools: `mcp_list_tools(server?)` (no server ⇒ the registered servers), `mcp_call(server, tool, arguments)` — usable from chat AND workflows. `mcp_call`'s text result is returned under `answer` so `{{_prev}}` flows; a remote `isError` is a *successful* call carrying the error text (like `execute_code`), never a chain-failing error. Servers are `(:McpServer {name,url,auth_scheme,auth_param,auth_env_var,enabled})` nodes seeded ON CREATE from each loaded plugin bundle's `mcp-servers/*.yaml` (graph-owned after, like SourceLists; `plugin` records the bundle; `dev_docs get plugins/loader`), or a bare `https://` URL passed directly (keyless). Auth mirrors `http_request`'s env-var-name pattern — the secret is NEVER stored, only the env var name; injected at call time in the brain process (has egress, never the sandbox). Transport is JSON-RPC over HTTP with a best-effort `initialize` handshake and handles plain-JSON or SSE-framed bodies (`extract_json_body`). Seeds: `aidevboard` (`X-API-Key`, full agentic apply flow — apply is gated **server-side** on a human-approved artifact hash, so passthrough can't submit on its own) `worklittle` (keyless job search), and `exa` / `tavily` (2026-09-26). Their search tools duplicate `search_web`'s engines exactly (same index, same sources, probed side by side), so search stays on `search_web`; they are here for **page reading** (`web_fetch_exa`, `tavily_extract`) and **site walking** (`tavily_map`, `tavily_crawl`), which the brain otherwise lacks. Keys go in headers (`x-api-key` / Bearer) from the existing `EXA_API_KEY`/`TAVILY_API_KEY`, never in the stored URL. `McpClient` sends a `User-Agent` because Exa's server 403s a request without one. Design + the apply workflow on top: `project-docs/MCP_CLIENT_PLAN.md`.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Retrieval evaluation harness (`services/retrieval_eval.rs`, `eval-retrieval` CLI)
content: `cargo run -- eval-retrieval [--fixture …] [--k 10]` runs a golden set (`eval/retrieval_golden.yaml`, human-owned) through the real pipeline and reports **recall@k** + **MRR**. `--bootstrap N` proposes cases to curate. Measurement must not perturb: `search_notes_readonly` → `search_notes_inner(track_access=false)` is the only non-perturbing path. Prefer `expect_substrings` over `expect_ids` (ids churn on re-embed). Tuning result (2026-08-31): recall@10 0.840→0.920, MRR 0.47→0.76 — from **widening the re-rank pool** + fixing a **chunk→parent order-scrambling bug**, *not* the embedder. Defaults stay `RETRIEVAL_RRF_WEIGHT=0.7`/`RETRIEVAL_RECENCY_TAU_DAYS=30`. Query embeddings need Ollama up (else BM25-only); the container carries whatever binary it was built with. Full story: history § Retrieval eval harness.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Workflow ownership (`managed_by`) (part 1/2)
content:
Built-in workflows live in a plugin bundle's `workflows/*.yaml` (the core's is `plugins/core/workflows/`), seeded at every startup by `seed_workflows` (`services/workflow_seeder.rs`) from every loaded bundle, core first, recording the bundle as `plugin`; a core bundle with no `workflows/` aborts startup, a file that fails to load or repeats an earlier bundle's name is skipped with a WARN. Bundles: `dev_docs get plugins/loader`. The model itself (inputs, `every`, the default, checks): `dev_docs get workflows/model`. The **graph is the runtime authority**; YAML is the definition source only for workflows it owns.
- **`managed_by`:** `yaml` (everything but `enabled` force-synced every startup: steps, description, `every`, inputs, checks, rubric, default, topic, kind — file edits win, runtime edits overwritten) vs `runtime` (seeder never touches). Transfer via `manage_workflow` upsert `managed_by`. Saving a yaml-owned workflow without `managed_by: runtime` succeeds with a warning that the next startup overwrites it.
- **A runtime node shadows its YAML file permanently** (matching is by exact `name`, which is the file stem; `sync_yaml_workflow` skips a runtime-owned name and the only sign is one WARN line per startup). Check `managed_by` before assuming a file is what executes: `manage_workflow(action=list, verbose=true)`.
- **`enabled` is graph-owned** (deliberately not synced) — so pausing survives restarts. Disable with `manage_workflow(upsert, {name, enabled: false, paused_reason})`: a save lays the body over the stored workflow, so nothing else changes (before 2026-10-10 upsert needed the full steps, and a targeted Cypher `SET` was the only safe pause; that still works). A disabled workflow refuses runs by name too, not only its timer. A workflow file may set **`enabled: false`** to seed it OFF on first creation (honored only on create, since `enabled` is never force-synced); absent ⇒ `true`. Use it to ship a workflow for human review before it can ever run (e.g. `workflows/api-scout.yaml`). `paused_reason`/`paused_at` record why. **`scripts/pause_cloud_schedules.sh {pause|resume|status}`** disables only cloud-routed scheduled workflows; audit targets against the graph (`provider_hint <> 'ollama' OR provider_hint IS NULL`). When a quota goes, check the ledger by `tool_name` first — chat, not schedules, usually spent it. **A chain's cloud cost is a multiplication (once per item), not a rate** — bound the item count before adding `ollama-cloud` to a fan-out step; cap burst and daily total separately.
- **A workflow declares `topic:` and `kind:`** (HBI plan Phase 11; on the node, in `workflows/*.yaml`, in the HBI form). A scheduled one (`every:`) must declare a `kind`:
  - `topic` is a `topics/*.yaml` name, or none for a schedule that spans topics on purpose. `kind` is one of `WORKFLOW_KINDS` (`monitor` · `brief` · `learning` · `maintenance` · `dataset`).
  - **Checked on every write path:**
    - the seeder warns and stores none for a wrong value;
    - `manage_workflow` upsert and REST `POST`/`PUT /workflows` reject one (`workflow_seeder::check_labels`, called by `workflows::save`);
    - `every_workflow_file_is_valid` fails the build on a bad file.
  - **The workflow is the one home of the link.** A topic's "Watched by" is computed from `Workflow.topic`; the old `schedules:` list in topic files is gone. A yaml-owned workflow's `topic`/`kind` are force-synced from its file like its steps; a runtime-owned one keeps what the graph holds.
- **The tool and REST share one save** (`services/workflows.rs` `save`): `manage_workflow` upsert and REST `/workflows` (the HBI's save path) both check the MERGED result (stored workflow + body) against the envelope schema, each step's arguments against its tool's `input_schema`, step models, step and input references, the slug name, labels and checks. `POST /workflows` is create-only. Only the advisory lint (`lint_chain_steps`) is tool-only.
- **What a schedule produced is traced, not guessed** (`GET /api/work/workflows/topic-mix?days=N`, `clients/work.rs`). Each note is counted once, by the first route that reaches it:
  1. **`run_stamp`:** the note's `produced_by_task` is one of the workflow's runs (Tasks with `workflow` = its name). The queue scopes `CURRENT_OWNER_TASK` around every job, so the note store and `store_claim` stamp every note a job writes, including those written inside a `run_agent` loop.
  2. **`job_result`:** a kept job reported the note's id. **Completed jobs are pruned after about two days**, which is why the stamp exists; job lineage alone covered 2 days, not 30.
  3. **`source_context`:** the note carries a literal `source_context` the schedule's own steps write (`step_source_contexts`). This is how notes from before the stamp are traced; no two schedules share one.
  4. **`claim_of`:** a claim asserted in a note traced by the first three.
  
  Chunks (`PART_OF`) are not counted: their parent is, and only the parent is classified.
- **The verdict** (`mix_verdict`, each note's main topic):
  - fewer than 3 classified notes is `too_few`;
  - a declared topic holding a third of the assessed notes, or the most, `matches`; otherwise `mismatch`, naming the top topic;
  - with no topic declared, a topic holding half is a `suggest`ion; otherwise `spans`.
  
  The HBI shows it on the list row and in the schedule drawer, with the per-route counts.
- **A workflow's steps are enqueued as written** (`dispatch_run`, `services/scheduler.rs`): templates rendered, then only what the workflow opted into (`checks: [evaluator, critic]`), a first step's `confidence_threshold` guardrail, a context-profile annotation and a closing `update_task` (skipped when a step already closes the run's own task). No auto-retrieval: step prompts must be correct alone, and a workflow needing fresh info must include its own `search_web`. **The semantic lint** → `lint_chain_steps` (`skills/scheduler.rs`) covers: a `reason` past position 1 with no `context`; a persisting step past position 1 not mentioning `{{_prev}}`; a `store_note` with no `source_context`; a `store_note` with an **unrecognized `note_type`** (checked against `VALID_NOTE_TYPES` — a chat-authored schedule stored an `analysis`-typed note on 2026-09-08 that then never labelled/recalled correctly); `semantic` in a web-searching chain; unregistered tool; a chain that never persists; **a step with no `provider_hint`** (omission ≠ local — `use_local` is `provider_hint == Some("ollama")`, so omission falls through to cloud; **and `provider_hint` is a step-TOP-LEVEL field, a sibling of `tool_name`/`arguments` — putting it *inside* `arguments` is silently ignored by routing, so the step runs on cloud. The same 2026-09-08 schedule made exactly this mistake on all six steps while its author reported "configured to use ollama".**). Warnings, not rejections. Runs in `upsert` (`step_warnings`/`needs_fix`) and `audit`. Behavioural half: `BUILD RULE` in `contexts/general.yaml`.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Workflow ownership (`managed_by`) (part 2/2)
content:
- **A tool argument at step level is a HARD reject** (`misplaced_arguments` in `services/validation.rs`). Serde drops unknown `ChainStep` fields, so `context: "{{_prev}}"` written beside `arguments` never reaches `reason` and nothing errors — the Trump Benefit monitor's reasoning never saw its search results. Only keys the tool's own schema declares are flagged; `CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS` must track `ChainStep`.
- **Deterministic structural validation (HARD reject, `services/validation.rs`).** Distinct from the semantic lint: every save (`workflows::save`, shared by `manage_workflow` upsert and REST `/workflows`) validates **each step's `arguments` against the tool's own registered `input_schema`** (snapshotted from the registry in `brain_core.rs` alongside `live_tools`) via the `jsonschema` crate, through `validation::validate_step_array`, and REJECT the write (nothing saved) on any type/required-field violation or an unregistered tool. This is the classic automated pushback: `ChainStep.arguments` is a free JSON value, so a wrong-typed arg (`query_params:"[object Object]"`, `timeout_ms:"15000"` — the HBI-editor corruption that silently killed the AI Dev Board Job Search schedule every run) passes the shape check and the semantic lint but is caught here before it can be stored. (The old `manage_chain` did no validation at all before this.) Object envelope schemas live in the `schemas/` seed dir (`workflow`, `task`, `context_profile`), loaded once from every loaded bundle's `schemas/` (core first; a later bundle cannot replace one) by `validation::load_schema_dir`; the **envelope layer is wired for workflows** (`schemas/workflow.json`, checked first in `workflows::save`: name, enums, min-items around the steps) and the `manage_workflow` **`audit` action runs the per-step structural gate over every STORED workflow** (`structural_errors`), so YAML-seeded ones are checkable on demand. Note `create_task` already parses typed serde input, so the untyped step `arguments` was the real gap. **Seeder skip-on-boot is deliberately NOT enabled** for schema violations (a file that does not parse — unknown key, name ≠ file stem, bad `every` — is skipped with a WARN, which is a different thing) — verified over all checked-in YAML, a hard boot-skip would silently disable real chains (a conditionally-registered `run_agent` when `SUBAGENT_ENABLED` is off; an invalid enum like the `meta-learn` `note_type: hypothesis` bug fixed 2026-09-09) — dropping a human-committed schedule on boot is worse than a loud warning, and any validator must use the in-process `registry.list()` full set, not the `MCP_TOOL_PROFILE`-bounded HTTP `tools/list`. Full design: `project-docs/VALIDATION_AND_APPLY_PLAN.md`.
- **One-shot run vs recurring workflow:** `create_task` (optionally with `workflow` + `inputs`) runs once on the next tick — cadence words in the goal are inert. Recurrence needs `every:` on a workflow (`manage_workflow` upsert or a `workflows/*.yaml`).
- **Reading prior runs:** chunks inherit `source_context` from their parent, so any Cypher retrieving a prior report by `source_context` must add `AND NOT (n)-[:PART_OF]->()`.
- **Critical Tech Dependency workflows** (`workflows/`) (three-tier standing investigation, each banks searches into a WorkingMemory scratch session and delta's against the prior run): `hardware-tripwire.yaml` (weekly, `hardware_tripwire`, 4 sweeps), `slm-benchmark-watch.yaml` (bi-weekly, `slm_benchmark_watch`, 3 sweeps), `tech-dependency-synthesis.yaml` (monthly, `tech_dependency_synthesis`, no web search — correlates the other two). Also `off-grid-networking-monitor.yaml` (weekly, `off_grid_networking_watch`, 3 sweeps).

Full story (the tripwire shadow/clobber incident, six duplicate schedules, the broken off-grid monitor, cost tables): history § ScheduledTask ownership.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Self-Improvement Loop
content:
`SchedulerService` background task, each tick: fires due scheduled workflows (`dispatch_due_workflows`), then lists `status=created` Tasks → resolves each Task's `workflow` (none ⇒ the `default: true` one; an unknown or disabled workflow, or a missing required input, fails the task with the reason) → `dispatch_run` → `enqueue_chain_owned` → marks `in_progress`. After `idle_sleep_after_ticks` (3) idle ticks → `enter_sleep()` (consolidate → prune → snapshot). `notify_activity()` resets the idle count. `QueueService` coordinator runs jobs serially per provider semaphore, retries transient failures, unparks dependents on success.

- **★ Crash recovery respects `max_attempts` — a hung job is NOT immortal.** `reset_running_agent_jobs` used to flip every `running` job back to `queued` unconditionally, which made `max_attempts` meaningless across a restart: a job that **hangs** is never marked failed, so it is still `running` at the next startup and gets resurrected, forever. It now dead-letters jobs already at their cap (with a `j.error` saying so) and requeues only those with attempts left; the count it returns is the REQUEUED count, dead ones logged at WARN. Observed 2026-09-11: an `ingest_media` job on a live stream reached **attempt 29 against a cap of 3**, revived by each restart during a day of rebuilds. **Not media-specific** — any job that hangs rather than failing hits this, which is why the fix is in recovery, not in a per-tool timeout.
- **Dead-job meta-learning:** on retry exhaustion, store a reflection note and — for non-infra tools (`should_meta_learn`) — enqueue an Analyze→Hypothesize→Test→Integrate chain. Guards: `is_transient_infra_error` (skip for quota/rate/timeout/5xx) and `recently_meta_learned` (≤ once/tool/24h).
- **Chain-death task attribution:** `enqueue_chain_owned(steps, session_id, Some(&task_id))` stamps `__owner_task_id` on every step; on step death the coordinator calls `fail_task_with_reason(task_id, reason)`, guarded to `status IN ['created','in_progress']`. `enqueue_chain` is the no-owner wrapper (chat/bedtime/meta-learning).

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Self-knowledge: making running state visible (part 1/5)
content:
A model that can't see running work reports it as absent, confidently. Rules that fix the class:

- `manage_workflow(action=list)` is a **tool** (lean payload; `verbose: true` for the rest); **empty-filter guardrail** returns every name + a warning rather than an empty list. `list_tasks` returns **totals** and leads with open work.
- **Truncated tool results are marked** (`truncate_tool_result` → `[TRUNCATED … INCOMPLETE]`). A `reason` result's declared limits are **hoisted to the front** (`annotate_tool_limits`/`reason_limits_marker`). `search_web` results are **prefixed with a numbered source list** (`search_sources_marker`, accepts `link` or `url`). `prepare_tool_result` is the single annotate-then-truncate entry point; the marker leads so truncation can't drop it.
- Failed protocol steps log at **WARN** (`tool_call FAILED`). A **dropped chat turn is reported** (`forward_chat_events`) instead of vanishing — and separately, an **abandoned** one is too: if the SSE client goes away mid-turn the handler future is dropped, that tail never runs, and the turn leaves no trace at all (on 2026-09-11 a turn ran `search_notes`, spent two gpt-oss calls / ~31K prompt tokens, and vanished leaving only an orphaned user row in working memory — indistinguishable in the logs from a request that never arrived). `TurnAbandonGuard` is a `Drop` guard, because cancellation is the one turn-ending path no `await`-side code can report; it is armed for the whole turn and disarmed once the event stream drains, so it never double-reports the dropped-turn case. A **malformed tool call is not prose**: the provider adapter returns `RoundReply.malformed` (the OpenAI-wire adapter when a call's arguments are not valid JSON; until Phase 6a also the `<tool_call>` text loop Gemini used), the model gets one correction round (`MAX_MALFORMED_TOOL_CALL_RETRIES`) with the tool receipt, and a second failure ends the turn with a visible "⚠ … did NOT run" line naming the tool — before this, "I am now setting this schedule up" stood as the answer while the upsert never ran (2026-09-24). An **empty completion is retried** (`MAX_EMPTY_COMPLETION_RETRIES`), not mistaken for a finished turn; `FINAL_ROUND_NUDGE` gives a tools-off wrap-up round when tool calls are exhausted. `chat_fallback_ladder` in `models.yaml`; a `reason` fallback to raw prose sets `structured_output_failed` (`confidence 0.0`, WARN).
- **General lesson:** a signal the model must act on belongs at **position zero in a loud delimiter**, not a field — prompt rules do not reliably beat payload position. Behavioural half: `PROJECT-STATUS RULE` in `contexts/general.yaml`.
- **A "what did we learn today / what happened" question is temporal, not topical, and needs a deterministic tool — not a prompt rule and not semantic search.** `recall_recent` (KnowledgeSkill; `KnowledgeStore::recall_window`) counts notes created in a **local-day** window by `note_type` + `source_context` with a bounded recent sample (excludes chunk fragments). It exists because the `general` `PROJECT-STATUS RULE` telling the model to "COUNT FIRST with a neo4j_query" was **ignored** — and, worse, when the orchestrator **delegated** the question to `knowledge-worker`, that profile had neither the rule nor `neo4j_query`, so it semantic-searched the literal date string `2026-09-07` (embeds to nothing), hit its round cap, and reported "no substantive findings" on a 377-note day. The fix is the tool in both `general` and `knowledge-worker` allowlists; a delegated whole-graph aggregate must go to a profile equipped for it. (2026-09-08)

- **★ A tool that reports a COUNT must be able to show the ROWS behind it, and its empty answer must carry the way out of it.** `recall_recent` takes `source_context` / `note_type` filters that narrow **every** aggregation and the sample alike (one shared predicate — `KnowledgeService::window_predicate`), so any bucket it reports is enumerable by asking again with that bucket's name; a filtered call also returns longer snippets (600 vs 200 chars), a larger default `sample_limit` (50), and **`complete`** — whether the sample IS the whole matching set. Why: on 2026-09-11 `recall_recent` correctly returned `video_learning: 43` at position 1, but nothing could enumerate a `source_context` (`search_notes` *requires* a `query` and applies `source_context` as a post-filter on similarity ranking; `list_notes` is an unfiltered last-20). So the `knowledge-worker` sub-agent fell back to `search_notes(query="video learning")`, whose top hit is a month-old IBM video *about* online learning, and told the user **twice** that no videos had been watched — on a day with 11, each with a stored summary — escalating to *"a thorough search… confirmed that no such notes exist"* while **citing its own correct count of 43 in the same breath**. Zero errors, 12 LLM calls: a pure quality miss. **The inversion is the lesson: a count already retrieved outranks a later search that finds nothing.** Second-order trap, hit while verifying the fix: the agent then guessed `note_type:"episodic"` alongside `source_context:"video_learning"` (those notes are `source_record`/`claim`), got `total: 0`, and reported absence again — so a zero-match **filtered** call now re-runs the aggregations **unfiltered** and returns `window_total_notes` + `available_note_types` + `available_source_contexts` with a note saying the FILTER is the likely fault, not the window (same shape as `list_endpoints` pointing a zero result at `list_apis`). A deterministic tool's empty answer must name the values that do exist, because the caller cannot guess a label it has never been shown. Behavioural half: `COUNT-THEN-DRILL` in `contexts/general.yaml` + `contexts/knowledge-worker.yaml`. Guards: `window_predicate_applies_each_filter_to_the_shared_predicate`, `recall_recent_forwards_drill_down_filters`, `recall_recent_treats_empty_filter_as_absent`. (2026-09-11)

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Self-knowledge: making running state visible (part 2/5)
content:
- **The same disease recurs for every STRUCTURAL question — "the last N tasks", "what APIs do we have", a specific note_type — and the fix is the same shape: a deterministic tool + a schema the model can see + a read-boundary guard, all model-agnostic.** Verified 2026-09-10 on `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` (chat worker; zero `model_usage` errors — a *quality* miss, not a failure): it answered "last 5 tasks" with stale consolidation tasks and *"completion timestamps were not stored"* (false — `Task.updated_at` is a native datetime on every node), reported 0 reflection notes when 4 existed, and said "no APIs" with 3 ingested contexts (agent-brain 48 / aidevboard 27 / home_assistant 20). A **smaller/local model will not fix this** — the failure is query construction, not capacity. Deterministic tools in `QuerySkill` (`skills/query.rs`): `recent_tasks` (`ORDER BY updated_at DESC`), `list_apis` (the `(:ApiContext)-[:EXPOSES]->(:ApiEndpoint)` aggregate), `list_endpoints(api)` (one API's endpoints — added 2026-09-11 after a chat listed HA's endpoints as "not stored": the graph had a parallel **legacy** `(:Resource)-[:HAS_ENDPOINT]->(:Endpoint)` structure — 18+40 orphan nodes from the original agent-api, since deleted — and `describe_graph` surfaced both, so hand-written Cypher non-deterministically picked the wrong one and got zero; the tool bakes the right one, and its zero-result path points at `list_apis` because the API name is case-sensitive), `describe_graph` (the **live** schema — labels, properties with ⏱ temporal flags, rel types — introspected via `db.schema.*` in `services/graph_schema.rs`, lazily cached, fails open). Both `general` and `knowledge-worker` gained all three (+`neo4j_query`, which `knowledge-worker` still lacked), plus a **STRUCTURAL QUERY RULE** (count/order/"last N"/"what X" → deterministic tool, never `search_notes`) and an **ABSENCE RULE** (never claim "not found / isn't stored" off a thin semantic search; a negative claim needs a deterministic query that ran this turn — the behavioural half of the guard). Load-bearing point for the local-knowledge-agent plan: the tools carry the query correctness, so a later move of knowledge lookups to local `gemma4:e4b` becomes *safe*. (2026-09-10)
- **★ The brain's OWN inventory is a structural question too, and `list_capabilities` (`skills/query.rs`) is the only tool that answers it.** Counts of tools/skills/profiles + the spawnable agent roster, read from the `(:ToolDef)`/`(:ContextProfile)`/`[:ALLOWS]` meta-graph that `self_model.rs` re-syncs from the live registry every `build_skills()`. No args = summary; `kind:"tools"` every tool name + per-skill tallies; `kind:"agents"`/`"profiles"`; `skill:"<name>"` / `profile:"<name>"` drill down. Both zero paths name what DOES exist (`available_skills`, or "call kind=profiles"). Added to `general`, `knowledge-worker`, `researcher`, `toolsmith`, `self-analyst`. Why: on 2026-09-11 "how many tools does the brain have?" was delegated to `toolsmith`, which called `analyze_own_structure` twice — correctly — and answered **"10"** against a registry of **90**; "how many agents" auto-routed to `researcher`, which semantic-searched the word "agent" for 8 rounds and gave up while the roster sat verbatim in the orchestrator's own `delegate` tool description. Zero errors on every row. **`analyze_own_structure` could not answer it**: its "Skill Registry" section is the 25 `pub mod` lines of `skills/mod.rs` — module names, no tools, no count — behind a directory tree, and `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` clipped even that. It now **leads** with the inventory (position zero, so truncation cannot drop it) and its description redirects inventory questions to `list_capabilities`. **A ground truth nothing surfaces is not self-knowledge.** Behavioural half: `STRUCTURAL QUERY RULE` in `contexts/general.yaml`, `OUR OWN INVENTORY` in `contexts/knowledge-worker.yaml`, and an `ABOUT THE BRAIN ITSELF` line in the front door routing these to `knowledge-worker`, never `researcher`. (2026-09-12)
- **★ GRAPH FIRST, WEB SECOND — every `search_web` result is prefixed with what the graph already holds.** `SearchSkill::prior_knowledge` runs unconditionally on both return paths and reports matching notes (hybrid via `search_notes_readonly`, BM25 fallback), **already-ingested APIs** ("use list_endpoints(…), do NOT search the web for its spec"), and **already-watched media**. Fails open everywhere — no graph, no index, no store, no block. Why unconditional: a worker asked to produce an OpenAPI doc for Home Assistant went web-searching for a spec while `(:ApiContext {name:'home_assistant'})` sat in the graph with 20 endpoints, listed in that same conversation two turns earlier. Consolidation dedupes *afterwards*; this stops the duplicate being created. **Precision is load-bearing**: media needs **two** matching query words (one word matched "Home Assistant" against three unrelated videos on "home" alone), and `chat_session`/`scheduler_dispatch` are excluded because they record that something HAPPENED, not what is KNOWN, and quote the question verbatim so they outrank real knowledge. Readonly on purpose — a housekeeping probe must not bump `access_count` and reshape spaced repetition. **The block is for agents, not verifiers** — anything judging evidence must pass `prior_knowledge: false`, or it reads our own notes as corroboration. Behavioural half in `researcher`/`api-scout`. (2026-09-12)

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Self-knowledge: making running state visible (part 3/5)
content:
- **★ A rule bolted on top of a numbered workflow loses to the workflow — put it IN the sequence, and give the agent the tools it names.** `api-integrator`'s prompt opened "1. DISCOVER. Use search_web…" under "do not skip steps", so a prepended GRAPH FIRST paragraph changed nothing. Making the lookup **step 0** still changed nothing, because the profile did not hold `list_apis` or `list_endpoints` — it had been instructed to call tools it could not reach. Adding those two tools is what actually worked: the request went from **5 web searches and a fabricated file write** to `list_apis` → `list_endpoints` → generate, **zero searches**. Check the allowlist before writing a rule that names a tool. (2026-09-12)
- **★ Two files can define the same profile `name`, and `read_dir` order decided which won.** The UI's `save_profile` wrote `<profile.name>.yaml` (until 2026-10-10; it now writes the graph), so editing a profile whose file is named differently (`general-default-orchestrator.yaml` for `GeneralDefault-Orchrestator`) creates a SECOND definition instead of updating the first — leaving the front door's model a coin flip per restart, one file pinning local `gemma4-e4b` and the other `gemini-2.5-flash`. Reading the bundle files (`profiles::BundleProfiles::read`) **sorts** and **WARNs** on a duplicate name, naming both paths and the winner. (2026-09-12)
- **The orchestrator delegates WRITES; it does not gain a write tool.** `contexts/scribe.yaml` is a spawnable worker that writes an artifact and confirms it in `list_workspace_files` before reporting success. The front door has a rule that it cannot write files and must put the write in the task. Why: it claimed *"I'll save this to `home_assistant_openapi.yaml`"* with no `write_workspace_file` in its allowlist and zero such calls in the log — `tool_trace_receipt` did not catch it because that covers a *worker's* tools, not the orchestrator's claim about what it will do next. A router that writes files stops being a router. (2026-09-12)
- **Gemini reported NULL tokens for weeks — a serde field-name mismatch.** `GeminiResponse`/`GeminiUsage` lacked `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, so `usageMetadata`/`promptTokenCount` never matched and the (correct) extraction always read from a `None`. Silent: no error, just NULLs on the one metered provider in the fleet, so orchestrator spend was invisible. The chat panel's usage strip also showed **call counts and success rate** — how often a model ran, not what it consumed — while `total_tokens_in`/`out`/`total_cost` sat unused in the same payload; it now shows a 24h token total with cost, per-model chips sorted by tokens, and flags any model with calls but no token counts as **`⚠ N unmetered`** rather than letting a broken ledger read as free. (2026-09-12)
- **★ A tool result has TWO audiences, and one cap cannot serve both — `ToolCallResult::bulk` is the human channel.** `content` goes to the model; `bulk` goes only to the person (the chat loop sends `content + bulk` to the SSE preview; `mcp/server.rs` folds them for MCP clients, since `bulk` is not in the spec). **A filtered `recall_recent` now delivers the COMPLETE matching set to the user unconditionally** — measured on the motivating request: **47,077 chars to the user, 5,875 to the model**, one call, no paging. The model's context cost is flat in the row count (`full_delivery_model_cost_is_flat_in_row_count` asserts it directly). Unfiltered recall stays a characterisation (counts are the answer, no bulk). `full: true` forces delivery for the unfiltered case too. **The user's streamed view is NOT capped at the model's ration** — that coupling (added a day earlier to stop the UI flagging TRUNCATED on results the model saw whole) capped what a person could see at what a 4B model could read; honesty is now carried by `model_saw_chars` on the event ("showing all 47,077 characters; the model read the first 5,875"), not by degrading the view. (2026-09-12)
- **★ When a behaviour MUST happen, do not make it a decision.** The delivery above was first gated on `full: true` with a system-prompt rule telling the worker when to use it — ignored. Then on an in-band advisory naming both options at the exact moment of the choice — also ignored; the worker answered that showing all 50 notes "would be impractical", **deciding on the user's behalf not to show them**. And the intent could not have survived anyway: the front door paraphrased *"I want to see all of what we learned"* into *"Search all stored notes for information related to video learning"*. **A small orchestrator rewriting a request into a `task` string is a lossy channel for anything that is not a question** — an imperative about *presentation* does not survive it, so anything load-bearing about presentation must be structural, not phrased. Guessing intent from wording only moves the guess; unconditional delivery cannot fail because nothing has to notice anything. (2026-09-12)

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Self-knowledge: making running state visible (part 4/5)
content:
- **★ The tool-result cap is now DERIVED from the allowlist in play (`tool_result_budget`, `clients/chat/tool_results.rs`), not a constant — and a result that asserts its own completeness must be sized for the channel that carries it.** `CLOUD_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` (2000) was sized for `general` (46 tools, ~33K chars of schema resent every round) and then applied unchanged to a `knowledge-worker` sub-agent whose 12 schemas are ~11K against E4B's 16384-token window (observed peak 8080 `tokens_in`). Budget = `(context_window × 0.35 × 4 chars/token) - schema_chars`, clamped to `[2000, 8000]` — or to 120K once the window is genuinely large. **It reads `context_window` from the DuckDB catalog**, because the first version was model-blind: a fixed 24,000-char allowance whether the loop drove E4B at 16384 tokens or a 1M-token cloud model, so a sub-agent was rationed like a small local model even when the orchestrator had a million tokens. Measured live, measured live, the 11-tool worker and 8-tool front door both went 2000 → **8000** while a 46-tool profile still clamps to 2000. Logged at INFO per loop — it is the number that explains the symptom and was invisible before. The display preview uses the SAME budget, or the UI shows `TRUNCATED` on results the model received whole. Why: on 2026-09-12 `recall_recent` returned `complete: true, returned: 41` + "These are ALL the notes matching the filter — summarise from it directly" in a 6254-char payload of which the worker saw 2000; it relayed the clip honestly ("not the complete list") and the user was told the graph could not produce what it had already produced. **`complete: true` plus a truncation marker is a contradiction the model always resolves pessimistically.** (2026-09-12)
- **★ Pagination is the honest answer to "show me more"; a bigger page is not.** `recall_recent` takes **`offset`** and returns `next_offset`/`seen_through` — raising `sample_limit` past the caller's channel does not enumerate more, it only moves where the clipping falls, so "show me all 50 video-learning notes" had no answer at any setting. Defaults are now picked by **measuring serialised bytes against the consumer's budget**: a sample row is ~450 chars unfiltered / ~850 filtered, so the old 24/50 produced 10562/14000+ (clipped before leaving the building) and 12 lands at 7227/5194 against 8000. Fewer rows that arrive whole beat more rows that arrive cut. Behavioural half: `A TRUNCATED RESULT IS NOT A MISSING ONE` in `contexts/knowledge-worker.yaml`. Guards: `recall_recent_forwards_offset`, `recall_recent_schema_steers_to_paging_not_a_bigger_limit`, `a_lean_allowlist_earns_the_full_tool_result_budget`, `a_large_allowlist_is_squeezed_back_to_the_floor`. (2026-09-12)
- **★ When a filter value belongs to the OTHER slot, say so by name — the escape hatch needs its own escape hatch.** A worker called `recall_recent(note_type:"video_learning", source_context:"video_learning")`, matched nothing, received `available_source_contexts: [{video_learning: 50}]` in the zero-match response, **and still reported that no video-learning notes existed**. `recall_recent` now detects a value absent from one slot's vocabulary but present in the other's and leads with `filter_error`: *"'video_learning' IS NOT A note_type — it is a source_context, and it has notes. Retry as recall_recent(source_context:…) with NO note_type."* Showing the caller a list it must still reason over is weaker than naming its exact mistake — and this is the mistake that manufactures a false absence. (2026-09-12)
- **A query-less `search_notes` enumeration that matches nothing names the labels that DO exist** — `graph_total_notes` + `available_note_types` + `available_source_contexts` via `KnowledgeService::label_buckets` (the unbounded sibling of `window_buckets`), plus a note saying the LABEL is the likely fault. The `recall_recent` drill-down fix of 2026-09-11 landed in one tool and not its sibling, so a guessed `note_type`/`source_context` still came back as a bare `count: 0` — indistinguishable from an empty graph. A delegated `researcher` probed `note_type:"agent"`, `source_context:"agent"`, then `note_type:"news"`, learned nothing from three consecutive misses, and reported it could not determine the answer. **Ship a doctrine to every tool that shares its shape, not just the one that failed.** Guards: `empty_enumeration_names_the_labels_that_exist`, `non_empty_enumeration_carries_no_absence_hint`. (2026-09-12)
- **★ A health or status report gets windowed counts, never all-time totals (2026-10-02).** `list_tasks` returns all-time totals; the health monitor fed them to `reason`, which read "428 failed" (9 in the past week) as current and reported the brain's health as "poor … systemic instability", and the daily brief printed the same number as "last 24 h". `workflows/health-monitor.yaml` is now one query whose every row names its window (`jobs_24h`, `tasks_finished_24h`/`_7d`, `tasks_open_now`, `failed_task_24h` with its `[FAILURE]` reason, `dead_job_24h`) and a prompt that compares 24h against the 7-day baseline; the brief's status block is windowed the same way. Also: only the IMMEDIATELY preceding step reaches `{{_prev}}`, so the old monitor's job counts and dead letters never reached its `reason` step at all (an earlier step's output is `{{steps.<id>}}` since 2026-10-10). Housekeeping that closes stale tasks leaves `updated_at` alone so it does not read as a failure spike.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Self-knowledge: making running state visible (part 5/5)
content:
- **`neo4j_query` now has a schema-aware read-boundary guard** (`services/cypher_guard.rs`, the read analogue of `services/validation.rs` — structural, not semantic; a linter over a known bad-set, never a prover). In **readonly** mode an unknown label or relationship type is a **Hard** reject (the message names the valid set; skipped for writes, since `CREATE`ing a new label is legal — the empty-but-valid-label case is the one caveat). An unknown property on a bound `var:Label`, and the datetime-vs-string literal anti-pattern, are **Soft** (advisory `warning` in the result envelope — `db.schema.nodeTypeProperties()` only reports properties present on ≥1 node, so a brand-new optional property must not hard-block). Fails open: no live schema ⇒ guard does not run. Plan: `project-docs/GRAPH_SCHEMA_GUARD_PLAN.md`.

Full story (the "conceptual blueprint" incident, all markers, the Nebula/Meshtastic case, the delegated-recall false negative): history § Self-knowledge.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › System health, logs, registry (`clients/system.rs`, 2026-10-08)
content:
- **One call answers "is the machine all right?"** That call is `GET /api/system/health`. It probes every service in the core bundle's `architecture/components.yaml` in parallel with a 3 s timeout, then adds the scheduler, the queue, the GPU lease, provider budgets and the running version. It returns `issues` worst first, so the UI never derives what is wrong itself.
- **A new dependency is a YAML entry, not code.** Give it a `name`, a `label`, a `probe` (`neo4j` | `duckdb` | `http`), a `url_env` plus a `path` (and an optional `strip_suffix`), and `required` when the brain is broken without it. An unset `url_env` is *not configured*, never *down*: the brain runs without optional sidecars. The response shows endpoints as scheme://host:port only, with no path and no credentials.
- **Logs are about the machine.** `GET /api/logs` filters by `level`, `target` (prefixes, `-prefix` to drop), `quiet` (prefixes shown only at WARN or above), `q` and `after`, and reports `matched`, `buffered` and `oldest`, so a capped page says it is capped and how far back the buffer reaches. The buffer holds 2,000 lines (500 covered about an hour). The HBI's "hide routine activity" quiets the scheduler, queue, skills, chat and knowledge-write modules (`ACTIVITY_TARGETS` in `hbi-frontend/src/api/system.ts`); their warnings and errors always show. Tasks and jobs belong in Work, not Logs.
- **Registry is read-only.** `GET /api/system/registry` lists skills and their tools, declared tools (with their bundle), agents, chains, MCP servers (whether each one's secret env var is set, never the secret), providers and the component list. Edits go through Settings.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › The brain's sense of time (`services/clock.rs`)
content: **Everything stored stays UTC; everything said is local.** Local time needs both `TZ`/`BRAIN_TIMEZONE` in the env *and* code asking for local (both failures silent) — `log_resolved_timezone()` warns at startup when unconfigured. Resolution: `BRAIN_TIMEZONE` → `TZ` → `/etc/localtime` → UTC. `TZ` on `agent-brain` only, not `neo4j`. The four date-producing call sites (chat prompt, both scheduler substitution sites, constructor) are local; `services/sleep.rs` keeps UTC for filenames. `now_stamp()` renders a fully-qualified instant per turn; `{{now}}`/`{{weekday}}` template vars; `label_claims` appends humanised age. Behavioural half: `TIME RULE` in `contexts/general.yaml`. Full story: history § sense of time.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Tool-integrated reasoning (`execute_code` + `sandbox` sidecar)
content:
Lets a step *compute* its figures instead of hallucinating them; a wrong number becomes a traceback. **Execution never happens in the brain process** — `skills/exec.rs` is an HTTP client for the `sandbox` compose service. Isolation contract (in `docker-compose.yml`): **`sandbox-net` is `internal: true`** (no egress — the only real boundary), no `env_file` (no creds), no bind mounts, `read_only` root, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `mem_limit: 2g`, `pids_limit: 128`, tmpfs `/tmp` `noexec`. **Do not put `sandbox` on `brain-internal` and do not add a `ports:` mapping.** Per-run limits in `sandbox/server.py`. **A failed run is a successful tool call** (`isError: false`, traceback in `stderr`) — a tool *error* would burn a retry and fail the owning Task. No state between calls; pass all input inline. `numpy`/`sympy`/`pandas` installed at build time (no run-time network). Routing: `computation` capability held by **`qwen2.5-coder:7b` alone** (`selection_rank 150`); `execute_code` in `general`/`self-analyst` allowlists. Behavioural half: `COMPUTATION RULE`.

**Rust goes through the same tool: `execute_code(language: "rust")` → the `rust-sandbox` service** (`RUST_SANDBOX_URL`). Takes `code` (a `main.rs`, `cargo run`) or `files` (a crate as path→content, default `cargo test`), plus `command` (`test`/`check`/`clippy`/`fmt`/`run`/`build`) and `include_ignored`; the result adds `tests_passed`/`tests_failed`/`compile_failed`, and for clippy `lint_findings` (one per diagnostic with a `-->` source location — clippy exits 0 on warnings, so the exit code says nothing). `fmt` runs `cargo fmt --check`: exit 1 + the diff on stdout, nothing rewritten. rust-analyzer is deliberately absent: it is a language server for a live editor session, and its one-shot `diagnostics` mode adds little over `check` + `clippy` on a single-request crate. A language is only offered in the schema when its sandbox URL is set, and `language` defaults to `python` so existing callers are unchanged. **Same isolation contract, two deliberate differences:** its `/work` tmpfs is **exec** (Rust must run the test binaries it compiles), and crates come from a **read-only cache fetched at image build** from `rust-sandbox/crates/Cargo.toml` with cargo run `--offline` — an uncached crate fails to resolve and the server appends the available list. The linker needs `TMPDIR`/`HOME` inside the writable scratch or it fails `Cannot create temporary file in ./: Read-only file system`. It runs as UID **10001**, not 1000, because `RLIMIT_NPROC` counts per real UID kernel-wide (the Python `sandbox` still shares UID 1000 with the host user). Built for `project-docs/RUST_FINETUNE_EXPERIMENT.md`. Full story: history § Tool-integrated reasoning.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Topics (`services/topics.rs`, 2026-10-08) (part 1/3)
content:
The domains the brain tracks. Schema: `schema.md` § Topic, plan: `HBI_REDESIGN_PLAN.md` §3. History: `engineering-history.md` § Topics.
- **Declared in YAML, assigned by the local model.** Every loaded bundle's `topics/*.yaml` (the core's, then plugins'; `_scope.yaml` from the core only) has one topic per file, and its `description` *is* the classifier's definition. Embedding centroids were measured and rejected (F1 0.61 against hand labels, against 0.83 held-out for the classifier). Sharpen a description with what does *not* belong ("general AI knowledge is ai-ml, not agent-brain"); that is what fixed the confusions. All descriptions share one local-model prompt, so keep each short (the test caps the shipped prompt at 3.2k chars; an HBI edit may take it to 3.6k).
- **Main topic first, a second only if it is as central**, at most 2 (`IN_TOPIC.rank`). Asking for "0–3 topics" over-tagged national security onto every war and government story.
- **Every note is accounted for.** Each top-level note is in a topic, assessed as fitting none, waiting, failed (3 tries), or skipped by `topics/_scope.yaml`. `GET /api/topics` returns those counts and they sum to the total. Don't add a filter that drops notes from all five buckets.
- **Skip rules compare coalesced values.** `n.source_context = 'x'` is null for a note without one, `NOT any(…)` is then null too, and the note silently leaves every bucket. That happened (5 notes stuck "waiting"). `SKIPPED_CYPHER` coalesces both sides.
- **The assigner runs only while the brain is idle** (no job `queued`/`running`, no GPU lease). It re-checks every 5 notes, runs batches back to back while idle, and is started only by the HTTP `serve`. `TOPIC_ASSIGNER_ENABLED=false` stops it. The model call is about 0.3 s, but end to end (reads, writes, idle checks) it measured about 56 notes a minute on 2026-10-09, so the whole graph (~13.7k notes) takes about 4 hours of idle time.
- **The version is a hash of every name, description and skip rule.** Changing any of them re-classifies everything. Labels and `source_lists:` don't count. Topics from a plugin that is off (dormant) still count, so a plugin toggle re-classifies nothing; the classifier leaves a note's edges to them alone (`dev_docs get plugins/loader`). A note the scope newly skips loses its old topics at the next `init-db`.
- **Activity records are skipped, not classified.** `scheduler_dispatch` episodic notes are a goal plus a task id. Classified, they landed in the goal's topic and buried what was learned.
- **The YAML seeds; the graph owns** (HBI plan Phase 14). `Topics::global()` is the graph's set, reloaded after every edit (`topics::reload`), so an HBI edit applies from the assigner's next batch, with no restart.
  - An HBI edit makes the topic `managed_by: runtime`, and the sync then skips it. This is the schedule rule: check `managed_by` before assuming the file is what runs. Reset puts the file's definition back.
  - Deleting a seeded topic leaves a `(:RetiredTopic)`, so `init-db` does not recreate it. A delete also clears `topics_version` on that topic's notes: a reset brings back the same version, and a note still stamped with it would look classified without its topic.
  - `init-db` syncs topics **before** seeding schedules, because a schedule's `topic` is checked against them.
- **An edit is checked before it is written** (`topics::check_def`):
  - the name is a 2–40 character slug, set once, and `map` and `new` are reserved;
  - a description is at most 500 characters;
  - the whole classifier prompt stays at most 3,600 characters;
  - a delete is refused while a schedule declares the topic, and the refusal names the schedules.
- **A topic about the user, or one of their programs, is assigned by rules, not by the classifier** (`assign: rules` + `members:` in its YAML or the HBI form). The model can't tell whose career or which agency a note is about, and a topic in its prompt that is small and personal draws notes that fit nothing else. Measured in Phases 14–15:
  - `career` took anyone's career: 22 of 56 other people's notes kept it, even with "any other person's career … is not career".
  - Renamed `my-job-search`, it halved that on the sample of Career's own notes. Live, all of the first 13 notes it took were strays: a murder trial, an Uber case, a news brief.
  - "intelligence agency" took CIA and FBI stories, and `nia` took the brain's daily stats reports and GDELT summaries.
  - **How a rules topic works:** it is left out of the prompt, so the model can't pick it even by name. A note joins by a `members` rule (`note_type` / `source_context` exactly, `content_contains` case-insensitively in the first 1,500 characters), ranked first, or by hand. The rules are part of the version hash. `topics::reload` applies them at once in Cypher (mirroring `MemberRule::matches`) and drops classifier edges on rules topics, so a rules topic doesn't wait for the hours-long re-classify.
  - **The name still matters** for a classifier topic. Test a new or renamed one on a sample against the sidecar before saving it, and include notes that fit **no** topic in the sample. Phase 14's sample left them out, and missed exactly the failure that showed up live.
- **A program is not a subject.** The NIA's monitors declare `topic: nia`, but their reports are classified by what they are about: a Trump-deal assessment is us-politics or geopolitics. The `nia` topic holds the notes that name the program. The schedule topic mix shows this as a mismatch, and the mismatch is true.
- **The user's word is final** (Phase 15):
  - **Note topics:** topics set in the note drawer are `method: 'manual'` and the note is `topics_locked`. The classifier never picks it, and `topics::reload` stamps it with each new version, so it never counts as waiting. "Let the classifier decide" unlocks it. Deleting a topic unlocks that topic's notes.
  - **Entity hides:** `(:Entity)-[:NOT_IN_TOPIC]->(:Topic)` keeps an entity off that topic's map and entity lists, whatever its notes say. The map, the topic drawer and the entity drawer each show the hides with undo. A merge carries the hides to the surviving entity.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Topics (`services/topics.rs`, 2026-10-08) (part 2/3)
content:
- **How entities relate is computed from shared notes** (`clients/related.rs`, Phase 16; no entity→entity edges exist until Phase 17).
  - **Rank by strength, never by raw count.** Strength is shared notes ÷ √((mentions A + 3) × (mentions B + 3)). Raw counts put C-SPAN (184 notes) first for 30 of the 300 entities it shares notes with; strength puts it first for 1. The +3 keeps two entities that share their only note from scoring a perfect 1.0. `strength` in Rust and `STRENGTH_CYPHER` must stay the same formula (a test checks them together).
  - **Every pair drills to its notes** (`/api/entities/pair`). A topic scope counts only that topic's notes and leaves out entities the user keeps out of it.
- **Claims get their entities from an idle-time loop, not at write time.** `store_claim` writes in raw Cypher, so before Phase 16 none of the 4,546 claims had a `MENTIONS` edge, and no entity view could see the most entity-dense notes. `spawn_claim_entity_backfill` takes claims with no mentions and no `entities_at`, newest first, and stamps every one, so it covers the backlog and each new claim (`CLAIM_ENTITY_BACKFILL=false` stops it).
  - **Claims use their own prompt.** With the general extraction prompt the local model answered `[]` for 22 of 30 claims, most of which name someone; the claim prompt left 5 of the same 30 empty, and those name nothing. The general prompt is unchanged, because it hasn't been measured on long notes.
- **Typed relationships** (Phase 17; the epistemics plugin's since Phase 4 pack 6: `relations.rs`, routes under `/api/plugins/epistemics/`): `(:Entity)-[:RELATES {type, method, status, evidence}]->(:Entity)`. The core's pair view and map no longer read them; the HBI asks the plugin (`relations/between`, `relations/among`) and shows none when it is off. The merge list's "related" answers (`RELATED_ENTITY`, core) are folded in by the plugin at start and before each read.
  - **A closed vocabulary** in the epistemics bundle's `relations.yaml`. Each type has a definition, a label and its inverse ("works for" / "employs"), and the entity types allowed at each end. Many real things are typed `concept`, so the "thing" ends allow it. `related_to` is the user's only (`extract: false`), and the merge list's "related" answers fold into it.
  - **The user's edges are final; extracted ones are proposals.** Accept makes one active, reject keeps it as `rejected`, and `propose` never revives a rejected edge (it only counts `seen_again`). Removing the user's own deletes it. Relabelling removes the old type (rejecting an extracted one) and sets the new one as the user's, with the old evidence.
  - **Extraction runs on the cloud, measured first.** The local Gemma-4-E4B got 2 of 8 relations right on the tuning set, and with stricter prompts it answered `[]` even for its own prompt's example. On 30 fresh held-out claims, gpt-oss:120b-cloud was right 8 of 9 times leniently and 5 of 9 strictly. So `workflows/relation-extraction.yaml` pins `model: gpt-oss:120b-cloud` (`no_log`, $0), and its proposals wait for review (Work → Feed → relationships to review).
  - **The prompt's examples are the measured failures:** something belonging to an entity ("a Ford plant in Mexico") taken for the entity, a forum's location taken for its host's, and a refused or alleged relationship taken as stated. `validate` drops anything naming an entity the claim doesn't mention, a type outside the vocabulary or a user-only one, an entity related to itself, and ends of the wrong type, and the tool reports each drop with its reason.
  - **Keep a measurement set frozen.** Claims gain entities while the backfill runs, so a sample drawn by query shifts between runs. The Phase 17 script saves its sample on first use.
- **Reference links** (`plugins/reference/crate/src/wiki.rs`, Phase 18): `(:Entity)-[:REFERS_TO {status, method}]->(:WikiItem {qid})`, which Wikidata item and English Wikipedia article an entity is.
  - **Background lookups cover only entities a claim mentions.** A lookup sends the entity's name to Wikimedia, and names also come from the résumé, job-search chats and other private notes. Claims come from videos, articles and news. `source_record` does not count, because the résumé is stored as one. `link_entities` without `entity_id` selects only claim-mentioned entities, and with `entity_id` but no `on_demand` it returns `skipped_private` without calling anyone. The drawer's "Look up" sets `on_demand`.
  - **The model chooses from the search, never the top result.** Wikidata's top hit was wrong 13 of 37 times (DRM → Digital Radio Mondiale, PNG → the image format). `pick_prompt` gives the candidates with their kinds and up to 3 claims, says the filed type may be wrong (the racehorse Shergar is typed `person`), and asks for 0 when unsure.
  - **The second search is for named things only.** When the model answers 0, it may suggest up to 2 search terms. That found garbled and short names (Pento Barbatale → pentobarbital, Kapo → Estonia's Internal Security Service). But for `concept`, `event` and `programme` entities it found a match that wasn't there: "system intelligence" → AGI, a makemore video → WaveNet, "Cuomo Full Show" → CNN's old Cuomo Prime Time. So those types never get one.
  - **Nationality words still slip through.** "Italian" → Italy, and "Chinese" → the People's Liberation Army through the second search, despite the prompt's rule. Picks are proposals; the drawer's "Not this" rejects one for good.
  - **Wikidata labels may be `mul`, not `en`.** Many items keep their name only as a language-neutral `mul` label (Albert Einstein has no English one), so every request asks for `en|mul`.
  - **One request at a time, with a contact.** Three parallel lookups drew HTTP 429, then a 41 s `Retry-After`. All Wikimedia calls go through one gate: serialised, at least 1.1 s apart, a 429 pauses every lookup for its `Retry-After`, and the run ends early saying so. `WIKIMEDIA_CONTACT` (in the user agent) is required; without it nothing is looked up, and the HBI says so.
  - **One place pins the model.** The drawer's "Look up" enqueues the `entity-linking` schedule's own `link_entities` step with `{entity_id, on_demand: true}`, so its `model: gpt-oss:120b-cloud` pin and the routing policy apply as for the hourly run.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Topics (`services/topics.rs`, 2026-10-08) (part 3/3)
content:
- **Two entities on one item are a merge candidate** (`reason: wikidata`), and the alias judge gives it a verdict like any other. A pair the user already answered (`NOT_SAME`, `RELATED_ENTITY`) is not proposed again, even when they share an item (MSS ↔ Ministry of State Security).
  - **Topics get a URL, not a lookup.** Most topics are the user's own groupings with no article, so `reference` is set in the topic form or YAML. It is outside the topic `version`, so editing it classifies nothing again.
- **Kinds** (`plugins/reference/crate/src/kinds.rs`, Phase 19): `entity_type` stays the coarse class the extractor gives; `kind` is the fine one (country, municipality, news outlet…), derived from the reference link.
  - **Derived, not judged.** The linked WikiItem's instance-of classes are walked up subclass-of to the roots in `plugins/reference/kinds.yaml`. The **nearest** root wins (ties: file order), and a `fallback` kind (organisation, website, product) only when no specific kind is reachable. Matching in file order over the whole tree made YouTube an event and every U.S. state a country; a fallback that could win at hop 0 made the WSJ a website. Wikidata's upper ontology is tangled, so keep roots narrow: "geographic location" (Q2221906) took the PRC government.
  - **A disagreement is a question, never a retype.** A link's kind applies only when its coarse type agrees with the filed one (decision §12.7.1: proposed links too). Otherwise `type_question_qid` is set and the Feed shows "entity types to check". On the first 226 items, a quarter of the disagreements came from wrong links.
  - **The user's type is final.** `type_source: manual` (set in the drawer, or by answering "keep" / "use the reference") stops the extraction vote (`entities.rs`) and the questions. "Let the brain decide" removes it and re-runs the vote. A seed's type stays fixed. "Keep" remembers the item in `type_kept_qids`, so that link never asks again.
