  - **Wikimedia pages are never references.** A candidate whose class label starts "Wikimedia " (disambiguation, set index, list) is dropped before the model sees it, a pasted URL to one is refused, and a proposed link to an item whose classes reach a `refuse` root is withdrawn.
  - **Classes are cached** as `(:WikiClass)` through the Wikimedia gate. `link_entities` refreshes kinds after its lookups (at most 60 requests a run; an incomplete walk waits for the next), and a link decision in the drawer refreshes that entity. `link_entities {limit: 0}` refreshes kinds only.
  - **`link_entities {limit: 0}` only refreshes kinds** (it clamped to 1 until Phase 21).
  - **Editing `kinds.yaml` re-derives every kind** (its hash is `kind_version`), from the cache. It shares `entities/` with the alias seed, whose loader ignores its keys; don't give it a top-level `types`, `titles`, `articles`, `keep_distinct` or `entities` key.
- **`wiki_background`** (`plugins/reference/crate/src/background.rs`, Phase 21) reads Wikipedia for a question: named subjects only, each article picked from Wikidata's candidates, then its lead, best-matching section and most-cited domains. **It is not in the gap chain:** three measured rounds failed to show a gain that held up twice, and the free cloud quota it needs (up to 5 calls a gap) is shared with `entity-linking` (HBI plan Phase 21 outcome, v2 and v3). If it is ever wired in, make the step `optional: true`: a refused step model dead-letters on the first attempt and would cancel the gap. Measure any v2 with `scripts/replay_gap_wikipedia.py` on `eval/gap_wikipedia_replay.json` before wiring it in, and remember that the reason step's 3,000-character distillation squeezed the background out entirely.
  - **Replaying gaps needs the old answers removed:** past runs stored "## Gap synthesis" notes, 1–7 per question, which `search_notes` hands straight back.
  - **Two runs of one query differ.** 2 of 8 same-query pairs differed materially, so compare arms on more cases or repeated runs.

subsystem: Web Search: engine failover ladder + usage ledger
title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Web Search: engine failover ladder + usage ledger (part 1/2)
content:
**★ Google syntax works on every engine, and `recency` replaces dates in queries (2026-10-02).** `skills/search_query.rs` parses Google's documented operators (`"phrase"`, `-word`, `-"phrase"`, `site:`, `-site:`, `filetype:`, `after:`, `before:`, `OR`, `(site:a OR site:b)` grouping) into a `QuerySpec`, and each engine renders what it reads: the Google family (SerpApi, Serper, CSE) gets the operators plus `tbs=qdr:`/`dateRestrict`; Google News gets `when:Nd`; Brave gets operators minus dates plus `freshness`; SearXNG gets operators but **no `time_range`** — it would drop every backend that cannot date-filter (Naver alone answered; news fell from 54 results to 2), so `searxng_items` enforces the window from each result's `publishedDate` and keeps undated ones; **Exa and Tavily read no operators**, so domains, dates, news and a short phrase become `includeDomains`/`excludeDomains`/`startPublishedDate`/`category`/`includeText`/`excludeText` (Exa) and `include_domains`/`exclude_domains`/`time_range`/`start_date`/`topic`/`exact_match` (Tavily). `search_web` takes `recency` (`day`/`week`/`month`/`year`) and `news: true`; a `source_list` becomes `site:` / include-domains on the spec. Why: Google News ranks by relevance, so the brief's "… today" queries returned months-old pages (0 of 8 current for world news on 10-02), while Exa news with a one-day window returned CNBC, Al Jazeera, France24 and Politico from that day; and `site:reuters.com` sent to Exa was searched as the word "site". **Write "latest …" plus `recency`, never a literal date** (a date over-constrains). The daily brief uses `engine: exa`, `recency: day`, `news: true`; the monitors carry `recency` matched to their cadence. An empty result still falls through the ladder, so a window too narrow for a niche query spends the keyed engines' quotas — keep daily monitors at `week`.


`search_web` walks an ordered **ladder** (`SEARCH_ENGINE_ORDER`, default the engines' `rank` order: `exa,tavily,tinyfish,serper,serpapi,google,searxng,brave`) until one answers **with results**. **Since 2026-10-16 the ladder's head is chosen by rotation** across the engines with a `budget` (paced free allowances); the ladder is the fallback behind it: `dev_docs search "search rotation"`.

**★ Engines are data (CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN 6c, 2026-10-11).** Each engine is a YAML file in a bundle's `search-engines/` dir (`plugins/core/search-engines/*.yaml`): endpoint, method, auth, `key_env`, parameter names, fixed and news parameters, result path and field mapping, snippet cap, spent-quota signals (`spent_status`, `spent_words`), a 200-with-`error` field, `limits` (window days, domains, filetype), `quota_group`, and `rank` (ladder position; none = explicit only). One executor, `skills/search_engines.rs::run`, calls them all. What cannot be data is a named hook the file picks: `syntax` (query rendering), `dialect` (Exa/Tavily/tbs/CSE/Brave dates, Currents and Webz builders) and `shape` (Google News clusters, SearXNG window + `unresponsive_engines`). A new engine that answers a plain result list is a YAML file and a key. Keys come from env vars only (empty counts as unset), not from `ApiContext` nodes.

- **Keyed engines are ordered by how they fail when spent:** monthly-refilling, no-card allowances first (Exa, then Tavily — Exa surfaced the primary source on 4 of 5 probe queries where Tavily returned blog posts, 2026-09-26), then Serper's one-time 2,500, then SerpApi (whose quota `google_news` needs), then Google CSE (closed to new customers, ends 2027-01-01) and Brave (card, no cap). Every engine maps to `{title, link, snippet, date}` (Google News adds `source`), and a spent allowance is reported as "quota exhausted" from the file's `spent_status`/`spent_words`, because none of the vendors uses a 429 for it (Exa 402, Tavily 432/433, Serper "Not enough credits"). **Every key must be passed through in `docker-compose.yml`** — the brain has no `env_file`, so a key only in `.env` never reaches it (Brave and Google never had a pass-through before 2026-09-26).

subsystem: Web Search: engine failover ladder + usage ledger
title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Web Search: engine failover ladder + usage ledger (part 2/2)
content:
- **★ `searxng` is the flagged last resort, not the lead (2026-10-06).** It always answers *something*, so leading with it starved the keyed engines (720 SearXNG searches vs 0 Tavily/Serper in a week), and with Google/Bing/DDG CAPTCHA-blocked its answers come from Naver, Seznam and Zapmeta: weaker relevance, undated, foreign-index pages. When it answers, the result leads with a `⚠ SEARXNG FALLBACK` banner naming each keyed engine passed over and why (and a date caveat when `recency` was asked), plus a WARN `Search answered by SearXNG fallback`. A caller that parses the result array must strip it with `web_result::strip_fallback_banner` (the claim verifier does, and records `searxng_fallback` on its output and evidence note). **Brave stays behind SearXNG**: card on file, no spend cap. The sidecar itself: self-hosted, no key/quota; `brain-internal` only, disabled `limiter` — do not add a `ports:` mapping without re-enabling it; keep `json` in `search.formats`). A **requested `engine:` is promoted, not made exclusive.** **Quota cooldown** (`QUOTA_COOLDOWN_HOURS` 6) moves an exhausted engine to the back, not out. Results normalised to `link`/`snippet`. Every attempt writes a `search_usage` row; `get_search_usage` reports per-engine + per-day.
- **★ Currents and Webz are NOT in the ladder — explicit `engine:` only (2026-10-06).** Measured on the brain's own schedule queries (intel monitor, Michigan brief, SLM watch, hardware tripwire; 7-day news): Currents ANDs every keyword and returned **0** for all four; Webz returned QAnon-style, partisan and off-topic pages (Michigan politics → Bangladesh and Nigeria), **no result from any SourceList**, and `domain_rank:<1000` left 0. Because a non-empty answer ends the ladder, leading with them displaced Exa — which answered the same intel query with AP, NBC, ABC and NPR. They had led news searches for about an hour before this was measured and reverted. Still usable when named: Currents for short specific queries, Webz restricted by `site:`/`source_list`. Rules that still apply when they run: Currents takes one include/exclude domain and ≤ 8-day windows clamped to 7 (`limits` in their files; `search_engines::currents_params`); Webz ≤ 31 days clamped to 30, 5 results (prepaid ~$0.01/result). **Measure an engine on the brain's real queries, classed by SourceList, before putting it in the ladder.** The same holds for a SourceList: `national-security` and `semiconductors` (2026-10-06) were each run against their schedule's real queries, current setup vs proposed, before any schedule used them. Engine errors pass through `redact` (Webz echoes its token).
- **Search-results pages are dropped from every engine's answer, before it is counted** (`drop_search_pages`, check in `services/web_result.rs::is_search_page`). `ecosia.org/search?q=…`-style pages restate the query in their snippet; an answer made only of them counts as empty and the ladder moves on. A `search` path segment counts only with a query string or a further segment after it (`/wiki/Search` is an article). The claim verifier additionally drops results whose snippet contains the whole claim (`drop_echo_results`).
- **An engine with no credentials is dropped from the ladder outright, not demoted** (`search_engines::configured` + `retain_configured` in `engine_ladder`). Unlike a spent quota (which recovers overnight, so demote), a missing key never fixes itself at runtime, and it fails `not_configured` on *every* call — the 2026-09-08 GDELT session put `engine: google` on each search with no `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, wasting the first rung and a WARN line on every one and helping exhaust the 8-round chat budget twice. `searxng` declares no key (always kept); `google` needs `key_env` **and** its `env_params` CX; `serpapi`/`google_news` share one key. An **empty** env var counts as unset: compose passes `BRAVE_API_KEY=${BRAVE_API_KEY:-}`, and before 6c an empty value counted as configured, so keyless Brave burned a failing rung. Never empties the ladder: if nothing is configured the original is kept so the caller still gets a real per-engine error. An unknown engine name is assumed configured. Guards: `unconfigured_engines_are_dropped_from_the_ladder` + siblings in `search.rs` tests; the files themselves in `search_engines.rs` tests.
- **Zero results is not an answer** — a rung returning `200` + empty falls through to the next; if *all* rungs come back empty, return `[]` (erroring would burn retries). Fall-through logged at WARN.
- **SerpApi signals failure as HTTP 200 + `{"error":…}`, not a 4xx/5xx** (quota, rate, "couldn't get valid results"). Their files declare `error_field: error`, so the executor checks it and return it as a real failure (raw message → `classify_search_error` → the ladder WARNs, records the right `error_kind`, and demotes on quota). Before this fix (2026-09-08) that response was read as `success` with 0 results and the ladder fell through to SearXNG **silently** — a real SerpApi outage looked like success in the logs and over-counted `serpapi` in the ledger. A genuinely-empty result with no `error` field is still a real empty (falls through with the zero-results WARN, no cooldown). **`unresponsive_engines` in the JSON is the diagnostic** (distinguishes "cannot connect" from "connected and refused"); `scripts/searxng_engine_health.py` probes both evergreen and fresh query shapes. **Never probe a single engine with `&engines=<name>`** (silent fallback to the default set); attribute by each result's own `engine` field. A relevance failure cannot be caught by a count.
- **News: `engine: "google_news"`** (`google_news.yaml`, SerpApi `engine=google_news`, `shape: google_news`). SerpApi free tier is **250/month** (not 100); `serpapi`+`google_news` share one account (`quota_group: serpapi`: the ladder demotes both when either is exhausted). No `source_list` on Google News steps. `google_news` is **not** in the default ladder. **Query rewriting was investigated and rejected** (null result — the queries were never the problem; the blocked engines were). **Quota exhaustion alerts** (`is_quota_exhausted_error`, deduped `:AgentNotification` once/tool/24h).

Full story (the four outages — DNS/empty results, bot-blocks, junk results — and the query-rewriting A/B): history § Web Search.

title: Architecture: subsystem rules › Worker/voice split + write guard
content:
`CHAT_SYNTHESIS_PROVIDER`/`CHAT_SYNTHESIS_MODEL` enable the split: the worker (`CHAT_LLM_MODEL`) runs the tool loop (its prose emitted as `Thinking`) — and with the voice on, the round loop passes no token sink, so the worker's content is never streamed as `Token`s (streaming it sent the user two answers, the worker's then the voice's; fixed 2026-10-02 for every provider), the voice model composes the reply from the gathered results (passed as an argument, not scraped from history). Runs on the cloud path via `config_for_catalog_entry`; replaces `NO_ANSWER_AFTER_TOOLS_MESSAGE`.

- **Ground-truth tool receipt (`tool_trace_receipt`, `clients/chat/loop_policy.rs`) — the chat-loop analogue of `AgentFindings.tool_trace`.** The shared round loop tracks every tool call this turn (`(name, success)`) and inject a receipt — the ONLY tools that ran, in order — at the tools-off wrap-up (appended to `FINAL_ROUND_NUDGE`) **and** at the top of the synthesis prompt. The worker's own prose is relabelled in that prompt as UNVERIFIED ("may describe actions that never ran"). This exists because on 2026-09-08 a turn asked to "find and use the GDELT API" reported it had probed the API (blocked by "the sandbox"), was drafting a Python client, and would register it — while the only tools that ran were `search_notes`+`search_web`: **no `http_request` (which runs in the brain and HAS egress — the sandbox story was fabricated), no `execute_code`, no `ingest_api`.** The worker's fabricated wrap-up was then handed to the voice model as "initial analysis" and polished into the answer the user saw. The receipt states plainly that anything absent did not happen, so the composer can no longer launder an invented action. It anchors the answer; it is not a hard block. (The GDELT request also failed for a real reason: the `researcher` sub-agent's allowlist was `search_web`-only — no `http_request`/`ingest_api` — so a delegated "find and ingest an API" could not physically run; both were added to `contexts/researcher.yaml`.)

**★ One round loop for every provider (`clients/chat/round_loop.rs`, 2026-10-02).** A provider implements only `ProviderTurn` (one call, append the assistant turn, append tool results); the guard, the derived tool-result budget and markers, the receipt, empty-completion retries, malformed-call correction, the tools-off wrap-up round, the voice split and the no-answer report live in `run_round_loop` once. They were four copies and had drifted: the Gemini text loop fed tool results to the model raw (no budget, no markers), the Anthropic and text loops had no wrap-up round, ignored the voice split, and ended silently when rounds ran out, and the host-Ollama loop streamed a worker's tokens under a voice model. Fix loop behaviour there, never in a provider. Contract tests: `round_loop_tests` (a scripted `FakeTurn`).

**Cited graph ids are checked** (`check_citations` in `forward_chat_events`, the one point every final reply passes). Every `id:<uuid>` is looked up in `:Note`/`:Task` via `neo4j_query`; any that do not exist get a visible "⚠ Citation check" line, in the stream and in working memory. Fails open. On 2026-09-24 Gemini cited `[[SOURCE RECORD · id:75368a57-…]]` — the retrieval-label format, invented ids — after running no tools.

**`TurnWriteGuard`** (every provider, via the round loop's `execute_guarded`), non-blocking: **grounding** — a `store_note` typed `semantic`/absent is rewritten to `unsourced_synthesis` (+ loud notice) when no retrieval tool has succeeded this turn; **duplicate suppression** — a write tool called twice with byte-identical args runs once (repeat returns success + notice). `observe()` runs after dispatch and takes the success flag; the duplicate check runs before the downgrade. `write_guard_tests`. Full story: history § worker/voice split.

title: Architecture Summary
content:
See `project-docs/architecture_context.md` for skill registry table, initialization order, and mechanics. See `project-docs/STATUS.md` for current tool counts and feature status.

**Nodes:**
- `Task` - High-level goals with `id`, `goal`, `context`, `success_criteria` (measurable definition of done — used by evaluator step), `status` (created/in_progress/completed/failed/blocked)
- `Note` - Stored text memories with optional vector `embedding`, `access_count`, `last_accessed_at`, `note_type` (`semantic`/`episodic`/`reflection`/`consolidated`/`outcome`/`inference`/`claim`/`source_record`/`news`), `next_review_at`, `review_interval_days`, `source_context`, `event_at`
- `Procedure` - Named multi-step workflows with `id`, `name`, `description`, `steps` (JSON array), `created_at`
- `WorkingMemory` - Session-scoped scratchpad entries with `id`, `session_id`, `content`, `role`, `turn_index`, `created_at`
- `Entity` - Named entities extracted from notes with `id`, `name` (unique, lowercased), `entity_type`, `created_at`
- `AgentJob` - Background job record with `id`, `tool_name`, `args_json`, `priority` (0-3), `status` (queued/running/completed/failed/dead/parked/cancelled), `attempt_count`, `max_attempts`, `result_json`, `error`, timestamps, `session_id`, `parent_job_id`
- `ModelSpec` - Registered LLM models with capabilities, cost, and usage stats
- `ToolDef` / `ContextProfile` / `ModelDef` - **Self-model meta-graph** (Phase 0b of the Agent Constructor plan). Generated by introspection in `services/self_model.rs` at the end of every `build_skills()` — never hand-edit: the tool registry, `contexts/*.yaml`, and the DuckDB model catalog are the sources of truth, and stale nodes are deleted on each sync. `(:ContextProfile)-[:ALLOWS]->(:ToolDef)` edges mirror profile tool allowlists (`allows_all: true` when the profile has no allowlist). Workflows are not duplicated here — `(:Workflow)` already is the graph representation.
- `BrainVersion` - **Singleton `{id:'current'}`** recording the commit this process is running (`sha`, `subject`, `branch`, `dirty`, `seen_at`, `deployed_at`). Written by `sync_code_version()` in `services/self_model.rs`, right after the meta-graph sync. When the sha differs from the stored one it also writes ONE episodic note (`source_context: "code_version <sha>"`) listing the changed files; an unchanged sha is a no-op, so restarts cost nothing.

  This replaced a `post-commit` → `scripts/self_update.py` round-trip (deleted 2026-08-10). That script re-derived over HTTP what the process already knows, and got it wrong: it parsed `analyze_own_structure`'s **Markdown** output as JSON inside a bare `except: pass`, printing `tools at runtime: 0` on every commit since March, and it indexed `result[0]` on a dict. It also fired on `git commit` — before the rebuild it triggered had finished — so the note described code that was not yet running, and it only ever covered a local `git commit` (not `docker compose restart`, CI, or a pull on another machine). Reading HEAD in-process at startup reports **what is actually loaded**. The hook is now just `docker compose up -d --build`.

**Relationships:**
- `(:Note)-[:RELATES_TO {similarity: float}]->(:Note)` — auto-created when similarity ≥ 0.75
- `(:Note)-[:SUMMARIZED_BY]->(:Note)` — source notes pointing to their consolidated summary
- `(:Note)-[:REFLECTS_ON]->(:Task)` — reflection/outcome notes linked to the task they critique
- `(:Note)-[:PART_OF]->(:Note)` — semantic chunk linked to its parent note
- `(:Note)-[:MENTIONS {count}]->(:Entity)` — entity mentions extracted from note content
- `(:Note {note_type:'inference'})-[:DERIVED_FROM]->(:Note)` — inference notes citing their sources
- `(:Task)-[:SUBTASK_OF]->(:Task)` — sub-tasks (`create_task` with a parent)
- `(:Task)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(:Task)` — dependency edges for task ordering
- `(:AgentSpec)-[:CONSTRUCTED_FOR]->(:Task)` — a constructed agent linked to the task it was dispatched for
- `(:AgentSpec)-[:PERFORMED {score, passed, at}]->(:Task)` — graded outcome written by the queue's evaluator hook; the constructor's reuse-before-construct prefers specs with avg score ≥ 3.5
- `(:ApiContext)-[:EXPOSES]->(:ApiEndpoint)` — endpoints ingested by `ingest_api` (see below). `:ApiEndpoint {api_name, method, path, summary, operation_id, parameters, security, tags}` MERGE'd on `(api_name, method, path)`, so re-ingest updates in place.

title: Architecture Summary › Native REST API ingestion (`ingest_api`) (part 1/2)
content:
`ingest_api` in `HttpSkill` (`skills/http.rs`) ingests a REST API's endpoints from **one of three sources** (pass exactly one) and stores each operation as an `(:ApiEndpoint)` under an `(:ApiContext)` via `[:EXPOSES]`. This is the properly-resurrected agent-api "spec → endpoint graph" idea (the old `ingest_openapi` was a doc-comment ghost; the code was never ported).
- **`spec_url`** — a direct OpenAPI 3.x / Swagger 2.0 doc (JSON **or** YAML).
- **`docs_url`** — an HTML docs page. Deterministically detects the linked spec: scans the page, then its referenced `.js` (Swagger UI keeps the `url:` in `swagger-initializer.js`); when a page advertises several specs (the Swagger demo dropdown) it **prefers one on the same host as the page**; unwraps `host=https://…` map entries. If a spec is found it ingests via the spec path (`source: html_spec`). If **no** spec is linked, it **falls back to LLM extraction** from the page text (`html_to_text` → `generate_json`, `source: html_llm`) — lower confidence (verify before relying on it), used only after deterministic detection fails. Needs the injected `Arc<dyn LlmProvider>` (unmetered `SharedLlm`); absent it, a clear error.
- **`codebase_path`** — a local dir searched (bounded, skips `node_modules`/`target`/…) for an existing spec file (`openapi`/`swagger` `.json`/`.yaml`, `api-docs.json`) → parse it (`codebase_spec`). No spec file → **build-from-routes**: `find_route_files` scores source files by route-marker density (axum/actix, FastAPI/Flask, Express, Spring, gin/echo), feeds a bounded corpus of the top files to the LLM, which returns the endpoint list (`source: codebase_generated`, lower confidence — it merges router prefixes and infers params from signatures, but reads registrations not a contract).

Spec-based parsing is a `serde_json::Value` walk — **no LLM**, so no truncation/hallucination. Every operation → method, path, summary, operationId, merged path+operation parameters, security scheme names, tags. base_url resolves 3.x `servers[0].url` (absolute or relative-to-origin) → 2.0 `schemes[0]://host+basePath` → the spec URL's origin. The `(:ApiContext)` records provenance: `source` (`openapi_spec`/`html_spec`/`codebase_spec` are deterministic; `html_llm`/`codebase_generated` are LLM-derived, lower confidence) + `discovered_from`. Endpoints MERGE on `(api_name, method, path)` (idempotent). Persistence (shared by spec and LLM paths, `persist_endpoints`) uses the atomic `UNWIND $endpoints` + `RETURN count` read-back (the dynamic-tool-fix lesson: one query, no cross-connection MATCH, verify the write landed). Fetch/file-read run **in the brain process** (has egress/FS), never the sandbox. Query results with `neo4j_query`. Parser/detection tests: `ingest_api_tests`. All four ingestion routes (spec URL, HTML docs, codebase spec-file, codebase build-from-routes) are implemented; the two LLM-derived sources are labelled lower-confidence rather than deferred. **`prune: true`** turns re-ingest into a true sync: after the upsert it deletes endpoints of the same API not written in this run (older `updated_at`), so a removed route disappears — the result adds `endpoints_pruned`. **The brain keeps its OWN API doc current with it**: `workflows/brain-api-sync.yaml` (weekly) runs `ingest_api(codebase_path=".../crates/app/src/mcp", name="agent-brain", prune=true)` on unmetered ollama-cloud — the brain publishes no OpenAPI spec, so this build-from-routes ingest over its Axum route table IS its self-documentation (`ApiContext` `agent-brain`, ~48 endpoints); step 2 banks a dated endpoint/prune-count record (`source_context: brain_api_sync`). Point the same tool + a workflow at any other service on the network (a spec URL, a Swagger UI page, or a repo) to give the brain a queryable map of that API too.

**Autonomous discovery (`api-scout`).** `contexts/api-scout.yaml` is a spawnable profile (search_web + http_request + ingest_api + notify_user) that scouts the web for free public REST APIs in the brain's interest areas and **ingests the keyless ones** (a spec reachable without an account) while **`notify_user`-flagging the key-gated ones** for a human to supply a key — it never signs up or invents a key. `workflows/api-scout.yaml` drives it weekly via a single `run_agent(agent="api-scout")` step and is **seeded disabled** (`enabled: false`) for review; turn it on with `manage_workflow(upsert, {name: "api-scout", enabled: true})` or the HBI toggle. It is the discovery half of the API toolchain; `api-integrator` is the build-a-client half. Requires `SUBAGENT_ENABLED=true`.

**Stdio Transport (Default)**
- Standard input/output for local CLI usage
- Best for MCP clients like Claude Desktop that spawn the server as subprocess

**HTTP Transport**
- Streamable HTTP with Server-Sent Events (SSE) per MCP specification
- POST `/mcp` - JSON-RPC requests, returns JSON or SSE stream
- GET `/mcp` - SSE stream for server-initiated messages
- DELETE `/mcp` - Terminate session
- GET `/health` - Health check endpoint
- Optional API key authentication via Bearer token

title: Critical Dev Notes (part 1/4)
content:
> Long root-cause narratives for the starred rules live verbatim in **`project-docs/engineering-history.md`** (§ *Critical Dev Notes*).

**LlmConfig:** `base_url` is `Option<String>`. Default model `"qwen3.5:4b"`. Tests: `config.base_url.as_deref()`.

**Parse the FIRST complete JSON object, never first-`{`-to-last-`}`.** If no candidate parses, it retries once with stray backslashes escaped inside strings (`escape_stray_backslashes`): a `$\approx$` in a `reason` answer failed the whole parse on 2026-09-30, and the raw JSON became a Task goal. `services::llm::first_json_object(text, must_have)` stops after one value and requires the named keys, so a repeated answer, trailing prose or a fence cannot break it. The old slice spanned two objects when a model wrote its ```json answer twice (2026-09-26), the parse failed, and the fenced raw reply was stored as a monitor report. `reason` (both paths), audit, counter-arguments, adversarial review, `parse_adversarial_robustness` and the constructor's plan parser all use it.

**Structured LLM output:** for strict JSON, call `LlmProvider::generate_json(prompt, system, required_keys, max_retries)` (self-correcting re-prompt loop) rather than hand-rolling `generate` + `extract_json` + `from_str().unwrap_or_else`. `extract_json` picks the **earliest-opening** delimiter; pass `&[]` for `required_keys` to accept any valid JSON.

**★ Pick the local model by VRAM residency, not leaderboard.** Residency is a cliff, not a curve: every model that fits generates at 67–125 tok/s, one that doesn't (`gemma4:latest`, 9.86 GB on an 8 GB card) at ~26. Models don't co-reside here — a swap is a replacement; unload the outgoing model (`keep_alive: 0`). **`granite4:latest`** is the local model (`OLLAMA_LOCAL_MODEL` in compose; already `selection_rank 120`), 18× faster than `gemma4` in production. Benchmark the **structured** path too (a fast model can emit unparseable JSON), and beware thinking models — `qwen3.5:4b` (the stale `DEFAULT_MODEL` in `llm.rs`) emits into `thinking` and returns an **empty** `response`. Output length is a cost, not a quality signal. Full tables: history.

**★ The local model has its own timeout.** `OLLAMA_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default **600**) applies to the local background config alone (built in `brain_core.rs`); cloud calls keep the 120s default. It's burstiness, not average load — `poll_media_sources` fans ~30 videos out at once; at 30–75 calls/hour latency climbs to 120s and every call clips. Killing a call at 120s throws away spent compute *and* the chain built on it. Not the cause: concurrency (Ollama batches) or Ollama being down. Full incident (the `0426218` fan-out move): history.

**★ llama.cpp backend for background jobs.** The generation backend for `provider_hint:"ollama"` steps is env-selectable via `LOCAL_LLM_BACKEND` (`ollama` | `llamacpp`); the switch is in `services/llm.rs::build_local_llm_config`, used by both `brain_core.rs` and `scheduler.rs`. `LlmProviderType::LlamaCpp` reuses the existing OpenAI-compatible provider (`openai_compat.rs`) — llama.cpp's `llama-server` speaks the same `/v1/chat/completions` wire format as Ollama Cloud. **Load-bearing facts:** (1) **Embeddings never move** — `build_local_llm_config` pins `embed_base_url` to `OLLAMA_LOCAL_URL` no matter the backend, because a single-model `llama-server` doesn't serve `/api/embeddings`; host Ollama stays up for bge-m3. (2) `keep_alive`/`num_ctx` are Ollama-native and **ignored** by the llama.cpp provider — set context/offload as `llama-server` launch flags in the compose `command:` (`-c`, `-ngl`, `--flash-attn`, `--cache-type-k/v`), not per-request. (3) `USE_LOCAL_LLM` routing is backend-agnostic (keyed on the flag, not the provider type), so a llama.cpp local route is still `is_local_route=true` and never falls back to cloud. (4) **The local model is a thinking model** — background steps that parse JSON need thinking OFF or the reasoning leaks into `content` and no JSON is emitted. **The flag is model-specific**: Qwen3 honors `--reasoning-budget 0`; **Gemma 4 IGNORES it and needs `--reasoning off`** (verified 2026-09-10 — E4B leaked its whole thought process until switched). Current production model is **Gemma-4-E4B** (`--reasoning off`), chosen over Qwen3-8B because it's fully resident at ~3.3 GB (weights) vs 6.0 GB and ~14% faster — see the residency note below. Provider variant + `build_local_llm_config` are covered by the lib tests; scope of the switch is background jobs only — human `/chat` stays on Ollama-Cloud.

title: Critical Dev Notes (part 2/4)
content:
**★ The llama.cpp CUDA image must match the host driver (`llamacpp/Dockerfile`).** The GPU is an RTX 3060 Ti (8 GB, sm_86); the host driver is **535 / CUDA 12.2**. The upstream prebuilt `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda` ships **CUDA 12.8** and will NOT run on this driver: its bundled forward-compat stub (`libcuda.so.570`) aborts CUDA init on a GeForce (`forward compatibility was attempted on non supported HW` → silent CPU fallback), and even with the stub removed the 12.8 cubins fail to load (`CUDA error: device kernel image is invalid`). So the sidecar is **built from source against CUDA 12.2** targeting sm_86. Two build gotchas the Dockerfile encodes: link with `-Wl,--allow-shlib-undefined` (libggml-cuda references CUDA Driver-API symbols the devel image keeps in `lib64/stubs`; they resolve at runtime when cudart loads the injected `libcuda.so.1`), and enable `-DLLAMA_OPENSSL=ON` + `libssl-dev`/`libssl3` (b10900's `-hf` downloader uses a native TLS client — without it, `HTTPS is not supported` and it can only load an already-cached GGUF). The production model **Gemma-4-E4B Q4_K_M sits ~3.3 GB** on the GPU (4.6 GB with the 16k KV cache) alongside bge-m3 and the whisper sidecar, leaving ~2.8 GB free. (It replaced Qwen3-8B at 6.0 GB / 70 tok/s: E4B is ~14% faster and half the VRAM — Gemma-3-**12B does not fit resident** on 8 GB, spilling to ~21 tok/s.) Full rationale in the Dockerfile header; benchmark detail in the memory note `llamacpp-switch`.

**A `reqwest` failure says what went wrong.** `describe_reqwest` (`llm_providers/mod.rs`) prefixes the kind (`operation timed out:` / `connection refused:`) — the "why" lives in `source()`, which `Display` drops — and appends the full cause chain. The prefix survives job-`error` truncation and matches the phrases `classify_unavailable` uses.

**Every failed LLM call records an `error_kind`.** `SharedLlm::generate`'s per-call `record_model_usage` used to hardcode `None`; now every attempt (primary and each fallback rung) goes through `run_and_record`, whose `failure_kind` reuses `classify_unavailable` and falls back to `"other"`.

**★ A cloud LLM that cannot answer walks a fallback chain; one that answers and refuses does not.** `classify_unavailable` (`services/shared_llm.rs`) qualifies four kinds: `rate_limited`, `subscription_required` (403 "requires a subscription"), `transport` (DNS/refused/TLS/client timeout — never reached the provider), `server_error` (5xx). Anything else propagates (falling back on a 400/401 just gets a worse rejection). `is_server_error` matches canonical reason phrases, not bare numbers (`contains("500")` fires on token counts). Fallback is guarded by `!is_local_route` (a local model never retries against itself) and the chain order comes from `build_fallback_chain`: a **capability-selected** cloud route (e.g. a `reasoning` step routed to `gemini-2.5-flash`) falls back to the **active config first** — the free Ollama-Cloud model, which does not share the selected model's quota, i.e. "what we were doing before" — and only then to local; a route that WAS the active config skips straight to local. This is why routing reasoning at `gemini-2.5-flash` and hitting its 1500 RPD ceiling degrades to `gpt-oss:120b-cloud`, not to weak local granite4. Each rung (primary included) records its own `model_usage` row via `run_and_record`. Full incident (the lost off-grid report): history.

The **chat path has its own ladder** (`chat_fallback_ladder` in `models.yaml`, walked by `run_one_attempt` in `clients/chat/turn.rs`) — it turns on "did the turn produce output", not the error class, and runs Ollama Cloud → Mistral → OpenRouter `:free` → local (the may_train rungs since 2026-10-10; OpenRouter's 50/day is metered by the budget, and the policy refuses it for sub-agents). **A model that fails mid-turn hands its work over (2026-09-26).** If it ran only read-only tools (`call_is_read_only`: not a `WRITE_TOOLS` member, no `manage_*`/`ingest_*`/… prefix, `http_request` GET/HEAD, `mcp_call` to a fetch/search/list tool; `delegate` counts as read-only because chat sub-agents cannot write), `run_one_attempt` returns `Interrupted` and the next rung gets a `WORK ALREADY DONE THIS TURN` block with each call and its result, told not to repeat them. A turn that ran a **write** still owns the turn and reports the error, so a write is never repeated by a second model. Before this, any error after the first tool call ended the turn: a `gemini-3.6-flash` 503 on the round after a delegate returned nothing. **A failed voice pass sends the worker's own answer** with a `⚠ voice model … failed` note (`voice_fallback`) instead of discarding it. **Chat calls now record `error_kind`** (`shared_llm::failure_kind_of`), and a `server_error` benches the model for 60 s in the budget, so the next turn skips a model that just returned a 503. **A profile may declare `fallback_models:`**, walked after its pin and before the global ladder (ahead of the chat default when the pin is refused); the front door steps `gemini-3.6-flash → gemini-3.8-flash → gemini-2.5-flash → Ollama Cloud → local`. Guards: `a_failure_after_read_only_tools_hands_the_work_over`, `a_failure_after_a_write_keeps_the_turn_and_its_error`, `every_profile_fallback_model_is_in_the_catalog`. **`run_bounded_loop` (the sub-agent loop behind `run_agent`/`delegate`) walks that same ladder**, so a transient 500 on a sub-agent's primary model degrades to the next rung instead of surfacing the raw error as the whole delegated answer — and every rung it walks is admitted by the routing policy for the sub-agent's purpose and data class (OpenRouter's rung is refused for sub-agents by its 50/day limit). Before this it dispatched a single provider loop with no fallback and failed a delegated task on a provider blip.

title: Critical Dev Notes (part 3/4)
content:
**A tool name is owned by the first skill that claims it.** Dispatch is first-match, and the built-ins register before later tools, so a later tool reusing a built-in's name never runs (since Phase 3d the loaders refuse such a name: a plugin whole, a declared tool alone). It was still listed and, worse, validated against: the step-schema snapshot was last-wins, so an obsolete 09-07 dynamic `ingest_api` (`spec_url` required) made the audit mark the brain-api-sync schedule broken. The snapshot is now first-wins with a startup WARN per duplicate, the definer refused a built-in's name, and the stray tool is removed. (Dynamic tools were replaced by declared tools in Phase 3d.)

**Skill registration:** push the skill ONCE onto the `skills` list in `BrainCore::build_skills`; the registry (`tools/list`) and the handler (`tools/call`) each get an `Arc` of that same instance (`impl Skill for Arc<T>` in the protocol crate). Before 2026-10-02 every skill was constructed twice, one copy per side, and the copies had drifted (the registry's `MediaSkill` had no knowledge store). Order matters: dispatch is first-match, so the declared tools stay last.

**★ Ollama serves a 4096-token context by default, whatever the model claims** — input past the window is **truncated silently**. Put the operative instruction **before and after** a large payload, never only after. `LlmConfig::num_ctx` (`Option<u32>`, default `None`) sets it per config; only the distiller raises it (`DISTILL_NUM_CTX=16384`). Detail: history.

**★ Embedding fails on LENGTH, and the limit is TOKENS — the old "`500 … NaN` for certain strings" diagnosis was wrong.** Probed against the live `bge-m3` 2026-09-12: emoji, control chars, zero-width joiners, CJK, punctuation and whitespace-only input all embed cleanly at 1024 dims. Two real failure modes: **empty input returns HTTP 200 with a ZERO-LENGTH vector** (worse than an error — it flows into `db.index.vector.queryNodes` as a silent no-op reading as "nothing is similar"), and **over-length input 500s**. The ceiling is ~3,200 tokens, which is **~10,327 chars of prose but only ~5,819 of dense JSON/URL content** — so a character cap cannot be right for both, and one set from the prose measurement still 500'd on 3 of the 4 notes it was meant to repair. `prepare_embed_input` (`llm_providers/mod.rs`) rejects empty and caps at **4,000 chars** on a char boundary (compile-time `const _: () = assert!` pins it below the measured dense ceiling); `embed_with_backoff` halves and retries up to 3× on a length-shaped failure only — a missing key is not retried. Wired into all three providers. Nothing truncated before this, so 4 notes (longest **201,259 chars**) sat unembedded and invisible to vector search; backfilled. Both vector-search entry points still degrade to the BM25 `note_content_fulltext` index (`search_notes_inner`, `fetch_similar_notes`) and any new embed call site must too — and `search_notes_inner` now **WARNs** when it does, because the `Err` was silently discarded by a let-chain, which is precisely why a wrong folk diagnosis survived for months. The BM25 fallback must run its query through `sanitize_lucene_query`. (2026-09-12)

**★ `neo4j_query`, and the graph's timestamps.** LIMIT injection now matches `RETURN`/`LIMIT` as whitespace-separated words (a substring test sent `LIMIT 20 LIMIT 100`). **Every temporal property is a native `DATETIME` in UTC** — read `project-docs/schema.md` § "Timestamps: one representation, always" before writing date Cypher (Cypher compares a temporal to a string as **null**, not false, so a mismatch silently drops the row and the query succeeds with zero results). Use `datetime($param)` on writes, compare against `datetime(...)`, `toString(prop)` when reading into a `String`, `repository::node_ts` for whole-node reads. Guards: `string_timestamp_violations()` (startup WARN), `no_string_timestamps` (integration test), and a `neo4j_query` hint on a zero-row date-literal filter. Migration: `scripts/migrate_timestamps_to_datetime.cypher` (run with the brain **stopped**). Full incident (the "we learned nothing" / 504-notes day): history.

**`McpServer`** is a thin backward-compatible wrapper around `McpServerCore` (stdio path only).

**HTTP session init:** always send `notifications/initialized` AFTER `initialize`, or the server stays `Initializing` and rejects all tool calls.

**HTTP sessions expire, and expired ones are evicted.** `SessionManager::spawn_cleanup` (started in `main.rs`) sweeps every `cleanup_interval`, and `create_session` evicts expired sessions before refusing at `max_sessions`. Until 2026-10-02 nothing ever evicted, so expired sessions counted against the 1,000 cap and the HTTP transport refused every new session once that many had been created since the last restart.

**Initialization order:** `SchedulerService::new()` after `QueueService::new()`; `QueueService::spawn_coordinator()` after the tool handler is set (end of `build_skills`).

title: Critical Dev Notes (part 4/4)
content:
**★ Consolidation clusters before it summarises (2026-10-01).** `consolidate_memories` takes up to 6 due eligible notes nearest the topic as SEEDS, and for the first seed with ≥2 neighbours at cosine ≥ **0.82** (bge-m3; shared `## Gap synthesis:` boilerplate puts hundreds of unrelated notes above 0.75) merges the seed plus at most 8 neighbours, drawn from all eligible notes, due or not. A seed with too few neighbours is deferred +30d so the next one gets a turn; "no cluster" is a no-op success. Eligibility is one shared predicate, `knowledge::CONSOLIDATION_SOURCE_PREDICATE`, also used by the scheduler's "≥50 notes due" trigger (the two had drifted: the trigger counted five types consolidation refused): **semantic notes only**, minus housekeeping contexts (`adversarial_review`, `codebase_self_analysis`, `todo_snapshot`, `brain_api_sync`, `chat_session`, `scheduler_dispatch`, `overdue_todo_review`) and **`resume`** (personal data, never merged), minus JSON-blob contexts, chunks, and notes already summarised. Why: the old selection summarised the top-10 due notes by similarity to the fixed topic "recent experiences and knowledge" with no clustering, so all 295 consolidated notes were grab-bags (a Hugging Face attack + birds of prey + a film scene in one paragraph; a chat answer's "127 notes today" folded into long-term memory), retrieved 1,749 times. `scripts/retire_grabbag_consolidations.cypher` deleted them and freed their sources (run 2026-10-01 with cutoff `2026-10-01T18:59:11Z`, the clustering deploy; full-graph snapshot beforehand: `snapshot_pre_consolidate_20261001_190119.json.gz`). Prompt uses `[Memory N]` labels and tells the model to drop records not about `[Memory 1]`'s subject. Source notes get `next_review_at = now + 30 days`. The knowledge service's local LLM now records to `model_usage` (it had no telemetry sink, so consolidation and entity extraction were invisible).

**`services/mod.rs`:** must re-export `pub use llm::{LlmClient, LlmConfig, LlmProviderType};`

**Context Profiles:** Seeded from each loaded bundle's `contexts/` (core first) into `(:ContextProfile)`, which is their authority; UI saves write the graph (`dev_docs get profiles/graph`). Loaded by `ContextBuilderService::load_profiles()` in `build_skills()`. `boot.yaml` runs after each `build_skills()`, `init.yaml` on an empty graph. `ContextSkill` registered when `context_builder_arc` is `Some`.

title: Subsystem rules — Agent Brain
content:
The operative rules for every subsystem, moved out of `CLAUDE.md` on **2026-10-06** so the always-loaded file stays small. Text is verbatim as it stood in `CLAUDE.md` that day. `CLAUDE.md` keeps a one-line pointer per subsystem; the long incident narratives behind these rules are in `engineering-history.md`.

**Read the matching section here before changing a subsystem.** Starred (★) rules mark failure modes that were expensive to find and are easy to re-introduce.

Contents: [Data model & transports](#architecture-summary) · [Subsystem rules](#architecture-subsystem-rules) · [Critical dev notes](#critical-dev-notes)

title: Design › 1. `manage_todo` — the missing primitive
content:
Mirrors `manage_scheduled_task`: `list | get | upsert | assign | approve |
complete`. Everything below depends on it.

`assign` validates `assignee` against the **live spawnable roster** at write
time, not dispatch time — an unknown agent should fail when a human types it,
not silently at 3am.

title: Design › 2. Dispatch is a TOOL, not a schedule
content:
**Load-bearing constraint: a ScheduledTask's steps are enqueued verbatim, so a
schedule cannot loop over N due todos.** The established pattern for fan-out in
this codebase is a tool that creates Tasks, driven by a thin schedule — exactly
how `poll_media_sources` works.

So: **`dispatch_due_todos`** + a small schedule that calls it.

The useful realisation: **an agent-assigned todo is just a Task with a delay.**
`create_task(goal: "run agent: <prompt>")` already routes through
`chains/run-agent.yaml` → `run_agent`, and inherits the queue, retries, and
chain-death attribution. The new work is the bridge and the writeback, not an
execution engine. The chain's last step calls `manage_todo(complete, …)`.

title: Design › 3. Side effects decide auto vs notify-first
content:
**Auto-dispatch only for agents that write nothing outside the graph.**
Everything else notifies first and waits for a human.

Derived from each profile's tool allowlist (2026-09-11):

| auto-dispatch | notify-first | why |
|---|---|---|
| `knowledge-worker` | `job-applicant` | `mcp_call` — aidevboard `apply_to_job` submits a real application |
| `code-analyst` | `api-scout`, `api-integrator`, `toolsmith`, `researcher` | `http_request` (POST/PUT reach third parties), `manage_dynamic_tool`, `write_workspace_file` |
| `schedule-author` | | |

**Derivation alone is too coarse, and the failure case matters.** `researcher`
is classified notify-first purely because it holds `http_request`, which it uses
for GETs — yet "research X" is the most natural delayed-prompt there is (the live
todo *"Research Sodium batteries"* is exactly this). So:

```yaml
# contexts/researcher.yaml
side_effects: read_only   # http_request is used for GETs; reviewed <date>
```

Absent the key it is **derived from the allowlist and fails safe to
`notify_first`**. An override is a deliberate, greppable, reviewable act. The
honest long-term fix is a GET-only fetch capability, so the declaration becomes
enforced rather than a promise.

title: Design › 4. Notify-first flow
content:
Uses machinery that already works:

1. `dispatch_due_todos` finds a due todo assigned to a writing agent.
2. Sets `status: awaiting_approval`; `notify_user` + `push_context` open a
   `todo-<date>` session naming the agent and showing the prompt.
3. The human replies; the front door calls `manage_todo(action: approve, id)` —
   it already owns the write role for exactly this reason (a sub-agent cannot
   write; one writer per turn).
4. That creates the Task → `chains/run-agent.yaml` → writeback.

Approval is **single-use and bound to that todo id**, mirroring the aidevboard
artifact-hash pattern: an approval cannot be replayed against a different todo.

title: Design › 5. User-assigned reminders
content:
`daily-news.yaml` (the Daily Brief) already ends
`store_note → claim → notify_user → push_context`. Add a `neo4j_query` step
pulling open `assignee: "user"` todos past due and fold them into the
`notify_user` message. Fixed step count, so it respects the verbatim constraint.

title: Guardrails
content:
- **Cap `dispatch_count`.** On 2026-09-11 an `ingest_media` job reached attempt
  29 against a cap of 3 because crash recovery requeued it on every restart. An
  uncapped retry outlives restarts; assume anything that can loop, will.
- **Bound fan-out per poll** (like `MEDIA_WATCH_MAX_PER_SOURCE`) so ten due
  todos do not dispatch at once — a cloud agent's cost is a multiplication, not
  a rate.
- **Validate `assignee` against the live roster** at assign time.
- **No recurrence.** A recurring todo is a `ScheduledTask`. CLAUDE.md already
  warns that one-shot Tasks and recurring ScheduledTasks are not interchangeable
  and that cadence words in a goal string do nothing. Todos stay
  one-shot-with-a-delay; a todo that wants recurrence should *create a schedule*.
- **Dispatch must be idempotent.** Status transition + `dispatched_at` guard, so
  a poll that overlaps a slow dispatch cannot fire the same todo twice.

title: Open questions
content:
1. Should a completed agent-run todo store its result as a note and link it
   (`result_note_id`), or write the summary onto the todo itself? A note is
   consistent with the rest of the graph and searchable; the todo field is
   simpler for the UI.
2. Does the HBI frontend need an assignee/approval affordance, or is chat enough
   for v1? (Chat is enough to ship; the UI is where a human will actually notice.)
3. `agent:auto` uses `select_agent`, whose token-overlap matching is known to
   score 0 on ordinary phrasings ("what did we learn today"). For an unattended
   dispatch a miss is worse than for a chat turn — consider requiring an explicit
   agent for auto-dispatch and reserving `auto` for the notify-first path, where
   a human sees the choice before it runs.

title: 2026-10-16: mcp_call arguments were never checked against the remote tool
content: Validation Phase 4. The dispatch check (Phase 1) saw `mcp_call`'s envelope only, so whatever went inside `arguments` reached the remote server unchecked, and remote servers drop an unknown argument silently: aidevboard `search_jobs` with `querry: "rust"` returned 10 unfiltered jobs as a success. Now checked against the remote `inputSchema`. First live run (shadow): the misspelling named `query`; an unknown tool listed aidevboard's 20 tools; and the stored `ai-dev-board-job-search` workflow (disabled) was found sending worklittle `search_jobs` a `workplace_type` argument it does not have, so its remote-only filter had been dropped on every run. The aidevboard `match_jobs` step fits. Not fixed in the workflow; reported to the owner.

title: Every tool call is checked against its schema, so the schema must be honest
content:
Since 2026-10-16 `ToolHandler::execute` checks every call (chat, agents, workflow steps, MCP) against the registered input_schema of the tool that runs it (`validation::check_tool_arguments`, `TOOL_ARG_CHECK`): unknown keys, types, enums, required. In shadow a misfit lands in DuckDB `arg_checks`; in enforce it is refused. So a schema is now a contract, not documentation:
- Declare every argument the handler reads. One it reads but the schema omits is reported as unknown (and refused under enforce).
- A tool whose arguments vary at run time (lookup's per-view slots) says so with `additionalProperties: true`; it then validates them itself and must say what fits when one does not.
- `properties: {}` means "takes no arguments" and is checked as such (list_tasks). A schema with no `properties` key is not checked for unknown keys.
- Keys starting `__` belong to the queue and always pass; never name a real argument that way.
- The check compiles the schema on each call (microseconds against a model call's seconds); cache only if arg_checks or a profile shows it matters.
- Declared plugin tools are registered tools, so the dispatch check covers them.
- **`mcp_call` is checked twice** (Phase 4, 2026-10-16): the dispatch check sees only its envelope (`server`, `tool`, `arguments`); `McpClientSkill::check_remote_arguments` then checks `arguments` against the remote tool's own `inputSchema` from the server's `tools/list` (cached 10 minutes per server), same checker and mode, recorded as `mcp_call:<server>/<tool>`. An unknown remote tool name lists the server's tools. If the server cannot be listed the call goes ahead unchecked (fail-open: the call itself would fail the same way). Remote servers drop unknown arguments silently and return unfiltered results (aidevboard `search_jobs` with `querry`), so this is the only place such a miss shows.

title: Tool schemas are hand-written for the model; only data-backed parts are generated
content:
Tool `input_schema`s are written by hand, for the model that reads them, and stay that way (CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN 6e, 2026-10-11, measured):

- Generating them from the typed input structs (schemars) made `search_web`'s schema 21% larger (1,821 vs 1,510 bytes) and added `$schema`, `title`, `format`, `minimum`, and `anyOf: [$ref, null]` + `definitions` for optional enums. Schema bytes ride on every tool-carrying call; `$ref`/`anyOf` are what Gemini and the small local models handle worst. Struct doc comments are written for developers, a different audience.
- Keep schemas flat and terse: `type`, `description`, `enum`, `required`. No `$ref`, no nullable type arrays, no `title`.
- A part that mirrors declared data is built from it, never copied: `search_web`'s `engine` enum and ladder text come from the engine files (`engine_property`). Never emit an empty `enum`; it rejects every value.
- The write-boundary validator (`services/validation.rs`) checks workflow step arguments against these registered schemas, so a schema `enum` is also a hard rule for stored workflows.

title: 1. The problem: one goal, three execution machines
content:
The brain has **three front doors** that all mean "accomplish a goal," but each
runs through a different machine, and only one of them has a real *agent*:

| Entrypoint | How a "step" runs today | Agent identity? | Evaluator / critic? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chat** (`clients/chat.rs`) | orchestrator → `delegate` → `run_subagent`: a **profile-driven bounded LLM tool loop** | **Yes** — the sub-agent *is* a `ContextProfile` (model + toolset + system prompt) | worker/voice split, write guard, grounding |
| **Task / todo** (`scheduler.rs::goal_to_steps` → chain) | each step is **one fixed tool call**; `provider_hint`/`required_capabilities` pick a **model** | **No** | yes (generator-evaluator + adversarial critic) |
| **Scheduled task** (`schedules/*.yaml`) | steps enqueued **verbatim** | **No** | **No** — no routing, no evaluator, no retrieval |

The load-bearing fact (documented in `scheduler.rs:344`):

> for background jobs [the context profile] is **ANNOTATION ONLY — the
> coordinator never reads `job.context_profile` at execution** … applies no
> profile tool-filter, system_prompt, or pre_load_query. Profiles only take
> effect on /chat turns.

So on the background path there is **no agent** — a step is a single stateless
tool invocation, and the only per-step intelligence is *which model runs it*. The
chat path got the good machinery (`run_subagent`: a profile that decides its own
steps, calls tools, returns structured findings). Tasks and schedules never did.

Every capability the user asked for is a consequence of closing that one gap:

- *"apply an actual agent to each step, or one agent to oversee the task"* → a
  step (or a whole task) that runs a **profile-driven agent loop**, not a fixed tool.
- *"choose an agent, or build one from the available models and tools"* → the
  roster (`spawnable` profiles) for *choose*, `construct_agent` for *build*.
- *"create a scheduled task from chat, but it came out malformed"* → let the
  orchestrator delegate schedule-authoring to a specialist agent whose job is a
  lint-clean chain (same pathway, different worker).
- *"pass a project back and forth until it meets the definition of done"* → the
  evaluator loop, generalised with **artifact continuity** and a durable node.
- *"the pathways from orchestrator to worker should be the same coming from
  todos, chat, or schedules"* → **one primitive, three front doors.**

---

title: 10. Risks
content:
- **Latency / cost multiplication** — bounded budgets, task-level grain, local
  default, measured before default-on (§7).
- **Recursion / runaway** — depth cap 1, agent-run tool stripped from inner sets.
- **Two "agent" notions confusing users** — keep the profile-agent vs
  constructed-agent split explicit (§4); one is a loop, one is a graded plan.
- **Guard divergence** — one `AgentRunner`, reused by both paths; no second
  implementation of the ladder / write guard.
- **Scope creep into the Project loop** — Phases 0–3 stand alone and deliver the
  unified pathway; Phase 4 is a distinct layer, sequenced last on purpose.

title: 2. What already exists (build on it; do not rebuild)
content:
- **`run_subagent` (chat).** `ChatService::run_subagent(agent, task)` builds a
  sub-agent's toolset + system prompt + model from a `ContextProfile`, runs a
  **bounded** provider loop (`MAX_SUBAGENT_ITERATIONS`), and returns structured
  findings (`answer` + `sources`). Read-only in chat; depth cap 1; grounded; all
  four provider loops route delegate interception through `dispatch_tool_call`.
  **This is the agent loop we want everywhere — it just lives inside `ChatService`
  and streams to a chat channel.**
- **Agents are profiles.** `ContextProfile` already carries `tools`,
  `system_prompt`, `pre_load_query`, `model_preference`/`provider_hint`, and
  (from the sub-agent work) `spawnable`/`specialty`. `spawnable_profiles()` +
  `format_roster()` already produce a live roster. No new "agent" concept needed.
- **`construct_agent` (build).** Plans a validated chain from the live tool
  inventory, persists an `(:AgentSpec)`, optionally dispatches it as a Task with a
  mandatory adversarial pre-flight + evaluator. **Reuse-before-construct** already
  prefers a proven spec (avg `PERFORMED` score ≥ 3.5, goal Jaccard ≥ 0.5). This is
  the *build* half of choose-or-build — currently underused.
- **Evaluator + adversarial loops.** A Task with `success_criteria` already gets a
  prepended adversarial review and an appended `reflect_on_work` evaluator; a
  sub-threshold score marks the task failed and **creates a new Task carrying the
  critique** (retry cap 3). This is build→review→retry — but it **re-plans from
  scratch each requeue** and has no artifact.
- **Workspace.** `write_workspace_file` + `list_workspace_files` exist.
  **`read_workspace_file` does not** — a gap the project loop must fill (a reviewer
  can't grade an artifact it can't read).
- **`ChainStep.context_profile`** field already exists on every step — today
  written for annotation and never read at execution. **The plan gives it meaning.**

---

title: 3. Core proposal — one primitive: `AgentRunner`
content:
Extract the sub-agent loop out of `ChatService` into a standalone service both
paths can call:

```
services/agent_runner.rs
  AgentRunner {
    llm, tool_handler, context_builder, telemetry
  }
  async fn run(profile: &str, task: &str, budget: AgentBudget,
               sink: Option<EventSink>) -> AgentFindings
```

- **`profile`** — a `spawnable` `ContextProfile` (the agent).
- **`task`** — a self-contained sub-goal (caller supplies needed context;
  the agent does not see chat history / other steps).
- **`budget`** — iteration cap, write-allowed flag, provider/tier policy, depth.
- **`sink`** — `Some(stream)` on the chat path (nested events forwarded to the
  user); `None` on the background path (findings collected, not streamed).
- **Returns** `AgentFindings { answer, sources, gaps, retrieved, artifacts }` —
  the same structured shape `run_subagent` already produces.

It **reuses** the existing loop machinery (fallback ladder, `execute_guarded` +
`TurnWriteGuard`, depth guard by stripping the agent-run tool from the inner
toolset). This is the one mechanism the whole codebase's history says to reuse
rather than re-implement per path.

`ChatService::run_subagent` becomes a **thin wrapper** over `AgentRunner::run`
with a streaming sink. This is the *correct* version of the deferred
SUBAGENT_ORCHESTRATION Phase 4: not "swap which model leads the default chat"
(rejected — a behaviour change dressed as a refactor), but "extract the shared
agent-loop core so background can reach it too" (pure structure, chat behaviour
unchanged).

title: 3. Core proposal — one primitive: `AgentRunner` › 3.1 Two ways to reach it
content:
1. **`run_agent(agent, task)` — a real tool** (new `AgentRunnerSkill`). Because a
   background chain step already flows through `ToolHandler` and its result
   becomes `{{_prev}}` for the next step, `run_agent` slots in as a step
   `tool_name` with **no coordinator interception** — unlike chat's `delegate`,
   which must be intercepted because its result re-enters the same live turn. A
   step `{tool_name: "run_agent", arguments: {agent, task}}` *is* "an agent for
   this step"; a one-step chain of it *is* "one agent overseeing the task."
2. **`delegate` (chat)** stays intercepted in the provider loops (its result
   must fold into the ongoing turn), but now calls `AgentRunner::run` under the
   hood instead of a private `ChatService` method.

**Depth / cost guard:** the inner agent's toolset has `run_agent` (and `delegate`)
stripped — depth cap 1, same as chat. A turn/chain's worst-case model-call budget
stays a bounded product (outer iterations × inner `AgentBudget`), and is surfaced.

title: 3. Core proposal — one primitive: `AgentRunner` › 3.2 Writes: background agents write, chat sub-agents don't
content:
In chat a sub-agent is read-only (one writer per turn). In the background, writing
*is* the job (`store_note`, `write_workspace_file`). So `AgentBudget.allow_writes`
is `true` on the background path — but the inner agent runs its own
`TurnWriteGuard` so grounding/duplicate rules still hold.

---

title: 4. Choose-or-build agent selection
content:
Two existing mechanisms, unified into one decision the orchestrator (or a routing
step) makes:

- **Choose** — pick a `spawnable` profile from the live roster whose `specialty`
  fits the sub-goal, and `run_agent` it. Cheap, curated, inspectable.
- **Build** — when no profile fits, `construct_agent` plans a bespoke validated
  chain (and reuse-before-construct means a proven bespoke agent is preferred
  automatically next time).

Prompt policy: **prefer the roster; construct only when nothing fits.** Optionally
a small `select_agent(goal) -> profile | none` helper (specialty match, same
`format_roster` source) so a chain step can route without an LLM call. The two
notions of "agent" stay distinct and both keep their place:

| | **profile-agent** (`run_agent`) | **constructed-agent** (`construct_agent`) |
|-|-|-|
| Is | model + toolset + prompt, decides its own steps | a fixed validated chain (a plan) |
| Runs | bounded loop, in-line, returns findings | through the queue, async, graded (`PERFORMED`) |
| Use for | an open-ended sub-goal | a repeatable procedure worth persisting + scoring |

---

title: 5. One pathway, three front doors
content:
With `AgentRunner` + `run_agent` in place, all three entrypoints reach the same
agent loop:

- **Chat** — `delegate` → `AgentRunner::run` (streaming). *(already works; now
  shares the core.)*
- **Task / todo** — `goal_to_steps()` may emit a `run_agent` step, or route the
  whole task to a single overseeing `run_agent` (the "one agent per task" grain),
  or `construct_agent` builds a chain. The default grain is **task-level**: the
  step is cheap deterministic tools, and `run_agent` is reached for the genuinely
  open-ended part — not every step becomes an autonomous loop (that would multiply
  cost on fan-outs; see §7).
- **Scheduled task** — a schedule step can be `run_agent`, so schedules finally
  get real agents instead of verbatim fixed tools. `lint_chain_steps` gains a rule:
  a `run_agent` step must name a `spawnable` agent.

The orchestrator's ability to *create a well-formed schedule* becomes: delegate to
a schedule-authoring agent (a profile whose specialty is emitting a lint-clean
chain), then `manage_scheduled_task(upsert)`.

---

title: 6. The iterative-project loop (the widget example)
content:
A durable primitive layered on `run_agent`, generalising the evaluator loop with
the two things it lacks: **artifact continuity** and a **project-owned iteration
budget** decoupled from the evaluator's retry cap of 3.

- **`(:Project {id, spec, definition_of_done, workspace_path, status, iteration,
  max_iterations, created_at})`** — the durable record.
- **Loop (one iteration):**
  1. **Builder** `run_agent` (a `developer`/builder profile) — input: spec +
     current artifact (read from `workspace_path`) + prior reviewer critique;
     edits the artifact in place. *Edits, does not rebuild.*
  2. **Reviewer** `run_agent` (a distinct reviewer profile) — reads the artifact,
     grades it against `definition_of_done`, emits `Score: N/5` + a critique
     (reuses the evaluator's parse).
  3. **Gate** — pass (≥ threshold) → mark project `done`; fail → increment
     `iteration`, requeue the builder **with the critique and the artifact carried
     forward**, until `max_iterations`.
- **New tool** `manage_project(action: create|status|advance|cancel)` +
  **`read_workspace_file`** (the missing workspace read).

Differences from today's evaluator loop that make this a real primitive, not just
tuning: builder and reviewer are **different agents** (separation of concerns,
like the adversarial critic); the artifact is **carried forward** (not re-derived
each round); the loop is owned by a `:Project` with its **own iteration counter**
and DoD, not the 3-retry evaluator cap.

---

title: 7. Guards, invariants, and the honest tensions
content:
- **Not everything should become an agent.** A step like "store this note with
  `source_context: X`" must stay a cheap deterministic tool. `run_agent` is the
  escape hatch for the open-ended step (research, build, review), not the default
  wrapper for every step. The default grain is one agent per *task*, not per *step*.
- **Cost is a multiplication on fan-outs.** Background is local-pinned for a
  reason. A `run_agent` inner loop that touches cloud (tier 2) multiplies once per
  invocation — putting it on `poll_media_sources`' ~30-video fan-out without a
  burst cap re-creates the quota-blowout the codebase already warns about. Rules:
  `run_agent` is task-level not fan-out-item-level; inner budget bounded; inner
  agent respects `provider_hint`/`CLOUD_TIER`; background default stays local
  unless the sub-goal opts into a cloud capability. Bound burst and daily total
  separately (the existing ScheduledTask cost rule).
- **Depth cap 1.** Inner agents cannot `run_agent`/`delegate` (strip from inner
  toolset). Worst-case model calls stay a bounded, surfaced product.
- **Reuse one mechanism.** `AgentRunner` reuses the fallback ladder, write guard,
  and dropped-event detection. Re-implementing any of them in a second path is
  exactly how this codebase grows "labelled-in-one-path-not-the-other" bugs.
- **Provider policy (decided): local-first, Ollama Cloud allowed, Gemini never.**
  A background `run_agent` defaults to the **local** model (`OLLAMA_LOCAL_MODEL`) —
  unmetered, private, and matching the existing background pinning. It may step up
  to **Ollama Cloud** (`gpt-oss:120b-cloud` — also unmetered) when the sub-goal
  needs stronger tool-driving, opted in per profile/step, never as the silent
  default. It **never** routes to Gemini or any rate-limited/metered model — an
  agent is many model calls, the exact shape that trips the 5-RPM ceiling.
  **Caveat to measure in Phase 1:** chat sub-agents run on gpt-oss *because* the
  local model is a weaker tool-caller (and gemma empty-completes ~1-in-4). So
  "get away with local" is a hypothesis, not a given — Phase 1 must measure
  whether the local model can actually drive a bounded agent loop (tool-call
  reliability, `OLLAMA_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` burst behaviour) before local-default
  is locked in. If it can't, the fallback is Ollama Cloud, still unmetered.
- **Feature-flagged, default OFF.** Ship behind a flag (`AGENT_RUNNER_ENABLED` /
  reuse `SUBAGENT_ENABLED`) like the chat primitive; measure before defaulting on.

---

title: 8. Decisions
content:
**Settled (2026-09-07):**
1. **Default grain — task-level.** One agent oversees a *task*; per-step
   `run_agent` is the exception, not the wrapper for every step (§7).
2. **Provider policy — local-first, Ollama Cloud allowed, Gemini never** (§7).
   Background agents default to the local model; may opt into Ollama Cloud
   (unmetered) for harder tool-driving; never a rate-limited/metered model.
   *Phase 1 measures whether local can actually drive an agent loop before
   local-default is locked in.*

**Still open:**
3. **`:Project` vs "a Task that never gives up"** — a real new node (§6) vs tuning
   the evaluator loop with artifact continuity. The node is the honest primitive
   for iterative builds; the tuning gets ~80% for the "keep trying" case.
   **Leaning: defer.** Sequenced as Phase 4 (tentative) either way, only after the
   shared core (Phases 0–3) exists — decide when we get there.
4. **Who may write** — background `run_agent` writes (§3.2); confirm the inner
   write guard is sufficient vs a one-writer-per-chain rule.
5. **Selection** — LLM-chosen agent (orchestrator prompt) vs a deterministic
   `select_agent(goal)` specialty-match helper vs both. Start with the prompt;
   add the helper if routing needs to be LLM-free.
6. **Naming** — `run_agent` (proposed) vs reusing `delegate` for both paths. Keep
   them distinct: `delegate` is intercepted + streams into a live turn; `run_agent`
   is a normal tool whose result flows via `{{_prev}}`.

---

title: 9. Phased plan (part 1/2)
content:
- **Phase 0 — Extract `AgentRunner` (no behaviour change). ✅ DONE (2026-09-07).**
  Lifted the sub-agent loop out of `ChatService::run_subagent` into
  `services/agent_runner.rs` (`AgentRunner::run(agent, task, budget, sink)`,
  returning structured `AgentFindings`); `run_subagent` is now a thin streaming
  wrapper over it. The four provider loops and catalog-aware model resolution stay
  on `ChatService` — the delicate, incident-laden machinery — and `AgentRunner`
  reaches them through the `SubagentLoopRunner` trait (`ChatService` implements it
  by dispatching to its existing loops unchanged). The ownership cycle
  (`ChatService` owns `Arc<AgentRunner>`; `AgentRunner` holds
  `Weak<dyn SubagentLoopRunner>`) is broken with a `Weak`, wired via
  `Arc::new_cyclic` in the shared `ChatService::build` constructor. `AgentBudget`
  carries `max_iterations` + `allow_writes` (chat passes `false`, read-only, one
  writer per turn; the background path will pass `true`). Behaviour proven
  unchanged: all 437 lib tests green, `cargo fmt`/`clippy` clean, sub-agent guard
  tests (`profiles_are_not_spawnable_by_default`,
  `subagent_budget_is_tighter_than_the_orchestrator`, roster/findings tests)
  still pass. This is the load-bearing refactor — everything else depends on it,
  and it is the *correct* form of the deferred SUBAGENT Phase 4 (share the core,
  don't swap the lead).
  - **Known follow-up (a later phase, not Phase 0):** `agent_runner.rs` imports
    `ChatEvent`/`ChatRequest` from `clients::chat` — a `services`→`clients` bend
    (legal, one crate). When the background path lands, rename/relocate these to
    a neutral `AgentEvent`/`AgentTask` so the engine's I/O types don't read as
    "chat". Left as-is here to keep Phase 0 a pure, reviewable refactor.
- **Phase 1 — `run_agent` background tool. ✅ DONE (2026-09-07).**
  `skills/agent_runner.rs` (`AgentRunnerSkill`) exposes `run_agent(agent, task)`:
  it calls `AgentRunner::run` with **no sink** and `allow_writes: true` (writing
  is the background job; the inner agent keeps its own `TurnWriteGuard`), a
  bounded loop (`MAX_BACKGROUND_AGENT_ITERATIONS = 8`), depth 1 (the inner
  toolset never contains `run_agent`/`delegate`). The tool result carries the
  findings under `answer` (so it flows through `{{_prev}}`) plus `ok`/`retrieved`/
  `agent`. Registered to **both** `tool_registry` and the `skills` vec, **gated on
  `SUBAGENT_ENABLED`** (default OFF, plan §7). `lint_chain_steps` gains a rule: a
  `run_agent` step must have non-empty `agent` and `task` (spawnable-membership is
  enforced live by `run_agent` itself, which returns the roster for a bad name —
  the scheduler lint has no roster).
  - **Wiring — where the engine comes from.** The loop engine is `ChatService`
    (Phase 0). So `AgentRunner` needs a live chat service. `BrainCore` gained a
    lazy `agent_runner: Arc<RwLock<Option<Arc<AgentRunner>>>>` slot; the
    `AgentRunnerSkill` (built before the chat service exists) holds that slot and
    reads it per-call. `McpServerCore::chat_service()` — the single factory point,
    called once at startup — publishes `chat.agent_runner()` into the slot. On a
    deployment with no chat service (stdio), the slot stays empty and `run_agent`
    reports itself unavailable cleanly. **This makes `run_agent` an HTTP-path
    feature for now** — the honest consequence of the engine living in a client
    adapter; a later phase (or the Phase 0 follow-up) can lift the engine to
    brain-core to make it transport-independent.
  - `AgentFindings` gained a `rejected` flag so a caller can tell a config/infra
    rejection (unknown/non-spawnable agent, empty task, engine gone → hard tool
    error) from a ran-but-empty result (non-fatal step result — same rationale as
    `execute_code` treating a failed run as a successful tool call, so it does not
    dead-letter the owning Task).
  - Guard tests: `run_agent` tool shape; empty agent/task → hard error;
    unavailable runner reports cleanly; lint flags a `run_agent` step missing
    `agent`/`task` and passes a well-formed one. 443 lib tests green,
    `fmt`/`clippy` clean.
- **Phase 2 — choose-or-build. ✅ DONE (2026-09-07).** The "choose" half is now
  deterministic and LLM-free (decision 5: shipped the helper, since background
  routing benefits from not spending a model call to pick an agent):
  - `AgentRunner::select_agent(goal) -> AgentSelection { agent, score, roster }`
    scores each spawnable profile by token overlap between the goal and its
    `name + specialty` (tiny stopword filter, min length 3), returns the best
    above `MIN_SELECTION_OVERLAP = 1`, else `agent: None` — the cue to build. The
    full roster is always returned.
  - `select_agent(goal)` **tool** exposes it (result's `answer` is the chosen name
    or `"none"`, so a `{{_prev}}` hands the routing decision to the next step).
  - `run_agent` accepts **`agent: "auto"`** — auto-selects, and on no match
    returns a rejection naming the roster (the "build" cue). One-call choose.
  - **Prompt policy** (prefer-roster-then-construct): the `run_agent` and
    `select_agent` tool descriptions state "prefer an existing agent; construct
    only when none fit." The *build* half is the existing `construct_agent`
    (already reuse-before-construct), unchanged.
  - Tests: `tokenize` filtering; overlap discriminates a research goal toward the
    researcher; the skill exposes both tools. 445 lib tests green, fmt/clippy
    clean. *Deferred:* wiring `select_agent`/`run_agent` into `goal_to_steps`
    routing chains is Phase 3 (three front doors).
- **Phase 3 — three front doors. ✅ DONE (2026-09-07).** All three entrypoints
  now reach the shared loop:
  - **Task / todo.** `chains/run-agent.yaml` — a Task whose goal is prefixed
    `run agent:` / `delegate to agent:` routes (priority 20) to a single
    `run_agent(agent: "auto", task: {{goal_topic}})` step, then persists the

title: 9. Phased plan (part 2/2)
content:
findings and completes the task. `no_evaluator`/`no_adversarial` (one agent
    owns the grain; the iterative critic loop is Phase 4). This is "one agent per
    task" via the externalized-chain mechanism — `goal_to_steps` emits it by
    pattern, no code change.
  - **Scheduled task.** Any schedule step can now be `run_agent` (the Phase-1
    tool + lint rule already support it). No live schedule ships using it (it
    would error while `SUBAGENT_ENABLED` is off); documented for the user to add
    once enabled.
  - **Chat.** Already reaches the loop via `delegate` (Phase 0). Unchanged.
  - **Schedule-authoring delegation flow** (the user's malformed-schedule pain):
    `contexts/schedule-author.yaml` — a **spawnable** drafting specialist whose
    system prompt encodes every `lint_chain_steps` rule and whose job is to
    return a lint-clean `{name, interval_seconds, steps}` draft. Because a
    sub-agent is read-only (one writer per turn), it **drafts**; the orchestrator
    **upserts**. `contexts/orchestrator.yaml` gained `manage_scheduled_task` (the
    one write it performs) and a RECURRING WORK rule: delegate to
    `schedule-author`, then `manage_scheduled_task(upsert)` the draft, and on
    `step_warnings` send them back to be fixed. This closes the gap where the
    gemma orchestrator could not create a schedule at all.
  - **Bug fixed along the way:** `chain_seeder.rs` parsed `no_evaluator` but not
    `no_adversarial`, so the documented YAML field was a silent no-op for every
    seeded chain (`goal_to_steps` reads `c.no_adversarial`; only `manage_chain`
    wrote it). Now seeded correctly.
  - Guard tests: every shipped chain + context profile parses (would have caught
    the missing required `pattern`); run-agent skips both critics; schedule-author
    is spawnable with a specialty. 449 lib tests green, fmt/clippy clean.
- **Phase 4 — ⬜ REMAINING (tentative — decision 3 open) — iterative Project
  loop.** `(:Project)` node, `read_workspace_file`, `manage_project`,
  builder↔reviewer `run_agent` loop with artifact continuity and a DoD gate. The
  widget example, fully realised. Gated on the §8.3 call — may instead be a
  lighter tuning of the existing evaluator loop. Phases 0–3 have landed, so this
  is now the one substantive decision left: build the node vs the lighter tuning
  vs leave it. Recommendation: decide from real usage of Phases 0–3 with the flag
  on, rather than building it speculatively.
- **Phase 5 — ⬜ REMAINING (optional) — automatic proven-agent preference.** Fold
  `construct_agent`'s `PERFORMED` grading into `run_agent` selection so a proven
  agent for a recurring sub-goal is chosen without asking.
