title: Unified Agent Execution — Design Proposal
content:
Status (2026-09-07): **Phases 0–3 COMPLETE and live-smoke-tested; Phases 4–5
REMAINING (both were always optional/deferred).** The core is delivered — one
shared `AgentRunner` primitive reachable from all three goal entrypoints (chat,
tasks, schedules) with choose-or-build selection. What remains is the durable
iterative-project loop (Phase 4, tentative — §8 decision 3) and automatic
proven-agent preference (Phase 5, optional). Per-phase detail is in §9.

- ✅ **Phase 0** — extract `AgentRunner` (behaviour-neutral).
- ✅ **Phase 1** — `run_agent` background tool.
- ✅ **Phase 2** — choose-or-build (`select_agent`, `agent:"auto"`).
- ✅ **Phase 3** — three front doors (`chains/run-agent.yaml`, `schedule-author`).
- ⬜ **Phase 4** — iterative `:Project` build↔review loop (tentative; decide vs a
  lighter evaluator-loop tuning).
- ⬜ **Phase 5** — automatic proven-agent preference (optional).

Gated behind `SUBAGENT_ENABLED` (default OFF). Smoke-tested functionally
(routing + a live end-to-end `run_agent`); **not** yet load-, cost-, or
answer-quality-tested.

Read first: `project-docs/SUBAGENT_ORCHESTRATION_PLAN.md` (the chat-side
`delegate`/`run_subagent` primitive this generalises), the Externalized Agent
Chains / ScheduledTask ownership / Evaluator Loop / Adversarial Critic sections of
`CLAUDE.md`, and `crates/app/src/skills/constructor.rs`. This design is entirely
constrained by hard-won behaviour in those.

title: Deterministic Validation Engine + AiDevBoard Apply Integration
content:
Status: **design + phased build** (2026-09-09). Two related tracks from one session:
a schema/validation engine that pushes back on the LLM deterministically, and the
AiDevBoard agentic apply integration — which is itself the reference model for the
"the model cannot do the stupid thing" pattern the validation engine generalizes.

---

title: Track 1 — Deterministic validation engine › Design — two layers
content:
**Layer 1 · Structural (JSON Schema, HARD-REJECT).** New dep `jsonschema`. New
module `crates/app/src/services/validation.rs` exposing a `Validator` that:
- validates the **object envelope** against a schema in a new `schemas/` seed dir
  (`schemas/scheduled_task.json`, `task.json`, `scheduler_chain.json`,
  `context_profile.json`, …) — declarative, editable without a rebuild, consistent
  with `chains/` `schedules/` `contexts/` `sources/` (and the no-hardcoded-data
  rule). `SCHEMAS_DIR` compose env, non-fatal if missing (degrade to layer-2 only).
- validates **each step's `arguments`** against the live registry's
  `input_schema` for `step.tool_name`. This is the corruption-catcher.
- returns `Vec<Violation { severity: Hard | Soft, path, message }>`.

**Layer 2 · Semantic (rule lint, SOFT warnings — keep as is).** `lint_chain_steps`
rules (`reason` needs `context`; `provider_hint` top-level & present; persisting
step references `{{_prev}}`; `store_note` `source_context` + known `note_type`;
`semantic` in a web-searching chain; chain never persists) stay **warnings** —
they are correctness advice JSON Schema can't express. One rule graduates to HARD:
**unregistered tool** (a step naming no live tool fails every run — reject it).

**Enforcement points (write boundary):**
- `manage_scheduled_task` upsert  ← first, the proven pain point
- `manage_chain` define
- `create_task`
- `construct_agent`
- YAML seeders (`schedule_seeder`, `chain_seeder`, context loader) — a HARD
  violation logs loud + skips that node rather than aborting startup (a bad
  checked-in file shouldn't wedge the boot; a missing `schedules/` dir stays fatal).

Hard violation → `ToolCallResult::error(...)`, nothing written. Soft → existing
`step_warnings` / `needs_fix` response unchanged.

title: Track 1 — Deterministic validation engine › Key lever: tools already ship their own JSON Schema
content:
Every registered tool has an `input_schema` (`ToolDefinition.input_schema`, what
`tools/list` returns). `http_request`'s already declares `query_params: {type:
object}`, `timeout_ms: {type: integer}`, `pick: {type: array}`, `required:
[method, url]`. A JSON-Schema validator run against it **rejects the exact
corruption above**, and it generalizes to every tool with **zero schema drift** —
the tool definition is the authority, not a hand-maintained copy.

title: Track 1 — Deterministic validation engine › Phases
content:
- **P1 — DONE (2026-09-09, committed).** dep + `validation.rs` (`Violation`,
  `validate_against_schema`, `validate_step_arguments`) + `schemas/scheduled_task.json`
  + per-step arg-vs-`input_schema` HARD-reject wired into `manage_scheduled_task`
  upsert; 5 unit tests incl. the `query_params`-corruption regression.
- **P2 — DONE (2026-09-09, uncommitted).** The gate is extracted to a shared
  `SchedulerSkill::hard_reject_steps(label, steps)` and now also runs in
  **`manage_chain` define** (which previously did NO validation). Materialized the
  remaining schema artifacts — `schemas/scheduler_chain.json`, `schemas/task.json`,
  `schemas/context_profile.json` (self-contained; no external `$ref` since the
  validator runs with remote resolution off). Added `validation::load_schema_dir`
  (the envelope-layer loader: reads `schemas/*.json` by file stem, logs+skips a bad
  file, empty on missing dir) + a `all_committed_schemas_compile` guard test. 490
  lib tests green.
- **P3 — DONE (2026-09-09, uncommitted).** `load_schema_dir` wired in `brain_core`
  (`SCHEMAS_DIR`, default `./schemas`) → envelope map passed to `SchedulerSkill`
  (`with_envelope_schemas`). **Envelope validation** now runs in `manage_scheduled_task`
  upsert (against `scheduled_task`) and `manage_chain` define (against `scheduler_chain`)
  via `hard_reject_envelope`, alongside the per-step gate (`hard_reject_steps`, now on
  raw `Value` steps via the shared `validation::validate_step_array`). The **`audit`
  action** runs the same structural per-step gate over every STORED ScheduledTask
  (including YAML-seeded ones) and reports `structural_errors` per task — on-demand,
  zero boot risk. 493 lib tests green (8 in validation.rs).

  **Seeder skip-on-boot was investigated and deliberately NOT enabled.** Before wiring
  it, the gate was run over all 34 checked-in `schedules/*.yaml` + `chains/*.yaml` using
  the live registry's schemas. Finding: a boot-time hard-skip would have silently
  disabled real chains — (1) `chains/meta-learn.yaml` had `note_type: hypothesis`, an
  invalid enum (the 2026-09-08 class); **fixed in this pass** → `inference`; (2) any
  chain/schedule using a **conditionally-registered** tool (`run_agent`, gated on
  `SUBAGENT_ENABLED`) would be skipped whenever that feature is off — dropping
  `run-agent.yaml` / `api-scout.yaml`. Silently dropping a human-committed schedule on
  boot is a worse failure than a loud warning, so the safe form of pushback for the
  YAML path is the **on-demand `audit`** (above) — not an autonomous boot-time skip.
  (Also: `tools/list` over HTTP is `MCP_TOOL_PROFILE`-bounded, so a validator must use
  the in-process `registry.list()` full set, never the HTTP tool list.)

- **P3-remainder / P4 (deferred).** (a) `task` envelope in `create_task` and
  `context_profile` envelope in `construct_agent`/`POST /api/contexts` + the context
  YAML loader — LOW priority because those paths already parse typed serde inputs
  (serde rejects wrong types / missing required today); the schemas are materialized
  and documented, enforcement is the only gap. (b) True seeder skip-on-hard, once
  conditional-tool registration is modelled and tool `input_schema`s are tightened
  (`additionalProperties: false`, one-of for `ingest_api`'s `spec_url`/`docs_url`/
  `codebase_path`, string value types on `query_params`).

Note: `create_task` and `construct_agent` already parse typed serde inputs, so
serde rejects wrong types / missing required today — the envelope schemas add
enum/min-length polish and a single documented contract, not the core protection.
The core protection is the per-step `arguments` gate (P1+P2), because
`ChainStep.arguments` is the one untyped `Value` on the write path.

---

title: Track 1 — Deterministic validation engine › Problem
content:
Objects the LLM (chat or a background loop) can write into the graph —
`ScheduledTask`, `Task`, `SchedulerChain`, agent (`ContextProfile`), and each
step's tool `arguments` — are only shape-checked today. `manage_scheduled_task`
upsert does `serde_json::from_str::<Vec<ChainStep>>` (envelope shape only) then
`lint_chain_steps` (semantic **warnings**, never rejects — it saves anyway and
tells the model "SAVED BUT LIKELY BROKEN"). `ChainStep.arguments` is a free
`serde_json::Value`, so wrong-typed tool args pass straight through.

The motivating failure: the **AI Dev Board Job Search** schedule was written with
`query_params: "[object Object]"` (a stringified JS object), `timeout_ms: "15000"`
(string), `pick` as a comma-string — the HBI editor serialized structured args to
strings. `http_request`'s strict `Input` struct rejected them at *runtime*, so the
step errored every run and the chain silently died. Nothing caught it at write time.

title: Track 1 — Deterministic validation engine › Why this is the "classic automated pushback"
content:
The gate is deterministic and runs before persistence, so the model cannot save a
structurally invalid object no matter how confidently it narrates success — the
same principle AiDevBoard enforces for applications (below).

title: Track 1 round 2 (2026-10-16): every boundary is a web form
content:
Owner's ask: validate and sanitise every input like a web form, agents and profiles included. Principle: one gate per boundary, every caller passes through it, refuse and say what is allowed (never drop silently). Shape (types, keys, enums) is parsed; free-text fields get a regex (`pattern` in the schema); authority (may this write / reach that host) is enforced by the engine or by where the call runs, never by text matching or an argument.

Measured before planning: no gate at dispatch (`ToolHandler::execute` passes arguments straight to the skill; serde rejects wrong types only). Replay of 25,325 calls since 09-16: ~230 calls logged as successes with an argument silently dropped (list_tasks status/limit 73 — it takes no arguments; store_note tags 33; search_web max_results/top_n/recency_days 21; lookup slots ~60). Profile save accepted an unknown tool, an unknown model, `../x` as a name and misspelled keys; the profile audit runs only at startup. `schemas/context_profile.json` and `task.json` are loaded and never used. REST workflow save passes `envelope: None`.

- **Phase 0 — DONE 2026-10-16.** Raw graph writes only from workflow steps and operator calls; read access mode for every read-only Cypher path; DuckDB single SELECT by its own parser; model-saved workflows cannot add raw writes; refusals stop teaching the bypass.
- **Phase 1 — BUILT 2026-10-16, in shadow; enforce decision after a week (~2026-10-23).** As designed below; the REST workflow save and its dry-run check now take the workflow.json envelope (which allows a null description, as the HBI sends). Live: 39 of 40 stored workflows pass the envelope (the 40th is the broken-on-purpose self-test fixture); the first deploy minutes recorded no misfit from workflow steps. Review: `SELECT tool, purpose, count(*) FROM arg_checks GROUP BY ALL`. Original design: In `ToolHandler::execute`, check arguments against the tool's registered input_schema: unknown keys (with a did-you-mean), types, enums, required; `__` keys pass. Fix lying schemas first (list_tasks, lookup's per-view slots). Shadow mode (log the would-be refusals to telemetry) for a week, then enforce. Also give the REST workflow save its envelope schema.
- **Phase 2 — DONE 2026-10-16** (rule "A profile save is checked like a form"). Original: Hard on save (and loud at seed): unknown keys, name `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}$`, tools exist (or their plugin is off), model_preference and fallback_models in the catalog, spawnable ⇒ specialty, routing targets exist and are spawnable. Soft: prompt size for a local pin, write tools on a spawnable agent. Re-run the audit on every save and show it in the HBI. Use or delete the two unused schema files.
- **Phase 3 — DONE 2026-10-16.** HTTP half: `net_policy` (rule "A model's URL reaches public hosts only"). DuckDB half: external access locked off at telemetry init, json compiled in (rule "Who may write is decided by where a call runs"). Original: http_request (and read_page) host policy: parse, resolve, refuse loopback/private/link-local/internal service names unless the host belongs to a registered ApiContext or an allowlist; measure which internal hosts are called today first. DuckDB external access (file/URL reads in a SELECT).
- **Phase 4 — DONE 2026-10-16, in shadow with Phase 1** (rule "Every tool call is checked against its schema"). Declared plugin tools were already covered by the dispatch check; `mcp_call` arguments are now checked against the remote tool's `inputSchema`. First run found the disabled `ai-dev-board-job-search` workflow sending worklittle a `workplace_type` it does not take. The 2026-10-23 enforce review covers both (`arg_checks` rows `mcp_call:%`). Not done: a workflow save does not check an `mcp_call` step's inner arguments (it would need the network at save time).
- Original Phase 4: Declared plugin tools and `mcp_call`: check arguments against the remote tool's published schema.

title: Track 2 — AiDevBoard agentic apply (full MCP-client loop) › Design
content:
- **Outbound MCP client** (`services/mcp_client.rs` or reuse an HTTP JSON-RPC
  helper) to `aidevboard.com/mcp`; auth via a seeded `aidevboard` `ApiContext`
  (injects `X-API-Key`, env `AIDEVEBOARD_KEY`).
- **Skill** exposing the toolchain as brain tools (thin wrappers with the
  human-in-the-loop preserved): search/analyze/compile are autonomous-safe;
  compile → `notify_user` with `artifact_markdown` **verbatim** + the approval
  question + `create_task("Apply: <title> @ <company>")`, then STOP. approve +
  submit run **only** on Ara's explicit in-chat approval. Brain never auto-submits.
- **Evidence** comes from the résumé notes (`source_context: "resume"`); the
  brain SELECTS relevant bullets per job (grounded selection, never invention) and
  uses `analyze_application_readiness` `missing_signals` to decide which further
  résumé bullets to pull before recompiling.
- **Rewire** the daily **AI Dev Board Job Search** schedule from
  `http_request` + `execute_code` filter to `match_jobs` (server-side ranking with
  Ara's skill vector).
- **Rewrite** the JOB APPLICATION RULE in `contexts/general.yaml` around this real
  toolchain (it predates the discovery and assumes apply is not API-reachable).

title: Track 2 — AiDevBoard agentic apply (full MCP-client loop) › Guardrails / conventions
content:
- Never claim an application was submitted unless `apply_to_job` returned success.
- Persisted compile is a benign draft (expires); approve/apply are the
  outward-facing, human-gated steps — treat like any hard-to-reverse action.
- One real walkthrough draft exists: `adb_art_S3knUSlXE1kFodZm` (Harvey AI Staff
  SWE Model Infra), expires 2026-09-16, unsubmitted.

title: Track 2 — AiDevBoard agentic apply (full MCP-client loop) › What exists (verified live 2026-09-09)
content:
`AIDEVEBOARD_KEY` in `.env` is an **email-verified** free developer key (100/hr).
Spec `https://aidevboard.com/openapi.yaml`. A full **MCP server at
`https://aidevboard.com/mcp`** (JSON-RPC, `X-API-Key`) exposes the apply toolchain;
the REST `/candidate/resume-preview` is transient-only, so the **persisted/approved/
submitted** path is MCP-only → the brain must be an MCP **client** to AiDevBoard.

6-stage gated flow (all $0 to candidate/agent):
1. `match_jobs {skills[],workplace,level,salary_*}` — server-side ranked matches
   (`match_score`, `matched_tags`, `match_reasons`). Recommended agentic search.
2. `get_job {id}` — full JD.
3. `analyze_application_readiness {job_id,candidate_skills,evidence_bullets}` —
   deterministic gap analysis: `matched_signals` vs `missing_signals`,
   `coverage_ratio`; NO acceptance probability; `improvement_loop.agent_rule` =
   "never invent/infer/embellish; recompile only with human-confirmed evidence."
4. `compile_job_specific_resume {job_id,evidence_bullets}` — with the verified key
   PERSISTS an immutable artifact: `artifact_id`, `artifact_hash` (sha256),
   `artifact_status: draft`, 7-day expiry, `artifact_markdown`. **Rejects hidden
   text / screening-model instructions / unsupported claims.** Returns
   `candidate_review.must_pause: true`.
5. `approve_compiled_application {artifact_id,artifact_hash,principal_authorized}`
   — single-use, short-lived authorization bound to exact hash + verified
   candidate + unchanged job.
6. `apply_to_job {job_id,principal_authorized,compiled_artifact_id,
   compiled_artifact_hash,compiled_authorization_id}` — submits ONLY the exact
   approved hash; consumes the authorization. Then
   `record_my_application_outcome` / `list_my_interview_outcomes`.

The apply path is content-addressed and human-gated at the protocol level: the
model cannot submit anything the human didn't approve by exact hash.

title: 1. Design decisions (locked)
content:
| Decision | Choice |
|----------|--------|
| Transcript source | **Captions first, Whisper fallback.** Pull YouTube/native captions via `yt-dlp` (free, no GPU). Only download audio + transcribe with Whisper when a video has no captions. |
| Source scope | **All of:** YouTube channels/playlists, ad-hoc video URLs, podcast RSS / audio files, local video files. |
| Trigger model | **Both:** autonomous scheduled watch of a channel/feed watchlist **and** on-demand ingestion of arbitrary links. |

These map onto the existing architecture almost 1:1 — the `learn` chain
(`chains/learn.yaml`: search → reason → store_note → update_task) is the exact
shape a video-learning chain takes, and a YouTube channel watchlist is the
`SourceList` pattern (`sources/*.yaml`, graph-owned after first seed).

---

title: 10. Risks & mitigations
content:
- **`yt-dlp` / YouTube fragility & ToS / rate limits** — prefer the free RSS feed
  for discovery (not scraping), poll politely (6h default), cap concurrency via
  the queue's Ollama semaphore. Keep `yt-dlp` a swappable binary.
- **Transcript length → LLM cost** — map on the local model, reduce on cloud;
  `MEDIA_MAX_DURATION_SECS` guard; skip re-ingest via `:Media` dedup.
- **Auto-caption noise** — acceptable for summarization; note
  `transcript_source` so downstream reasoning can weight accordingly.
- **Subprocess security** — arg arrays only, URL-scheme validation, `file://`
  allowlisted to `MEDIA_DIR`.
- **Summary contamination** — the compare `reason` step MUST pass prior output
  via `context: "{{_prev}}"`, never inline in the question (RAG-contamination
  footgun).

---

title: 11. Docs to update (per branch strategy: docs first)
content:
- `CLAUDE.md` — new skill in the structure tree + skill count, env var table,
  a "Media Learning" section describing the watch→ingest→learn loop, the new
  nodes/relationships, and `sources-media/` ownership semantics.
- `project-docs/STATUS.md` — tool count + feature status.
- `MEMORY.md` + a topic file — one-line index entry pointing to a
  `media-learning.md` memory capturing the non-obvious wiring (RSS discovery →
  Task fan-out → chain; captions-before-whisper; map-reduce inside the tool).

---

title: 2. Why this fits the current architecture
content:
The brain already has every primitive this feature needs:

- **External-fetch skill pattern** — `skills/search.rs` shells to an HTTP API,
  returns JSON, degrades gracefully when unconfigured (logs a knowledge gap).
  Media ingestion is the same shape with `yt-dlp` instead of SerpApi.
- **Fetch → reason → store_note chains** — `chains/learn.yaml` and
  `chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml`. A video chain is a drop-in sibling.
- **Task-driven scheduler** — `status=created` Tasks are matched to chains by
  `goal_to_steps()` and dispatched. New videos become Tasks; the scheduler does
  the rest. No new dispatch machinery required.
- **YAML-seeded, graph-owned config lists** — `SourceList` (`sources/*.yaml`),
  `ScheduledTask` (`schedules/*.yaml`), `SchedulerChain` (`chains/*.yaml`). A
  `MediaSource` watchlist follows the `SourceList` seeder pattern exactly.
- **store_note pipeline** — already runs async entity extraction
  (`spawn_extract_entities`), similarity linking, and spaced-repetition
  scheduling. Video summaries flow into this for free, so concepts become
  `:Entity` nodes and relate to existing knowledge automatically.
- **Per-step model routing** — `provider_hint` / `required_capabilities` let the
  cheap map-summaries run on the local model and the final synthesis run on a
  stronger cloud model (see how `daily-news.yaml` uses `provider_hint: ollama-cloud`
  only for the final write step).

**Net:** almost no new *architecture*. The new surface is one skill, one service
module, a couple of graph nodes, and YAML for chains/schedules/watchlist.

---

title: 3. New components › 3.1 `services/media.rs` — transcript acquisition + summarization service
content:
Owns the subprocess boundary and the LLM map-reduce. Pure logic, no MCP types.

Responsibilities:
1. **Metadata** — `yt-dlp -J <url>` → parse JSON for `id`, `title`, `uploader`,
   `channel_id`, `upload_date`, `duration`, `description`, `webpage_url`,
   available `subtitles` / `automatic_captions`.
2. **Captions** — request `en` (configurable) subtitle track in `json3` or `vtt`
   via `yt-dlp --skip-download --write-subs --write-auto-subs --sub-lang en
   --sub-format json3 -o <tmp>`; parse the cue file into plain text (strip
   timestamps/formatting). Prefer human subs over auto-captions when both exist.
3. **Whisper fallback** (Phase 4) — if no caption track: `yt-dlp -x --audio-format
   mp3 -o <tmp>` then transcribe via a pluggable transcriber (see §6).
4. **Map-reduce summarization** — transcripts run long (a 1-hr talk ≈ 8–12k
   words), and the chain is fixed-length, so **the windowing must happen *inside*
   the tool, not as chain steps.** Chunk the transcript (reuse the knowledge
   chunker's philosophy: split on paragraph, then sentence, ~1500-char windows),
   summarize each window ("map") with the local model, then synthesize
   ("reduce") into a structured summary with a stronger model. Return:
   `{ video_id, title, channel, channel_id, url, published_at, duration_secs,
   transcript_source: "captions"|"whisper", summary, key_concepts: [..],
   transcript_len }`. Optionally include the full transcript when asked.

Subprocess rules:
- Invoke `yt-dlp`/`ffmpeg` with **arg arrays, never a shell string** (no
  injection surface). Validate the URL scheme (`http/https`, or a `file://`
  allowlisted to `MEDIA_DIR` for local files).
- Binaries are configurable (`YT_DLP_PATH`, `FFMPEG_PATH`) and default to PATH
  lookup. If the binary is missing, return a clear, actionable error and (like
  `search.rs`) log a tool-config knowledge gap — do **not** panic.
- Temp files go under `MEDIA_DIR` (default: the session scratch/tmp); clean up
  after parse.

title: 3. New components › 3.2 `skills/media.rs` — MCP tools
content:
New `MediaSkill`. Holds `Arc<RwLock<Option<LlmConfig>>>` (read per call via
`make_llm()`, same as other skills) plus `Neo4jClient` and the media service.
Tools:

- `ingest_media(url, source_context?, store?)` — the workhorse. Fetch metadata +
  transcript (captions→whisper), run map-reduce summary, upsert a `:Media` node
  for dedup, and return the structured summary. When `store: true`, also writes
  the summary `:Note` and links it (see §4). Default `store: false` so chains
  keep control of storage (consistent with `search_web` returning, `store_note`
  storing).
- `fetch_transcript(url, lang?)` — lower-level: return raw transcript text only
  (no summary). For direct Q&A / RAG grounding.
- `list_channel_videos(source, since?)` — given a channel/playlist/RSS ref,
  return recent videos **filtered to those not yet ingested** (no `:Media` node).
  Uses YouTube's free per-channel RSS feed
  `https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=<id>` (and
  `?playlist_id=<id>`) — no API key, ~15 latest items with IDs + publish dates.
- `poll_media_sources()` — iterate all active `:MediaSource` nodes, call
  `list_channel_videos` for each, and **`create_task("watch video: <url>", …)`**
  for every new video. This is the autonomous entry point; the scheduler then
  routes each Task through the video-learning chain. (Chains can't loop over a
  dynamic list, so we fan out into Tasks instead — matches the Task-driven core.)
- `manage_media_source(action, name, kind, ref, description?, active?)` —
  runtime CRUD for the watchlist (mirrors `manage_scheduled_task`). YAML is the
  seed source; graph is authority after first create (see §5).

**Registration:** register every tool in BOTH `tool_registry` (for `tools/list`)
AND the `skills` vec (for `tools/call`) in `brain_core.rs::build_skills()` —
forgetting either yields an invisible tool or a dispatch failure. `self_model.rs`
introspection re-syncs the meta-graph automatically at the end of `build_skills`.

title: 3. New components › 3.3 Chains
content:
**`chains/video-learning.yaml`** — pattern `"watch video:"` (+ patterns
`"summarize video"`, `"ingest video"`). This is the learning loop:

1. `ingest_media` — `url` extracted from the goal; returns structured summary.
   `provider_hint: ollama` for the map pass; the reduce inside the tool can use a
   `required_capabilities: ["reasoning"]` step-level hint.
2. `search_notes` — query on the returned `key_concepts` to pull *existing*
   related knowledge (this is what turns "summarize" into "learn").
3. `reason` — **context = `{{_prev}}`** (critical: scheduled `reason` steps must
   pass prior output via `context`, never inline in the question, or RAG eats its
   own output → garbage loop; see the reason-RAG-contamination note). Prompt:
   "Given this new video summary and the existing related notes, state (a) what
   is genuinely NEW vs. what the brain already knew, (b) what CHANGED/updated an
   existing understanding, (c) concepts that are important but thinly covered."
   Use `provider_hint: ollama-cloud` for this synthesis step.
4. `store_note` — `note_type: semantic`, `source_context: video_learning`,
   content = the video summary + the new/changed analysis. Links to `:Media`
   (via `ingest_media` storing, or a follow-up `neo4j_query` step creating
   `(:Note)-[:SUMMARIZES]->(:Media)`).
5. `create_task` (conditional) — for each thinly-covered key concept, create a
   `"fill knowledge gap: <concept>"` Task, feeding the **existing** curiosity
   engine (`chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml`). This is how watching a video
   triggers deeper autonomous research.
6. `update_task` — mark the video Task `completed`.

Set `no_adversarial: true` (ingestion isn't high-stakes planning). Let the
evaluator run only if the Task carries `success_criteria`.

title: 3. New components › 3.4 Schedules
content:
**`schedules/media-watch.yaml`** — a single-step ScheduledTask running
`poll_media_sources` on an interval (default 6h / 21600s). It creates one
`"watch video: <url>"` Task per new video; the scheduler dispatches them through
`chains/video-learning.yaml` on subsequent ticks. Gate the whole thing behind
`MEDIA_WATCH_ENABLED` so deployments without `yt-dlp` don't spawn failing tasks.

---

title: 4. Data model additions
content:
New nodes (declare indexes in `repository/client.rs::init_schema`):

- **`:MediaSource`** — the watchlist. `{ name (unique), kind:
  'youtube_channel'|'youtube_playlist'|'podcast_rss', ref (channel_id /
  playlist_id / rss_url), description, active: bool, managed_by: 'yaml'|'runtime' }`.
  YAML-seeded (§5). Analogous to `:SourceList`.
- **`:Media`** — dedup + provenance ledger. `{ id (video_id, unique), url, title,
  channel, channel_id, published_at, duration_secs, transcript_source, ingested_at,
  source_media_name }`. Existence check gates re-ingestion.

Relationships:

- `(:Media)-[:FROM_SOURCE]->(:MediaSource)` — which watchlist entry surfaced it.
- `(:Note)-[:SUMMARIZES]->(:Media)` — the summary note ↔ its source video.
- Reuse existing `(:Note)-[:MENTIONS {count}]->(:Entity)` from the store_note
  pipeline — concepts in the summary become first-class entities and connect to
  everything else the brain knows. No new extraction code needed.
- Optional later: `(:Media)-[:COVERS]->(:Entity)` for direct video→concept lookup.

**"Stay up to date on things it already knows"** falls out of this: the watch
schedule tracks channels about known topics; a new video that `MENTIONS` an
`:Entity` the brain already has, and whose `reason` step flags a CHANGE, gets an
`inference`/`outcome` note capturing *what updated* — surfacing deltas rather than
re-storing what's known.

---

title: 5. Watchlist seeding (`sources-media/*.yaml`)
content:
New seed dir `SOURCES_MEDIA_DIR` (default `./sources-media`), a new
`services/media_source_seeder.rs` modeled on `services/source_seeder.rs`:
**seed ON CREATE only**, graph-owned thereafter (runtime edits via
`manage_media_source` / `neo4j_query` persist across restarts; delete a node to
re-seed from YAML). Missing directory is non-fatal.

Example `sources-media/ai-research.yaml`:
```yaml
name: ai-research
description: Channels covering AI/ML research and engineering.
sources:
  - kind: youtube_channel
    ref: UCbfYPyITQ-7l4upoX8nvctg   # channel_id
    description: Two Minute Papers
  - kind: youtube_playlist
    ref: PLxxxxxx
    description: A curated playlist
```
Per the **no-hardcoded-data-in-Rust** rule, all channel IDs / feed URLs live in
YAML + graph, never Rust literals.

---

title: 6. Whisper transcriber abstraction (Phase 4)
content:
Mirror the LLM provider pattern (`services/llm.rs` is multi-provider, config-driven).
Add a `Transcriber` trait with implementations selected by env:

- `WHISPER_PROVIDER` = `none` (default) | `whisper-local` (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper
  binary) | `openai` | `groq` (both cheap hosted Whisper).
- `WHISPER_MODEL`, `WHISPER_API_KEY`, `WHISPER_BASE_URL`, `WHISPER_BIN_PATH`.

Only invoked when captions are absent. Podcasts and local files (§ Phase 5)
always use this path.

---

title: 7. Config / env vars (add to `config.rs` + CLAUDE.md table)
content:
| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `YT_DLP_PATH` | `yt-dlp` | Path to yt-dlp binary. |
| `FFMPEG_PATH` | `ffmpeg` | Path to ffmpeg (audio extraction for Whisper). |
| `MEDIA_DIR` | session scratch | Temp dir for downloads/caption files; also the allowlist root for `file://` local ingestion. |
| `MEDIA_CAPTION_LANG` | `en` | Preferred caption language. |
| `MEDIA_MAX_DURATION_SECS` | `10800` | Skip videos longer than this (cost guard). |
| `MEDIA_WATCH_ENABLED` | `false` | Enable the autonomous watch schedule. |
| `SOURCES_MEDIA_DIR` | `./sources-media` | MediaSource watchlist YAML seeds. |
| `WHISPER_PROVIDER` | `none` | `none`/`whisper-local`/`openai`/`groq`. |
| `WHISPER_MODEL` / `WHISPER_API_KEY` / `WHISPER_BASE_URL` / `WHISPER_BIN_PATH` | — | Whisper config (Phase 4). |

---

title: 8. Phased implementation
content:
> **Status (implemented):** Phases 1–5 are built. Phase 1–3:
> `MediaService`, `MediaSkill` (6 tools incl. `spawn_gap_tasks`), `:Media`/`:MediaSource`
> nodes + schema, `media_source_seeder`, `chains/video-learning.yaml`,
> `schedules/media-watch.yaml`, a 13-channel watchlist, all wired into `build_skills`
> with a `MEDIA_WATCH_MAX_PER_SOURCE` first-poll guard. **Phase 4 (Whisper):**
> `services/transcribe.rs` (`Transcriber` trait → `HttpTranscriber`) POSTs best-audio
> (via `yt-dlp -f bestaudio`) to a **self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible** Whisper endpoint;
> the `whisper` compose sidecar runs `faster-whisper-server` on **GPU** (`:latest-cuda`,
> `float16`) — host driver 535.261.03 / CUDA 12.2 satisfies the image; falls back to
> `:latest-cpu` if the driver ever lags. Requires `yt-dlp` on PATH. **Phase 5
> (podcasts + local files):** `fetch_transcript` classifies its input (`MediaInput`
> enum) and dispatches — yt-dlp URLs (captions-first), direct audio URLs (podcast
> enclosures / hosted `.mp3`/`.mp4` → reqwest download + Whisper), and `file://` local
> files (canonicalized + confined to `MEDIA_DIR`, symlink-escape safe → Whisper).
> `kind: podcast_rss` sources are polled like YouTube channels (`parse_rss_feed` reads
> RSS 2.0 `<enclosure>` URLs) and fan out into `watch video:` Tasks; dedup ids for
> non-yt-dlp media are a stable FNV-1a hash of the URL/path.

**Phase 1 — Captions MVP, on-demand (highest value, lowest cost).**
`services/media.rs` (metadata + caption fetch + map-reduce summary), `MediaSkill`
with `ingest_media` + `fetch_transcript`, `:Media` dedup node,
`chains/video-learning.yaml` routed by `"watch video:"`, summary stored as a
`semantic` note. Deliverable: paste a URL / create a "watch video:" Task → get a
stored, entity-linked summary.

**Phase 2 — Autonomous channel/playlist watch.** `:MediaSource` node + YAML
seeder + `manage_media_source`, `list_channel_videos` (RSS), `poll_media_sources`,
`schedules/media-watch.yaml`. Deliverable: tracked channels auto-ingest new
uploads.

**Phase 3 — Learning loop.** Add the `search_notes` + compare `reason` +
gap-task-spawning steps to the chain; `SUMMARIZES` links; new-vs-changed
analysis. Deliverable: videos update known topics and trigger curiosity research.

**Phase 4 — Whisper fallback.** `Transcriber` trait + providers; caption-less
YouTube videos become ingestible.

**Phase 5 — Podcasts + local files.** Podcast RSS `kind` in MediaSource; local
`file://` ingestion under `MEDIA_DIR`. Both ride the Phase-4 Whisper path.

---

title: 9. Testing
content:
- **Unit (CI-safe, no network/binaries):** caption parsing (json3/vtt fixtures →
  plain text), RSS feed parsing (sample XML fixture), dedup logic, map-reduce
  chunk windowing, URL validation / injection guards. Store fixtures under
  `crates/app/tests/fixtures/media/`.
- **Integration (gated):** put live `yt-dlp`/RSS tests behind an env gate
  (e.g. `MEDIA_IT=1`) and a stable known video, so `cargo test` on CI without
  `yt-dlp` stays green. Mirror how Neo4j integration tests are separated.
- Verify graceful degradation: missing `yt-dlp` → clean error + logged gap, not a
  panic.

---

title: Appendix A — Full example `chains/video-learning.yaml` (part 1/2)
content:
Routed to any Task whose goal starts with `watch video:` (created on-demand or by
`poll_media_sources`). This is the **learning** version, with the new-vs-known
comparison. A minimal "just summarize" variant drops steps 2–6 and stores the
raw summary directly (like `learn.yaml`).

**Why the working-memory bank/reassemble steps:** a chain's `{{_prev}}` carries
**only the immediately preceding step's output**. The final note must contain
BOTH the video summary AND the new-vs-known analysis, and the `reason` step needs
the summary as its `context`. So — exactly as `daily-news.yaml` does — each
intermediate output is banked into a per-task `WorkingMemory` session with
`push_context`, then a `neo4j_query` step reassembles the pieces before the step
that needs more than one of them. The final step deletes the scratch session.

```yaml
# chains/video-learning.yaml
#
# Watch/ingest a video and learn from it: fetch transcript, summarize,
# compare against existing knowledge (NEW vs KNOWN vs CHANGED), and store a
# sourced note linked to a :Media dedup node.
#
# {{_prev}} only carries the PREVIOUS step's output, so intermediate outputs are
# banked in the WorkingMemory session "video-{{task_id}}" and reassembled with a
# neo4j_query step before any step that needs more than one of them. The final
# step deletes the scratch session (same idiom as chains/daily-news.yaml).
name: video-learning
pattern: "watch video:"
patterns:
  - "summarize video"
  - "ingest video"
  - "watch this video"
priority: 40
no_adversarial: true       # ingestion isn't high-stakes planning — skip pre-flight
description: "Watch/ingest a video: fetch transcript, map-reduce summarize, compare against existing knowledge, and store a sourced semantic note linked to its :Media node."
steps:
  # 1. Fetch metadata + transcript (captions → whisper fallback) and map-reduce
  #    summarize INSIDE the tool (chains are fixed-length; transcripts are not).
  #    `url` accepts the raw goal ("watch video: <url>"); the tool extracts the
  #    first http(s) URL. Upserts a :Media node (dedup) and returns structured
  #    JSON: { video_id, title, channel, url, summary, key_concepts, ... }.
  - tool_name: ingest_media
    arguments:
      url: "{{goal}}"
      source_context: video_learning
      store: false
    priority: 1
    max_attempts: 3
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Fetch transcript + map-reduce summary"

  # 2. Bank the summary so it survives past the reason step below.
  - tool_name: push_context
    arguments:
      session_id: "video-{{task_id}}"
      content: "## VIDEO SUMMARY\n{{_prev}}"
      role: observation
    priority: 1
    max_attempts: 2
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Bank the summary in working memory"

  # 3. Reassemble the banked summary so it can be passed as `context` (not the
  #    push confirmation that {{_prev}} now holds).
  - tool_name: neo4j_query
    arguments:
      cypher: "MATCH (w:WorkingMemory {session_id: 'video-{{task_id}}'}) RETURN w.content AS content ORDER BY w.turn_index"
    priority: 1
    max_attempts: 3
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Reassemble summary for the reason step"

  # 4. Compare the new material against what the brain already knows. context =
  #    the summary (NEVER restate it inside `question` — scheduled reason RAGs the
  #    graph off the question and would eat its own output → garbage loop). The
  #    reason tool's internal RAG surfaces topically-related existing notes.
  - tool_name: reason
    arguments:
      question: |
        The CONTEXT contains a summary of a video the brain just watched.
        Compare it against what is already known and write three sections:
        ## NEW — concepts/claims genuinely new to the brain
        ## CHANGED — where this updates or contradicts prior understanding
        ## FOLLOW UP — important concepts that are thinly covered and worth
        researching further (one concise line each; these seed gap tasks)
        Ground every point in the CONTEXT. If nothing is new, say so plainly.
      context: "{{_prev}}"
      store_inference: false
    priority: 2
    max_attempts: 3
    # Synthesis benefits from a stronger model; router picks the best catalog
    # match within CLOUD_TIER. Any hint other than "ollama" uses the active
    # config instead of the weak local model.
    provider_hint: ollama-cloud
    required_capabilities: ["reasoning"]
    description: "New-vs-known comparison"

  # 5. Bank the analysis alongside the summary.
  - tool_name: push_context
    arguments:
      session_id: "video-{{task_id}}"
      content: "## NEW vs KNOWN ANALYSIS\n{{_prev}}"
      role: observation
    priority: 1
    max_attempts: 2
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Bank the analysis in working memory"

  # 6. Reassemble summary + analysis into one blob for the stored note.
  - tool_name: neo4j_query
    arguments:
      cypher: "MATCH (w:WorkingMemory {session_id: 'video-{{task_id}}'}) RETURN w.content AS content ORDER BY w.turn_index"
    priority: 1
    max_attempts: 3
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Reassemble summary + analysis for storage"

  # 7. Persist the durable semantic note. store_note's async pipeline runs entity
  #    extraction + similarity linking, so key concepts become :Entity nodes and
  #    connect to existing knowledge automatically. A follow-up neo4j_query (or
  #    ingest_media store:true) creates (:Note)-[:SUMMARIZES]->(:Media).
  - tool_name: store_note
    arguments:
      content: "# Video learning: {{goal}}\n\n{{_prev}}"
      note_type: semantic
      source_context: video_learning
    priority: 1
    max_attempts: 3
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Store the sourced summary note"

  # 8. Mark the video Task done.
  - tool_name: update_task
    arguments:
      task_id: "{{task_id}}"
      status: completed
    priority: 1
    max_attempts: 3
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Complete the task"

title: Appendix A — Full example `chains/video-learning.yaml` (part 2/2)
content:
# 9. Clean up the scratch working-memory session.
  - tool_name: neo4j_query
    arguments:
      cypher: "MATCH (w:WorkingMemory {session_id: 'video-{{task_id}}'}) DETACH DELETE w"
      readonly: false
    priority: 0
    max_attempts: 2
    provider_hint: ollama
    description: "Delete scratch session"
```

**Gap-task fan-out (deliberately not a chain step):** the `## FOLLOW UP`
concepts should become `"fill knowledge gap: <concept>"` Tasks so the existing
curiosity engine (`chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml`) researches them. A chain
can't loop over a dynamic list, so do this the same way new videos are handled:
have `ingest_media` (or a small dedicated tool) parse the follow-up concepts and
call `create_task` per concept. Keep it out of the linear YAML.

---

title: Appendix B — `init_schema` Cypher (add to `crates/repository/src/client.rs`)
Media Learning Plan — Watch & Summarize Videos to Learn and Stay Current
content:
Handoff plan for implementing autonomous video/audio ingestion in the Agent Brain.
Goal: let the brain **watch and summarize videos (and podcasts/audio)** so it can
**learn new concepts** and **stay up to date on topics it already knows**.

This document is the spec. Implement it in phases; each phase is independently
shippable and testable.

---

title: A named thing is a view; the model picks it and fills its slots, it does not write Cypher
content:
Rules (built 2026-10-13; `crates/host/src/views.rs`):

- **A view is data:** `views/<name>.yaml` in the bundle that owns the data, with `{name, kind, description, words}`. `words` is what people call the thing ("daily brief", "news brief"), because Phase 1 measured that free-form Cypher fails on *where things live in this brain*, not on Cypher: E4B got 10 of 33, codestral 8 and Text2Cypher 4B 2.
- **`kind: cypher`** is a fixed read query on the declared-tool rules (`bundle_tools::check_query`). The caller always supplies `$today`, `$day_start`, `$now` and `$tz`, so a view never does its own time arithmetic or compares a datetime to a string.
- **`kind: notes`** is a preset over `NoteSpec` (window, on, kinds, from, topic, entity, words, status, as, order, limit). Its compiler bounds windows in local days (`clock::local_midnight_utc`), matches entity names lower-case or by alias, and passes every value as a parameter. A call may not set a slot the preset fixes; the generic `notes` view fixes nothing.
- **Views are not MCP tools.** One tool, `lookup`, runs a view or (with no arguments) lists them all, with their slots and any skipped files. Don't register views as tools: the tool list would grow with the catalog, and small models pick tools badly.
- **Names a model cannot guess are closed lists from the live graph.** `lookup {}` gives the note slots `topic`, `from` and `kinds` their live values (with labels), and a cypher view's slot may declare `values_from: <query returning value[, label]>`. An unknown topic or value is refused with the list. Without this, every writer invented names (`entity: "mesh networks"` for the topic `off-grid-networking`, workflow `daily_brief`).
- **`words` in rows matches any word, ranked by how many a note holds;** a count or breakdown needs all of them. A count taken *for* rows (their total, a `wide` breakdown, an empty answer's counts) matches as the rows did, any word (`NoteSpec::any_words`); counting all words once showed 30 rows as "total 12", so the cut went unmarked. Questions carry wrong premises ("the Biden administration" for a Newsom order), and an all-words match returns nothing.
- **Lenient on shape, strict on names.** Empty values (`""`, `[]`, `{}`) are unset slots, and a list of strings for a text slot is joined; small models fill schemas that way.
- **Every query runs through `neo4j_query`'s read path** (read-only, schema guard, LIMIT).
- **An answer says what it is:** rows carry `standing` (a claim's status, "unsourced", or "not checked"). A cut is marked `truncated` with the total. `neo4j_query` adds a silent `LIMIT 100`, so `lookup` runs aggregates to 1,000 groups and every capped query one row past its limit (`run_capped`): the extra row coming back is what marks the cut. The brief index once stopped at 2026-09-16 and 403 sources showed as 100, unmarked.
- **A shape rule a model must follow belongs in code when it is measured to fail.** A notes view may declare `wide: <by_* shape>`: a call that asks for no shape and matches more notes than the limit gets that shape, with a `wide` line saying why. `learned` has `wide: by_topic` because the same rule in its description was ignored 6 of 6 times (E4B, codestral); a description sentence did work in `notes` and `daily_brief`. `by_topic` counts untopiced notes as `(no topic)`: half of September's learned notes have none. An empty answer repeats the filter in words and counts what exists without the window and without the narrowing slots; an unknown entity names the nearest ones.
- **Measured (2026-10-13):** `eval/cypher_golden.yaml` cases carry `view:` and `slots:`, and 36 of 39 returned exactly the reference rows through their golden view (the other 3 were cut at 30 rows and marked). As writers: E4B with output constrained to the catalog got 15 of 32 full and 18 near-full, against 10 of 33 with free Cypher, and tied free codestral. Nimble choosing the view was worse (32/39 views) and cost 34 s. Picking the view and then filling its slots in two steps was worse too.
- **Lists bind as lists:** `neo4j_query` params go through `bolt_param` (neo4rs's JSON-to-Bolt conversion). Before this, a list arrived as JSON text and `UNWIND $ids` matched nothing.
- **Upkeep is not learning:** a notes view's `except_work_kinds` leaves out notes whose `produced_by_task` is a task of a workflow of those kinds; `learned` sets `[maintenance]` (the owner, 2026-10-14). Notes from before `produced_by_task` was set (10-11) can't be traced and still count.
- **A thin short window says so:** a rows call with a window of one day, up to 24 hours, or `days: 1` that finds under half its usual share gets `thin`: the count against the 7 days before, by day (today's share is the part of the day gone by; under 4 usual says nothing). One note "today" otherwise reads as all there is, when the feeder had stalled (workflow-audit history, 2026-10-14).
- **Small negative integers:** neo4rs 0.8.0 read -1..-16 as 255..240; `vendor/neo4rs` (`[patch.crates-io]`) carries 0.9's fix. Drop it when 0.9 is stable.

subsystem: Web Search: engine failover ladder + usage ledger
title: Search rotation: paced free allowances first, the ladder behind
content:
Rules (built 2026-10-16; `crates/retrieve/src/search_rotation.rs`, `search_quality.rs`, `search.rs::engine_ladder`):

- **The first engine is rotated; the ladder is the fallback.** An engine whose YAML declares `budget` (`free`, `unit: call|usd`, `per: day|month|once`, optional `per_hour`/`per_minute`/`weight`, usd needs `cost_default` and may name `cost_field`) is in the rotation. Each call goes first to the budgeted engine that is *on pace* with the fewest calls today per unit of `weight`; ties keep `SEARCH_ENGINE_ORDER`. Then the remaining ladder in order; rate-limited and spent engines last. `SEARCH_ROTATION=off` restores the plain ladder.
- **Pacing is the point.** A monthly allowance may be spent up to `free × elapsed share of the month + 3% burst`; past that the engine is `AheadOfPace` and only a fallback (it borrows from later days). Daily allowances are not paced (they reset first); a one-time grant (`per: once`, Serper) is all available. A recent `quota_exhausted` makes an engine `Spent` whatever the ledger's arithmetic says (vendors that refill on the signup anniversary).
- **Spend comes from the ledger, in the budget's unit.** `search_usage.units`: Exa prices each answer itself (`costDollars.total`, $0.007 for an auto search with highlights), so its budget is dollars; every other engine is one unit per call. Only successful attempts count (no vendor bills a failed call); rows from before 2026-10-16 count at `cost_default`. Rate limits count attempts.
- **`rate_limited` is not `quota_exhausted`.** A 429 / "too many requests" without a spent-allowance phrase is `rate_limited`, which does not trigger the 6 h demotion; spent phrases (credits, quota, run out, insufficient_credits) are checked first.
- **Naming an engine skips the rotation for that call** (`picked: pinned`); the rest of the ladder still rotates behind it. The tool description now says to leave `engine` unset; the only pinned workflow is the owner's daily news (`engine: exa`, deliberate). A fallback rung is `picked: fallback`.
- **What is in the rotation is decided by measurement, not by price.** SerpApi (its 250/month is `google_news`'s), SearXNG (junk-prone last resort) and Brave (card, no cap) have no `budget` and stay fallback-only; Currents/Webz stay explicit-only. A new engine joins after a trial on real ledger queries: pin it on the same queries as the incumbents and compare the ledger's hints (`picked='pinned'`, `purpose='direct'`).
- **The ledger is the performance record.** Every attempt records who searched (`purpose`, `tool`, `task_id`), how it was picked, units, and quality hints from the results in hand (`dated`, `in_window`, `known_source` = on any `:SourceList`, `domains`); `search_results` keeps the links 90 days. `get_search_usage` adds `rotation` (each budgeted engine's used / allowed-so-far / standing) and `used` (results whose link was later cited in a claim-evidence edge's `sources` or ingested as `Note.source_url`). Hints are proxies: a count cannot see relevance (the 2026-09-01 junk-results lesson); `used` is the closest real signal, and `weight` is where it should go once there is enough of it.

subsystem: Web Search: engine failover ladder + usage ledger
title: Search rotation: why, and the TinyFish trial
content:
**Why rotation (2026-10-16).** The owner asked to spread search across the free tools ("I feel like the market will become over saturated in these tools and they'll all give some away for free, and we should take advantage of that") after adding Parallel and TinyFish keys. The ledger showed the ladder doing the opposite: from 10-02 to 10-16 Exa carried 1,359 of ~1,960 attempts (SearXNG 571, mostly named; Tavily 9, Serper 7), because a rung that answers stops the walk. Exa prices every answer ($0.007), so it had spent $9.50 of its $10 monthly credit by the 16th, while Tavily's 1,000/month and Serper's one-time 2,500 sat idle. On deploy the rotation marked Exa `AheadOfPace` (allowed $5.37 by mid-month) and the next six unpinned searches went tinyfish, serper, tavily, tinyfish, serper, tavily.

**TinyFish trial before it joined.** Ten real ledger queries (claim sentences and `recency` news) pinned on TinyFish, Tavily and Serper: dated share 0.71 / 0.87 / 0.81 (TinyFish web answers carry no date; its news answers do, relative: "2 days ago"), known-source share 0.32 / 0.28 / 0.34, ~6.5–7.2 distinct domains each, in-window 1.0 for all, latency 1.5 s / 2.9 s / 3.8 s. One TinyFish news+week query returned nothing and fell through to Tavily. Primary sources surfaced on claim queries (justice.gov, interpol.int, npr.org, congress.gov CRS, GAO). It joined `SEARCH_ENGINE_ORDER` after Tavily. Its limits (30/min, 500/hour, read from `X-RateLimit-*` and the docs) are `per_minute`/`per_hour` in its budget.

title: An audit pause lifts itself; any other pause is a decision
content:
- The boot protocol (`contexts/boot.yaml`) runs `manage_workflow audit disable_broken: true` on every startup. It pauses a workflow whose EVERY step names a tool missing from the live registry, with `paused_reason` = `AUDIT_PAUSE` (`skills/scheduler.rs`).
- The same audit re-enables a workflow whose `paused_reason` is exactly `AUDIT_PAUSE` once every step's tool is live again. Both directions log at WARN.
- **To keep a workflow off, give it a real `paused_reason`.** `enabled: false` in YAML is honoured only when the workflow is created (`enabled` is graph-owned), so a file edit does not pause an existing one; `manage_workflow upsert {name, enabled: false, paused_reason: "why"}` does, and keeps it yaml-owned.
- `health-monitor` lists every audit pause (`paused_by_audit_now`) and compares non-episodic notes written in 24 h with the 7-day rate, so a stalled feeder shows up within 12 h.
- A tool can be missing at boot for reasons that pass: a plugin moved or disabled mid-refactor. A pause that never lifts turns a passing miss into a silent outage.

title: media-watch paused for three days by a boot audit (2026-10-11..14)
content: The 10-11 plugin carve moved the media tools into a plugin (a97fe5f). A boot at 08:46 that day ran the workflow audit while `poll_media_sources` was not registered, and the audit paused `media-watch`: every step named a dead tool. media-watch is the poller that creates the `video-learning` and `article-learning` tasks, so learning stopped. Non-episodic notes per day went 261, 252, 257, 225 (10-07 to 10-10), then 83, 37, 22, and 1 on 10-14. The tool was back within hours; the audit only ever disabled, so the pause stayed. The same boot also paused entity-linking and relation-extraction, which were then kept off on purpose for the cloud quota (10-12) under the audit's reason. Nothing reported it. It surfaced when the owner asked 'what have we learned today?' and got the health monitor's own analysis, the one note of the day, and gave it a thumbs-down. Fixed 2026-10-14: the audit lifts its own pauses, the quota pauses got their real reason, and health-monitor reports audit pauses and the notes-written rate.

title: Workflows: one model for chains and schedules
content:
A workflow is a named job chain, `(:Workflow {name})`, seeded from `workflows/<name>.yaml` (the name must equal the file stem and be a slug). It replaced `:SchedulerChain` (steps picked by a regex on a task's goal) and `:ScheduledTask` (steps on a timer) on 2026-10-10 (CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN Phase 2b).

When it runs:
- On its schedule, if the file has `every: 30m|6h|1d|1w` (`interval_seconds` in the graph). The scheduler fires it (`fire_workflow`): a run Task, timers advanced first, chain enqueued.
- By name, with inputs, whenever something asks: `manage_workflow action=run`, `create_task workflow=… inputs=…`, `POST /api/work/workflows/{id}/run` (the HBI's Run now), and the Rust callers through `services::workflows::start_run` (media polling: video-learning / article-learning; spawn_gap_tasks and gap detection: fill-knowledge-gap; perception scan: consolidate / codebase / diagnose; the default for a queue backlog).
- A Task with no `workflow` (a free-text goal from chat) runs the one workflow marked `default: true`. Nothing routes by matching goal text any more.

A run is a `:Task` with `workflow` and `inputs_json`; run history is `MATCH (t:Task {workflow: $name})`. A run that names an unknown or disabled workflow, or lacks a required input, is refused when created (start_run) or failed visibly at dispatch, never left `created`.

File format: `name`, `description`, `every`, `enabled` (honoured only at creation; `enabled` is graph-owned), `default`, `inputs: [{name, description, required}]`, `checks: [evaluator, critic]`, `evaluation_rubric`, `data_class`, `topic`, `kind` (required when scheduled), `defaults:` (merged into each step), `steps`. Unknown keys are refused (`deny_unknown_fields`), so a leftover `pattern` or `interval_seconds` fails loudly instead of being ignored.

Steps see `{{task_id}}`, `{{goal}}`, `{{date}}`/`{{now}}`/`{{weekday}}` (local), `{{inputs.<name>}}`, `{{_prev}}`, `{{steps.<id>}}`. An undeclared `{{inputs.x}}` is rejected on save and in the seed-file test. `{{goal_topic}}` and `{{file_slug}}` no longer exist: the subject of a run is an input.

Checks are opt-in per workflow (`checks:`); none of the migrated ones opts in (measured: evaluator ran once in 60 days, critic never). The confidence guardrail (a first step's `confidence_threshold`) still applies; on `diagnose` it makes every diagnosis run stop as blocked for review.

Dispatch appends `update_task(completed)` unless a step already closes the run's own task.

Saving: `manage_workflow upsert` and REST `POST/PUT /workflows` share `services::workflows::save`: the body is laid over the stored workflow and the whole is checked (envelope schema for the tool, each step against its tool's input_schema, pinned models, step and input references, topic/kind, slug name). REST POST refuses an existing name; the tool's upsert edits it. A yaml-owned workflow edited at runtime is overwritten on the next startup unless `managed_by: runtime` is passed.

title: Monitors read their own claims as the prior report
content: On 2026-10-14 the intelligence-agency-claims-monitor's NEW section was 6 of 10 items it had reported the day before. Step 1 reads the prior report as the newest unchunked note with the monitor's source_context, but the claim step stores its claims under that same source_context after the report, so the prior report was yesterday's last claim: one line with no date. Sonnet flagged the missing date in its gaps and could not do the delta. slm-benchmark-watch and off-grid-networking-monitor had the same query. Fixed by filtering the note type (source_record, or not claim where a semantic baseline note is also read). Rule: a step that reads a monitor's last report filters by note_type, never by source_context alone. Same day: ApiTube was removed from the intelligence monitor; its JSON was ~200K of the report step's 232K characters for 6 articles, 5 of them aggregator copies or fringe, and Sonnet's input fell accordingly.

title: Crate layering: new code goes in the lowest crate that can hold it; old paths are re-exports
content:
Since CORE_AND_PLUGINS_PLAN 6f (2026-10-11) the core is 13 crates under the per-crate budget (scripts/size_budget.sh fails over 8K code lines; 6K is the soft target). Order, lowest first: protocol/models/repository, llm, graph, knowledge, work, scheduler and chat, retrieve, skills, api and host, app. A crate depends only on crates before it.
- The app's services::, skills:: and clients:: modules re-export the moved modules (pub use agent_brain_llm::{llm, routing, ...}), so crate::services::llm::X still resolves inside the app. Inside a split crate, write the real path (agent_brain_llm::..., crate::...), not services::.
- Several names exist twice (knowledge, scheduler, agent_runner, items, topics, search are both a service and a skill/client). Check which crate you mean.
- Ambient state that many layers read lives at the bottom: the job task-locals (USE_LOCAL_LLM, SELECTED_LLM, CURRENT_TOOL, CURRENT_OWNER_TASK) in agent_brain_llm::ctx (queue re-exports them); the bundle loader, plugin code status, architecture files and logging in agent_brain_graph; BrainEvent and the plugin retrieval-tool list in agent_brain_work.
- A trait's impl for a foreign type must live with the trait (orphan rule): TaskStore and WorkingMemoryStore live in work::store_impls beside their Neo4jClient impls, because a run starts through workflows.
- Test helpers under #[cfg(test)] are not visible across crates; skills::test_helpers serves the skills crate only.
- include_str! is relative to the file: the router source the developer plugin parses is the app's mcp::ROUTER_SOURCE, handed to the plugin Host as router_source.
- A new crate needs its Cargo.toml copied in the Dockerfile's dependency-cache stage (and a dummy lib.rs); scripts/size_budget.sh and check_plugin_deps.sh run in CI.

next exercise run sees it among prior deep dives and can go one level deeper.

title: fill-knowledge-gap.yaml: chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml
content:
Comment moved out of `chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml` (above `name: fill-knowledge-gap`):

chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml

The curiosity engine. Gap tasks are spawned by `spawn_gap_tasks` (from a
video's "## FOLLOW UP" section) and by the daily news-analysis schedule.

This chain searches BOTH the graph and the web, then answers the gap from the
union of the two. Searching only internal notes — which is what this chain did
before 2026-08-10 — cannot fill a knowledge gap by definition: a gap is
precisely the thing the graph does not contain. The result was self-referential
"Gap synthesis" notes that re-chewed prior notes and drifted into meta-
commentary about the source material instead of answering anything.

{{_prev}} only carries the PREVIOUS step's output, so the two search results
are banked in the WorkingMemory session "gap-{{task_id}}" and reassembled with
a neo4j_query step before the reason step (same idiom as chains/daily-news.yaml
and chains/video-learning.yaml).

{{goal_topic}} is {{goal}} with the "fill knowledge gap:" prefix stripped — the
prefix is for chain routing and is noise inside a search query.

title: fill-knowledge-gap.yaml: 3. Reassemble both sections so `context` carries them together rather than
content:
Comment moved out of `chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml` (above `- tool_name: neo4j_query`):

3. Reassemble both sections so `context` carries them together rather than
   only the push confirmation that {{_prev}} currently holds.

   ALREADY KNOWN is capped at 15,000 characters, with a marker saying how
   much was left out. The reason step's distiller reads at most 24,000
   characters (the first 16,000 and the last 8,000) and silently drops the
   middle. Measured 2026-10-10 on 143 runs: the stored notes ran to 20,500
   characters at the median (67,000 max), so 73 handoffs went over and lost
   a median 9,000 characters of stored notes from the middle, unmarked. The
   web section never exceeded 7,412, so 15,000 + web stays inside the window.
   search_notes ranks best first, so the cap drops the lowest-ranked notes.

title: fill-knowledge-gap.yaml: LOCAL, deliberately — this step is the single largest cloud consumer in
content:
Comment moved out of `chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml` (above `provider_hint: ollama`):

LOCAL, deliberately — this step is the single largest cloud consumer in
the system, and it is the one where per-call quality matters least.

The cost is not per run, it is per gap task, and gap tasks fan out
multiplicatively: `poll_media_sources` takes MEDIA_WATCH_MAX_PER_SOURCE (2)
videos from each of 15 active sources, and chains/video-learning.yaml calls
`spawn_gap_tasks` with `max` per video. Measured 2026-08-31: one 12-hourly
poll produced 29 `watch video:` tasks and 59 `fill knowledge gap:` tasks in
three hours — 88 cloud `reason` calls at ~5.1k input tokens each, against a
prior baseline of 47-80 cloud calls PER DAY. The five standing weekly
reports together are 1.4 cloud calls/day. This chain, uncapped, is ~99% of
background cloud spend, and every token it takes is a token chat cannot use.

Nothing about the work needs a frontier model: the step summarises search
results the chain just fetched into three fixed headings, with the payload
already distilled locally below. If a specific gap genuinely needs stronger
synthesis, raise it as a one-shot Task rather than putting every gap on cloud.

title: fill-knowledge-gap.yaml: 5. Clean up the scratch working-memory session.
content:
Comment moved out of `chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml` (above `- tool_name: neo4j_query`):

5. Clean up the scratch working-memory session.

   priority 1, NOT 0. The queue is a max-heap — `PrioritizedJob`'s Ord sorts
   priority descending, and `repository/src/agent_job.rs` pops with
   `ORDER BY j.priority DESC, j.created_at ASC` — so 0 is the LOWEST
   priority and runs only when nothing at 1 or 2 is waiting. Under a
   continuously-fed queue that resolves to never: measured 2026-08-31, the
   last priority-0 job to complete finished at 06:31Z, ~10 hours earlier,
   with 93 queued behind it (89 of them this cleanup step, oldest 3h38m).
   Cleanup stopped running the moment the media poll began filling the queue
   with priority-1/2 work, and left 203 orphaned WorkingMemory nodes across
   99 abandoned scratch sessions. It does not self-correct while work arrives.

   Priority 0 was expressing "not urgent", which is true and not the same as
   "skippable" — this step must eventually run or the graph accumulates
   scratch forever. At priority 1 it interleaves with the search steps at
   negligible cost: one Cypher DETACH DELETE, no LLM call, no network.
   Deferring something that costs nothing buys nothing.

  2. reason     → facts grounded ONLY in the gathered results

title: run-agent.yaml: chains/run-agent.yaml
content:
Comment moved out of `chains/run-agent.yaml` (above `name: run-agent`):

chains/run-agent.yaml

The Task front door to the shared agent loop (Phase 3 of
UNIFIED_AGENT_EXECUTION_PLAN). A Task whose goal is prefixed "run agent:" (or
"delegate to agent:") is handed to ONE overseeing agent that decides its own
steps, calls tools, and returns a cited answer — the "one agent per task" grain
(plan §5). This is how a background Task reaches the same loop chat's `delegate`
uses, instead of a fixed sequence of single tool calls.

`agent: "auto"` lets run_agent pick the best-fitting spawnable agent by
specialty (Phase 2 select_agent). If none fit, the step is rejected naming the
roster — the cue to construct one instead.

GATING: `run_agent` is only registered when SUBAGENT_ENABLED is on (default
OFF). With the feature off this chain is still seeded, but its run_agent step
fails as "no such tool" if a matching Task is ever created — so only create
"run agent:" Tasks with the feature enabled.

{{goal_topic}} is {{goal}} with the routing prefix stripped.

watchlist and nothing bounds it.

This step also has a second-order cost the others do not: its "## FOLLOW UP"
section is what `spawn_gap_tasks` turns into gap tasks, so every run here
creates up to `max` further chain runs. Keeping it local caps both.

content:

    back unchanged, so {{_prev}} still carries it into the banking step below.
`max` is a fan-out multiplier, not a quality knob. Each gap task is a full
chains/fill-knowledge-gap.yaml run (2 searches + a reason step), so this
number multiplies against the videos-per-poll cap: 15 active sources x 2
videos x `max` x 2 polls/day. At 4 that is up to 240 gap-fill chains a day,
which is what buried the queue on 2026-08-31 (54 jobs still queued and 18
reason steps parked three hours into the day). Lowered to 2. The follow-up
concepts are ranked, so the ones dropped are the weakest of each video's list.

title: video-learning.yaml: Extract checkable assertions from the stored note into individual claims.
content:

Extract checkable assertions from the stored note into individual claims.
{{_prev}} is store_note's echo of the note content. The extractor reads
attribution out of the text itself (the summary names the channel), so the
claims carry who asserted them. Pure side-effect on the chain: this is the
last content step, so nothing downstream depends on its output.

title: ai-dev-board-job-search.yaml: AI Dev Board Job Search — daily, two boards, RESUME-MATCHED, deterministic.
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/ai-dev-board-job-search.yaml` (above `name: AI Dev Board Job Search`):

AI Dev Board Job Search — daily, two boards, RESUME-MATCHED, deterministic.

Reads each job's DESCRIPTION against Ara's resume and surfaces only the roles
whose JD actually matches his stack, best-fit first. The board's own match_score
ranks against a generic skill list; this chain re-reads the full JD text (title,
tags, description) against resume-grounded signals and ranks by that fit — all
deterministically in execute_code (Python; never let the local model reproduce
links or invent a fit). The resume is pulled live from the graph
(source_context:"resume") so it tracks resume edits.

ACTIVATION: the live node is YAML-managed + enabled, so editing these steps
force-syncs on the next brain restart (enabled is graph-owned and stays true).

Pattern (mirrors hardware-tripwire): each source + the resume is banked into a
jobsearch-scratch-<date> WorkingMemory session under a unique MARKER line,
reassembled with neo4j_query, matched/ranked by execute_code, pushed into the
fresh jobsearch-<date> session so notify_user opens a resumable chat where a
reply routes to the job-applicant profile (session-pinned in clients/chat/turn.rs).

title: api-scout.yaml: Weekly API scout — SEEDED DISABLED for human review.
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/api-scout.yaml` (above `name: "Weekly API scout: discover free public REST APIs for our interests, inges`):

Weekly API scout — SEEDED DISABLED for human review.

`enabled: false` is honored ONLY on first creation (enabled is graph-owned and
never force-synced — see CLAUDE.md "ScheduledTask ownership"). So this task is
created OFF and will not run until you turn it on after reviewing what it does:

  MATCH (s:ScheduledTask {name:'Weekly API scout: discover free public REST APIs for our interests, ingest the keyless ones, flag key-gated ones to the human'})
  SET s.enabled = true, s.next_run_at = datetime()

It runs ONE run_agent step driving the `api-scout` spawnable profile through the
shared AgentRunner. Requires SUBAGENT_ENABLED=true (it is). The sub-agent runs
on the unmetered base model, ingests keyless APIs via ingest_api, and
notify_user's the human about key-gated ones — it never signs up or invents a
key. Its own procedure/safety rules live in contexts/api-scout.yaml.

A ScheduledTask's steps run VERBATIM (no chain matching, no evaluator), so the
behaviour is defined by the agent profile, not by chain routing.

(:ScheduledTask) node, or the old one keeps running alongside this one.
