title: capability-mining.yaml: schedules/capability-mining.yaml
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/capability-mining.yaml` (above `name: "Capability mining: identify agent/tool candidates from todos and repeated`):

schedules/capability-mining.yaml

Weekly capability mining. Reframed to mine REAL signal instead of an empty
`(:Todo)` set: the previous query matched `(:Todo)` nodes, of which there are
none, so the local model received no grounding and free-associated generic
"an LLM agent should have..." suggestions the brain already implements.

The durable capability-gap signal is repeatedly-FAILING tasks: when the same
capability (goal prefix) fails or blocks over and over, that is a concrete,
grounded gap worth building for. Their `context` carries the reason WHY: an
evaluator/adversarial critique when the task had success_criteria, and — for
scheduler-dispatched chains that simply died — a "[FAILURE]" line written by
the queue coordinator (fail_task_with_reason) naming the dead step and its
last error. Earlier, a died chain left the run stuck in_progress until the
6-hour stale reaper flipped it to 'failed' with only boilerplate context, so
this step reasoned over nothing and free-associated; that gap is now closed.

NOTE: the name is kept byte-for-byte identical to the pre-existing node. The
seeder only force-syncs yaml-owned (or legacy) nodes — a runtime-owned node is
skipped — so the live node's `managed_by` was flipped to 'yaml' once to hand
ownership to this file. From then on the seeder force-syncs these steps on
every startup.

title: capability-mining.yaml: Step flow and {{_prev}} chain:
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/capability-mining.yaml` (above `- tool_name: neo4j_query`):

Step flow and {{_prev}} chain:
  1. neo4j_query → capabilities (goal prefixes) that fail/block repeatedly,
                   with counts + a sample of each one's failure context.
  2. reason      → grounded ONLY on {{_prev}} (passed via `context`, NOT the
                   question — passing it in the question triggers the RAG
                   self-contamination loop where reason retrieves its own
                   prior capability_mining notes). Emits JSON candidates.
  3. store_note  → persists the candidates as a reflection for review.
  4. run_agent   → deep-diver takes the FIRST candidate and grounds it in
                   this codebase: the files and functions it touches, and
                   a Rust sketch of the change, compile-checked in the
                   sandbox where it can stand alone. Before this step every
                   run ended in general advice ("add retry logic", "improve
                   validation") with no file, no function, and no code.
  5. store_note  → persists the grounded proposal.

title: claim-verification.yaml: Claim verification sweep — work through the unverified claim backlog.
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/claim-verification.yaml` (above `name: "Claim verification: gather evidence for unverified claims and record what`):

Claim verification sweep — work through the unverified claim backlog.

Claim extraction (video-learning, daily-news, learn) is cheap and runs at
ingest; verification costs a web search plus an assessment call per claim, so
it runs here in bounded batches rather than inline. That keeps ingestion fast
and spends the search budget deliberately.

`claim(action=verify)` searches for independent coverage, records the evidence
as its own note, judges support/contradiction from that evidence alone, and
recomputes status from the resulting edges. It never rewrites a claim: the
assertion is preserved exactly as made, and only what surrounds it changes.

Absence of evidence leaves a claim UNVERIFIED, never refuted. A niche claim
nobody else has covered is not thereby false, and treating silence as
refutation would quietly mark true-but-unreported things wrong.

The `name` is the Neo4j MERGE key — do not change it without deleting the old
(:ScheduledTask) node.

title: daily-news.yaml: Daily news briefing — expanded coverage (metro Detroit, Michigan, national,
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/daily-news.yaml` (above `name: "Daily news aggregation and briefing: aggregate headlines from world, tech`):

Daily news briefing — expanded coverage (metro Detroit, Michigan, national,
world, tech, business, markets, weather).

Engine note (2026-10-02): the seven news searches request `engine: exa` with
`recency: day` and `news: true` — see the note above the first search step.
The history below is why google_news was used until then; it ranked by
relevance and returned stale stories once the queries said "today".

Earlier engine note: the seven news searches requested `engine: google_news`, which
routes to SerpApi's Google News engine. `engine` only PROMOTES that engine to
the head of the failover ladder — SearXNG and the rest remain as fallbacks —
so once SerpApi's shared monthly quota is spent, the brief degrades to SearXNG
automatically instead of failing (see skills/search.rs). General/background
data mining does NOT set `engine`, so it keeps leading with the unmetered
self-hosted SearXNG.

Outage + recovery (resolved 2026-09-08): from 2026-09-05 SerpApi's Google News
engine returned `503 "We couldn't get valid results … Please try again later."`
after a 90s timeout (4 of 7 news searches failed on 2026-09-05), which dropped
every failed section through to SearXNG's news-incapable engine set and made
the brief read "no news." As a stopgap the steps were switched to plain
`engine: serpapi` (Google organic). That stopgap under-delivered: organic
results are undated evergreen pages, so on 2026-09-08 the reason step could not
date-verify them and the brief came back near-empty (weather + one 3-month-old
story). google_news was re-tested live on 2026-09-08 and answers again with
dated, source-named stories, so the steps are reverted to it here — that is the
correct engine for a dated daily brief. If it 503s again, the ladder still
falls through, but the right stopgap is to fix the query freshness, not to drop
to organic. `source_list` is intentionally omitted: news queries already return
usable metro/Michigan results without a site: restriction, and the
site-restricted SearXNG queries were what produced the junk-results problem.

Pattern note: {{_prev}} only carries the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING step's output,
so each search_web step is followed by a push_context step that banks the
results into the date-scoped working-memory session "news-raw-{{date}}".
A neo4j_query step then collects every section at once and hands the full
bundle to the reason step. The final step deletes the raw session entries.

The `name` is the Neo4j MERGE key — do not change it without deleting the
old (:ScheduledTask) node, or the old chain keeps running alongside this one.

title: daily-news.yaml: Clear any leftover raw session FIRST (self-healing)
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/daily-news.yaml` (above `- tool_name: neo4j_query`):

── Clear any leftover raw session FIRST (self-healing) ──────────────────
The cleanup step at the END only runs if the whole chain succeeds. If a
later step dies (e.g. the writer hits a provider error), its banked blocks
survive in news-raw-{{date}}, and the NEXT run's gather pulls the
accumulation — which compounds until the writer's context overflows
(observed 2026-09-08: four failed runs stacked to ~306K tokens and every
subsequent run 400'd on context length). Deleting at the start makes each
run idempotent regardless of how the previous one ended.

title: daily-news.yaml: Collect: search each topic, bank results in working memory
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/daily-news.yaml` (above `- tool_name: search_web`):

── Collect: search each topic, bank results in working memory ──────────
2026-10-02: Exa news + recency:day, not google_news. Google News ranks by
relevance, so "… today" returned months-old pages (0 of 8 current for the
world query); Exa with a one-day window returned CNBC, Al Jazeera, France24
and Politico from that day. ~210 Exa searches/month of the $10 credit. The
ladder still falls back to SearXNG and Tavily with the same recency/news
filters. Queries say "latest", never a date: a literal date over-constrains.
"-sports": the user does not want sports in the brief.

title: daily-news.yaml: Weather: an API, not a web search
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/daily-news.yaml` (above `- tool_name: http_request`):

── Weather: an API, not a web search ───────────────────────────────────
This was `search_web "Detroit Michigan weather forecast today"` until
2026-09-01, and it never once produced a forecast. A forecast is
structured, perishable data; a search returns *links to pages that render
it*, and a result snippet almost never contains the numbers. With the
mainstream SearXNG engines CAPTCHA-blocked (see searxng/settings.yml) the
four results on 09-01 were: the Detroit-Windsor tunnel Wikipedia article,
a Michigan weather blog last updated January 2023, a Detroit nostalgia
site, and a Czech forecast page. The model then correctly wrote "No results
collected today" — the brief was honest, the input was junk.

Because that is 4 results and not 0, `search_web`'s ladder counted rung one
as having answered and never fell through to a keyed engine. Zero-result
fall-through cannot catch this; only using the right source can.

api.weather.gov (US NWS) is free, needs no key, and has no quota. The
gridpoint URL is stable for a fixed location and was derived once from
https://api.weather.gov/points/42.3314,-83.0458 (Detroit, MI) ->
.properties.forecast. Re-derive it that way if the location changes.
NWS requires a descriptive User-Agent and 403s without one.

title: daily-news.yaml: ApiTube: TOPICAL structured, dated articles (supplements google_news)
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/daily-news.yaml` (above `- tool_name: http_request`):

── ApiTube: TOPICAL structured, dated articles (supplements google_news) ──
Additive, not a replacement: if ApiTube is unreachable, these blocks are
simply absent and the google_news sections above still carry the brief. Auth
(X-API-Key) is injected from the seeded `apitube` ApiContext, so no key
appears here. Free tier is 100 req/day; these are 2 calls/run.

Verified live 2026-09-08: `title=<keyword>` is the only reliable topical
filter — `category` and `source.country.code` returned unrelated/global
results, so they are NOT used. `title=Michigan` and `title=artificial
intelligence` both return today-dated, on-topic articles with source + date.
Response: results[] with title, href, published_at, source.domain, description.

title: daily-news.yaml: Write the brief on the active cloud model (OLLAMA_MODEL), which is now
content:

content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/entity-linking.yaml` (above `name: "Entity linking: propose Wikipedia reference links for entities"`):

Entity linking (HBI plan Phase 18, §11).

Finds which Wikidata item (and English Wikipedia article) entities are and
proposes it as their reference link, for the user to confirm in the entity
drawer. Only entities named in claims (public sources: videos, articles,
news) are looked up here; anything else only when the user presses "Look up".
The step pins gpt-oss:120b-cloud (Ollama Cloud, no_log, $0): choosing from

wrong on the tuning set, while taking the top search result was wrong 13 of

one place the model is pinned.

with WIKIMEDIA_CONTACT in the user agent, and a 429 ends the run early.
20 entities an hour clears the ~3,100 public entities in about a week.

accelerator supply chain for disruption signals before they reach mainstream news.

{{_prev}} only carries the PREVIOUS step's output, so each search_web result is
banked into the WorkingMemory session "tripwire-{{task_id}}" and reassembled with
a neo4j_query step before the reason step (same idiom as chains/video-learning.yaml).
The prior run's note is banked first so the reason step performs a DELTA against
it rather than re-describing the world from scratch.

EVERY step must carry `provider_hint: ollama` except the single synthesis step.
`use_local` in queue.rs is `provider_hint == Some("ollama")`, so an OMITTED hint
is not "default local" — it routes to the active config, which is a cloud model.
The runtime definition that shadowed this file for two weeks omitted the hint on
all six of its steps and put four searches and a store_note on cloud for nothing.

    chemistries returns worse results for all three.

    semiconductors list, battery and material substitution are not (no

title: intelligence-agency-claims-monitor.yaml: Intelligence agency claims monitor — daily.
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/intelligence-agency-claims-monitor.yaml` (above `name: "intelligence-agency-claims-monitor"`):

Intelligence agency claims monitor — daily.

Replaces the runtime-authored GDELT version (disabled 2026-09-26): it called
https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/events/events, which does not exist, so 14
of 15 runs since 09-08 reasoned over a 404 page and were recorded "completed".
See project-docs/BRAIN_ASSESSMENT_FIXES_PLAN.md, step 5.

Sources, both already free and keyed:
  - ApiTube (`apitube` ApiContext, 100 req/day; 3 calls/run). `title=` is the
    only topical filter that works, and it is AND-ed: `title=CIA OR Mossad`
    returned only titles naming BOTH (verified 2026-09-26), so each keyword is
    its own call. `sort.by=published_at` returns newest first; ApiTube defaults
    the window to the last 31 days. ~17 KB per article, so per_page stays at 2.
  - SearXNG via search_web, restricted to the `news` SourceList.

Every search passes `prior_knowledge: false`. The graph-first block would quote
our own earlier notes, and the report would restate them as today's news. The
prior report is supplied separately, labelled as such, for the delta.

The first run (2026-09-26) reached back to 2016 because an empty prior report
was read as "everything is new", and a spy-museum travel piece matched
`espionage`. Gates 2 and 4 of the report prompt exist for those two cases.

This is public news, so the report runs as data_class: public.

title: item-dispatch.yaml: Item dispatch (HBI plan Phase 13; TODO_DELAYED_PROMPT_PLAN.md Phase 3).
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/item-dispatch.yaml` (above `name: "Item dispatch: run the user's items assigned to an agent when they are du`):

Item dispatch (HBI plan Phase 13; TODO_DELAYED_PROMPT_PLAN.md Phase 3).

Runs the user's items assigned to an agent once they are due. A schedule's
steps are enqueued verbatim, so it cannot loop over N items itself: the loop
is the tool (`dispatch_due_todos`), as `poll_media_sources` is for media.
An item handed over in the HBI is offered a run at once; this poll catches
due dates and failed runs. Hourly: a run is a Task in Work's lineage, and a
15-minute poll would add ~96 run records a day for no faster answer.

The tool keeps the guardrails: an agent that can act outside the graph waits
for the user's approval, at most 3 runs per item, at most 3 started per poll.

title: media-watch.yaml: Media watch — autonomous channel/playlist polling.
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/media-watch.yaml` (above `name: "Media watch: poll subscribed channels for new videos to learn from"`):

Media watch — autonomous channel/playlist polling.

A single poll_media_sources step checks every active :MediaSource for new
videos and creates a "watch video: <url>" Task per new upload; the scheduler
then routes each Task through chains/video-learning.yaml on a later tick.

Self-gating: poll_media_sources is a no-op unless MEDIA_WATCH_ENABLED=true,
so this schedule is safe to seed on deployments without yt-dlp / a watchlist.

The `name` is the Neo4j MERGE key — do not change it without deleting the old
(:ScheduledTask) node.

title: media-watch.yaml: 6 hours, paired with MEDIA_WATCH_MAX_PER_SOURCE=1 — this is a burst-shaping
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/media-watch.yaml` (above `kind: learning`):

6 hours, paired with MEDIA_WATCH_MAX_PER_SOURCE=1 — this is a burst-shaping
pair, and neither half works alone.

The daily *cap* is unchanged (15 sources x 1 video x 4 polls = 60/day, the
same as the old 15 x 2 x 2), so nothing the brain would have learned is lost.
What changes is the delivery: at most 15 videos arrive at once instead of 30,
four times a day instead of twice. One burst is ~15 x 19 GPU-minutes = 4.75
GPU-hours, which drains across two `semaphore_ollama` permits in ~2.4 wall
hours and leaves 3.6 hours of headroom before the next poll. The old 30-video
burst needed ~4.8 hours and overlapped everything else on the queue — that
saturation is what pinned local calls at the 120s ceiling on 2026-08-31.

The cap was never the binding constraint in steady state: measured upstream
publishing is ~9-19 videos/day across the whole watchlist, well under 60. It
binds during *backlog drain* — a newly activated source's RSS carries ~15
recent uploads — which is exactly when the burst hurt. Polling more often
with a lower per-source cap also improves freshness: a channel posting twice
in a day yields 1+1 across two polls rather than being clipped at the cap.
topic: none — spans topics on purpose

title: off-grid-networking-monitor.yaml: schedules/off-grid-networking-monitor.yaml
content:
Comment moved out of `schedules/off-grid-networking-monitor.yaml` (above `name: "Off-Grid Networking Monitor"`):

schedules/off-grid-networking-monitor.yaml

Standing watch on off-grid / decentralized mesh networking (Meshtastic,
Reticulum, LoRa, and adjacent protocols), backing the "Off Grid Decentralized
network" todo.

This schedule was originally created at runtime from a chat session on
2026-08-12 and was structurally broken in three ways. Its first and only run
is the documentation for why each rule below exists:

  1. The `reason` step passed no `context`, so the search results it had just
     fetched were discarded and it answered from RAG over the graph:
     "there is no information regarding new hardware releases or specific
     protocol updates" — written moments after a search returned 5 results.
  2. The `store_note` content was the literal string
     "Updates on off-grid networking research for {{date}}." with no
     {{_prev}}, so the stored note WAS that sentence. The findings were
     thrown away every run.
  3. It stored `semantic` with no `source_context`, so the placeholder
     accumulated as "knowledge the brain established" and no future run
     could retrieve its predecessor to perform a delta.

A fourth failure, from the rewritten version, on 2026-08-19: step 6 is the
only cloud-routed step here, and it died 3/3 on a transport error reaching
ollama.com, dead-lettering and failing the owning Task. `SharedLlm` only fell
back to local on 429/403 at the time, so an unreachable host burned all three
attempts while the local model sat idle, and the week's report simply did not
exist. `classify_unavailable` now covers transport and 5xx failures too — see
the fallback note under Critical Dev Notes in CLAUDE.md. The lesson for this
file: a single cloud step is a single point of failure for the whole run, and
a missing weekly report looks exactly like a quiet week in the field.

Same banking idiom as slm-benchmark-watch.yaml — {{_prev}} carries only the
previous step's output, so consecutive searches would discard all but the
last. Each sweep is banked into "offgrid-{{task_id}}" and reassembled.
